epochs.name: Security Hardening
epochs.goal: Validate every saved security candidate, fix each confirmed root cause, add hostile regression proof, and close with an independent security review and a clean follow-up scan.

epochs.name: Cross Platform
epochs.goal: macOS, Windows, and every other non-Linux target. Jet development targets Linux first, so cross-platform support is sequenced deliberately after the Linux experience is right, and a red macOS or Windows row never blocks Linux work.

epochs.name: Developer Experience
epochs.goal: Jet programs on every target get the best developer experience of any ecosystem: one-command entry, one observation protocol with panels rendered in the browser, dev dashboard, terminal, editor, and native overlays, a live loop that keeps state on every tier, a first-party web suite, and equal-depth tooling for games, backend, live debugging, systems, mobile, data, and CLI work.

epochs.name: Foundations for every domain
epochs.goal: Every critical area (web, games, CLI and scripts, data analysis, backend services, AI/ML apps, GUI apps, embedded) can be built by a library author with Jet's primitives, ecosystem tools, core library, and shared data types. Probes find the primitive gaps; only primitives are proposed; buildable niches get executable examples; critical areas get batteries as needed. Replaces the withdrawn domain-matrix slate (owner, 2026-09-02).

epochs.name: Sprint: owner goals
epochs.goal: Owner sprint goals (2026-10): live high-level targets with measured completion; each goal is a milestone whose criteria are its checkpoints; finished goals are closed out and archived.

epochs.name: Best scripting language
epochs.goal: Jet becomes the best scripting language of all time: it beats Lua, JavaScript, TypeScript, Bash and Python on startup and run time for real scripts, and on how easy a script is to write, read and reason about, measured by tokens per task and by review of the same programs written in each language. Jet already runs the repository's own tooling, so its scripting surface is infrastructure.

epochs.name: Declarations as types
epochs.goal: Markers, diagnostics, effects, facts and derives are ordinary types with Core traits; reflection, code generation and const generics are complete; Core declares its own host leaves.
exitCriteria: Every card in the epoch is done: `tower chain` shows 0 open criteria for it.
The batch compiler that lands its last card runs the full suite (cases, ui, golden, core) with no new failure against the previous cycle.

Every marker, diagnostic, effect, fact and derive is declared as an ordinary Core type with a Core trait: the compiler has no hardcoded marker or effect table that a Core declaration does not back (CoreDeclarations guard passes).
Every owner ballot the epoch's cards wait on is ratified or withdrawn: `tower ballots` lists none posted for an E18 card.

cards.title: Executable leases: non-Linux empty and data-only runtime proof
cards.body: [R-POSTE3-1:#467:0] Split from the former #467 umbrella. This card owns only “Executable leases: non-Linux empty and data-only runtime proof.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #467. The other 6 delivery slices have separate cards.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove on native macOS and Windows that the Jet Jetpack's empty and data-only executable leases hold (D-JPK-EXECLEASE1=A): lease, replacement, stale lease, crash or interrupted replacement, and rollback, without ever publishing a partial executable or deleting the last good version.

## Current state
- Rust reference: crates/jetpack/src/RuntimePolicy/ExecutableLease.rs (2381 lines). According to the card log, it implements non-Linux data-only and empty leases and fails closed on unsupported targets. It has only been exercised on Linux.
- Jet: Jetpack/Store/Source/ArtifactStore/Leases.jet (259 lines) and Jetpack/Foundation/Source/ProjectLock.jet exist. The lease protocol and state port is #3646 (not started).
- Foundation/Source/NativeSandbox.jet:98 fails closed on Windows.
- The owner paused cross-platform epoch e13 on 2026-09-11. Linux evidence cannot close this card.

## Changes
1. After #3646, add platform claims to Jetpack/Environment/Tests/ExecutableLease.jet for the empty and data-only cases: acquire, replace while leased, stale-lease recovery, interrupted replacement, and rollback to the last good generation.
2. Add a native macOS and Windows runner job to .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs the Jetpack check with `--tests` on those hosts.
3. crates/jetpack stays behavioural reference only.

## Proof
On macOS and Windows runners, `JETPACK_WORKER=b19lease Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area Environment --tests` -> `JETPACK CHECK OK (check, default run, AOT test)`, with the lease claims passing. A variant that bypasses the Jet lease store makes those claims fail.

## Batch
batch-deferred: e13 cross-platform is owner-deferred, and native runners are required.

## Dependencies
#3646 (the Jet lease protocol and state). Resumes when the owner reopens e13.

One agent adds both Windows rows in one coherent patch. ABI-substance criteria below replace the mispasted filesystem/os-facts template.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Add a non-skipping native Windows C ABI runtime matrix for x64 and x86 (it absorbed #997). Production-generated Jet Rust links against real MSVC C, and the matrix proves per architecture:
- exact imported and exported symbols;
- struct and enum layout checked against C;
- capture-free callbacks under reentrant and concurrent foreign threads;
- poison-byte safety of status and out-pointers;
- borrowed UTF-8 string returns;
- default C/system and every supported Windows calling convention, including the x86 stdcall and fastcall spellings.

**Deferral**
The owner moved this to e13. Linux cannot prove it.

**Current state**
- The harness is `tests/cffi_native_matrix.rs` (Linux rows only) plus `tests/cffi.rs`.
- Self-hosted FFI lowering is `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/ForeignFunctions.jet` and `CffiFacts.jet`, with jet-ffi-descriptor-v1 per-language ABI leaves.
- The Rust parser and sema mirrors are in `crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/ffi.rs` and `crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/external_tests_ffi.rs`.
- #436 exhaustiveness and hostile gates are done.

**Changes**
1. Add Windows x64 and x86 rows to the shared fixture in `tests/cffi_native_matrix.rs`, with pinned `cl.exe` and rustc identities. A missing tool, architecture row, or case fails the job.
2. Add CI jobs for `windows-latest` (x64 and x86 MSVC) in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
3. Fix convention and layout defects in ForeignFunctions.jet and the Rust mirror. Update `Docs/spec/diagnostics.md` if a diagnostic changes.

**Proof**
- On Windows x64 and x86 runners, `cargo test --test cffi_native_matrix` passes with both Windows rows executed.
- `cargo test --test cffi` passes.
- Independent review confirms the #436 gates are unregressed.

**Batch**
`batch-deferred`: e13 cross-platform.

**Dependencies**
Native Windows MSVC runners (external).

## Gate and ownership

This card remains frozen until the owner explicitly unfreezes it. Preparation does not claim implementation, measurement, or ratification. It owns only the source ledger and adversarial crosswalk; it does not own compiler-speed architecture, a profiler, a budget engine, or a task runtime.

## Current authority

Use the current one-core/two-lens contract in docs/spec/reference/compiler-speed.md and the production architecture boundary in docs/spec/architecture.md:468-502. Treat docs/audits/compiler-latency-video-crosswalk-2026-08-24.md as the existing evidence crosswalk. #666 is the canonical corpus and runner; #2859 owns the current measurement gate. Follow-up implementation belongs to #666, #669, #441, #241, or #126.

## Work after unfreeze

1. Re-read the source ledger and separate transcript claims, linked-author corrections, repeated comments, disputed anecdotes, and Jet inference.
2. Cross-check only the existing #666 clean/no-change/edit corpus, environment identity, phase totals, cache identities, construct-scale rows, and parity rail. Do not create another benchmark path.

4. Hand each uncovered gap to its owner with a targeted proof request. Keep semantic, diagnostic, safety, determinism, and feature-parity gates intact.

## Dependencies and exit

No card prerequisite is missing. The owner unfreeze is required. Existing criteria 1-8 remain the exit contract; do not reset their statuses or duplicate #666/#2859 measurement ownership.

cards.title: Cross compilation: target toolchain and sysroot resolution
cards.body: [R-POSTE3-1:#758:0] Split from the former #758 umbrella. This card owns only “Cross compilation: target toolchain and sysroot resolution.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #758. The other 3 delivery slices have separate cards.
cards.plan:
## Goal
This is the toolchain and sysroot slice of the #758 cross-compilation umbrella (siblings #1058, #1059, #1060). For a selected target, the host must resolve the real toolchain, standard library, sysroot and linker, and pass them to the Jet driver as HostFacts. Jet owns the list of supported target names. A missing prerequisite fails honestly, with Jet wording that never tells the user to run a rustc or rustup command. No artifact built for the host is ever labeled with a target name.

## Current state
- The Jet side is ported:
  - `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Target/TargetMachine.jet:47` (hosted), `:71` (bare metal), `:464` (`jet_target_machine_for_facts`), `:487`/`:508` (wasm browser/wasi) and `:529` (dossier).
  - `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:732-761` selects the machine from `HostFacts.target_triple` (E0003 when it is missing or empty). `:760` always passes `no_os: false`.
- On the host side, `Source/CmdCompile.rs:10786-10805` (`validate_target`) calls `Doctor::probe_target_component` (`Source/Doctor.rs:535`) and emits E3302. rustc and rustup text leaks to the user:
  - `Source/Doctor.rs:524` says "run `rustup target add {triple}`".
  - `Doctor.rs:156` and `CmdCompile.rs:14251,14401` say "install Rust from https://rustup.rs".
  - `Source/main.rs:2897` says "or a rustc target triple".
- The target-name list is the Rust const `crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:995` (`TARGET_MACHINE_NAMES`). There is no Jet-owned list.
- `tests/cross.rs` covers freestanding E3301 and OS gating only. There is no toolchain or sysroot check. The old plan's `crates/jet-foundation/src/TargetProfile.rs` does not exist.

## Changes
1. **JetFoundation.** Add `jet_target_supported_names()` in `TargetMachine.jet` as the single list of machine names and triples. Point the host at it and delete the Rust `TARGET_MACHINE_NAMES` duplicate.
2. **JetDriver.** `Pipeline.jet` passes the HostFacts toolchain facts (sysroot, linker, standard-library path) into the target machine and dossier, so provenance records the resolved toolchain.
3. **Host CLI (retained).**
   - `Doctor.rs` and `CmdCompile.rs::validate_target` resolve the sysroot, linker and standard library for the selected triple.
   - Rewrite the E3302 fix text and the E2105 texts in Jet terms. The fix names the Jet-owned remedy (`jet toolchain`, which exists at `main.rs:3691`) or the supported-target list.
   - Register the text in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet` and its Prelude twin.
   - Owner gate: if a new `jet toolchain` verb is needed to install a target library, stop and put it on a ballot; do not ship it unapproved.
4. Update `Docs/spec/architecture.md` where it describes target resolution.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test cross cross_toolchain_resolution`: the new test covers success, a missing standard library, and a bypass that must fail.
- `cargo test --test cross`: existing tests stay green.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/target_std_missing.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`, if the diagnostic is renderable as a fixture.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-host-cli`: most of the work is in `Source/` CLI and Doctor toolchain resolution. The Jet side is a small registry and driver edit.

## Dependencies
None blocking. #1059 and #1060 build on this slice.

Target ABI, Core runtime, linker inputs, sysroot, artifacts, debug data, provenance, and runtime smoke match native-target results where applicable.
Missing target tools, host leakage, ABI mismatch, unsupported features, link failure, and emulator divergence fail honestly with no host-native artifact mislabeled as target output.
Targeted success and failure checks exercise the real production path. They fail when the key implementation is removed or bypassed.
Affected docs, examples, diagnostics, goldens, and audit output match the shipped behavior. Full-suite proof stays at epoch closeout.

[retarget] Jet-side proof (Rust freeze 2026-10-01): the behavior the replaced Rust test checks holds on the Jet compiler or the Jet-hosted tool, shown by an equivalent test against the Jet implementation; no new Rust test and no Rust compiler change. Replaces the Rust-compiler proof: "`cargo test --test cross cross_toolchain_resolution` passes: (a) `jet build --target=<installed foreign triple>` produces an artifact whose file header matches the target (ELF machine / Mach-O / PE / wasm) and whose provenance names the selected target machine; (b) with the target standard library absent (test points the probe at an empty sysroot) the build stops with registered E3302 whose rendered text contains no `rustc`/`rustup` and lists the Jet-supported target names; (c) the check fails if `Compiler/JetDriver` target selection or the `Source/CmdCompile.rs::validate_target` probe is bypassed."
[#1058] C headers, libraries, linker inputs and runtime objects bind to the selected target. Host leakage, ABI mismatch and link failure fail honestly, with no mislabeled host artifact.

[#1059] A typed target profile controls ABI, Core runtime, linker inputs, sysroot, artifacts, debug data and provenance. Unknown or duplicate profiles and missing tools are rejected before codegen. The check fails when JetDriver target validation is bypassed.

[#1060] Every declared native-to-foreign row in Tests/cross.rs (Jet-side successor) builds and smoke-runs or validates, and matches native results where applicable. The check fails when JetDriver target selection is bypassed.

From a Linux x86-64 host, `jet build --target=<t> hello.jet` for aarch64-linux, x86_64-macos, aarch64-macos and x86_64-windows produces binaries that run on matching CI runners; each is smaller and builds faster than `deno compile --target <t>` of the JS hello (Jet/Deno < 1.00 for size and for time).

Plain `jet build` in a package whose targets: selects a non-host profile (Examples/embedded/heap_free_core, web.no_os) builds for that target or refuses with a registered diagnostic; it never silently produces a host x86-64 ELF (BallotDesign repro q/bd/probe/fx/target_today: od -N4 .jet/build/run prints 7f 45 4c 46)

cards.body:
[R-POSTE3-1:#322:1] Split from the former #322 umbrella. This card owns only “jet deploy: authenticated artifact transfer and host activation.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #322. The other 4 delivery slices have separate cards.

## Lessons learned (deploy-rs mine 2026-08-06)

Track: docs/research/deploy-rs-lessons-2026-08-06.md

- Real path is local build → authenticated copy → remote activate. Shell tar stubs are not product closeout.
- Split connect identity from activation privilege (deploy-rs `sshUser` / `user`). Owner ballot: **D-JOS-FLEETPRIV1**.
- First deploy needs keys and privilege path on the host before push; preflight must fail closed with a clear diagnostic.
- Install media and first boot stay out of this card (install ≠ deploy).

Depends on ratified D-JOS-FLEETTARGET1=A. Honor D-JOS-FLEETPRIV1 once ratified.
cards.plan:
## Outcome

Ship **jet deploy: authenticated artifact transfer and host activation** as a complete slice. Every behavior in the title, body, and ratified decisions is required.

## Work

1. Apply the card body and referenced ratified law. Stop for a ballot before new syntax, public names, dependencies, or invariant exceptions.
2. Start with docs/plans/epoch-7/native-jetos.md, docs/proposals/ecosystem-shape.md, crates/jet-env-model/src/ModuleEval/Types.rs, crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/theme_fleet_lifecycle.rs, tests/jetpack_jetos.rs. Own only these paths and direct callers or tests found by the trace.
3. Trace the public entry point through the production model to the observable result.
4. Map each named behavior to implementation and proof before writing.
5. Deploy the proven system closure through the shared remote authority and rollout model with bounded concurrency and durable receipts.
6. Partition, stale host, mixed generation, failed health check, credential loss, and controller restart stop or roll back within the declared policy.
7. Update affected docs, examples, diagnostics, goldens, and audit output.

## Proof

Run focused unit, integration, and example checks for this slice. Exercise the real production path and its main failure case. A stub, canned result, mock-only path, or skipped check does not count. Full-suite proof belongs to Epoch 9 closeout.

## Scope

Do not absorb sibling cards or create a second mechanism. Record any newly found owner choice as a Tower ballot before code.

## Lessons learned gate

Honor docs/research/deploy-rs-lessons-2026-08-06.md and any open ballots on this card before claiming done.

cards.title: jet deploy: automatic stop and rollback policy
cards.body:
[R-POSTE3-1:#322:3] Split from the former #322 umbrella. This card owns only “jet deploy: automatic stop and rollback policy.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #322. The other 4 delivery slices have separate cards.

## Lessons learned (deploy-rs mine 2026-08-06)

Track: docs/research/deploy-rs-lessons-2026-08-06.md

- deploy-rs magic rollback confirms the controller can still reach the host after activation, then rolls back if not.
- File-presence health checks are weaker than reconnect proof; do not treat the current facade as done.
- Owner ballot: **D-JOS-FLEETHEALTH1** (default health bar after switch). Amends D-JOS-FLEETROLLOUT1 health meaning.
- Intentional SSH/IP/port changes need an explicit expert opt-out visible in proof.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Ship `jet deploy` stop and rollback as the final policy over the shared rollout object. After a switch, the controller must reconnect and run declared host health before declaring success.

4. On stale identity, mixed generation, transfer or credential loss, failed reconnect, failed declared health, or controller restart, stop new waves and roll the affected host to its last known-good generation. Keep per-host and fleet summaries consistent.
5. Update diagnostics and docs to explain the stop reason, rollback result, reconnect status, and any opt-out.

After #833 integrates, exercise canary success, wave stop, reconnect failure, declared health failure, credential loss, stale host, and controller restart through the production authority. cards.title: jet cc: hermetic C/C++ toolchain front end
cards.body: Zig's adoption wedge: teams adopt the toolchain before the language. Ship jet cc / jet c++ as drop-in C/C++ compiler entry points that behave identically on every machine and cross-compile to every supported target, so CC="jet cc" works in unmodified Makefiles/CMake. Toolchain sourcing strategy (bundle vs store-provisioned vs host wrapper) is owner-gated: D-ADOPT-CC1. Gap G2 in the field audit. Proof: build unmodified upstream C projects (curl/sqlite class) natively and cross-target.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove `jet cc` / `jet c++` as hermetic, flag-compatible C/C++ front ends over the ratified Hangar-provisioned toolchain (D-ADOPT-CC1=B, D-ADOPT-CCSPELL1=A). Unmodified Make/CMake projects must build natively and cross-target, reproducibly, including offline and air-gapped. They must never use a host compiler, a PATH fallback or a test key.

## Current state
- Criterion 1 is verified. The shipped Rust driver is `crates/jetpack/src/CLI/cc.rs` (integrated e9fd8f756), and `tests/cc_cli.rs:4` checks registration.
- The Jet port exists at `Jetpack/CLI/Source/CcDriver/{DriverArguments,DriverInvocation}.jet`, with acquisition in `Jetpack/Provider/Source/Toolchain/{CcToolchainAcquisition,CcToolchainDescriptor,CcToolchainHangar}.jet`. `DriverInvocation.jet:265` uses `NixIndexClient`, which is not yet defined in Jetpack; it is owned by the #3622 NixIndex port.
- The contract is `Docs/spec/reference/cc-driver.md`. The old plan named `Source/CmdCompile.rs`, but the driver lives in the Jetpack CLI, not the compile command.

## Changes
1. Build fixtures under `tests/fixtures/cc/`: an unmodified sqlite amalgamation with its Makefile, and a small CMake C++ project with a dependency file and a response file. No source edits.
2. Add `tests/cc_cli.rs` cases:
   - `cc_builds_unmodified_make_and_cmake_projects_natively_and_cross`: `CC='jet cc' CXX='jet c++'`, native plus one declared cross target, validating artifacts with the target oracle (run natively, `file`/qemu-user for the cross target).
   - `cc_negative_cases_publish_nothing`: a PATH compiler shim, an unsupported target, a corrupt closure member, an ABI/sysroot mismatch, a path escape and a link failure. Each gives an actionable diagnostic and no output file.
   - `cc_offline_and_airgap_bundle_reuse_identical_identities`.
3. Fix defects found by these runs in the Jet CcDriver/Provider first, and mirror them into `cc.rs` only so the shipped binary proves them.
4. Reproducibility: build on two clean machines and compare artifact and descriptor digests and tool identities. Time first use, cached use, offline preload and air-gapped bundle, and document the results in `cc-driver.md`.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cc_cli` passes all cases above.
- Two-machine digest comparison is recorded (equal).
- Production acquisition goes through the owner-controlled signed index/cache and pinned key (criterion 6). A fixture key cannot satisfy it, and that step runs only once the owner provides the chain.

## Batch
`batch-jetpack-cli`: the driver's canonical home is the Jetpack CLI CcDriver and Provider toolchain.

## Dependencies
Owner-provided signed index/cache chain and a second clean machine, both for criteria 3 and 6 (environment prerequisites). #3622 is needed for the Jet driver to compile, but it does not block the shipped-binary proof.

cards.title: Enterprise source-importer wave and migration tier map
cards.body: D-MIGRATE-SRC1 ratified the jet import contract with Python as first proof. No other language has a ruling, so enterprises with Java/C#/TS/Go/C++ estates have no named transition story. Ratify a per-language tier map (source importer vs binder-only vs overlay-first) via D-ADOPT-TIER1, then card the importer wave for the ratified tiers. Every language gets an explicit verdict, including an honest no-source-import verdict where conversion would produce unmaintainable output. Gap G4 in the field audit.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close the enterprise source-importer wave under D-ADOPT-TIER1=A and D-MIGRATE-SRC1=A. Every tier-one importer named by the published tier map needs proven behaviour, and the map must match the tested subsets exactly.

## Current state
- Importers are implemented in the host `jet import` path. `Source/CmdImport.rs:97` covers py|pascal|ada|java|csharp|ts|js|go, with aliases at `:177-198` and `translate_enterprise_file` at `:315-317`.
- `Docs/spec/reference/migration-tier-map.md:19-29` gives per-language verdicts:
  - Source importers: Python, Java, C#, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go.
  - Binder-only: Ada, Pascal, VBA/COM, C.
  - Deliberate no-import: C++.
- Tests in `tests/source_import.rs`:
  - Python has a real oracle differential: `python_source_import_matches_python_oracle_fixed_corpus` :128.
  - `enterprise_importers_match_scalar_behavior_fixtures_and_keep_source_unchanged` :414 compares Java/C#/TS/JS/Go against fixed expected outputs (:514), not a foreign-toolchain oracle.
  - Failure, partial and hostile cases: :116, :326, :386, :523, :593, :617.
- Criterion 4 is verified.
- The old plan named `crates/jetpack/src/MigrationImport.rs`. That is the package-manifest importer (nix/cargo/npm/pypi/swiftpm, ported by #3659), not this source importer. Blocker #1156 is done.

## Changes
1. `tests/source_import.rs`: add `enterprise_importers_match_foreign_oracle_where_toolchain_present`. For each of Java (javac/java), C# (dotnet), TypeScript (tsc+node), JavaScript (node) and Go (go), run the original source and the imported Jet on the same inputs and compare outputs. A missing toolchain prints an explicit `unavailable:<lang>` line and never counts as a pass.
2. Fix any importer divergence in `Source/CmdImport.rs` that the oracle exposes. Keep JT0101 TODOs, spans, provenance, idempotence and JT0199 conflict behaviour.
3. `migration-tier-map.md`: reconcile each row's supported subset and known loss against the tested constructs, and change only what the evidence shows. The "child ledger" is recorded as per-language evidence rows on this card: one focused test set per importer. No separate child cards are needed, because every importer already runs through the one `jet import` path.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test source_import` passes all tests.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test source_import -- enterprise_importers_match_foreign_oracle_where_toolchain_present` passes, with each available language's differential equal and unavailable toolchains listed.

## Batch
`batch-host-cli`: `jet import` is a host CLI command.

## Dependencies
None open (#1156 done).

cards.title: jetos takeover: reversible in-place adoption from a running Linux host
cards.plan:
## Why

Bedrock Linux's main adoption path installs onto the user's running system (its hijack script). No spare machine, no repartition. Its documented flaw: the conversion is one way — the installer makes the user type "Not reversible!". jetos already owns generations, activation proof, and rollback, so it can offer the same on-ramp reversibly: capture the current install as generation 0, switch only after proof passes, and let `jet os rollback` restore the original system exactly.

Evidence: video mine 2026-08-04 (youtu.be/ENejkGhMTww, Bedrock segment) + bedrocklinux.org FAQ/installation docs. Claim ledger at /tmp/ENejkGhMTww.claims.json (topic: hijack-in-place-install).

## Scope (blocked on D-JOS-TAKEOVER1)

- In: takeover surface per the ratified option; generation-0 capture contract; refusal diagnostics for unsupported layouts; proof gate reuse; rollback-to-host proof.
- Out: fleet rollout; non-Linux hosts; the NixOS config importer (#415 owns migration semantics).

Do not start before the ballot is ratified and the native terminal baseline boots (epoch spine).

## Owned paths and ordered work

- `docs/proposals/jetos/native-jetos.md`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/generations_activation.rs`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/activation_provenance.rs`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/kernel_bootstrap.rs`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/initrd_overlay.rs`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/vm_proof.rs`
- `tests/jetpack_jetos.rs`

1. After #410's native terminal baseline is available (D-JOS-TAKEOVER1=A is already ratified), trace the existing switch, activation-proof, generation, and rollback paths; do not create a second proof gate.
2. Define the supported disk/layout contract from the ratified option. Capture the managed root, boot entry, closure identity, generation-0 provenance, and mutable-data policy; refuse layouts that cannot retain two bootable roots before any mutation.
3. Implement `jet os takeover` through the existing generation and activation models. Switch only after the same activation proof as `jet os switch` succeeds; preserve byte identity for managed and declared immutable paths.
4. Add VM proofs for supported capture/switch/rollback and unsupported-layout refusal with a registered diagnostic and pre-mutation snapshot. Keep fleet, non-Linux, and NixOS importer scope out.
5. Move the `/tmp/ENejkGhMTww.claims.json` evidence pointer to a committed `docs/research/` path before completion; retain the source URLs and claim boundaries.

## Proof

Use the existing activation-proof and VM proof mechanisms. The supported VM must capture generation 0, switch, and restore it byte-identically under the declared mutable-data policy; the unsupported VM must refuse before mutation. A targeted check must fail if the shared activation-proof path is bypassed.

cards.plan:
## Authority and dependency gate

D-JOS-PROVENANCE1=A is ratified: extend `jet info` rather than create a new public command. The old “blocked on D-JOS-PROVENANCE1” wording is stale. Implementation remains gated by #969, which owns the configuration-side provenance contender. Keep trust/signature provenance with #950/#958 and do not absorb those cards.

## Owned paths

- `docs/proposals/jetos/native-jetos.md`, `docs/proposals/jetos/jetos-studio.md`
- `Source/main.rs` and `Source/CmdInspect.rs` (existing `info`/inspection dispatch)
- `crates/jetpack/src/CLI/update_search_info.rs` (package-info seam)
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/activation_provenance.rs` and `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/studio_projection.rs`
- `tests/jetpack_jetos.rs` (native/imported/PID/unowned proof)

## Ordered implementation

1. Wait for #969 and consume its typed option/provenance boundary; apply ratified D-JOS-PROVENANCE1=A without reopening a ballot or adding a second resolver.
2. Trace one resolver from artifact to package to universe (native hangar or imported Nix closure) to generation to declaring option. Accept file, command, and `--pid` targets, preserve exact identity, and return an honest unowned result for user/runtime-created artifacts.
3. Route the existing `jet info` dispatch and the existing inspection/package seams through that resolver. Studio must consume the same result via `studio_projection.rs`; keep JetOS source canonical and make human and structured output derive from one fact model.
4. Cut over all direct callers found by the trace, remove obsolete parallel provenance lookup, and preserve the out-of-scope #950/#958 trust/signature ownership.
5. Add focused tests for native and imported-closure package paths, command/file/PID targets, unowned artifacts, and the Studio projection. Move the research claims from the temporary ledger to the committed claims file before close.

## Acceptance and proof

After #969 and implementation, use the real `jet info`/inspection and Studio production paths. Receipts must show one identical resolver answer for native, imported, PID, and unowned cases, with package/universe/generation/declaring-option identity and the ratified public surface. Targeted tests must fail if either command or Studio bypasses the resolver; no `/tmp`-only claim ledger or canned projection counts. This preparation does not claim runtime proof.

## Dependencies and non-goals

#969 is the board dependency. #950/#958 remain separate trust/signature provenance owners. Do not invent a new command, duplicate config provenance, or infer ownership when the resolver cannot establish it.

### Canonical ownership handoff — #3398

Use #323/#470 for option facts and #1424 for provenance. Keep activation, live-switch, CAS, UI and foreign-evaluation authority separate; preserve #410’s full no-nix native pipeline.

cards.title: JetOS install trust: safety without App Store gatekeeping
cards.body:
Implement jetos install trust under ratified D-JOS-INSTALLTRUST1=A (capability-first freedom): deny-by-default app capabilities, honest identity signals, generation rollback, no App Store-style notarization or category bans for owner-built software.

Desktop jetos now; same law for any future device class unless amended. Mobile implementation stays deferred (D-VERDICT-480-1).

Downstream: #975 Studio Apps, #335 Flatpak, #994 hangar sign/verify (identity only), #1424 provenance, e12 sandbox honesty.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Implement and prove the ratified capability-first install-trust law for desktop JetOS. Owner-built local software remains runnable without Jet review; foreign software starts sandboxed with explicit capability grants; trust and provenance remain honest signals; generations provide recovery.

## Ordered work
1. Treat D-JOS-INSTALLTRUST1=A as immutable law. Do not add a central notary, category ban, silent signature gate, or mobile implementation; D-VERDICT-480-1 keeps mobile deferred.
2. Align the current JetOS docs, Studio projection, Flatpak reconciliation, generation activation, Hangar identity, and provenance projection. Keep one capability policy and one generation transaction.
3. Prove the beginner paths: install from Studio and run an owner-built local package without central review. Prove the expert path: explicit family or enterprise tightening.
4. Prove hostile cases: unsigned local run succeeds with a capability prompt, unsigned remote catalog warns but is not blocked, escalation requires an explicit grant, bad install rolls back atomically, and provenance names source and publisher or absence.
5. Keep Hangar signing and package trust as identity or supply-chain evidence only. Update docs, diagnostics, and receipts without changing the already verified criteria.

## Exit proof
Criteria 3-5 remain open until the real Studio, local install, generation, and provenance paths produce focused evidence. No new owner ballot is needed; all public trust choices are ratified.

cards.title: wasm32-wasip2 as a full supported server target (D-WASISRV1=A)
cards.body:
The WASM-on-backend argument treats server-side wasm as the deployment unit; its comments dispute that containers already won. E3302 refuses the triple today and the CryptoEntropy prelude carries wasi shims. 

STATE CORRECTION 2026-08-19: D-WASISRV1 is RATIFIED =A. This is an implementation card for the ratified outcome; no ballot wait remains.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Finish D-WASISRV1=A: `jet build Examples/features/net/http_server_wasip2.jet --target=wasm32-wasip2` produces a component that wasmtime runs, and the server binds, listens and answers a request.

## Current state
- Met: target support (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Target/TargetMachine.jet:467,508-512`), the stdlib surface and teaching diagnostics (`tests/ui/wasip2_unsupported_*_e3304/e3305.jet`), the CI lane and E3302 retirement. Criterion 9 is also met: D-WASISRV1=A is recorded at `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7296-7300`.
- Gap (card log 2026-09-15): the generated Rust passes `JetOutcome<T, JetAbsent>` values for the optional TLS/deadline parameters of `jet_http_server_bind(addr, mux, tls: Option<..>, deadline: Option<..>)` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HTTPServer.rs:1916-1929`). MIR `Option` emits as `JetOutcome<_, JetAbsent>` (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Types.jet:69`), while `jet_rust_emit_core_operation` (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Operations.jet:1508-1560`) forwards arguments unprojected. The route row allows arity 2..4 (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1799`), so omitted trailing optionals also need an explicit `None`.
- The example exists at `Examples/features/net/http_server_wasip2.jet:1-12`. No test builds it or serves it under wasmtime.

## Changes
1. `Emit/Operations.jet` (`jet_rust_emit_call_arguments` path for Core routes): project every `Option`-typed argument into the host `Option` carrier (`.ok()`), and emit `None` for omitted trailing optional parameters up to `max_arity`. Apply this to every Core route with optional parameters, not only this one.
2. Keep HTTPServer.rs and the wasi-sockets adapter as the host leaf. No signature change.
3. Add `tests/wasip2_http_server.rs::wasip2_http_server_serves_under_wasmtime`. It builds the example for wasm32-wasip2, runs `wasmtime run -S inherit-network`, requests `/` and asserts `hello from wasip2` plus the `true` address line. When wasmtime is absent the test fails loudly (a named missing tool), never passes silently.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test wasip2_http_server -- wasip2_http_server_serves_under_wasmtime` passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/http_server Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes natively, so the native bind with omitted optionals is unchanged.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: the fix is in the self-hosted Rust emitter (JetCodegen Emit).

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: jet dev live-reload latency loses to Vite, Bun, and nodemon
cards.body: Fresh gauntlet live_reload axis (2026-09-02, `gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --axis live_reload`, 6/6 samples per runner) measured median edit-to-result latency: jet dev cold/warm 288.96/297.22 ms; Vite 21.69/0.92 ms; Bun 42.75/43.43 ms; nodemon 82.81/64.78 ms; entr+cc 470.25/472.13 ms. Jet wins only against entr+cc. Under the competitive performance gate every non-Rust peer requires Jet/peer < 1.00, so this axis is a loss on three cells and blocks #2272 criterion 3 and the #2268 campaign.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make `jet dev` edit-to-result latency strictly beat Vite, Bun and nodemon (Jet/peer < 1.00) on the gauntlet `live_reload` axis, cold and warm. Reload semantics must not change (I9): output after a reload is byte-identical to a fresh `jet run` of the edited source on every engine.

## Current state
- Measurements:
  - 2026-09-02: jet dev cold/warm 288.96/297.22 ms, Vite 21.69/0.92, Bun 42.75/43.43, nodemon 82.81/64.78, entr+cc 470.25/472.13.
  - 2026-09-03: Jet 215 ms both.
  - Jet wins only against entr+cc, so this axis blocks #2272 criterion 3 and the #2268 campaign.
- Criterion 2 (semantics unchanged) is met. The watch-loop fix 532775b7e ("fix(dev): wait for web file changes") is in HEAD.
- The retained host pieces exist: `Source/CmdDevTools.rs` (`run_dev_inner`), `crates/jet-jit/src/Watcher.rs`, and `crates/jet-jit/src/lib.rs:361-364` (`RESIDENT_MODULE`, `RESIDENT_RUNTIME`, reuse counter).
- Warm front-end reuse exists only in the archived `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/HotSwap.rs` and the `crates/jet-driver` incremental check. `Compiler/JetDriver` and `Compiler/JetSema` have no resident-bundle or incremental reuse. The only D-HOTSWAP1 mention in Compiler/ is `DiagnosticRows.jet:13021`.
- Harness: `Tools/gauntlet/harness/live-reload.mjs`, `run.mjs` and `status.mjs` (stale `gauntlet/` and `scripts/agent` paths are fixed here).

## Changes
1. **Attribute first.** Run `jet dev` on the axis program with `JET_TRACE_TIERS_PATH` and the dev trace. Split the latency into watch debounce, front end (lex/parse/sema), lowering, JIT re-lower, swap/restart, and first output. Record the split on this card.
2. **Host (retained, shipped path).**
   - `Watcher.rs`: no fixed wait beyond the coalescing window (target < 5 ms), using a content digest shared with #2504 slice 1.
   - `lib.rs`: re-lower only the changed functions into `RESIDENT_MODULE`.
   - The restart path must not rebuild the heap from scratch.
3. **Front-end reuse, Jet compiler first.** `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet` keeps the resident checked bundle and re-checks only the changed module. `Compiler/JetSema` computes the D-HOTSWAP1 type-surface comparison that chooses swap or restart.
   - Mirror it in the shipped Rust driver, the existing `HotSwap.rs` and incremental path, until #218 makes the Jet driver the shipped front end. Delete those Rust files then, not before, because the measurement uses the shipped binary.
4. Non-goals: no change to the swap-versus-restart law (#2504 owns it), no harness change, and no edits to the live_reload axis programs.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev --test dev_latency --test dev_default_parity --test dev_tier_parity --test dev_interp_parity`: green.
- Measurement: `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --axis live_reload` then `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/status.mjs --merge Tools/gauntlet/results`. All three live_reload cells (Vite, Bun, nodemon) show Jet warm and cold medians with Jet/peer < 1.00 and verdict `win`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-host-cli`: the latency is won or lost in the `jet dev` host (watcher, resident JIT, dev command), and the proof is a CLI measurement run.

## Dependencies
None blocking. #2504 is related (the shared content digest and the hot-swap default).

cards.title: Define multi-window lifetime on the existing native UI host
cards.body:
Wails v3 separates application services from window creation and provides window lookup and close operations. Jet already owns native widget strategy, typed UI trees, host services, and backend instances. JetGtkBackend owns a window, while present blocks its event loop. The inspected public surface lacks one portable multi-window lifetime contract. This is not permission to replace native widgets with WebView or to create another app graph.

Source and reproduction evidence belongs to the 2026-09-09 playlist audit #2989. This card is not a completion claim.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement ratified D-UI-WINDOW-LIFE1=A: one application that owns typed windows over the existing UI tree. A settings window can close while the main window keeps working, window identity is stable, and closing the last window returns control and releases subscriptions.

## Current state
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/UiGtk.rs:1323-1325` `JetGtkBackend` wraps a single `GtkState` whose `window` field (`:874`) is the only window; `present(title)` (`:1553`) blocks that one loop.
- JIT host slots: `crates/jet-jit/src/Ui.rs:127-157`. Self-hosted handle routing: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet:409-410`.
- `Core/ui/ui.jet` and `Core/ui/host.jet` have no UiApplication/UiWindow (grep: no matches). Mobile stays with frozen #480; native widget strategy is unchanged (no WebView).

## Changes
1. `Core/ui/ui.jet`: add `UiApplication` and `UiWindow` handles with a stable window id; `app()`, `app.open_window(title, root: UiNode) -> UiWindow UiHostError!`, idempotent `window.close()`, `app.run()` (blocks until the last window closes and then returns), and `app.windows()`. A method on a closed window returns a typed `UiHostError` variant (for example StaleWindow) through the canonical report path. Shared state uses the existing signals/reactive model; no second app graph.
2. Self-hosted compiler: JetFoundation registry rows/signatures/exports for the new members, and `HandleMethods.jet` routing for the UiApplication/UiWindow handle methods.
3. Prelude `UiGtk.rs`: one GtkApplication owning a map from window id to per-window state; the close-request signal drops that window's click bindings and subscriptions; the last close quits the loop. Headless mode keeps window records so open/close/stale behavior is deterministic. `Prelude/Ui.rs` and the JIT `Ui.rs` gain matching host slots.
4. `Examples/features/ui/multi_window.jet` plus golden: two windows share a counter signal, settings closes, main still updates, a double close is a no-op, a stale-handle call prints the typed error, and `run` returns with zero live subscriptions.
5. `Docs/research/`: record the Wails v3 comparison (create/reload/error/close/package/recovery) without size or performance claims (criterion 5).

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=ui/multi_window Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes (headless, AOT and `jet run`).
- Criterion 4 (manual): a Linux GTK run with `JET_UI_GTK_TRACE=1` shows two windows created, one closed, and loop exit on the last close; macOS and Windows are recorded as missing-backend prerequisites, not as passes.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: a Core/ui surface plus GTK leaf and registry rows, proven by a ui golden.

## Dependencies
None. Criterion 1 is satisfied by the D-UI-WINDOW-LIFE1=A ratification.

Implement owned windows over the existing UI tree, the GTK host and the self-hosted handle routing. Separate native windows necessarily consume native resources. D-UI-WINDOW-LIFE1 is a complete short ballot. Existing native proof remains #3004 regardless of the vote.

criteria.text: Two windows share state without duplicating domain policy; closing one preserves the other, and closing the last returns control and releases subscriptions.
Explicit close is idempotent and stale handles fail through the canonical typed report path.
Real Linux, macOS, and Windows evidence names supported behavior and missing prerequisites; a headless run cannot substitute for visible native proof.
The Wails comparison covers create, reload, error, close, package, and recovery without unsupported size or performance claims.

`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=ui/multi_window Tools/Agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and default `jet run`: two windows share state, per-window close, idempotent close, typed stale-handle error, and `run` returns after the last close.

[#3004] On a real Linux display, ui_native_linux.jet opens the GTK window, a click updates the counter, and closing the window exits the process cleanly on every level. The loop quits through a close-request handler. Headless or null output is not counted as proof.

[#3006] A supported host shows a real tray icon whose activation and menu actions route to app state. A headless or unsupported host reports unavailability and keeps the window action path. Removing the tray releases callbacks and handles. No second event graph.

[#3007] A real print dialog submits exactly the confirmed document and settings. Cancel, headless, spool failure and no printer return typed outcomes and never fake success. File export still works without a printer. The ui/print_request golden matches on every level.

[#3403] Omitted and explicit root constraints follow the ratified allocation and resize policy across TUI (pty 120x40 to 100x30), DOM (container resize) and GTK (real display). Null viewport and hit-testing agree. No second default and no new unit.

cards.title: Generated code from Jet source: `jet emit --asm` and an exact, read-only `jet inspect code` (D-CODE-INSPECT1=A, D-CODE-INSPECT2=A)
cards.body:
Destination: `jet emit --asm <file.jet> [--symbol S]` prints pre-link assembly mapped to Jet source without running the program (D-CODE-INSPECT2=A). `jet inspect code` gives an exact, source-linked, read-only view of asm, disassembly, IR and the bridge from existing artifacts (D-CODE-INSPECT1=A). An explicit `jet run --observe --capture-code` captures code from a live run. The application never starts during emission or inspection.

The plan's Rust homes are retired; the work lands in Compiler/ on the JetIR path.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Deliver the ratified code inspector and source emission.
- D-CODE-INSPECT1=A: `jet inspect code` gives an exact, source-linked view of pre-link asm, disasm, mir, backend-ir, and bridge from existing artifacts.
- D-CODE-INSPECT2=A: `jet emit --asm <file.jet> [--symbol S]` compiles current source when no matching compiler output exists and prints pre-link assembly mapped to Jet source.
- The explicit `run --observe --capture-code` producer is included.
- The application never starts during emission or inspection, and removed option B is not implemented.

**Current state**
- Nothing exists yet. There is no `--asm`, `--artifact`, `--capture-code`, or `inspect code` in Source/, crates/jet-cli/src, or Compiler/.
- `Source/main.rs:4801-4823` accepts only `emit --rust`. Anything else gets E2102 with "today only `--rust` is supported".
- `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:2029` has the `--rust` FlagSpec.
- `inspect compiler <lex|parse|check|source-map>` exists (`CLI.rs:692`) and is the source-map precedent.
- Assembly comes from rustc emission (host). The Jet span-to-symbol map comes from `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/*`.

**Changes (slices, each landable)**
1. Record and renderer (host). In Source/, add one `CodeRecord` carrying:
   - schema, stage (`asm` pre-link, `final-linked-artifact`, `captured-code-generation`, `mir`, `backend-ir`, `bridge`), and status (`available`, `missing`, `stale`, `expired`, `unsupported`, `redacted`, `unavailable`, `exhausted-budget`);
   - identity fields: source hash, symbol, target, CPU features, ABI, profile, toolchain, artifact hash, build/run id, and generation;
   - ranges.
   Text and JSON render from this one record. Exit codes: 0 when all rows are available, 1 for an unavailable row, 2 for an invalid or ambiguous request, 101 for an internal failure.
2. `jet emit --asm`:
   - Add the FlagSpec row and parse it in the `emit` route.
   - Reuse `run_emit_rust`'s build path to request rustc `--emit=asm` for the entry, map symbols through the JetCodegen Emit symbol table, and cache by the stage-relevant input closure only, excluding linker-only inputs.
   - Never run the entry.
   - `--view` with `emit` is exit 2.
3. `jet inspect code`: a new `NestedCommandSpec` in `INSPECT_ACTIONS` with `--symbol`, `--view`, `--artifact <sha256>`, `--build <id>`, `--live <pid>`, `--run <id> --generation <n>`. The scopes are mutually exclusive. It reads artifacts only.
4. `run --observe --capture-code`: bounded capture into D-RECORD1 code-artifact records, with tombstones. Capture failure never changes program output or exit status.

cards.title: Fast correct Jetpack shell entry across cache states
cards.body: Owner's latest shell instruction reinterprets idea b0cz1fux. Make `jetpack env`, `jetpack use`, and the existing `jet env export` activation path as fast as possible by removing real redundant critical-path work while keeping a fully ready environment before shell/activation handoff. Reuse verified receipts, sealed objects, locks, leases, and existing trust/acquisition policy. Cover cold, warm, partial-cache, invalidated, offline, interactive, noninteractive, hook, and concurrent entry without promising a universal two-second cold start. Do not require or default to PATH stubs, deferred fetches, background closure completion, or a new lazy flag. Keep command semantics, reproducibility, diagnostics, and the visible #2217 banner unchanged. This is a sidequest source plan; no owner product choice remains.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make `jetpack env`, `jetpack use` and `jet env export` activation as fast as possible on the Jet Jetpack while the environment stays fully ready before handoff. This is also the #3590 Phase 3 cell: warm env, Jet/Rust ratio of 1.05 or lower.

## Current state
- Rust reference: crates/jetpack/src/CLI/run_enter_dev.rs:1663 (`jetpack env [<name>] [-- cmd]`), with JETPACK_TIMING and warm selection at :1826-2016.
- Commit 1c8ae58a4 (run_enter_dev.rs, trust_env_build.rs) fixed the multiset count of duplicate warm refs.
- #2330 (done) holds the recorded warm bound.
- Jet homes do not exist yet. Jetpack/Environment/Source has only Shell/BrandedShell.jet and EnvironmentError.jet (#3644). Jetpack/Store/Source has no Reuse/ directory (#3632). The CLI has no run/enter slice (#3655).
- The Rust scenario tests are in tests/jetpack_env_use_offline.rs:51,173,415.

## Changes
These land in the Jet homes after #3644, #3655 and #3632. They change no command, trust rule, readiness contract or #2217 banner.
1. Baseline the shipped Rust Jetpack first. Use JETPACK_TIMING=1 on the disk-backed fixture at 1, 28 and 64 packages. Cover cold, exact warm, partial, invalidated, offline and concurrent entry. Time preparation, PTY-ready (a sentinel after shell startup) and first tool completion separately.
2. In the Jetpack/CLI run/enter path, compose once. Use one verified composite receipt to skip locked-Nix replay and catalog planning, without bypassing trust, definition, target, loader or secret checks. Batch Store Reuse lookups under the existing lock and lease rules. Add no parallel cache and no speculative fast path.
3. Store/Source/Reuse reuses only members whose definition and producer identities are independently valid, and realizes the actual holes. Recheck journal, seal and object, including a seal changed with the same stat. Carry the duplicate-warm-ref fix as a parity claim.
4. The Environment/Source/Activation hook emits replacement shell code only after the new environment is ready. A failed hook or a source race leaves the previous activation intact, and stdout carries only shell code.
5. No lazy or stub default, no background completion and no new telemetry schema.

## Proof
- The added criterion's Jet check with --tests passes.
- Rust parity guard: `jet test Compiler --profile cases jetpack_env_use_offline/ -- --exact fully_materialized_env_and_use_enter_without_network_or_prompt` passes.
- Measurement: same-run medians and spread for Jet and Rust entry at 1, 28 and 64 packages. Warm entry must be at a ratio of 1.05 or lower, and the #2330 bound must hold.

## Batch
batch-jetpack-cli: the entry path is proven through the CLI area unit, which includes Environment and Store.

## Dependencies
#3644 (shell and hooks), #3655 (CLI run/enter), #3632 (Store verified reuse).

Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Entry/duplicate_warm_refs` and a committed before-and-after entry receipt.

A partial cache reuses only independently valid members and realizes its holes, and source, lock or channel, target, selection, profile, loader, authority, journal, seal and output changes invalidate the affected reuse, same-stat tampering included. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Entry/partial_store_hole_realization` and `--filter entry/same_stat_seal_tamper_invalidation`.

An offline, complete environment enters without network; a missing requirement fails before the child starts, under the existing errors and confirmation policy; and no host-store fallback, untrusted object or stale lease is accepted.
PTY readiness and first meaningful tool completion are measured separately from preparation and process spawn, and output, exit status, PATH, variables and tool behavior match the baseline.
Hook replacement is atomic from the parent shell's view: a failure or source race leaves the previous working activation intact and emits no partial replacement script.
Concurrent entrants keep bounded locking, revalidation after waiting, atomic publication and valid child leases, with no duplicate acquisition or partial receipt.

cards.title: User-authored Jet compute kernels
cards.body: Connect user-authored #Kernel(.parallel) Jet functions to real device execution through the existing core.compute family. The owner requires safe typed authoring, explicit GPU work and clear unavailable-capability errors, with CPU fallback only when requested. The launch spelling remains gated by D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1. Existing Tensor .Auto, raw-provider contracts and built-in operations retain their law. The launch ballot settles the ordinary elementwise call. This card also owns the indexed/resource contract and its exact public amendment before implementation; it cannot close on elementwise execution alone.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Connect user-authored `#Kernel(.parallel)` Jet functions to real device execution through the one Core operation ratified by D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1=A (`compute.launch`). This needs safe typed authoring, explicit GPU work, and clear typed errors when a capability is missing. CPU runs only when the user explicitly asks for it. Indexed/resource authoring is part of closure, but it waits on the open D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1 ballot.

## Current state
- AST carriers exist: `Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST/Items.jet:614-632` (`KernelMode`, `KernelProof`, `KernelMarker`). `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet:1928` and `MIR/MIR.jet:2112` carry `kernel_proof`. Codegen lowers a proof to `MirKernelFacts` at `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:1124-1132,1434`.
- The Jet checker never produces a proof: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet:801` sets `kernel_proof: None`, and no JetSema or JetParser code builds a `KernelProof`. The six obligations exist only in the archived `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerKernel.rs`. Only the ownership crossing (`Sema/Ownership/Crossings.jet:10,55`) knows about kernels.
- `Core/compute/compute.jet` has the Tensor, device and stream model (`device_cpu`/`device_auto`/`device_vulkan` at `:80-85`, `from_list` at `:114`, `on_device` at `:152`). It has no `launch`. The witness `Examples/features/tooling/compute_kernel.jet:12` only calls a kernel as a plain function.
- D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1=A is ratified: one `compute.launch`. Omitting the device or passing `device_auto()` selects a compatible real GPU; `device_cpu()` selects the reference. The call allocates a fresh output, borrows inputs read-only, and fails with a typed error before submission. D-GPU-F32-STORAGE1=A is ratified; D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1 is open (recommendation A). #1139 and #1140 are done.

## Changes
1. **JetParser/JetSema.** Attach `#Kernel(.parallel)` as a `KernelMarker`. Port the six obligations from `CheckerKernel.rs` into a new `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Kernels.jet`: bounds, alias-free, captures, races, uniform barriers/control flow, and output coverage. The checker fills `KernelProof`, and unsupported bodies get registered diagnostics.
2. **JetSema `compute.launch`.** Resolve the callee to a proved kernel declaration. Take a typed tuple of inputs, infer the extent from their exact common F32 shape, and check shape, precision, layout, alias, empty-domain and overflow before dispatch. Keep grid, output, stream and device controls on the same operation.
3. **Registry and Core.** Add one `core.compute.launch` row in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet` and its Jet body in `Core/compute/compute.jet`. Reuse `from_list` and Tensor/View ownership; add no `from_list_f32` and no second tensor owner.
4. **JetCodegen.** Carry `MirKernelFacts` and the authored body to one device-program representation. Backend rejection is an internal compiler error, never user validation.
5. **Retained host.** The Prelude compute/GPU adapters handle native Vulkan and browser WebGPU allocation, upload, submit, sync and readback, plus receipts naming the real provider, program and profile. The Rust mirror of steps 1-4 is limited to what the shipped binary needs to prove this.
6. **Indexed/resource amendment.** After D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1 is ratified, add the bounded indexed example on the same operation.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_launch cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: `[5, 7, 9]` on the explicit CPU reference.
- `JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=tooling/compute_launch cargo test --test dev_corpus cranelift_three_way_differential_battery`: tiers agree.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/compute_launch_unproved_kernel.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` and the same for `compute_launch_shape_mismatch.jet`.
- `cargo test --test compute_parity`: unchanged.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.
- Real-GPU receipts from `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/tooling/compute_launch.jet` on a Vulkan host and from the web WebGPU path.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-back`: most of the change is kernel lowering through JetCodegen to the device program. Sema and Core land in the same patch.

## Dependencies
The indexed/resource slice needs D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1 ratified. It is an owner gate on closure, not on starting the elementwise path. #1139 and #1140 are done, so they are stale blockers.

Omitted device and Auto both select a compatible real GPU; explicit CPU selects the reference. Ordinary Tensor operations retain their law.

Simple typed tuple inputs infer extent/output. Expert controls use the same operation. cards.title: Typed Jet graphics shader stages and draw pipelines
cards.body: Add typed Jet vertex/fragment authoring to the existing core.game renderer/backend boundary. D-GPU-SHADER-SURFACE1 chooses whether stage identity uses the existing Kernel marker, a Shader spelling, or typed function conversion. All options share one device-program/proof mechanism and the same pipeline/resource contract. Foreign shader strings, a new core.graphics family and a second renderer are out of scope.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Add typed Jet vertex and fragment authoring to the existing `core.game` renderer/backend boundary, using the ratified D-GPU-SHADER-SURFACE1=B spelling. `#Kernel(.parallel)` stays for compute; graphics uses `#Shader(.vertex)` and `#Shader(.fragment)`. Both marks feed one device-program type and one proof engine. Out of scope: foreign shader strings, a new `core.graphics` family and a second renderer.

## Current state
- There is no shader stage anywhere. `Core/game/game.jet` and `raylib.jet` hold the game surface.
- Kernel proof facts exist (`Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST/Items.jet:614-631`), but the self-hosted sema leaves them unset (`CheckProgram.jet:801`).
- Both prerequisites are open: the typed device program from #3026 (user-authored compute kernels, ready) and the backend lifecycle from #824 (core.game backend interfaces, ready).

## Changes
1. Front end: in JetParser/JetAst, add `#Shader(.vertex|.fragment)` as a marker kind sharing `KernelProof`. Update the syntax tables (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs` for the shipped front end), the syntax-decisions.md log and `jet devtools grammars`.
2. JetSema: check the full stage interface before pipeline creation. The checks cover typed inputs and varyings, the required clip position (`game.VertexOut<V>`), `Texture2D` and `Sampler` resources, deterministic default locations and bindings, explicit layout overrides, target formats, and device compatibility. Host effects, unsupported derivatives, non-uniform barriers, races and captures fail with registered, source-located diagnostics. The same kernel proof engine from #3026/#3218 is used.
3. JetCodegen: lower the checked stages to the one device-program representation, and generate backend shader source internally for Vulkan and WebGPU (never user-supplied).
   - Draw returns the existing `ComputeStream`, and `compute.stream_sync` is the completion boundary.
   - Live handles are rechecked at submission, and queued resources are retained until completion.
4. `Core/game`: add pipeline and draw declarations only, on the #824 lifecycle. Preserve #480 mobile packaging and the existing primitive APIs. Fallback is an explicit application branch.

## Proof
- `Examples/features/game/textured_triangle.jet` covers real mesh, texture, sampler and target, then pipeline, draw and readback. `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=game/textured_triangle.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, and the CPU reference is labeled as reference, not GPU output. `jet run --interpret` matches.
- A native Vulkan run and a browser WebGPU run are recorded with image invariants.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/shader_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` covers wrong varyings, duplicate bindings, target mismatch, a destroyed resource and a missing feature.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test grammar` and `--test syntax_reconciliation` pass.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`. The stage and resource checks and the shared proof engine are the core of the change.

## Dependencies
#3026 (typed device program, authored-kernel launch) and #824 (core.game backend lifecycle).

Voxel optimisation (40JzyaOYJeY 02:00-09:20): a 28-byte vertex shrinks to one 32-bit word (6+6+6 position bits, 3-bit normal index, 7-bit texture id; later 5-bit positions plus run lengths) unpacked in the shader by hand masks that must mirror the CPU packer; instancing a 4-vertex base quad with one instance record cuts memory 6x; one shared buffer, an indirect command buffer and a storage buffer indexed by draw id replace per-chunk draws (author-reported FPS, single machine). cards.title: Sandboxed plugins: denied imports, limits, failures and release are proven at the Component boundary, and native libraries stay explicitly trusted
cards.body:
Destination: the existing Component plugin path is the boundary for untrusted extensions, and its trust and resource controls are proven case by case: denied imports fail before the operation, limits report real failures, a failed guest leaves the host running, blocking import work is bounded, release happens exactly once, and failures are typed (D-PLUGIN-FAILURE1=A). Native in-process libraries stay explicitly trusted and are never covered by a sandbox receipt.

Why: an environment, memory-safe source and a native library are not the same as a resource- and fault-isolated extension; the controls deserve exact proof, not another sandbox.

Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f04, with #3072, #3073, #3109-#3111, #3114, #3115, #3253 and #3670 absorbed. The plan's Rust homes (crates/jet-pkg-model, tests/authority.rs) are retired; the cases live in tests/cases/authority.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove, and repair where needed, the existing Component plugin trust and resource boundary (finding: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f04). The cases are: denied imports fail before the operation, limits report real failure, a failed guest leaves host work and the handle usable, and blocking import work is bounded. Native in-process libraries stay explicitly trusted.

## Current state
- `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/Plugin.rs` sets fuel and epoch config (`:239-243`), sets fuel per call (`:1192`, `:1364`), enforces the 16 MiB wire budget (`:1279-1284`, `:1422-1452`), and checks denied imports before adapter work (`:893-899`, `:936-955`).
- There is a real gap in the network import. `to_socket_addrs` (`:743`) is unbounded DNS resolution after the authority check. Only the connect is bounded (`connect_timeout`, `:748`, `PLUGIN_TIMEOUT_MS`). FS host imports have no I/O deadline.
- Runtime tests in `tests/authority.rs` cover the argument-frame limit (`:136`, `:1145`), non-terminating component (`:581`), memory growth (`:609`), table growth (`:638`) and symlink escape (`:1208`). The harness is `assert_plugin_failure_on_all_hosted_tiers` (`:494`). No test yet covers denied-import-without-side-effect, result wire limit, or same-handle recovery.
- Canonical workload: `Examples/features/packages/sandbox_mathkit/`.

## Changes
1. `Plugin.rs` network import: resolve DNS on a bounded worker under the same `PLUGIN_TIMEOUT_MS` deadline as connect. A timeout classifies as `BudgetExhausted`.
2. FS imports: bound the read and write size, and the blocking time where the platform allows. Where a blocking FS call cannot be interrupted, return an explicit unsupported/`BudgetExhausted` reason (criterion 4) instead of an unbounded wait. Re-entry stays refused (`:1116`).
3. `tests/authority.rs`, new tests reusing the all-tier harness:
   - `plugin_denied_import_performs_no_side_effect`: a denied FS.Write import leaves no file.
   - `plugin_result_wire_over_budget_fails_without_fake_success`.
   - `plugin_failed_call_leaves_host_and_handle_usable`: a trapping export, then a good export on the same handle, then host work continues.
   - A `Plugin.rs` unit test drives the deadline-bounded resolver with a blocking resolver closure and asserts `BudgetExhausted` within deadline plus slack.
4. Record source and binary identity in the evidence. Claim nothing about native Library panic containment.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test authority -- plugin_` passes all plugin tests, new and existing, on AOT, default run and `--interpret`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-pkg-model --lib -- plugin_dns_resolution_is_deadline_bounded` passes.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: Prelude plugin host and tier parity.

## Dependencies
None.

5. The result records source/binary identity and does not generalize a sandbox receipt to native Library panic containment.

criteria.text: A denied host import in a sandboxed component fails before the external operation starts.

Fuel, memory, wire and call-time limits report the real failure to the consumer, never a fabricated success. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Authority/plugin_limit_`, one case per limit.
A failed guest call leaves unrelated host work running and the plugin handle usable.

Blocking import work (DNS resolution, file I/O) and re-entry are bounded by the call deadline or refused as unsupported with an exact reason; on 2026-09-12 DNS resolution ran unbounded after the authority check and file imports had no deadline.
Each plugin receipt records the source and binary identity and never extends a sandbox receipt to native in-process library panic containment; native libraries stay explicitly trusted.

Public `close(plugin)` (close takes `&&`) releases exactly once: use after close is refused by the ownership check, and a stale host handle fails before any store access. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Packages/SandboxMathkit` (load, call, close, reload, close after failure).

No borrowed host view outlives its call, recursive host-to-guest-to-host calls work or are refused with a type, and a managed callback's stop, unsubscribe and cancel are proven, with native and Component evidence kept separate.

Retention is measured at 1k and 100k iterations for prepare, call, failure and release, separating allocator, managed and external roots. Proof: a committed measurement receipt, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Authority/plugin_retention_flat` holds the 100k run flat.
Plugin artifacts name runtime, toolchain, target, ABI and system assets, a wrong ABI, version or digest is refused, and C-safe ownership is observable on both sides.
The native and Component adapters show the same exports, values, errors and denials through no-execution preparation, first and repeated calls, and release (D-EMBED1=E, D-EMBED2=C).
The typed plugin ABI covers version, ownership, error and unload contracts, proven with real host and guest fixtures; any ABI addition goes to a ballot first.
Plugin and build-plugin budgets, failure kinds, file-system scoping, authority mapping, connect scope and load admission are Jet source, and the plugin authority cases pass on O0, O1 and O2.

criteria.text: D-PLUGIN-FAILURE1=A is built in one cutover: a failed sandbox plugin call returns a typed PluginError with one case per cause, across the compiler, Core, tools, every in-repo caller, examples with goldens, errors with UI snapshots and the docs. Type identity and dispatch across a loaded library: a value whose type a loaded .jetlib declares keeps one TypeId in the host and the library, so type tables, trait-value dispatch and reflection give the same answer on each side, and a type the host never saw reaches else, not a wrong arm (D-LIB-DYNTRUST1; raised by the D-PRIM-ANY1 ballot's plugin job, claim L13). cards.title: Measure flat enum layout, niches and collection locality
cards.body:
Measure flat enum layout, niches and collection locality.

Tag/payload overhead, niche opportunities and object-backed peer layouts depend on representation, optimizer and workload. The video and source inventory do not measure them.

Create a flat-layout/locality comparison card for unit, mixed-payload and optional/error-like sums in arrays and maps. Compare the best valid C/C++/Rust/Zig/Swift/Java/C# representation for the same job, pinning versions and optimization settings.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f16-flat-layout-locality. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Measure flat enum layout, niche use and collection locality for three shapes: unit, mixed-payload and optional/error-like sums, each held in `[T]` and `[K: T]`. Compare with the best valid C, C++, Rust, Zig, Swift, Java and C# representation of the same job. Report size, alignment and working set separately from dispatch time, and label unavailable peers instead of claiming a universal zero-cost result.

## Current state
- The self-hosted layout engine computes the enum layout facts.
  - `MirTypeDef.enum_layout: LayoutFacts?` and `c_layout_tag`: `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/MIR/MIR.jet:1201-1204`.
  - Reflection reads them at `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet:665-667`.
  - `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Types.jet:197-208` emits the tag and payload types.
- `jet inspect expand --facts layout <file>` already prints layout facts for the shipped chain.
- #218 (log 2026-09-28): the Jet compiler does not yet build executables, so its layouts cannot be timed.
- The finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f16-flat-layout-locality`; the card cites the stale `docs/` path. The performance-admission-before-new-option chain applies.

## Changes
1. Add `Tools/gauntlet/entries/enum-layout-locality/` with Jet, C, C++, Rust, Zig, Swift, Java and C# sources. Each builds 1M elements of each shape into an array and a map with the same invalid-state constraints, then iterates with black-boxed dispatch and prints a checksum. Pin each compiler version and its optimization flags in entry.json.
2. Record per shape: size/alignment (from `jet inspect expand --facts layout` and peer `sizeof`/`MemoryLayout`/JOL), allocations and object counts, peak working set, and dispatch/iteration medians. Warm up the JVM and .NET peers and note escape analysis.
3. Record the generated layout and code of the self-hosted Jet pipeline once it runs. Any niche/layout improvement goes to a separate `Compiler/JetFoundation` Layout / `Emit/Types.jet` card and requires the paired two-program performance cell.

## Proof
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry enum-layout-locality --runs 11` produces identical checksums across peers. It writes the size/alignment, allocation, working-set and median columns to `Tools/gauntlet/results/`.
- The card log lists pinned versions and flags, the jet binary and input hashes, and every unavailable peer by name.

## Batch
`batch-measure`: evidence only.

## Dependencies
#218. Self-hosted executables are needed for the Jet cells. The peer programs and harness can be written now.
