cards.title: Foundations: value and ref memory model, soundness fixes, and compiler-owned stack layers
cards.body:
One home for the 2026-09-27 foundations review, so these critical items do not scatter across the board. Evidence and design live in Docs/proposals/memory-model-foundations-2026-09-27.md (findings F1-F10 with repro programs, proposals, and the stack-replacement analysis). The owner asked for every owner decision to be balloted here. Self-hosting is done and every ballot here is ratified (16 of 16), so implementation proceeds.

Soundness defects found (not owner choices, still critical): F1 generic code bypasses the task sendability check (check passes, jet run runs, AOT ICE 101); F2 the JIT tier has no second checker and documents a stale stack-slot hazard in crates/jet-jit/src/Concurrency.rs. Conflicts with ratified text: F3 recursive Shared types rejected by E0221; F4 #Policy(gc) stores copy, contrary to D-OPTGC1=A; F5 storing a Shared handle consumes it; F6 ~ on Cell aliases; F9 misplaced #Unsafe site diagnostic after an earlier error.
cards.plan:
## Goal
This is the single home for the 2026-09-27 foundations review (Docs/proposals/memory-model-foundations-2026-09-27.md). It fixes soundness defect F1 now, puts the F2 differential oracle into the #217 soundness campaign, and turns each ratified memory ballot into its own build card. F3-F6 and F9 are resolved against ratified law.

## Current state
- Ballots: 15 of 16 are ratified A (D-MEMREF1, -LIFE1, -EXCL1, -TASK1, D-RAWPTR2, D-AUTOPIN1, D-DENY-COST1, D-REACT-REF1, D-INVALIDATE1, D-OPTIMISTIC1, D-RESUME1, D-WIRESKEW1, D-HOTSTATE1, D-STACKBOUND1, D-SECRETEDGE1). D-SYSSCHED1 (parallel game systems from their data access) is open with recommendation A. That is the only reason the phase is `deciding`. The plan below assumes A.
- F1 (proposal :64-90): `fn spawn_with<T>(value: ^T) { task ^value {…} }` called with a `Cell` passes `jet check`, prints 1 under `jet run`, and fails AOT with ICE 101 (rustc: `Rc<JetCellInner>` is not Sync). The same defect exists in the Jet compiler. Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership/Crossings.jet:176 returns None (sendable) for any generic parameter, and thread confinement is a hand-kept name list (:102-106 core.mem and Browser types, :232-237 Cell and SharedGuard). The Rust twin is `sendability_problem_inner` in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs.
- F2: crates/jet-jit/src/Concurrency.rs `jet_jit_sender_send` documents a stale stack-slot hazard, and nothing checks JIT runs a second time.
- The owner's condition on waiting for self-hosting (#218) no longer applies, because Compiler/ is the primary target.

## Changes
1. F1, Jet compiler: at each generic instantiation that reaches a crossing (task spawn, channel send, shared storage), check sendability of the concrete type argument instead of skipping the parameter at Crossings.jet:176. Use the instantiation bindings from Calls/Inference, and report E1102 at the call site with the generic path in the note. Replace the name lists with a `ThreadConfined` fact on the type's registration (opt-out, like an auto trait), set in the declaring Core module.
2. F1, Rust mirror: the shipped binary executes this unsoundness, so mirror the check in CheckerOwnership.rs.
3. F2: add the differential oracle to #217. For generated programs, when sema accepts and rustc rejects, the harness records a sema bug card.
4. Open one build card per ratified ballot, each linking this card and the proposal. Link F3 (recursive Shared, E0221), F4 (#Policy(gc) copies, contrary to D-OPTGC1=A), F5 (storing Shared consumes it), F6 (`~` on Cell aliases) and F9 (misplaced #Unsafe site after an earlier error) to those cards, or fix them against current law.
5. After D-SYSSCHED1 is ratified, open its build card.

## Proof
- Add tests/ui/generic_task_sendability.jet (the F1 program) with E1102: `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/generic_task_sendability cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`.
- `~/.cache/jet-luna/safe-jet.sh run tests/ui/generic_task_sendability.jet` reports E1102 and no longer prints 1.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- The F2 oracle's first run is recorded on #217.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: F1 is a sendability rule in JetSema plus its mirror. The remaining work is card creation.

## Dependencies
D-SYSSCHED1 (open owner ballot) blocks criterion 1 only; F1, F2 and the build cards can proceed now.

log.text: c7 split (Main, 2026-11-13, at G10Safe-1's finding): the only placement fact sema records is the web partition, FnBody.web_bucket JS|Wasm, which #Target locks and E-WEB-TARGET-BROWSER/E-WEB-CROSS-PARTITION refuse. No browser-or-server placement or update-notification choice exists. c7 now covers the kinds that exist, with web_bucket as the placement kind. The two missing kinds moved to a new criterion that depends on D-WEB-RUNTIME-API1 (#6445). No scope was dropped.

c9 decision (Main, within D-MEM-FACTS1, no new spelling): when the build is an executable, the compiler seals each function-value call and each trait call to the functions the program takes as values and to the impls of a matching type. A library build stays open and reports E0921 as today. A #Test shows that adding an impl changes the set and the bound, and `jet inspect memory` names the sealed set.

c9 part d (!Mem.Alloc(above: N) bounds the total heap of any call path) already holds on dev fd72bf4d8d. Main ran it on seed-b14: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter arena_bounded` gives PASS 4, REFUSED 0 (arena_bounded_transitive_overflow, unsized_allocation, unsized_transitive_allocation and open_multiplicity). cards.title: jet check is too slow for a large single unit: 9.2k Jetpack lines take 329 s (NixEval 5.5k = 195 s alone)
cards.body: Measured by the Jetpack port (#3590) with target/debug/jet (built 2026-09-26), each under a cgroup cap. jet check src/jetpack.jet on the assembled Jetpack unit: NixEval area only (5,539 lines) 195 s, 680 MB peak; Foundation+PackageModel only (3,663 lines) 79 s; both together (9.2k lines, master 31b1e0bf3) 329 s, 800 MB peak, 0 errors, 199 lints. Receipts: ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-bootstrap/lead-c3e0b738ad/check.receipt and 5efbbecdee/check.receipt. The port targets ~120k lines in one unit (mirroring Compiler/Bootstrap); at this rate a single check would take far longer than an hour, which blocks the per-slice proof loop and later the build-time performance cell. Note the binary is a debug build; release timings are unmeasured. Needs: profile where check time goes on this unit (the unit is available by re-running Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh) and a root fix.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make `jet check` on a large single unit roughly linear in source size, and stop it running out of memory. Today it blocks three things: the Jetpack per-slice proof loop (#3590), stage zero of self-hosting (#218 criterion 12), and later the build-time performance cell.

## Current state
Measured with the debug `target/debug/jet` (built 2026-09-26), under a cgroup cap. Release timings are unmeasured.

| Unit | Lines | Wall | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jetpack NixEval only | 5,539 | 195 s | 680 MB |
| Foundation + PackageModel | 3,663 | 79 s | — |
| Both (master 31b1e0bf3) | 9.2k | 329 s | 800 MB (0 errors, 199 lints) |
| Compiler front slice (70 files, 2.93 MB) | — | 39 min single-core, OOM-killed | 8 GB, no verdict |
| EnvModel unit (185 sources) | — | exceeds the 6 GB cap in ~8 s | — |

- The lexer slice (94 KB) takes 25 s. Receipts: `~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-bootstrap/lead-c3e0b738ad/check.receipt` and `5efbbecdee/check.receipt`.
- Root-cause lead (`~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/jet-packages-study.md` §3): cost follows content, not size. The NixEval prefix timings are:
  - Text (225 lines): 0.5 s.
  - Adding API types and NixJson (825 lines): 37.4 s.
  - Adding the Lexer and Parser (1,588 lines): 69.6 s.
  - Adding `Jetpack/NixEval/Source/Evaluator/Values.jet` (260 lines of recursive `NixEvalValue`/`NixEvalNative`/`NixEvalThunk` enums and impls): 180.2 s, i.e. +110.6 s.
  - Adding 1,796 lines of evaluator methods: only +15.9 s.
- Splitting into files or packages does not help: a 5-line app over NixEval takes 207.6 s on the first run and 209.7 s on an unchanged rerun.
- Receipts are never reused under systemd-run. The environment identity at `Source/ReceiptStore.rs:3566-3573` ignores the Nix temp variables but not `INVOCATION_ID`.
- The bootstrap assembles one compiler unit on purpose (`Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list`), and `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet` carries the whole module graph into checking.

## Changes
1. Profile first. Run `perf record` (or the sema phase timers) with a release `jet check` on `Jetpack/NixEval` and on a synthetic recursive-enum fixture. Name the pass whose cost grows with the recursive type graph times its use sites; likely suspects are drop/copy/derive/structural-recursion or type-identity walks without memoization.
2. Fix it at the root in the shipped checker (`crates/jet-sema`, the bootstrap checker used for stage zero). Memoize per type identity, or compute the fixpoint once per SCC. Then make the same fix in `Compiler/JetSema` so the self-hosted checker never inherits the algorithm.
3. Add `INVOCATION_ID` to the receipt environment-ignore list (`ReceiptStore.rs:3571`) as an immediate fix. #2517 later deletes ReceiptStore and replaces it with per-module memoization.
4. Add the scaling regression `recursive_enum_check_scales_linearly` in `tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs`. Checking N and 4N use sites of a three-way recursive enum must take at most 5x the time, with a fixed memory ceiling.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases cli_compiler_speed/recursive_enum_check_scales_linearly`: passes.
- Measurement with a release build: `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area NixEval` finishes in under 20 s (today 195 s on a debug build) and stays under 1 GB peak. The receipt is recorded.
- `bash ~/.cache/jet-luna/slice-scaling.sh target/release/jet after lexer parser front`: the front slice finishes under the 6 GB cap with a verdict.
- An unchanged rerun under systemd-run replays the receipt.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: the root cause is in the checker. The Rust bootstrap checker and Compiler/JetSema get the same fix in one build.

## Dependencies
None. This card unblocks #3590 and #218 stage zero.

Scale data point (JetCompilerRunPath): Rust jet check of the Jet compiler front slice (70 files, 2.93 MB) ran 39 min single-core and was OOM-killed at 8 GB without a verdict; a 94 KB lexer slice takes 25 s. This blocks stage zero of self-hosting (#218 criterion 12), not only Jetpack.

Triage 2026-09-28 (Luna 5.6 high legwork, Pip reviewed): RETARGET_JET. This is a compiler-loop performance defect, not Jetpack implementation policy: the Jet bootstrap intentionally assembles one compiler unit (sources.list:1-4) and its Driver carries the complete module graph into checking (Identity.jet:109-147). The measured regression is reported and still actionable, but release performance is unverified (bugs-4.json:64-80). Evidence: The card reports 329 seconds for a 9.2k-line assembled check and 195 seconds for the 5.5k-line NixEval slice at ~/.cache/jet-luna/triage/bugs-4.json:64-80; release timing is unverified. ; Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list:1-4 defines one unqualified Compiler unit and says the list is the only assembly order. ; Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:1-2 identifies the Jet front-end as parse, check, lower, and assemble. Jet target: Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet, Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet, Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet, Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list.

Also: check results are never reused between runs under systemd-run because the receipt environment identity includes INVOCATION_ID (ReceiptStore.rs:3568-3573 already ignores Nix temp variables for the same reason), and receipts are not stored for ../ path deps.

Root-cause lead from JetPackagesStudy (report ~/.cache/jet-luna/jetpack-port/jet-packages-study.md section 3): check cost follows content, not size. NixEval prefix timings: Text 225 lines 0.5 s; +API types/NixJson 825 lines 37.4 s; +Lexer/Parser 1,588 lines 69.6 s; +Values.jet (260 lines: recursive NixEvalValue/NixEvalNative/NixEvalThunk enums and impls) 1,848 lines 180.2 s (+110.6 s); +1,796 lines of evaluator methods 196.1 s (+15.9 s). Splitting into files or packages does not help: a dependency is re-checked in full every time and nothing is reused between runs (5-line app over NixEval: 207.6 s first run, 209.7 s unchanged rerun). Suspect a whole-unit pass that scales with the recursive enum/type graph times use sites. A PhaseTiming profile is the next step.

criteria.text: A profile names the super-linear pass in the Jet checker (Compiler/JetSema) on the recursive NixEval enums, and a check of a fixture with 4N use sites takes at most 5x the N-site time with bounded memory.
A release `JET=jet jet Jetpack/Bootstrap/Check.jet --area NixEval` finishes in under 20 s and 1 GB peak (from 195 s and 680 MB on a debug build). Proof: the committed receipt of that run.

The 30-variant named-payload `#Comparable` enum program (Examples/features/types/enum_many_variants) builds on every level within the compile-speed budget, with generated code size linear in variant count and derived equality, compare, Debug and cleanup bodies no longer exploding. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CompileBudget/enum_many_variants` with 12- and 30-variant rows.

Each kept generated-code compile-cost lever (derive trimming, explicit types, backend-specific trimming) has a before-and-after backend time on the corpus, a keep-or-drop decision and a passing level differential. Proof: a committed receipt per lever.

A `jet check` of a small program returns within 1 s of its result being known, even on a contended disk, and its receipt stays durable: the receipt write costs one barrier per check (objects first, then one fsync of the directory and index), or the write is handed off with the next command waiting on it. cards.title: One lane type: width-parameterized and scalable SIMD vectors
cards.body:
Owner request: start from what hardware can do and turn it into high-level constructs, keeping both a bottom-up and a top-down path. Mojo defines every scalar and vector as one library type `SIMD[dtype, width]` (`Int = Scalar[DType.int]`, Modular commit 99e3a880 `std/simd.mojo:115-240,443-468`).

Today Jet has a closed family of named lanes (D-SIMD3=B: F32x4, F32x8, F64x2, F64x4, I32x4, I32x8, I64x2, I64x4, U8x16, U8x32; Examples/features/lowlevel/simd_wide.jet). A width cannot be a parameter, so generic code over "the widest native width" cannot be written, and vector-length-agnostic hardware (Arm SVE, RISC-V V) has no spelling. Const generics (D-CONSTGEN1=A, #3505) make a parameterized lane type possible.

Ballot D-LANES1 decides the lane surface.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-LANES1. Implementation waits on #3505 const generics; then define the lane type in Core over compiler intrinsics, migrate the named family in one cutover, and add SVE/RVV lowering where the target supports it.

cards.title: Use newer CPU instructions in one binary: multiversioned functions and typed intrinsics
cards.body:
Owner request: leverage what hardware can do now (bottom-up), give experts direct access to machine instructions, and stay forward-facing for new hardware.

Today D-FFI-ASM-CPU1=B builds for the target baseline and needs explicit CPU flags for newer instructions; a shipped binary cannot use AVX-512 when present and fall back otherwise. Experts can reach instructions only through audited `#FFI(asm)`; the compiler-only `__core_intrinsic` namespace (D-CORE-CALL1) is closed to users. Prior art: Rust `#[target_feature]` + `is_x86_feature_detected!` + `core::arch`; GCC `target_clones`; Google Highway dynamic dispatch; Mojo `CompilationTarget` queries and `comptime if`; Odin `@(enable_target_feature=...)` and `base:intrinsics` (265 procedures).

Ballot D-CPU-DISPATCH1 decides how code opts into newer instructions.
cards.plan: D-CPU-DISPATCH1=A is ratified. Add the chosen target-feature function form, a per-process feature probe in the Prelude, safe typed intrinsics in Core for the chosen ISAs, and dispatch on every tier.

cards.title: C header import depth: read real headers with a full C front end
cards.body:
Owner request: use Zig's cross-compatibility as a wedge: import C headers directly, act as a drop-in C/C++ compiler, build foreign projects in Jetpack, and export C ABI libraries.

Today `jet cc`/`jet c++` exist and use the pinned Jetpack toolchain (`crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1333-1349`); `#Export(c)` exists (Examples/features/packages/library_loadable); foreign builds are on #1347; cross toolchains on #758/#1058/#1060. The weak link is header import: `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/CBind.rs:1-12` is a focused std-only parser that maps scalars, strings, pointers, slices, and layout records, and skips the rest. Zig's `@cImport`/`translate-c` reads real headers through a full C front end, including macros, unions, bitfields, function pointers, and variadics; Zig probe Z6 cross-compiled C to Windows and AArch64-musl from one host.

Ballot D-CIMPORT1 decides the header engine.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-CIMPORT1. Then extend the binder, run it against a corpus (zlib, sqlite3, libcurl, SDL3) for every supported target, and report unmapped declarations with registered diagnostics.

log.text: Frozen by owner direction (2026-11-01): cross-platform work (non-Linux OS, AArch64 or other targets) is frozen for now. CardClose-1's ready sweep listed this card's remaining blocker as cross-platform.

mine-for-jet V (2026-10-16): V has no C header parser; every C symbol is redeclared by hand (fn C.name / struct C.Name, need not match the header; vlang/v doc/docs.md:10408-10498). Live probe: a wrong fn C.strlen declaration passes V's checker and fails only as raw TinyCC output on generated src.c ('too many arguments to function'). Jet's checked binder + overlay is the beat vector; real-header import here is what makes it true. Related probe card #5037; C source translation ballot D-CSRC-IMPORT1 on #5034. Note: criterion 1 still reads open although D-CIMPORT1 is ratified A.
Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: absorbed #3401, #3729, #3873, #3875, #3876, #3985, #4011, #2420, #3502, #3559, #4185; their criteria are carried here as [#n] rows.

cards.title: Portable sandboxed app format: what Jet ships to run anywhere (Docker/Nix/WebAssembly replacement)
cards.body:
Owner direction (2026-10-01): Jet should be portable and better than WebAssembly, and replace Docker and Nix. EYG ships a checked program and lets the host supply effects.

Jet today: native binaries (trusted code), OCI images projected from environments (D-ENV-IMAGE1=A), wasm32-wasip2 (D-WASISRV1=A, #1914), sandbox components (--target=sandbox), Wasmtime plugins (D-PLUGIN1=A, D-DEP-WASM1=A), Hangar store and build-step sandbox (D-JPK-SANDBOX2=D). Output.Bundle is the closed catch-all kind for distributables (D-ECO-OUTPUT-KINDS1=A). The portable-platform proposal (JPM/1, JPH/1) is unratified with no prior card.

Ballot D-PORTABLE1 decides the portable app form of Bundle.
cards.plan: Owner decides D-PORTABLE1. Then specify the .jetapp layout, host selection, confinement reporting (confined/verified/TRUSTED), and grant storage; paired cell against an OCI container and plain wasmtime on startup, size, and throughput.

log.text: Frozen by owner direction (2026-11-01): cross-platform work (non-Linux OS, AArch64 or other targets) is frozen for now. CardClose-1's ready sweep listed this card's remaining blocker as cross-platform.

Folded #4762 "Extensible hardware requirements with trusted scan, target facts and pre-entry admission" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of parent #4195 (Portable sandboxed app format: what Jet ships to); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: D-HOST-CAPS1=A Proposes Core Hardware, HardwareKind, HardwareRequirement, HardwareProbe and ScanContext as specified in the explainer. Hardware contains main memory, storage and typed device entries. Target gains hardware; every Output gains target, requires and uses. Package-defined kinds use pure type-owned satisfies/coarse methods; scan probes are separately trust-granted. $build.hardware shares D-CONF's typed fact plane and merge law; $build.cpu remains the CPU entry. Host observations, grants and kind/probe package identities determine launch admission/cache identity, never a producer's asserted facts. Free amounts are checked before each GPU job. Implementation areas: Core hardware typ

Independent witness (Blow, cKyrT8OVbDo 00:00-09:40): untrusted plugins should share structured data without serialize/parse, get write permission only to chosen memory without a separate process, and a plugin that crashes inside shared lock-free code after incrementing a counter leaves the host unrecoverable; containers exist because the OS stopped reliably rerunning programs; wanted: one portable, sandboxed, backend-neutral instruction format. Today D-PLUGIN1=A / D-DEP-WASM1=A accept copied boundary values as a loss; the portable proposal (Docs/proposals/jetpack/portable-platform-specification.md H-ISP-002, L-11a, CV-15; unratified) already specifies sealed zero-copy and trap termination, which this corroborates. Research lead for C2 measurement (not verified): in-process hardware write isolation (x86 protection keys, Arm permission overlays) for verified guests, with known limits (few keys, no speculative-read protection). Local IPC culture serializes to JSON even on one machine (CK-07): include a large structured value crossing the boundary in the C2 measurement against wasm and OCI.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

cards.body:

**Scope:** Reserved Package source-file law; Jet root noun for the complete checked graph; runtime: package field for runtime PATH deps; First-class cargo build field: Recipe.cargo(lock:); How much must plain jet check prove?; Build/config: one plane of typed facts; Facts in text, actions in the function; One meaning for the word profile; What jet split does with inline Package facts; formatter: passthrough for non-.jet files; jet split/fold law (Fold-only); Public typed package model for Jet tools; Build file versions without lost locks or rewritten evidence; Package policy and exception source surface

**Decision IDs:** D-ECO-FILEROOT1, D-ECO-ROOTNAME2, D-ECO11, D-ECO2, D-ECO1, D-CHECKSCOPE1, D-CONF-PLANE1, D-CONF-SPLIT1, D-CONF-WORD1, D-ECO-SPLITPOLICY1, D-ECO12, D-ECO13, D-PACKAGE-MODEL1, D-BUILDCOMPAT1, D-JPK-POLICYSURFACE1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-BUILDCOMPAT1:** Use version in a clear scope, preserve originals, and automatically read supported older data without changing its meaning. Version-1 locks from older Jet releases remain readable.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Jet has registered unsupported lock-version diagnostics and refuses unknown required marker meanings (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:11310-11312). Complete original-evidence preservation, linked readable views and automatic older-version translation in Rust and Jet were not established.
- **D-CHECKSCOPE1:** Resolve the owning project and every declared runnable output; Validate imports, reachable Core closure, canonical TIR, and every applicable execution-tier lowering; Preserve isolated single-file checks.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust project check explicitly sets inspect-only execute:false/no authority grant (crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:3477-3481); tests/project_check.rs is the consumer suite. Jet CLI exposes file check (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Host.jet:47-61; Front.jet:502), not an established all-runnable-output/workspace check.
- **D-CONF-PLANE1:** Adopt the model; Configuration is the program's knowledge about itself: every build fact (identity, machine, profile, settings, policy) is a typed value on one registered plane, with one contribution law and one audit command; The ratified role-typed Package shape becomes the only manifest vocabulary; the legacy flat parser is deleted. build.os, which already works this way, becomes the plane's first row; Later D-CONF ballots (fact reads, settings, contribution law) land on this substrate.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust folded fact vocabulary is registered (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs:36-37). Jet has folded snapshots (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Items.jet:462-464), but loader explicitly lacks declared manifest settings (Expressions/FactReads.jet:640-643); complete typed single fact plane/cutover missing.
- **D-CONF-SPLIT1:** Manifest text is the complete index of what is configurable: every fact is declared there with its type and default. fn build performs actions — probes, steps, generated code — and may contribute a value to a declared fact; Every computed contribution is recorded in .jet/lock and named by jet explain. fn build can never mint an undeclared fact; The pushback the owner asked for is honest: a flat facts-in-text-only rule fails, because a probed toolchain or a find() member list is only knowable by computation; The law keeps those as computed contributions instead of banning them.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust pipeline records contributions/generated modules in .jet/lock (Source/CmdCompile.rs:3682-3686). Jet loader still declares no manifest settings (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/FactReads.jet:640-643), so text-declared facts plus checked computed contributions are not complete.
- **D-CONF-WORD1:** release, debug, and ci keep the word, matching --profile and its ratified sugar --release; The board identity is a machine description; before its unbuilt surface ships, it is renamed into the machine vocabulary and selected beside triples with --target; Environment profiles become presets (amends D-ENV-PROFILE1's field and flag spelling). Package/user profiles are already generation snapshots and take the generation word (amends D-JPK-PROFILE1's wording only). Each rename is an amendment named here; none changes behavior.

Jet environment command is unavailable (Front.jet:491-506); full profile/generation manifest vocabulary cutover not established.

Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-ECO2:** build takes a typed recipe. Recipe.cargo(lock:) maps buildRustPackage and cargoLock.lockFile in one line.

cards.title: IR ownership verifier and sanitizer gates (no MIR/LIR)
cards.body:
Build an independent ownership verifier over the JetIR form, plus fuzzing and sanitizer gates for the Jet compiler. The MIR and LIR verifiers are removed with Cutover A (#5073), so do not build on them. Acceptance: the verifier rejects a seeded set of ownership violations; gates run in CI. Blocked on #5073.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Today rustc acts as an accidental second safety check: some Jet checker or lowering ownership bugs surface as rustc rejections of emitted code (example: last-use conversion moving an owner while a derived View is live, reported as rustc E0502 by SolLower2 #6), and I2 classifies those as internal errors. With the Jet-native backend (D-EXEC1) nothing would catch them: they become undefined behaviour in native code. Jet's guarantee must rest on its own checks: sema ownership/borrow/effect checking (I3) plus an independent verifier, never on a host compiler. Work: (1) complete the independent MIR and LIR verifiers (#4125/#4126 scope: moved values, active borrows/views vs writes, definite initialization, drop exactly once, aliasing of mutable access, cleanup on every exit) as simple dataflow that re-checks lowered code without trusting sema; (2) keep rustc as a CI-only differential oracle during the transition: every rustc rejection of emitted code is a filed defect; (3) grammar-based program fuzzing with the verifier and runtime checks as oracles; (4) debug-build runtime sanitizing on the native backend (poisoned frees, guard pages, use-after-move traps, borrow-state tracking); (5) a gate: zero verifier findings and zero sanitizer faults over the whole example corpus and fuzz budget, sustained, before the native backend replaces rustc output by default.
cards.plan: 1. Inventory today's rustc rejections of emitted code (census, stage-1 runs) and classify each as emitter shape vs real ownership defect. 2. Finish verifier coverage for borrows/views and definite init; fixtures per defect class. 3. Fuzz harness + nightly budget. 4. Debug sanitizers in the native runtime. 5. Gate wiring in the performance/safety manifests.

cards.title: Core Path: lossless native OS paths (D-OSPATH-NATIVE1)
cards.body:
Make Core Path represent non-UTF-8 OS paths losslessly, with target-native separators, as ratified in D-OSPATH-NATIVE1. No new ballot is needed. Acceptance: a non-UTF-8 path round-trips through Path without loss on the supported targets, plus the original criteria.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Raised 2026-10-02 by the CLI port (CLI-36, Flash host, via PortLead-7). Core files.path `Path` holds `raw: String`, so a non-UTF-8 OS path (possible on Unix: parent directories, PATH entries) cannot be represented. Rust's CLI keeps PathBuf and only displays lossily; a String-keyed Jet port would alias distinct paths that share a lossy display. Interim ruling (Main): the port refuses non-UTF-8 paths at the host seam with a typed error and a test, so aliasing is impossible; no CLI-local path type. Open owner decision: should Core Path carry raw OS bytes (with text as a checked view), stay UTF-8-only with refusal as the contract, or something else? This is public Core API and needs a ballot with same-program alternatives (beginner path unchanged: Path from a string literal).

Related platform-semantics gap (TOOLS-S25 via ToolsLead-1): Core files path helpers (Core/files/files.jet is_absolute/join/dirname, Core/files/path.jet) treat backslash and drive letters as separators/absolute on every platform, while the Rust reference uses host Path semantics: on POSIX  is a relative single filename and backslash is an ordinary character. Ports that need Rust parity on receipt and protocol paths therefore diverge. The ballot for this card should decide both questions together: raw OS bytes vs UTF-8, and host-native vs platform-neutral separator law. Ports keep using Core paths (no tools-local normalizer) and mark the divergent tests with this card.

cards.title: Core List: keep only some items, in place (D-LIST-RETAIN1)
cards.body:
Add an in-place stable retain to Core List, as ratified in D-LIST-RETAIN1. Ports of Vec::retain must not allocate a new list. No new ballot is needed. Acceptance: retain keeps order, removes in place, and a golden checks no reallocation on the performance cell.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Found 2026-10-03 by the tools port (TOOLS-N10 notebook trust store, ToolsLead-1). Core and Foundation lists have push/pop/remove/reverse/update_first but no in-place stable retain (filter by predicate keeping order), truncate or swap. Ports of Rust Vec::retain must drain by ownership into a new vector (linear, one allocation) or do quadratic removes. A canonical List.retain is public Core API, so the spelling needs the usual surface approval; it would remove the allocation in every such port (notebook trust insert, store indexes, GC tables).

cards.title: Core HTTP: raw request body bytes and one form decoder (D-HTTP-BYTES-FORM1)
cards.body:
Carry raw request body bytes in Core HTTP for the devserver and binary uploads, with one form decoder, as ratified in D-HTTP-BYTES-FORM1. No new ballot is needed. Acceptance: a binary upload round-trips byte for byte, and the form decoder has one entry point.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Raised 2026-10-03 by the tools port (DEV-T1, ToolsLead-1). The devserver must use Core's HTTP request parser (one HTTP parser, I8), but Core http.parse_request (Core ~509-561) exposes the body only as UTF-8 text, while the devserver (and any upload/binary API) needs the raw request body bytes. Decide the public Core surface for byte bodies (e.g. a [U8] body field or accessor alongside the text view, with the existing framing limits). Public API: owner ballot. Related Main rulings (no ballot needed): the devserver's lenient framing in the frozen Rust (LF-only line endings, missing Host, arbitrary method/target, HTTP/1.1-only) is dropped in favour of Core's strict framing, with a Rust tandem; the devserver keeps only its policy (duplicate-header refusals and messages) as an adapter over Core's parsed request; query parameters reuse Core's lower percent codec, not Core's query policy.

log.text: Folded into #6008 as a criterion (CardTrim 2026-10-28).

Rewritten for the Jet architecture (self-hosted compiler, AST + fact tables, JetIR slot IR, no Rust) in the 2026-10-22 board burndown: Tagged ballot-needed, but D-HTTP-BYTES-FORM1 (ratified A: raw HTTP request bodies and one form decoder) answers the body-bytes question. Drop the ballot. The earlier text is kept at the end of the body.

Same defect on the response side: parse_response turns the body into a String and refuses non-UTF-8 with UnsupportedEncoding (http.jet:498), so a video/mp4 or image/png response cannot be parsed (course FknTw9bJsXM 272:24-275:20). Proposed criterion: non-UTF-8 response bodies stay bytes through the existing body API. Also exercised: the ratified D-HTTP-BYTES-FORM1 example writes "POST / HTTP/1.1\r\n...", which fails E0001 because plain strings have no \r escape; fix the example to the byte form [U8]{"...\x0D\x0A..."} (works: 27 bytes) or to the outcome of D-STR-ESCAPE1 (DistillLang's ballot). The v3 H2 re-mine (B56) confirms the response-side defect on dev 3f64b4fb6.
Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: absorbed #4431, #4360, #4338; their criteria are carried here as [#n] rows.

Second Core HTTP surface question for the same ballot (DEV-T1): Core http.jet:1114 percent_decode is private and on invalid decoded UTF-8 returns the original encoded text (:1136), while Rust devserver uses String::from_utf8_lossy (U+FFFD replacement); Core net.url.percent_decode (:274, public) is strict and does not map + to space. There is no public tolerant form-decoding codec. Options: (a) expose one public form/query decoding function with a stated malformed-escape and invalid-UTF-8 policy (lossy U+FFFD matches Rust and WHATWG application/x-www-form-urlencoded parsing), used by Core http and the devserver; (b) keep strict-only public decoding and drop lossy decoding from the devserver (behaviour change). Recommendation: (a) with WHATWG semantics, also fixing Core http's private copy to the same law (one codec).

cards.title: One lossless terminal key decoder (D-TERM-INCREMENTAL1)
cards.body:
Implement the single lossless terminal key decoder ratified in D-TERM-INCREMENTAL1 in Core terminal code. Remove the second decoder path. The Rust REPL is not an oracle. Acceptance: every key sequence in the decoder table decodes the same way from the REPL and from Core.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Raised 2026-10-03 by the runtime port (RuntimeLead-3) with ToolsLead-1 and PortLead-10. Three decoders disagree: Core/term TermKey (partial, Char(String)); native TermKey.rs:1-239 (Char(char), Enter, Delete, F(i64), Ctrl(char); reads a six-byte chunk and keeps the first char, discarding the rest); REPLTerm.rs:233-372 (incremental scalar decoding with Idle, Eof, EscapeEnter, Home, End, SS3 F1/F3, Ctrl actions).
Option A: keep framed Core semantics with ONE decoder and an explicit framing parameter. Option B: one canonical incremental decoder: Char(Char), Enter, Delete, EscapeEnter, Home, End, F(I64), Ctrl(Char), plus a typed Timeout/EOF transport; migrate all Core, CLI, tools and native callers.
Same input: 'ab' -> A Char(a) and b dropped; B a then b. ESC O P -> A Unknown; B F1. Timeout -> A Unknown; B Idle. Ctrl-D stays Ctrl(d) in both; the caller's EOF policy is explicit.
Recommendation: B (no lost input, beginner-friendly), but it changes a public product carrier and framing, so it needs owner approval. PortLead-10 then cuts over HelpState/Headless (removing HostTermKey); tools R11 stays held.

criteria.text: D-MEMREF-EXCL1=A is built: where sema proves no conflict, a write while an @ link reads stays a compile-time error (E0204/E0212 extended to links). Where two links might reach one value, a small runtime access check at the lend or loop stops the program with the source location, and a function denying !Mem.Check refuses the runtime check at compile time. D-MEMREF-LIFE1=A is built: when sema cannot prove an owner outlives a link, it chooses counted storage for that binding at compile time and never moves memory at run time. Types that can form cycles get cycle collection, and E0221 selects it instead of being an error. jet gc report lists each case with a concrete fix, jet fix applies the mechanical ones, and !Mem.Rc or !Mem.Gc forbid the cost, with Shared.Weak<T> (downgrade, upgrade) as the expert back link. A task capture copies the link, never the binding. jet inspect lists each switch with the task that caused it. Proof: cases for the auto switch, the #Local refusal (UI snapshot), #Shared and #Transact, on O0, O1 and O2, with no data race under a two-task stress row, plus a jet inspect golden naming the switch.

Today the crossing is refused with ValueNotSendable, 'no registered ownership facts for @'. Repro: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/g1facts/e3link/ (lr1-3.jet), found by the #6999 E-3 probes.

Safety (I1): a brief link (lowered to Borrow) to a callee-owned place cannot be stored into a record that outlives that place. Today assigning check.environment = @scope.environment inside a callee is accepted without a check, so a swap that is not restored leaves a dangling link in safe code. Sema must prove the place outlives the record, or refuse the store with a registered diagnostic and UI snapshot. Repro: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/g1facts/e3link/.

Safety (I1): a link to a place handed through a call cannot outlive that place. Three cases are accepted today with no check, and each leaves a dangling link in safe code: a callee storing a link parameter into another parameter's record (attach(r: ^Rec, e: @Env) { r.env = e } called as attach(r, @local)); a link pushed into a collection that outlives its place (list.push(@x) through a ^[@T] parameter or an outer list); and returning a link to a local (return @local). Sema must track which parameters each function's links flow into (per-function link facts), so that every such flow is proven or refused with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot per case. Found by the c10 work (4500-c10-link-outlives-place, which closes only plain stores).

Cost: a kept link that never crosses a task pays no atomic reference counting. After c9 (4500-c9-link-record-crosses-task), every kept link takes the atomic rc_* path on each retain and release, including single-threaded code. Each link block must pay atomic operations only once it crosses, either through a promotion bit in the link block header (BuildLinks.jet in JetIR, Links.jet in JetRuntime) or through a static proof of no crossing. A paired two-program cell shows single-threaded link retain/release at the plain-RC cost and a crossing program still correct on O0, O1 and O2.

Diagnostics: detaching a task that captured a live link reports link wording, not E1106's "captured a `view` borrow". This means a link variant of the E1106 text, or a separate registered code, with what/why/fix and a UI snapshot.

cards.title: SQL statement classes: infer and enforce Query/Mutation/Schema/Dynamic on SQL values (D-SQL-CLASS1=A)
cards.body:
D-SQL-CLASS1=A (ratified 2026-10-04, ballot card #4501). First of the SQL-safety cards: D-SQL-AUTHORITY1, D-SQL-GUARD1 and D-SQL-RAW1 build on the class carried here; D-SQL-SAFETY (schema map) is independent.

Scope (core.db, sema, both compilers, Web transport):
- Infer the travelling statement class for ordinary SQL{...} literals and enforce it at every receiving method (query/execute/etc.), with the complete record, constructor, method and error rules in the decision detail.
- Beginners keep SQL{...}; experts get checked head/from constructors and an audited Dynamic route. No schema authority or raw permission is added here.
- Class tags and bindings survive return, storage and Web decode; forged known tags, altered bindings, stale identities and intent through untrusted decode are refused.
- Keep existing fallible row extraction and runtime migration restrictions.

Acceptance: decision checkInstructions (returned/stored Query/Mutation/Schema/Dynamic, Rows/Count, DELETE...RETURNING optional cardinality, forgery attacks, CLASS-only mode engine authorizer/prepare facts, fail-closed unsupported enforcement, version1 fields across adapters, original DB/typed-text/row-policy tests).

criteria.text: D-SQL-AUTHORITY1=A is built: DB.Schema is inferred and enforced on migration and table-change routes.

cards.title: Unsafe as an inferred effect discharged at audited boundaries (D-UNSAFE-EFFECT)
cards.body:
Make Unsafe an inferred effect in Compiler/JetSema, discharged at audited #Unsafe boundaries, per ratified D-UNSAFE-EFFECT (A). Safe callers do not change. Acceptance: an unaudited unsafe call is rejected at its effect boundary, and audited boundaries pass.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

D-UNSAFE-EFFECT=A (ratified 2026-10-04). Upstream of D-RT-NATIVE-CAP1 (every core.mem.native declaration adopts this rule) and of D-SQL-RAW1.

Scope (Rust sema and Compiler/JetSema, one solver):
- Add Unsafe to the existing effect solver. Locally executed raw operations and calls to #Unsafe-marked APIs introduce Unsafe; their reviewed #Unsafe(reason) boundary discharges only that known component; other effects remain.
- Open rows: unknown callback row E stays E; when known Unsafe is added beside E locally, remove only the added component; never subtract a possibly inherited Unsafe from unknown E.
- An #Unsafe-marked function publishes its body row plus Unsafe and keeps its unsafe-call bit: entering it needs caller review; a wrapper calling it inside its own gate discharges the known entry component; an ungated call is refused.
- Audit/report: audit version, identity, dedup, recursive and unknown policy; keep unsafe_sentries, tir_unsafe_and_runtime, authority_manifest and inspect fixtures green.

Acceptance: decision checkInstructions: direct/higher-order/recursive/open-row E and E|Unsafe programs across all levels; prove unknown E never subtracted; store/return/spawn callback rows and owning/borrowed raw handles; caller permission stays distinct. Exit obligations are a separate card (D-UNSAFE-EXIT-OBLIGATIONS).

cards.title: Adaptive specialization: rebuild with a run record (D-ADAPTIVE-TIER1)
cards.body:
Implement the ratified D-ADAPTIVE-TIER1 choice (B): a profile record from real runs drives a rebuild on the one native backend, with an optional in-program re-optimize. The Cranelift JIT is retired (D-EXEC1) and is not a target. Acceptance: a record-and-rebuild loop exists and is measured in a golden.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Owner 2026-10-04: "would it be possible for jit to outperform aot? if we are trying to squeeze absolute maximum possible performance out of every possible scenario, is there any benefit of keeping a jit in some form, even an evolutionary modern hybrid form?"
Ruling for tonight: the existing Cranelift jet-jit crate is not ported (D-EXEC1 retires it; 77 packets stay deferred). Research question: where a runtime tier measurably beats AOT (profile-guided re-specialization, runtime-constant folding, CPU feature dispatch, deoptimization, dynamic code loading, REPL/notebooks) and how much of that AOT already captures (PGO, #Multiversion, comptime); whether a tiered or adaptive mode built on the same native backend and the one shared runtime (no second implementation, I9) is worth it. cards.title: Compiler scaling gate: every phase provably linear on any codebase shape (generated corpora, work counters, superlinear detection)
cards.body: Owner 2026-10-05: the compiler itself must handle hundreds of thousands of lines per second on ANY codebase, not only on Jet sources tuned for compile speed; and there must be profiling/checks that catch superlinear phases or other compile-time regressions so high performance is maintained consistently. Scope: (1) a generator family (extending Tools/perf/throughput, bench30k/bench300k) producing corpora that stress each dimension independently: many modules, many small functions, few huge functions, deep nesting, wide enums and big match/arm tables, many impls and traits, heavy generics and monomorphization, many comptime items, long string/data tables, many imports, deep call chains, error-heavy code (diagnostics); each at sizes N, 2N, 4N, 8N. (2) deterministic work counters per phase inside the compiler (both halves): items visited, scope lookups, impl/trait scans, copies of whole-program structures, allocations, so complexity is measured without timing noise. (3) a gate (CI-runnable, under the performance manifest) that fails when any phase's counter or time grows faster than k*N log N across the size ladder for any corpus, naming the phase and the dominating counter; plus absolute lines/s floors per phase. (4) a static audit kept current (StaticHotAudit) for loops over whole-program tables inside per-item work. Done when the gate runs on every landing, passes on the current compiler or names each superlinear phase on a card, and its report is part of the speed briefing.

cards.title: Repository PascalCase paths and host-independent word-key module resolution
cards.body:
Adopted D-PATH-CASE2=A. PascalCase is Jet repository house style enforced by repository tooling, not a compiler restriction on user packages. package.jet and run.jet keep exact lowercase spellings everywhere. Imports resolve by word keys and reject ambiguity, never host lookup order. D-WIRE-CASE1=A and D-WIRE-ACRONYM1=A have a distinct projection implementation child card. D-CASE-LAW3 remains OPEN: no source camelCase migration is authorized.

Current application amendment (2026-10-07, #27 clarified by #29/#31; Sol writes / Opus reviews #28):
D-PATH-CASE2=A
One word-key resolver across roots, module declarations and file aliases; reject ambiguity before package read on every host; E0603/E0606/reserved-file fixes exact; user paths unrestricted except reserved names; repository gate and scaffolds enforce PascalCase with package.jet/run.jet exceptions; module/member resolution and all migrated source manifests remain correct.
Paths: Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Loader.jet; Jetpack/Foundation/Source/Syntax.jet naming lexicon; Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Host.jet scaffolds; Tools/agent repository naming gate and source generators; Core/, Compiler/, Jetpack/, Examples/, tests/ source path cutover
Registry/spec/UI/goldens: Legacy Syntax.rs + Syntax/acronyms.rs module_source_path and Syntax/package_files.rs DEFAULT_ENTRY_FILE / jetpack_config.rs PACKAGE_FILE; Jet Syntax counterpart records D-PATH-CASE2=A, keeps package.jet/run.jet exact lowercase; Docs/spec/spec.md module/file resolution; Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md D-PATH-CASE1 amendment; Docs/proposals/casing-2026-10-05.md distinguish dated proposal from adopted scope; E0603 no-match examples; E0606 all candidates and longer-name fix; same-folder word/case twins; wrong-case reserved files with rename fixes; Fixtures for http_client/HTTPClient/HttpClient/http-client/httpClient, HTTP_APIClient/UTF8, dotted Core/dependency roots, run.jet directory entry, module declarations and member fallback; file alias from stem words; scaffold and repo gate goldens
Timing: UNDER #27 Jet-half-only implementation was permitted; latest #29 schedules NEW FEATURE delivery after port/Rust-exit feature resumption. Record docs/contracts/tests plan NOW; an independently justified MINIMAL seam required to port an existing row/layer/harness is PORT NOW and may mirror both halves with dies-at-cutover ledger. Do not let this feature block current port merely because its contract is ratified. Earlier #27 assessment: JET NOW for resolver/tools; broad repository rename lands only after current landing waves/seed consumers are coordinated. No new Rust-half loader; last Rust bootstrap need is an exception only if Main establishes it today. Do not merge stale rename train wholesale. CURRENT #29/#31: a MINIMAL seam necessary to port an existing Core row/runtime layer/test harness may also change the Rust half, registered as dies at cutover; all actual layer policy/carriers must still be ported to Jet. This exception does not permit duplicating new features. #28 Sol authors, Opus reviews. Features outside required port work resume after port/Rust exit; contract/docs/tests planning may be prepared now.
Open prerequisite/conflict: #4613 body still applies PascalCase to user packages and demands no lowercase paths; parked aggregate branch contains Package.jet renames (OrphanAudit compare2). D-CASE-LAW3 remains OPEN: do not rename value identifiers to camelCase. Gate-2/RuntimeJet/Jetpack source manifests are in flight.

log.text: Parked 2026-11-18 (DeclTypes moved to #6841 by owner order). c1 is half done in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/DeclTypes-6-1/pc/wip-4613-c1.patch (base 5f8eb469cd). Done: sema_casing_path_key and its test, key-matched module imports and name: module, the E0603/E0606/E0607 wording, dotted paths, dead index removed. Left: the collision and reserved-name refusal (it hits Jetpack/CLI/Source/Entry/Run.jet, Tools/CanvasTest/Run.jet, Tools/Perf/UnicodeLiteral/Run.jet, Tests/UI/ModulePathMatchesTwoFiles, RoutesSameWords), file-alias words, the PathCase/ cases, CLI reach, the repo_pascal_case gate (about 5.8k non-Pascal test .jet files need kept classes). c2 not started.

Folded #4755 "One Jet naming projection for every outside medium and package defaults" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #4613 (Repository PascalCase paths and host-independent word-key module resolution); 2 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: D-WIRE-CASE1=A One naming module owns word splitting, the acronym list and every projection. It replaces the five copied conversions, the private kebab helpers and Shape.rs's two default functions. ShapeFieldNames stays the only place a projected name is stored. Defaults per place. JSON, CBOR, TOML, YAML, XML and CSV keys: the name's words in the Jet value case, camelCase under D-CASE-LAW2=A. Enum cases use the same style. Acronyms follow D-WIRE-ACRONYM1. Query parameters: the package's JSON style. Flags and enum flag values: lowercase words joined by hyphens. Environment: prefix plus SCREAMING words, with __ between nesting levels. SQL: lowercase snake_case, never pluralized. HTML attribute

Destination: Host-independent word-key module resolution.
Notes: Batch PATHS of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (sonic), one build, one proof run: self-compile and goldens unchanged after the rename. Order: #4755.
Decisions so far: D-PATH-CASE1 (ratified=A) on #4613; D-ROUTE-FILES1 (ratified=A) on #4613; D-CASE-LAW1 (ratified=A) on #4613; D-PATH-CASE2 (ratified=A) on #4613; D-ROUTE-FILES2 (ratified=A) on #4613; D-WIRE-CASE1 (ratified=A) on #4613; D-WIRE-ACRONYM1 (ratified=A) on #4613; D-CASE-LAW3 (ratified=C) on #4613
Fog: none recorded.
Out of scope: cards outside this list; other batches of the consolidation plan.

Dedup 2026-10-28 (TowerDedup): merged #4912 (duplicate). Both apply D-PATH-CASE2=A (PascalCase repository paths); #4613 holds the decisions and criterion, #4912 the parked bundle refs. | #4912 "Apply D-PATH-CASE2 option A on dev (word-key imports, twin error, reserved lowercase package.jet/run.jet)" (planning, P2). Body: D-PATH-CASE2 ratified A on 2026-10-07. Prior implementation attempts live only in the 2026-10-09 consolidation bundle ($JET_STATE_ROOT/backup/, all-refs bundles): fix/runtime-wiring-pathcase-parked@abb51f87f and feat/path-case@e0b69e681 (~14k paths; they rename package.jet to Package.jet, which contradicts A). Branches are not merged wholesale into dev. Follow-up: check what dev already implements of A; port the A-consistent parts (word-key resolver, twin diagnostic, capitalized code files) on dev; keep package.jet and run.jet lowercase. Lower priority than Rust removal (owner #47/#48). Log 2026-10-09: RustExitLead finding on dev 2aa8b0349: JetDriver still matches exact relative_path/module_name strings (Compiler JetDriver Loader.jet:1592-1602, 1619ff, 1674, 1702, 1831; Identity.jet:485-497); E0606 is exact-name ambiguity, not the word-key twin error. So A is NOT implemented on dev. Reusable source: feat/path-case@e0b69e681 adds Foundation/ModulePath.jet (170 lines), a generated mapping and scoped loader changes, layered on the ~14k PascalCase rename; abb51f87f mixes that rename with runtime parse support. Both excluded from the consolidation as inseparable; extract ModulePath.jet and the loader changes from the bundle when this card is worked.

D-PATH-CASE2=A ratified; application contract updated. No implementation/build/test or closure receipt claimed. Owners: unowned (PathCase2 parked, STREAMS:117,198,302). Latest owner #29 permits only minimal port seams both halves, dies at cutover; #31 requires actual Jet ports.
Case-only identifier look-alikes (learning-compilers:VA10) need the identifier-level rule beside D-PATH-CASE1; route through D-IDENT-CHARS1.

Distill 2026-10-05, naming evidence for the open casing ballots on this card (D-CASE-LAW1, D-PATH-CASE2) and ratified D-PATH-CASE1. (1) Jon Blow reviving 2003 C (youtube DaJWWePhRsM 32:20-32:41): wrong-case #includes compile on Windows' case-insensitive file system and fail on Linux; acceptance: import resolution is host-independent and two paths differing only by case are a collision diagnostic on every host. (2) 'Naming files and directories' (youtube pjnSE99-cz0): teach naming from day one; shell metacharacters and spaces break tools; dots are reserved for extensions; case sensitivity differs by host, so assume it matters; 'when in doubt use lowercase' is refuted for Jet source paths by the owner's PascalCase choice but still applies to user data and web addresses. (3) A 7-hour beginner Python course (youtube 4M87qBgpafk 00:50-00:57, 01:20) teaches snake_case and SCREAMING constants by convention only, and two names differing only by case are distinct and confusing; E0107 already suggests the right-cased name (probe p05) but no lint flags two live names in one scope that differ only by case. Candidate criterion for the case law: a same-scope case-only collision gets an advisory.

Evidence for D-ROUTE-FILES2 (D-ROUTE-FILES1 is superseded): naming-practice video pjnSE99-cz0 01:07-01:23 and 04:22-04:58 says spaces in URLs become %20, hyphens are the common web separator, and lowercase is the server convention because case sensitivity differs by tool. Supports lowercase hyphenated web addresses derived from page-file names; it does not bear on PascalCase source paths (D-PATH-CASE1=A). Teaching commentary from one channel, not measured user data.

criteria.text: D-PATH-CASE2=A: one word-key resolver serves roots, module declarations and file aliases; ambiguity is refused before the package is read, on every host; E0603, E0606 and the reserved-file fixes are exact; user paths are unrestricted except reserved names; and the repository gate and scaffolds enforce PascalCase with the package.jet and run.jet exceptions. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter PathCase/` and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter repo_pascal_case`.

One naming module owns word splitting, the acronym list and every outside projection (JSON, environment, flag, SQL, header) under D-WIRE-CASE1=A and D-WIRE-ACRONYM1=A, including each package default, and a Jet test pins each projection. Proof: `jet test Core --filter naming/projection_` and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter single_case_converter` (fails on a second case-conversion helper in Compiler/, Core/ or Jetpack/).

The 4 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: OutputCallable/qualified_entry_follows_nested_quoted_import_graph, OutputCallable/qualified_entry_keeps_one_definition_and_effect_identity, BuildEntry/module_directory_entry_requires_run_jet_not_main_jet, BuildEntry/nested_workspace_is_the_module_import_root. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Package deps imply a prepared environment (D-DEPS-ENV1)
cards.body:
Implement D-DEPS-ENV1: listing deps in package.jet is enough for jet env --prep to build the default environment; env.jet is not required. Update the first-party battery examples that list deps without env.jet. Acceptance: each battery example compiles after jet env --prep with no env.jet.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Found 2026-10-05 by GoldenFix5 (#4599): first-party battery examples list deps in package.jet but have no env.jet, and `jet env --prep` consumes only an explicit Env plan, so they cannot compile. The spec is silent (S52, D-ECO-ENV1 defers the environment schema; D-ECO-FILEROOT1: only package.jet is reserved, env.jet is ordinary Config). Owner-authorized ballot D-DEPS-ENV1 decides it; this card carries the ballot and its implementation, preserving D-ECO-FILEROOT1 and D-NAME-ROLEMOD1. Related: #4275.

log.text: Folded into #5980 as a criterion (CardTrim 2026-10-28).

Rewritten for the Jet architecture (self-hosted compiler, AST + fact tables, JetIR slot IR, no Rust) in the 2026-10-22 board burndown: Owner gate on env.jet vs package.jet deps. D-DEPS-ENV1 is ratified, so the open question is settled. D-ECO-ENV1 is MISSING from the index; rewrite uses D-DEPS-ENV1 only. The earlier text is kept at the end of the body.

Distill 2026-10-05: nine source witnesses for this owner gate (D-DEPS-ENV1); evidence only, no new criterion.
- languages-a:N01 (maw2hptpErI 00:22–00:36): Setup knowledge in a README ("install OpenSSL 3.2 first") is unread and unverified; the fix is executable decl
- languages-a:N03 (maw2hptpErI 05:06–05:16): Uncached Dockerfile reruns can produce different results; reproducibility needs pinned inputs, not cached snap
- languages-a:N07 (maw2hptpErI 08:33–09:00): Mental model: Docker snapshots filesystem state; Nix is a lock file. Teaching via the familiar lockfile is eff
- languages-a:N08 (maw2hptpErI 09:53–10:28): Pin by content hash, not only version number, because version meaning can change; Git pins give byte identity.
- languages-a:N16 (maw2hptpErI 17:24–17:53): Newcomer runs one command (`nix develop`) instead of following README steps.
- languages-a:N34 (maw2hptpErI 36:03–37:07): Returning to an old project rebuilds exactly; deps may otherwise be unobtainable or upgraded silently.
- languages-a:N35 (maw2hptpErI 37:14–38:16): Explicit environment declaration is an up-front cost that pays back for years.
- languages-a:N36 (maw2hptpErI 38:20–38:49): Upstream cache keeps outputs indefinitely 'but that will probably change'; reproducibility depends on archive 
- languages-a:N66 (maw2hptpErI 74:20–74:26): Earliest value: a working dev shell for my project.

cards.title: Memory model: Rust-or-better safety, easier than Rust, never copy where Rust borrows or moves, Polonius-level acceptance, stored references solved
cards.body:
Owner goal (2026-10-05): Jet must be at least as memory safe as Rust, ideally more, and far easier to reason about (no fighting the borrow checker, no lifetime annotations). Once Rust leaves the toolchain Jet must beat Rust's performance, so it may never copy, retain, lock or refcount where Rust would borrow or move. Every program shape Rust and Polonius accept as safe must be expressible in Jet without hassle. Stored references (struct fields, parent links, self-reference, lending iterators) need a real answer; check whether @ links (D-MEMREF1) replace View<T> and suffice, else design what works.

Criteria:
1. Research-backed proposal Docs/proposals/memory-model-*.md (agent MemModelLead) with the Rust/Polonius shape matrix, current Jet verdicts, recommended design, beginner and expert paths; owner choices as ballots.
2. Acceptance corpus mirroring rustc NLL/Polonius cases with zero false accepts and every false reject either fixed or justified (agent MemEvidence).
3. Copy audit: every implicit copy/retain/lock/refcount where Rust would borrow or move is removed or justified; paired perf cells prove no loss versus Rust.
4. MIR Lint (#4619) re-proves the final rules independently.
Related: #4392, #4617, #4619.

Wave 3A flips SEMA_OWNERSHIP_DISJOINT_METHOD_FOOTPRINT live, fixes c21 (non-storing Map/Set string-view lookups & trim_start/trim_end), and streamlines Compiler/.

c5 ruling (Main, 2026-11-13): a public function !Mem.* denial and its bound are part of its API row, like its effect row. Removing a denial or loosening a bound is semver-breaking (major), and adding or tightening one is minor. jet inspect expand --facts memory shows the denial and its bound. The MemoryPolicies example and its ui rows already pass on o0, o1 and o2; the inspect and API/semver parts remain (G9Web-1-2).

The compiler refuses it with E0118, but evaluated_statement_accesses_are_scoped_and_mode_aware_2's oracle allows it. S9, several oracles carry rendering artifacts (lambda spans cut short, a column on the open paren). implicit_take_keeps_mark's oracle conflicts with its four passing split twins. S1 now covers 2 rows; the other 6 have their own roots, S11-S16.

Owner gate found by SelfMem2 (ui A-OWNERSHIP sub-root S1, 8 rows, E0204 missing in composite arguments): struct-literal fields check their lambdas as escaping (Constructors.jet 389/461/504), so those lambdas clone their captures and reserved & reads pass. The ui oracle expects the lambdas to borrow when the struct goes to a read parameter. That changes capture lowering, and it is unsound if the callee copies the struct out. A language-semantics choice, so it needs a ballot; the 8 rows stay failing until then. Details: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sm2/a43-subroots.md.

Docs: proposal Docs/proposals/memory-model-2026-10-05.md and evidence Docs/research/memory-safety-evidence-2026-10-05.md are in the docs tree (master 29ccc04f8 and the next commit). Correction owed in the proposal: it cites a 64-case corpus (final: 87) and counts C36 as a safe extra accept, but the corpus and #4621 classify C36 as a false accept; corpus case 52 does not test push. The evidence doc's Limits section records all three. The paired copy-cost timing (MemEvidence-copybench) failed on environment (CARGO_TARGET_DIR guard, missing bc), so no measured cost ratios exist yet; CopyCut2's perf cells are the next measurement.

CopyCut finding (perf/copy-cut, $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/CopyCut/RANKED.md): the largest remaining copy class is ~791 read-parameter sites where Rust would move because the callee keeps the value. Removing them needs callee 'keeps-parameter' (^T) inference or an explicit contract change, which conflicts with the ratified rule that sema never raises a parameter's access from body usage (spec 'Ownership and borrowing'). That is an owner choice: draft it as a ballot with the K-cards. Also not yet done: loop-source/fold-receiver borrowing (needs a read-only-body fact and a borrowed fold route on all tiers) and read-only list captures (needs K15 static closures).

Evidence landed (MemEvidence, release jet dev-05ea86f65). Corpus $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/scratch/memcorpus/RESULTS.md: 87 programs (Rust NLL accept 49 / reject 38; Polonius accept 53); Jet agrees on 59; 20 false rejects (top: writing method through a write window E0212+E0202; no mutable map lookup/Entry; no mutable iteration loop p in &ps; @ links unbuilt; no write window into option/enum payload; no swap/take/replace through &; View<str> field/methods gaps; bogus E0121 in task ^tx); 2 static false accepts (cases 36, 62 = #4621, blocked today by a lowering ICE); 6 sound extra accepts. Copy audit $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/scratch/memcorpus/AUDIT.md (estimates, paired timing job queued): ~920 heap copies where Rust would move, 604 needless ~ copies into read params in Core, 7,600 allocating string literals, closures boxed as Rc<RefCell<Option<Box<dyn FnMut>>>>, whole-list clones to iterate/fold/capture, 45,694 Int retains, 5,444 per-element bounds checks, map.get clones (no get_mut/Entry), shared lock + 2 allocations per access, task ^x clones, print/compare clone, share-on-reuse is eager deep copy. jet audit copies over-reports scalars and misses emitted-code clones. AUDIT.md was not seen by the proposal author; fold it into the K1-K15 card drafts.

cards.title: Names in every script, one stored form, look-alike names are tidy errors (D-IDENT-CHARS1)
cards.body:
Job: a learner names things in their own language, and a reviewer sees exactly the names that compile.

Today (exercised with release jet dev-05ea86f65; probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/mine/legwork/languages-b/probes/):
- Probe A: `café` typed with a one-piece é works; the same-looking `café` typed as e + U+0301 fails with E0001 'The character U+0301 doesn't mean anything here (yet)'. Probe C: Devanagari `नमस्ते` fails on U+094D. Combining marks are never allowed, so mark-based scripts cannot be used for names.
- Probe D: Latin `a` and Cyrillic `а` bind two silent, different names.
- Source reading: both lexers accept 'alphabetic or numeric' scalars only (Scan.jet:47-55; Scan.rs:772), with no normal form and no look-alike check. The self-hosted lexer uses Core's approximate classifier (#4426), so the two compilers can disagree.

Not in this card: invisible bidirectional controls in source (Trojan Source, CVE-2021-42574) are already owned without an owner gate as #3881 criterion [#4204] (merged from #4204). This card depends on that work and on #4426's pinned UCD data.

Source witnesses: CURSED (youtube BiFt4vw1-uM 13:29-24:08): an agent 'added emoji names' by editing only identifier start/continue tables; the generated JavaScript could not run and the compiler copy segfaulted (name rules are end-to-end law, not a lexer table). DreamBerd reaction (_oiBWfuf0Oo 03:52-04:31). Rule 9: Rust RFC 2457 (UAX #31 + NFC + confusable_idents warning), Python PEP 3131 (NFKC), C++ P1949 (UAX #31, no emoji).

The ballot decides the character law. After ratification: one generated XID/NFC/confusable data home shared by both lexers, formatter NFC rewrite, UTS #39 skeleton warning per package, spec.md:47-48 rewrite, syntax registry and editor grammars regenerated, UI goldens.

cards.title: Unused fields and enum cases are tidy errors: fields never read and cases never built (D-MEMBER-LIVE1=A)
cards.body:
New card hosting owner ballot D-MEMBER-LIVE1. Extends D-STRUCT-LIVE1=A (four name-level liveness verdicts, card #2052/#2132) to members; reuses its `_name` repair (D-NAME-SIGIL1) and D-LINTPOLICY1 (warnings never block). Library `pub` stays exempt exactly as in D-STRUCT-LIVE1. No new spelling, suppression marker or tool.

Job: an application grows; fields and cases from old experiments stay in types, mislead newcomers, and cost bytes and fetches.

Today (exercised 2026-10-05 with release jet dev-05ea86f65, probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/mine/legwork/languages-b/probes/F-member-liveness.*): `jet check` warns L0104 on a private `unused_helper`, but says nothing about `User.nickname` (written once, never read) or `Plan.Legacy` (matched, never built). D-STRUCT-LIVE1 covers imports, bindings, private functions and unreachable exports only (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7596-7601).

Source witness: ReScript reanalyze (Gabriel Nordeborn, yKl2fSdnw7w 52:39-60:06): whole-program detection of never-read record fields and never-constructed variant cases; teams 'switch it on, get thousands of errors' and delete old experiments; ReScript-Relay uses the same facts to drop unused GraphQL selections in CI. Rule-9 research (legwork resources 11-15): reanalyze README (case dead if never constructed, matching does not count; field dead if never read, creating does not count; needs @live for FFI); Rust dead_code ('field is never read', 'variant is never constructed'; 1.57 PR 85200 stopped derived Clone/Debug from counting as reads, which broke deny(dead_code) builds); Periphery (external indexer: synthesized Codable/Equatable code invisible, false positives need retain flags); staticcheck U1000 (field accesses use fields; anonymous structs assumed fully used).

The ballot decides whether these become compiler warnings. Implementation after ratification: member facts in the existing liveness pass (closed package/application graph), use rules from the ballot technical text, machine fix (delete or `_` rename), UI goldens, `jet explain` rows.

Noise evidence for the loss mitigation: Jon Blow (youtube DaJWWePhRsM) disables unused-variable warnings globally because macro-only uses make them noisy, and calls Go's unused-is-error annoying; Jet keeps every liveness warning advisory (D-LINTPOLICY1) and counts encode/decode, derive, reflection and FFI as uses.

Distilled 2026-10-05 by DistillLang from the six mining batches; Tower snapshot rev 74843 (jet-state digest INCONSISTENT during collection: rerun before posting).

cards.title: Constant ranges that can never run: one advisory lint and one written stride law (S19/S22)
cards.body:
Split from the NC-DIAG draft by the fresh review (2026-10-05) and extended with the v3-P2 delta.

NEW small card completing existing law. S22 (inclusive `a..b`) and D-RANGE-EXCL1=C (half-open empty when a >= b) are ratified; S19 states a dynamic nonpositive stride raises E0123. The law never states what a constant inclusive range with start above end, or a constant stride whose sign contradicts the bounds, does; observed behavior is zero iterations. This card documents that behavior (no semantic change) and adds an advisory lint under D-LINTPOLICY1=A, visible per D-LINT-VISIBILITY2=A. Joins the lint family owned by #2141/#3919. No existing card (searched 'reversed range|empty range|descending').

## Actual (dev candidate jet dev-05ea86f65, 2026-10-05; probe p17)

```jet
loop n in 10..1 -> print(n)        // prints nothing; jet check: no problems
loop n in 10..1, -1 -> print(n)    // 10 down to 1
loop n in 1..10, -1 -> print(n)    // prints nothing; jet check: no problems
```

A beginner Python course shows the presenter repeatedly writing a countdown whose start and stride disagree and wondering why nothing happens (youtube 4M87qBgpafk 03:37-03:39). Rust's Clippy treats this as a correctness lint (`reversed_empty_ranges`: "this range is empty so it will yield no values"); R's `1:length(x)`, which counts down to 0 when x is empty, is the commonly cited counterexample against automatic reversal (unfetched corroboration lead; not load-bearing).

## Expected

When both bounds and the stride of a source-loop range or slice bound are compile-time constants and the range is empty because direction and stride disagree, jet check and the editor report a registered advisory with the fix that counts the intended way (`10..1, -1`). Dynamic bounds stay silent: an empty range at run time is legitimate work. The spec states once that a constant inclusive range with start above end and positive stride is empty.

## Stride law gap (PYB-61)

S19 (syntax-decisions.md:537,542-544) specifies only a positive source stride ("Stride N visits source indexes 0, N, 2N") and makes a dynamic nonpositive stride E0123. A constant negative stride is accepted and counts down over the inclusive bounds (`10..1, -1` prints 10..1, prior probe p17) but that meaning is written nowhere. With an empty list the countdown header `xs.len() - 1..0, -1` runs zero times with no error (probe p6). The spec sentence this card adds must cover both: reversed bounds with a positive or omitted stride run zero times; a constant negative stride walks from the first bound down to the second inclusive.

Re-confirmed on release dev-05ea86f65 (sha256 bc088ced...f9b): probe p4 `loop i in 10..1` and `loop j in 0..1, -1` print nothing, `jet check` clean; probe p6 empty-list countdown prints only 'done'. Course witnesses: 4M87 3:37-3:39 (PYB-3) and 5:15-5:17 descending index loop (PYB-61).

criteria.text: `10..1` and `1..10, -1` with constant bounds in a source loop produce one registered advisory lint each with a structured fix; `0..<0`, ranges with any non-constant bound, and intentionally empty fixture ranges do not.
The lint never changes exit codes and follows D-LINT-VISIBILITY2; a UI snapshot pins the report.
Docs/Spec/syntax-decisions.md S22 states the empty-range rule for inclusive ranges in one sentence; range_step.jet shows the countdown form.

S19 states the meaning of a constant negative stride (countdown over inclusive bounds) and of reversed bounds without one, with an example in Examples/features/basics/range_step.jet whose expected output is golden-tested.

cards.title: jet learn: a zero-experience beginner arc from first value to first small project
cards.body:
NEW content card attaching to ratified D-LEARN1 (#1918: 'one offline path from install to competence'; exercise suite runs in CI) and D-LEARN-FEEDBACK1=A (#2947: predict, then reveal), consuming the learning census (#2926) and the first-hour script (#2900). Uses the existing jet learn runner, schema jet-learning-curriculum-v1 and Examples/learn layout; no new runner, tutor, AI mode or language levels (D-LEARN1 scope; learnability report 5.1 notes one-mechanism excludes language levels). Builds on D-EXAMPLES-SHORTPATH1=A (short path first). Not a duplicate: today's curriculum has 3 repair katas (Examples/learn/first_arc) and 4 predict tasks (loop, borrow/state, effects, foreign bindings); no task covers values, functions/return, branches, collections, maps/sets, failures or tests for a learner with no prior programming.

## Why

Jet's goal includes people who have never programmed. D-LEARN1 ratified a toolchain track 'from install to competence'. The packaged curriculum today starts at loop ranges and jumps to borrow views, effect rows and foreign bindings; the first-hour guide teaches the tool flow (new, run, check, test, explain), not programming. A complete 7-hour beginner course (Boot.dev Python for Beginners, youtube 4M87qBgpafk, ~100 exercises, 12 chapters, reviewed end to end in this batch) gives a measured-in-practice ordering and, more valuable, a corpus of misconceptions the instructor herself demonstrated on camera.

## Deliverable

One additional arc in the existing curriculum, about 12-16 tasks, each a jet-learning-curriculum-v1 task with prediction, reveal, counterexample, controlled edit and transfer. Order (course chapter in parentheses):

1. Output and values; `print` vs program result (ch1-2).
2. Bindings `::`/`:=`, interpolation and `{x=}` (ch2).
3. Functions with a result type; return vs print (ch3; the course's most repeated error).
4. Block scope and if-as-value (ch4; Python's function scope is the transfer trap).
5. Tests beside code and `debug(value)` instead of temporary prints (ch5; the course repeatedly tells learners to delete debug prints before submitting; Jet's debug() writes to stderr and release builds reject leftovers, E3405).
6. Exact division, `/%` floor division and signs (ch6; the instructor's own negative floor-division slip).
7. Bool-only conditions and ordered arm tables (ch7; truthiness and overlapping independent ifs).
8. Inclusive ranges, stride and the countdown (ch8; off-by-one and empty countdown).
9. Lists: value iteration first, indexes on demand, empty-list contracts (ch9).
10. Maps: missing-key outcome, counting, sorted iteration (ch10).
11. Sets: membership vs multiplicity; what dedupe preserves (ch11). Open evidence gap: no verified order-preserving distinct-values spelling (`.unique()` is E0311; `lazy().dedup()` collapses only consecutive runs) — resolve the canonical spelling before authoring this task.
12. Failures as typed values: `??`, propagation, matching by case not by message text, unreachable arms (ch12).
13. Capstone: a small text-processing project combining 9-12 (course ch9 capstone shape).

## Misconception seeds (wrong_model fields) taken from the source body

Floor division is truncation (01:59-02:03); the last index is the length (03:50-04:00); a set prints in a different order every time (06:22-06:23); distinct values have distinct hashes (06:25-06:27); removing an absent key is invisible (06:02-06:04; in Jet `&m.pop(k)` returns `.None`, which the learner must handle); None and 0 mean the same 'no arrows' (06:56-06:58); a broad handler before a specific one is fine (06:59-07:00); an error is identified by its message text (07:04-07:06); printing a value returns it (01:13-01:16).

## Hidden boundary case per task

The course's run-versus-submit split catches empty input, ties and absent keys that the visible examples omit. Each task's oracle adds at least one boundary input (empty, absent, zero, tie) that the learner does not see before the reveal.

Extra witness: '31 nooby C++ habits' (youtube i_wDa2AS_8w) shows that most beginner traps are structurally absent in Jet; the arc should show the absence (the compile error or the missing construct) rather than only the happy path.

Additions from the v3-P1 depth-gate re-mine of the course's first half ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/mine/v3/P1-python-a, supersedes the first-pass PY claims for 0:00-3:35): the course's single-domain ordering (print, variables, functions, scope, tests, arithmetic, comparisons, loops) is the arc's spine (PYA-001); hidden Submit cases map to D-TEST1 property generation for each task's boundary inputs (PYA-059); visible branch coverage (#1904) answers 'which branches did my tests reach' (PYA-099); the equal-bounds transfer trap is new: Python range(5, 5) is empty but Jet 5..5 has one item and only 5..<5 is empty (PYA-110); the course's 'make it global' NameError fix is an anti-lesson the arc must teach against, because Jet does have mutable module globals (spec.md:230-237; PYA-055); never copy the plaintext-password login demo (Argon2id policy; PYA-086); the 'a decimal point means float' and container-of-value definitions are misconception seeds (PYA-021, PYA-012).

Distilled 2026-10-05 by DistillLang from the six mining batches; Tower snapshot rev 74843 (jet-state digest INCONSISTENT during collection: rerun before posting).
