D-LEARN1 / D-LEARN-FEEDBACK1 content work is suspended with it; unfreezing needs the owner, then a fresh design against the current CLI and docs. Removal tracked on its own sprint card.

Learn arc additions from the claims pass: hidden boundary cases from property tests (v3-P1:PYA-059, v3-P2:PYB-59), learner-visible branch coverage (PYA-099), zero-install browser lane balloted separately.

Distill 2026-10-05, v3-P2 task seeds (4M87qBgpafk 3:35-7:08; $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/mine/v3/P2-python-b/drafts/card-learn-beginner-arc.delta.json): predict iteration counts for 0..<1000, 10..1 and 10..1, -1 (PYB-2); `gold :: inv[0]` then writing inv[0] is E0212 in Jet while Python prints the old value (probe p5, PYB-13); a running max seeded with 0 on [-54, -3], then `[].max()` (PYB-38); how often the else runs while tracking a max (PYB-42); stride versus guard on unseen data (PYB-43); first() with a hidden empty case (PYB-59); nested-loop trace order (PYB-67); a container choice table (PYB-100); validate before acting (PYB-111); closed string sets become enums (PYB-30); name the code after the plan (PYB-40).
Later-track leads, not this arc and no demand evidence yet: Exercism-style challenges (Gleam RntfkL8lUY4), click-to-explain samples and a CLI-then-server tutorial (Roc DzhIprQan68), a web playground first try (ReScript yKl2fSdnw7w), and memory-layout, OS, build-a-compiler, recursion-stepper and HTTP-from-TCP tracks.

criteria.text: Examples/learn/curriculum.json gains the beginner arc as ordinary jet-learning-curriculum-v1 tasks with prerequisites, predict-then-reveal, counterexample, controlled edit, transfer and accessibility fields; the existing four tasks and first_arc keep working.
Each task's oracle includes at least one hidden boundary input (empty, absent, zero or tie) checked after the learner's edit; Tests/learn.rs exercises one task per family offline and piped.
Every task's source, solution, change and transfer files run green on default jet run, AOT and the interpreter in CI, so a language change that breaks a lesson fails the build (D-LEARN1).
Each misconception listed in the body is the wrong_model of exactly one task and its counterexample disproves it with observable output.
Task 5 teaches debug(value) and `{x=}` before tests; no lesson asks learners to delete temporary prints.
The first-hour guide links the arc as the next step after `jet explain`; Examples/learn/README.md lists the arc without duplicating curriculum data.
A fresh agent with no Jet context completes the arc with jet learn alone, and the log records any task it could not pass with the reason.
The arc includes a predict task where `loop i in 5..5` prints one line and `5..<5` prints none, with the Python range(5, 5) habit as the wrong model.
Hidden boundary inputs for each task come from D-TEST1 property generation where a generator exists, and a learner can view which branches the visible cases reached (#1904).

The arc follows the v3-P2 structure rules: a composition task after each block of single-concept tasks, records before maps, failures taught as three buckets (check-time errors, typed failures, stops), and an explicit next step after the capstone.

cards.title: Two-argument math.max/min/clamp reject Float; make them generic over Comparable with the pinned NaN rule
cards.body: Proven: math.max(1.5, 2.5) gives three E0112 "wants Int" (p04_maxfloat). Only list .max() works. #2298 already pins the NaN rule (return the non-NaN operand). Fix: generic min/max/clamp over Comparable; Float uses the #2298 rule; one name per job.

cards.title: Python and C spellings get misleading reports: ** suggests #Unsafe, // hides as an unclosed paren, # comments report E0927 twice
cards.body: Proven: print(2 ** 3) gives E0208 "Taking a raw pointer requires #Unsafe" (t25). print(7 // 2) gives only E0083 unclosed ( (t26). "# this is a comment" gives E0927 twice for one span (t12). Fix: ** in binary position teaches ^; a // comment opening inside an unclosed bracket after an operand adds "floor division is /%"; # followed by a space or lowercase word teaches // once.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c4 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-14): the asset-action program (G2) waits for the c4 ballot. A toolchain-shipped program run by b.jet() is lexed as user code, so it cannot call `__`-named core.web helpers (E0067, JetLexer Payload.jet:1056). The ways out are lexing it as a Core unit (a new loader rule), a public variant-bytes function (new API), or the CLI handing it to the action as compiler-generated text (lex_generated, as codemods do; G5DevX-2`s recommendation). Ballot option (b) of c4, encoding at compile time at the call site, would need no action program at all, so G1 and G2 are held until c4 is ratified to avoid building the wrong mechanism. G3 (a non-literal app.images setting is a check-time error with its snapshot) is independent and proceeds. c4`s ballot must state G2`s consequence for each option.

Decisions (Main, 2026-11-14) on the build writer gaps G5DevX-2 found on tree 18334dc55f. G1 approved: a `jet build` entry that collects web.image sources makes a BuildPlanExecution (one asset-bundle target, one action per source) and runs it through jet_cli_build_run_graph. G2: no new `jet self` command (owner-gated); the asset action runs a toolchain-shipped Jet program through b.jet(), using core.image plus `__`-named core.web helpers. G3 approved: planning needs the app.images settings known at compile time; a non-literal setting is a check-time error with a registered code and ui snapshot, never a silent fallback to runtime encoding. G4 OWNER GATE: c1`s clause "variants cached ... so only new or changed images encode" needs the build action store, which BuildOptions.jet:810 keeps closed (BUILD_REUSE_SAVED_WORK = false) until a ballot ratifies how a run opts in. Until then every build re-encodes. G5: actions run only in the native sandbox (bubblewrap, Linux x86-64; BuildExecute.jet:124-175), so a web build with images inherits that limit; accepted under the existing sandbox contract and recorded as a gap. G6: the built app must find its variants without runtime encoding. Preferred: link the asset bundle`s variant bytes into the executable (no new API); G5DevX-2 checks the asset-bundle contract first.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-14): c1`s "`jet dev` serves the same variant bytes as `jet build`" means the files `jet build` writes, per D-WEB-IMAGE1 option A ("Convert at build; dev on demand": web.image registers an asset node with b.add_asset_bundle, and variants are cached by source hash, width, format, quality and encoder version in the project cache). A built program converting on first request would be option B, which was not chosen. Staged so far: core.image items 1–6 (batches 43 and 44) and web.image items 1–5 (variants, settings, the AppImages example; batch 46). Still to build: the WebGraph collection plus the asset node, the build writer with its cache key, and the dev==build hash case.

c1 split, without WebP (G9Web-1-2, 2026-11-12). Items of about an hour each, in order, starting after the #6445 move (D-WEB-RUNTIME-API1): (1) the core.image home and records (Image, ImageError, decode limits), with the Ui/Draw PNG decoder moved behind it; (2-3) a baseline JPEG decoder, refusing progressive with a typed error; (4) a PNG encoder over the shared Core/Archive deflater; (5) a baseline JPEG encoder within a PSNR bound; (6) an area-average downscaler; (7) web.image asset-graph nodes plus their diagnostic; (8) a variant cache keyed on 5 identity inputs; (9) picture markup; (10) jet dev serving variants with hashes equal to jet build; (11) images settings and their snapshots; (12) an example with goldens on O0/O1/O2, plus docs. Gate: any public core.image name beyond what D-WEB-IMAGE1 ratifies goes on a ballot before item 1. Deferred tonight for G10 (a 05:30 target).

D-WEB-IMAGE1=A, D-IMAGE-ENCODE1=A ratified; application contract updated. No implementation/build/test or closure receipt claimed. Owners: unowned (WebGolden1 parked owns route/marker goldens, not image pipeline; JetpackHost1 explicitly excludes this feature); unowned (same #4695 pipeline+encoder owner). Latest owner #29 permits only minimal port seams both halves, dies at cutover; #31 requires actual Jet ports.

Proof: a web example with one PNG and one JPEG builds picture markup with variants and the original fallback, `jet dev` serves the same variant bytes as `jet build` (a case compares their hashes), and each images setting changes the output (goldens on O0, O1 and O2). criteria.text: The web image variant cache follows the one on/off build cache setting (D-BUILD-REUSESET1=A, with reuse on by default per D-EFF-BUILD-REUSE1=B): a second `jet build` with unchanged sources encodes nothing (trace count 0).

Ballot (on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15)): how a built web app serves the build-time variants without encoding at run time. An asset-bundle target delivers nothing to the built program (spec.md:6484, BuildExecute.jet:869), and Core cannot read a generated program module. The options to ballot: (a) the compiler supplies the body of an internal Core table (`__app_embedded_images`) from the bundle`s generated embed_bytes module, which is a new compiler-known link (I8); (b) web.image with a literal source encodes at compile time in the comptime child and embeds the bytes at the call site, which reuses #run and embed but replaces the ratified asset-node sketch; (c) the app serves the build output directory found next to the executable, which needs a new public executable-path API. Proof once ratified: the built AppImages example serves byte-identical variants to `jet dev` with no encode on its first request (trace), on O0, O1 and O2.

Jet-only, memory-safe WebP (D-IMAGE-ENCODE1=A): VP8L lossless encode and decode with fuzz coverage, then VP8 lossy encode, reusing the shared inflater; the encoder depends on neither Rust nor C. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Image/webp_` and the fuzz target run.

A committed manifest fixes the image corpus, the size margin at equal SSIM and the encode-time comparator, and its receipt passes before a source type enables automatic WebP; AVIF stays a later ballot. Proof: the manifest and receipt under Tools/Perf, checked by `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Image/webp_gate`.

Item (1) follows the ratified reservation; if review finds any method name needs owner choice, raise a short ballot for it. Endian types are ballot D-ENDIAN-TYPES1.

cards.title: Stored sibling links: inferred ties, Within disambiguation, frozen-source lifetime
cards.body:
D-LINK-SIBLING1=A
Eligibility, decided on the declaration. A link field of type @T or [@T] has as candidates the sibling fields of type T or [T]. For @String, a String field also qualifies, since @String reaches a string or part of one (memory-model proposal 5.5). A field whose type is a type parameter counts as a candidate, so a generic record's tie never changes with its instantiation. One candidate: the tie is inferred. Two or more: #Within(field) is required. None: no tie.

When a record is tied. A record is tied when a construction in its own module stores links taken from the candidate. From then on every construction and every later assignment to the link field, anywhere, must take links from that field; an empty list is fine. A construction that stores outside links, or might on some path, is an error naming the constructor. If no construction in the module takes links from the candidate, the record is untied and its links follow today's stored-link rules.

Adding a second candidate field later turns an inferred tie into the two-candidate error until #Within names one; writing #Within up front locks the tie against that. The tie is published like inferred link sources (D-MEMPROVENANCE2=A), so any change shows as an API change.

Freeze and lifetime. The source is frozen in shape and value while any link into it lives, not only while the record lives. Links inside the record are plain pointers. A link that leaves the record, such as a returned key, is a kept link holding a count on the source (memory-model proposal 5.4). So the source outlives it and stays frozen until it is gone.

Taking a record apart by move hands back both fields. The text stays frozen while the keys or any link from them lives, and is an ordinary string afterwards.

Copies. Copying a tied record shares its frozen source with one count and copies the other fields by their usual rules (D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A). Nothing can write the source, so the first-write copy never happens and both copies' links stay correct. Allowing item writes in a tied list would need copies to detach and retarget every link; that was rejected as costlier and harder to explain.

Decoders. A derived decoder (#Decode, #Codable) builds each field from saved data on its own, so it cannot know that keys point into text; it is rejected with an error naming the tie. #Encode still saves the fields. The durable form is the text: a loader decodes the text and reruns the parser, so keys are rebuilt, not loaded.

Implementation areas: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/{Registration/Items,Ownership/Checks,Ownership/WindowFacts}.jet tie inference/constructor analysis/freeze; Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/{AST,TIR,MIR}/ tie facts; Compiler/JetBackend/Source/Lower/ ownership/drop and kept links; Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Verification/Lint.jet; runtime link/source lifetime; derived codecs; hover/inspect types
Spec/registry: Docs/proposals/memory-model-2026-10-05.md 5.4/5.5 and C30; Docs/spec/{safety,mir-lint}.md; syntax-decisions D-LINK-ITEM1 exception and D-LINK-SIBLING1 inference, NOT from field grammar; Legacy Syntax/markers.rs + Policy::APPLIED_RULES reference; Jet Prelude Markers.jet + AppliedRules metadata add #Within(field) citing D-LINK-SIBLING1=A; no new from clause; registry ceiling approval traced
Diagnostics/UI: Two candidates/generic ambiguity needs Within; outside-link constructor error; frozen value/shape/item write errors; #Decode/#Codable tie refusal; hover/inspect tie facts
Examples/goldens: C30 parser golden; inferred/explicit tie, empty links and untied record, alias lifetime beyond record, copies, move-apart until final link dies, tied frozen [Node] exception; MIR Lint mutations; parser cost cell vs copies/positions
Timing: UNDER #27 Jet-half-only implementation was permitted; latest #29 schedules NEW FEATURE delivery after port/Rust-exit feature resumption. Record docs/contracts/tests plan NOW; an independently justified MINIMAL seam required to port an existing row/layer/harness is PORT NOW and may mirror both halves with dies-at-cutover ledger. Do not let this feature block current port merely because its contract is ratified. Earlier #27 assessment: JET NOW design/implementation allowed, but admission waits on #3645 real link substrate/runtime and standing safety coverage. Not required to wait for Rust removal; prohibit new Rust mirror. CURRENT #29/#31: a MINIMAL seam necessary to port an existing Core row/runtime layer/test harness may also change the Rust half, registered as dies at cutover; all actual layer policy/carriers must still be ported to Jet. This exception does not permit duplicating new features. #28 Sol authors, Opus reviews. Features outside required port work resume after port/Rust exit; contract/docs/tests planning may be prepared now.
Owner: unowned (RatifyMemory parked STREAMS:224; SafetyNet8 owns independent MIR safety gate, not this feature)

A tied record's source field stays frozen while any link taken from it is alive, including links kept past an escape or a move-apart, and a copy of the record shares the frozen source without retargeting its links. The tie is published as a fact like inferred link sources, and hover and `jet inspect` show which field a link field is tied to.

cards.title: Pinned shared Jet globals and isolated Core state providers
cards.body:
D-CORE-GLOBAL-STATE1=A
Proposed compiler law: sema admits a shared initializer for #Persist, checks T under existing Shared crossing rules, and records stable binding identity and type/layout facts. The new branch requires a `name: value` declaration (not `:=`) so the module handle cannot be reassigned, moved out, or transiently absent.

The initializer must be a closed, non-suspending, infallible state-construction expression: literal data and checked pure construction, no task/world capture, external effects, or access to other lazy globals. Cyclic global initialization is rejected, not allowed to hang. The example creates only an empty typed map inside Storage. Allocation remains subject to existing allocation behavior; no new retry policy is introduced.

All execution modes implement identical once-only publication. State is inaccessible until initialization finishes. Ordinary statements use the existing Shared lock/cleanup law, not scalar persist take/set. Transactions and guards remain unchanged; this ballot adds no new atomicity mechanism. A failed or cancelled ordinary update releases locks under existing Shared rules; this ballot does not promise rollback outside #Transact.

Reload never runs the initializer again for a retained cell. Layout/migration checks complete at the existing reload boundary before new code uses old storage. The process default and each test-world provider are implemented in Jet. Vetted #Unsafe FFI/syscalls may supply host synchronization, but no Rust implementation is retained.

Implementation areas: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Items.jet E0622 admission, stable Global binding facts; Compiler/JetBackend/Source/Lower/Statics.jet once/Shared global path; Jet runtime once+lock/reload/world provider; Core/math/random.jet, Core/sys/sys.jet env overlay, Core/testing/testing.jet fault switches, Core/auth/auth.jet and Core/web/storage*.jet; no scalar take/set gap

Examples/goldens: Contended first access exactly once/no partial publication; indexed Shared map update #4751 mandatory; counter atomic statement; two-key Transact invariant + cancellation/panic guard release; compatible body/init reload retains; rename fresh/process restart empty; parallel worlds/children local-session separation; browser scope unchanged

Broader unrelated feature work remains frozen. Runtime policy, once/lock/world/reload implementations are Jet-owned; scalar Alloc root does not prove shared-cell semantics. This exception does not permit duplicating new features. #28 Sol authors, Opus reviews. cards.title: Toolchain-private Core seams for Jetpack (D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A) (held-directory process, held link)
cards.body: Decided: D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A (ratified 2026-11-01), a toolchain-private module, as c1 states. The ballot text below is history. Jetpack (the Jet package manager) needs two capabilities that exist only as raw Core kernels: run a child process with a held Directory as its cwd (#4895: kernel core.process.__with_directory_raw, CoreSystem2 d13edcfff) and the held link (compiler_link_held). Today they're reached through reserved __ names that the parser now rejects (E0067), so the Jet CLI's assembled source doesn't parse. Renaming them to legal names (files.compiler_process_directory, compiler_link_held) makes them ORDINARY PUBLIC Core functions: CoreReview5-2-2 traced Sema core_call 2607-2653: there is NO caller-privacy fence; the only gate (compiler_api_allowed, CompilerServices.jet:98-111) is a compile-time-only gate for core.compiler, not privacy; #Unsafe and names don't restrict callers. Visibility law today (D-VIS-MODULE1): public by default, priv only on modules and fields. Options (same program: Jetpack's TreeHash runs git with a held directory): A) Make them public, documented Core functions (e.g. process.spawn_in(spec, dir: Directory)). Beginner: one more safe capability (held handle, no path races). Expert: same. Cost: permanent public API to maintain. B) Add ONE toolchain-private visibility: a module-level marker so a Core module is importable only by the compiler and Jetpack (checked by sema, registered in Syntax.rs with a decision ID). Beginner: never sees it. Expert: can't call it. Cost: a new visibility mechanism (I8 allows it with this ratification). C) Jetpack calls the raw runtime route directly (#Import / ABI binding of the existing route symbol) with no Core wrapper. Beginner: unaffected. Cost: Jetpack carries unsafe ABI glue; violates the one-mechanism preference for Core access. Main recommends B if more toolchain-only seams are expected (they are: link, process dir, build receipts), else A for process.spawn_in only. Blocks: CLIParity1 / CLIParity2 composition (goal 4).

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): body, title reworded; the text waited on an owner answer that ratified decisions already give, or on a choice within ratified scope; it is recorded as decided (Main's operational authority) and nothing waits.

Main 2026-11-01: D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A is ratified; this card now tracks building it. Criteria 1-4 come from CardClose-1's plan (CardClose-63), and criterion 5 keeps seam 5 (build-receipt producer) here because no other card holds it. Seam 3 (pass a held lock to a child) stays on #5089 criterion 6. CardClose-1 is building criteria 1-2.
Board burndown 2026-10-22: the open decision in this card is drafted as owner ballot D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1 (draft for Main to file). The card text is background, not the decision.

Fourth case (NativeLead24-2 ruling on CLIParity2's retained-root lock): the Jet RuntimeLock must own an AdvisoryLock taken through the existing Core Directory.lock (same root inode, EX|NB flock on the held '.'); acquire / probe / marker / journal all from the same held root authority; nested identity from FileID, not path. A child process lease must INHERIT that same locked open file description (no reopen / re-flock / raw Int cast), but Core/process has no typed AdvisoryLock attachment / inheritance today. That's a Core/process seam needed by Jetpack only: public option (A) = a documented ProcessSpec capability to inherit a held AdvisoryLock; toolchain-private option (B) = the same seam behind the toolchain-private visibility. Same decision as the other three cases.

Third case (CopyPareto1, #4884 native List.sort_by): the compiler's sort_by intrinsic should lower to ONE private Core kernel (Core/collections, ordinary generic Jet function) so every tier shares the meaning (I9). Same-module private generic calls are fine today, but an EXTERNAL compiler intrinsic -> PRIVATE Core kernel call is not authorized by the current permission model (Sema Calls/Core.jet:160 / resolver 172 use public export / privacy); it must keep the registered declaration SymbolID / module owner / generics -> MIRCallee.User and still deny direct user calls to the private kernel. Options as in the ballot: A) make the kernel a public documented Core function; B) the toolchain-private visibility would also let compiler-lowered intrinsics target private Core kernels; C) n/a here (no raw route). Main's recommendation (B) now covers three cases: Jetpack seams, the compiler's build-receipt producer, and compiler intrinsics -> private Core kernels.

Additional case (CLIParity3, producer 0af618774): the compiler's own build-receipt producer needs Core/build internals that are module-private today: Core/build/keys.jet:280 (priv factory), session 127 / 147 (priv state / session, finished plan storage and target output readers). The pre-existing Driver BuildQueries already reaches the priv Core build session as a whole gateway, but that predates any ruling and isn't an authorized seam. So the ballot's question covers compiler -> Core-private access as well as Jetpack -> Core-private access; option B (one toolchain-private visibility) would cover both uniformly.

CoreReview5-2-2 confirmed there's no existing fence to reuse: compiler_api_allowed is granted only to the selected build entry (Rust BodyCheck 4232-45 / state 9902225: bundle.entry only), ordinary TreeHash / Git helpers don't qualify, and user comptime bypasses the gate anyway (6336 2680 / 2722); semantically core.build is a read-only graph / receipt query surface (6336 2712-49, D-BUILDQUERY1), not a mutable FS / Exec ProcessSpec carrier. So the ballot's options stand as written.

criteria.text: Mechanism (D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A, ratified 2026-11-01). `priv(toolchain) module` parses only in a toolchain package, meaning one whose source root lies inside the Jet distribution root that supplied Core (Core, Compiler/*, Jetpack/*); package names play no part. In any other package it is E0414, whose registry text becomes "only `priv(package)` exists outside the toolchain". A `use` or qualified path into a toolchain-private module from a non-toolchain package is E0605 ("`core.files.toolchain` is private to the Jet toolchain"). LSP completion and the generated reference never list such a module. Proof: new UI snapshots Tests/UI/priv_toolchain_in_user_package.{jet,stderr} (E0414) and Tests/UI/core_files_toolchain_user_use.{jet,stderr} (E0605). The ballot probe (a user `run()` calling the held-folder seam, today `jet check` clean) becomes E0605. A JetLSP completion test shows `core.files.` does not offer `toolchain`.

Seams 1 and 2 have their home. Core/Files gains `priv(toolchain) module toolchain` with `run_in(spec: ProcessSpec, folder: Directory) -[FS, Exec, Env]> ProcessSpec IOError!` and `link_into(source: FileReader, folder: Directory, name: String) -[FS.Write]> Bool IOError!`. Both are typed and have no `#Unsafe` marker. `files.compiler_with_process_directory` and `files.compiler_link_held` are deleted, along with their registry rows (Prelude/Core.jet, CoreSourceOwned, CoreCallRows, StructureRegistry, RawHostKeys test). Jetpack/Foundation/Source/TreeHash.jet calls `held.run_in` / `held.link_into` with no `#Unsafe` block. Proof: the Core/Files held-directory tests pass on run_in; the Jetpack Foundation TreeHash tests pass; `grep -r 'compiler_with_process_directory\|compiler_link_held'` over Core/Compiler/Jetpack/tests returns 0 rows.

A call the compiler lowers into a toolchain-private module is admitted, while the same name written in user source is E0605: user `list.sort_by(f)` lowers to the Core collections sort kernel inside a `priv(toolchain) module`. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Sort` on O0, O1 and O2, and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter sort_kernel_user_call` shows E0605.

Syntax-decisions S18 gains the `priv(toolchain)` line with the Spellings ledger regenerated, and spec.md's visibility section and the E0414, E0605 and E0609 rows name `priv(toolchain)`, with their diagnostic pages regenerated. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter syntax_ratification` and `jet Tools/Agent/DiagnosticRows.jet --check` pass.

Seam 5 under D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A: the compiler's build-receipt producer reads Core/build's session and key state (keys factory, session plan, target storage) through a `priv(toolchain)` reader instead of module-private access; the receipt is unchanged and a user `use` of the reader is E0605. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CoreSeams/build_receipt_reader` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0605_toolchain_reader`.

D-EMBED-TOOLCHAIN1=A table cutover, part 2: the five Core-declaration tables (CoreSourceOwned, EnumRows, StructureRows, the EnumPayload tail, CoreCallRows) are computed at build time from toolchain: reads, their copies and generator modes are deleted, and the declaration parser lives in one package. Walked and data-named reads use computed embed_file and find paths (D-EMBED-WALK1=A). The comptime cost of CoreCallRows (896 KB) against the generator run is recorded in the card log. Proof: the five generated files are absent from `git ls-files Compiler` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter comptime_embed_` passes.

criteria.text: `jet --help | wc -l` prints at most 50: the common commands, one line each (419 lines on 2026-10-28).
`jet help <command>` prints only that command's flags, and `jet help --all` prints the full table, all from the one option table.
No help summary line wraps mid-word at 80 columns.

D-JET-HOME1=A is carried out as one verified cutover that keeps keys, trust and retention records. After any jet command on a clean home directory, only ~/.config/jet/ and ~/.cache/jet/ exist (honouring XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME), and ~/.jet and ~/.local/share/jet are never created. The same work sits on frozen #4573.

No two registry flags share a meaning: of each pair the Jet CLI accepts today (--route/--path, --cook/--cook-mode, --force-clean/--clean in Compiler/JetCLI/Source/CLI/Commands.jet), one spelling is kept, and a removed spelling gets the ordinary unknown-flag error with its normal suggestion. Which spelling of each pair is kept is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Help, completion and CLI snapshots are regenerated, and in-repo callers use the kept spellings. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLIPartsSurface/` passes, and git grep finds no removed spelling outside tests that pin its rejection.

Build profile names have one home, the stock-profile table beside JET_BUILD_OPTIONS (census F29). Inspect.jet and Front.jet derive from it (Inspect.jet also knew `hardened` and `ci`; Front.jet did not), and a gate guard fails on any copy that differs.
Every flag of check, build, run, test and dev has a build-config key, and every build-config key has a flag, both generated from the one option table beside JET_BUILD_OPTIONS (owner rule 2026-10-09).

CLI flag ownership derives from the compiler's command declarations, while application command schemas and output-envelope contracts stay distinct. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter cli_flags_from_command_declarations`. (was #3186 c6)

Args decoding outside the entry, checked builder plans and the flag, env and default merge use the one Args projection, and an invalid present value is reported. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter args_projection_`. (was #3236 c30)

`jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/ArgsReference` passes, and a Jet test validates the man, ReST, Markdown and YAML output with real consumers (man, a ReST parser, a CommonMark renderer and an independent YAML reader), reporting a missing consumer as SKIP-HOST. Proof: those two commands. (was #3242 c31)

Nested, inherited and repeated flags, aliases, grouping, cardinality, double-dash, dynamic completion, hooks and lifecycle errors have conformance goldens. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/Conformance`. (was #3242 c36)

Run, build, dev and test overrides and argument forwarding keep the launcher's and the application's namespaces apart, and an absent override behaves as stock. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLIPartsCommands/override_namespaces`. (was #3242 c37)

Builders still support runtime-defined schemas through the same Core parser, with no second semantic parser and no compiler-CLI DSL migration. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/RuntimeSchemaBuilder`. (was #3242 c38)

Equivalent #CLI and builder grammars produce identical values, help, errors and completion on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/MarkerBuilderPair`. (was #3242 c40)

A plain `jet test Compiler/JetCLI/Tests/FrontDoor.jet` (no JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY, no Tests/.jet/build/IDENTITY, no extra runtime dir) passes every test: the tests that compile fixtures get the identity and runtime pack of the jet under test from the jet running them, never from a train-only environment variable or a build-tree file. On seed-t23 (dev 9755703c76), 18-20 FrontDoor tests fail only on E0003 'native host omitted its compiler identity' or 'no runtime pack': 10 semver/public-API tests, 3 receipt tests, jobs_metadata, the exported run library feed, inspect_build (2), inspect_output, try and fix_recheck_rolls_back (G6Meta, 2026-11-11). Proof: that plain command reports 0 failed on the train compiler. (was #3242 c43)

Each reference format carries the parse/help fixture's names, defaults, inherited options, visibility and examples, omits hidden and secret options, and escapes punctuation, fences, multiline text, descendant anchors and adversarial input correctly. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CLI/ArgsReference` and the consumer test's fixture comparison. (was #3242 c46)

cards.title: Report ALL errors by default: promote keep-going diagnostics from compiler-internal JET_KEEP_GOING to the default user behavior
cards.body: Owner 2026-10-09: the compiler must not stop at the first error; by default it reports ALL errors so a user or agent can fix them in one pass. Today (dev 2026-10-09): within a phase the Jet compiler already collects many diagnostics, but between phases it stops once errors exist (e.g. JetDriver Pipeline.jet:2220 'if jet_driver_has_errors(diagnostics) && !keep_going -> return None', BodyComptime.jet:221). A full all-phases mode exists only as the compiler-internal JET_KEEP_GOING=1 env var (Compiler/Bootstrap/Host/Entry.jet:10-128; JetDriverKeepGoing in JetDriver Identity.jet:524; sema keep-going traps CheckProgram.jet:2243+; comptime drops failed items; the optimizer traps rejected functions and reruns; the emitter keeps every failure), documented as never shipped. Work (Jet side only): make all-phases collection the default for check/build/run/test, with failed items replaced by typed traps so later phases still run without cascade noise (dedupe and suppress errors caused by an already-reported failure); no artifact is produced when any error exists; one canonical option to stop at the first error, available both as a CLI flag and as a build-config setting (owner rule #51: CLI and declarative config never diverge); registered diagnostics/snapshots for the summary line; docs. Keep the internal skip list (JET_KEEP_GOING_SKIP) as a compiler-developer tool only if still needed.

A keep-going build reaches lowering and reports a lowering census for the clean items.
Identical diagnostics in one invocation render once with a repeat-count line, and a multi-failure repro shows one block per root cause.

`jet run` on a file with check errors stops at check with exactly the diagnostics `jet check` prints for that file and prints no program output (checked by a scratch probe on 2026-10-31; no repository case pins it yet).

Keep-going has one failure-capture path per phase (the task join with a typed trap) instead of a second control flow on JET_KEEP_GOING in sema, comptime, lowering and optimization (15 Compiler files read it on dev 72a8142651); normal mode stops after the phase that reported, and both modes use the same thread schedule (architecture review Rel3, Docs/Audits/2026-10-22-architecture-review.md). Proof: `git grep -l JET_KEEP_GOING -- Compiler` lists only the driver flag reader, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter keep_going_`.

D-COLLECT-ALL-DEFAULT1=A: by default check, build, run and test run every phase and report every root error. An error caused by an earlier one is hidden from the text output and counted in the summary. No output file is written when an error occurs, and one option sets this in both the CLI and the build config. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter collect_all_default_reports_every_root_error` and `--filter cli_settings/keep_going_flag_setting_and_variable_write_one_census`.

criteria.text: Keep-going never changes emitted code: `jet build -O1 Compiler` with and without JET_KEEP_GOING=1 gives a byte-identical jet-bare and runtime pack. Measured 2026-11-18 at 94e95e4a5d: the keep-going build (every Core body loaded) gives jet-bare 07515342…, the default build (reach-pruned Core) gives ae94870d…, and about 50 Core functions differ, e.g. ssl_srv13_key_exchange_is_psk_available inlines ssl_get_extension_mask only under keep-going. Release admit rebuilds the pack under keep-going to match the chain until this holds. Proof: both builds' jet-bare sha256 are equal.

Core and Prelude bodies compute their local values while compiling once more, in the one check every compile shares: the Core library's check lands them (it lands none today, so jet_core.o keeps core.image.jpeg_codes as run-time code) and its bodies file carries the landed values, while a keep-going or --deep-checks compile, which checks Core from text, lands the same values, so c14's byte identity still holds. cards.title: Build swap and replace out of a borrowed place (D-TAKE-REPLACE1=A, D-WRITE-TAKE1=A)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-09 while fixing Core: Core CSV (streaming rows, ~791 self.fields) and crypto (~99 hash.pending.bytes) want to move a value out of a field below a read/write borrow and immediately reinitialize it. The current rules make that E0201 by design (spec.md:1077-1082, 1e1825f4e); there is no general take/replace/swap API (only Cell.replace, spec 1313-1316). Interim: crypto restructured to consume at finish; CSV uses a restructure or an explicit .copy() then reset (an extra allocation per row). Decided: D-TAKE-REPLACE1=A and D-WRITE-TAKE1=A (ratified) add the canonical take and replace; this card builds them.

Moved from ready to planning: an idea with no acceptance criteria can't be implemented or closed. It needs criteria first (CardClose-1 ready sweep, 2026-11-01).

D-TAKE-REPLACE1=A is ratified, so this card moves from ballot to build. Also: Docs/audits memory-model-2026-10-05.md:167 still names the older 'old :: ^x; x = new' route; the build must match the ratified form.

Related (2026-10-09): Core/crypto/jetc.jet needs to turn an owned Secret into an X25519SecretKey; there is no audited owner-transfer (only the copying expert.secret_bytes). Interim: build the key from the audited copy and let the Secret close and zeroize itself. Owner decision: add an audited expert transfer, e.g. expert.x25519_secret_from_secret(^Secret) plus a secret length accessor, with the take/replace question above.

Interim taken 2026-10-09: Core CSVReader row handoff now copies the fields and resets the borrowed storage (61a4cfa1c), an extra allocation per row; crypto SHA-256 finalizes the pending buffer in place instead (d0989d126, no copy). Revisit CSV if a canonical take/replace API is ratified.

criteria.text: Core CSV row handoff and the crypto pending bytes use replace instead of the interim copy-then-reset, with no extra allocation per row. Proof: git grep finds no copy-then-reset in Core/Csv and Core/Crypto, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter CSV/` passes.

D-TAKE-REPLACE1=A, extended by D-WRITE-TAKE1=A (ratified 2026-11-04): core.mem has `swap<T>` and `replace<T>` (`-[!Panic]>`), named by the prelude with no import, a user-defined swap or replace still wins, and List and Map gain swap. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/TakeReplace` on O0, O1 and O2.

Sema tracks each moved-out gap in a borrowed place (E0121): an exit, or a call that can stop, inside a gap is E0201, and its fix offers swap or replace. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0201_moved_out_gap` with the fix shown in the snapshot.

The generated code moves the value back into the place on every stop path inside a gap, so no place is left empty after a failure. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/TakeReplaceGapRestore` on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: One build plan produces several configurations of the same program
cards.body:
## Outcome

`fn build` can register one program in several configurations in a single plan: debug, release, web, or a cross target. Each configuration has its own profile and target, and all are built by one `jet build` with separate outputs.

## Evidence

- In Jai, every `compiler_create_workspace` call carries its own `Build_Options` (The Way to Jai @19cb4b7 `examples/30/30.1_workspaces.jai`, `30.13_dynamic_libraries.jai`).
- Blow's "build all" builds a debug workspace and a release workspace in parallel (`OHZwYYW9koI` 00:03:01, 2015-10-15). Tsoding's game build produces release, debug and WebAssembly outputs on every build (`kjF_YuLsPqo` 00:05:13, 2022).
- In Jet, `BuildTarget` has a toolchain handle but no profile (`crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/targets.rs:129-143`). The profile is chosen once per invocation (`--profile`/`--release`, D-BUILD-DEFAULT1). Two configurations of one program need two invocations.

## Ballot

The public `BuildContext` API shape, on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15): a profile and target argument on each registered target, or a named configuration set applied to a target. Builds on #4913's one option table and D-BUILDCTX-FLAGS1 defaults.

One review: Round3Review.

D-JAI-CONFIG1 rewritten on owner instruction 2026-10-19 to align with card #5069's slate: now a short ballot (one review, CohesionReview) deciding only when build code may change an output (A: until fn build returns; B: Jai-style message loop, expert-gated). Old option C and the exact-options rule removed; per-output options moved to D-TARGET-ONE1, precedence to D-SETTING-ORDER1, BuildOptions to D-ENTRY-NAMES1, plan sealing to D-ENTRY-SHAPE1. Present fifth in the slate order.

criteria.text: One `fn build` registers the same program in at least two configurations with different profiles and targets, and one `jet build` writes both artifacts to distinct output paths.

Each configuration's receipt names its profile and target, and changing one configuration's settings leaves the other configurations' outputs byte-identical. Proof: a cases row under `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter build_multi_config` builds twice with one setting changed and compares the output digests.
An executable example of the multi-configuration plan has golden output on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Host facts for prep and build-time code
cards.body:
## Outcome

Prep code and build-time code can tell the machine they run on (the host) from the machine the program is built for (the target). When an evaluated Core call has per-OS behaviour, the rule for which OS it uses is written down and tested.

## Evidence

- Jai hit this problem. A `#run` inside a module with per-OS implementations must use the host version, not the target version (Blow `jjCfAg_gtDw` 00:43:50, April 2023). By September 2024 Jai had added an extra hidden "host imports" workspace for compile-time code (`LPdMNsL5MgI` 00:03:21).
- Jet exposes only target facts: `$build.os` (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/OSTarget.rs:13-15`). No host fact root exists (searched `$host`, `host.os` and `HOST_OS` over `crates/jet-foundation/src`, `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source`, `syntax-decisions.md` and `metaprogramming.md`: no hits). Toolchain handles record host and target triples (D-BUILDTOOLCHAIN1), but prep code cannot read them.

## Owner gate

Adding a fact root or a `BuildContext` member is new registered surface (I7). The owner also decides what a prep-time call with per-OS behaviour does when cross-compiling (I9 keeps one meaning).

Notes: Batch N01 of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (opus), one build, one proof run: cd <worktree> && Tools/agent/jet-env node <memory-safety gate per #5093> over the golden corpus; leak count 0. Order: #4309 #4767 #5059 #5093 #5478 #5922 #5890 #5939.

LEAK HARNESS AT ZERO (LeakBurn4, 03:25 agent clock): chain fac9f48bd -> db70df8a2 -> 638234ca8 -> a8219c403 -> 28f7d7452 (Main: E0212 view fix) -> 00df51951. Last 7 roots: View<str> slot owned by the backend but never dropped by MIR -> released before return; string/list slice receivers are borrowing builtins; lower_trait_call: the rejected release was correctly unsafe (a view indexes with the old `at` after the write) -> the Int read takes its own copy released after last use (lower_release_owning_read). Remaining for the zero-leak gate: runtime proofs (write-drop RSS 30 shapes on a stage 1; runtime tracker floor) and lircheck blind spot (buffers escaping from inline stack aggregates: covered by the RSS proofs). These commits go into the chain after clean2 (not in clean2).

All 56 remaining LEAK rows are in bk (backend unit own MIR); LeakBurn3 working them by class. Queued for the chain after clean2.

MEASURED (LeakAudit exact diff, candidate backend 1912fb7a1 = clean1/clean2 backend minus 2 non-backend commits, vs old tree a35c36310; leak harness, same 55 cases + bk = the backend unit own MIR, 192 MB): lircheck LEAK 260 -> 98 (-62%); bk alone 181 -> 56; DOUBLE 0 -> 0; UAF 0 -> 0 (after the frame-box modeling fix). BEFORE table for the write-drop leak class (WriteDrops2, runtime RSS, r29g stage 1 at a35c36310, 100 vs 400 rounds; writedrops2/rss-base/result.txt): 13 of 26 buildable shapes LEAK: literal rebind +375 MB, pushed +187, moved +188, element overwrite +188, branch +281, map_index +375, map_string +1501, map_method +375, set +375, bits +750, struct_field +188, struct_entry +1501; 13 flat. tally/queue/pqueue/bytes do not build natively on r29g (O0 gaps, not leaks: separate defect). VERDICT (LeakAudit, 23:10): the 59 DOUBLE + 2 UAF on the rehearsal tree a84219f42 are lircheck ARTIFACTS. Evidence: current lircheck on the old tree LIR (leakint/vc-d) still gives 0/0/60 (tool unchanged); every flagged row starts with A3 d078567e2 lower_frame_box (vS = stack N; store vS+0, i64::MIN; vP = ptradd vS, 24; store vP+8, vOwner; call f(vP); ... drop vOwner): a frame box is a borrowed carrier with an immortal count (never released/freed; its clone is a private copy), so the store is a bitwise borrow and the later drop is the only end; lircheck counted the store as a hand-off. Tool fix: lircheck.mjs treats stores into an immortal-count stack slot (or anything derived) as copy stores. Rerun: DOUBLE 0 / UAF 0 / LEAK 102 / UNKNOWN 0. Open: LEAK 102 vs the old 60 baseline (mF2 42, mP4 27, mO1 22, ...: files.jet open/stat/open_directory owned at return; mF2 full_roots chains) -> LeakAudit attributing.

ALERT (23:00): the calibrated leak harness on the REHEARSAL tree a84219f42 reports lircheck 59 DOUBLE / 2 UAF / 102 LEAK over 53 cases, identical with and without the write-drop fix 20252843c (perfile-{base,fix}.tsv identical). Earlier baseline (older tree) was 0 DOUBLE / 0 UAF. Hypotheses: (a) lircheck models refcount release (String/List-family/box, a305928a6/83a1388ce/d078567e2) as a free and ignores retain -> false DOUBLE; (b) real double frees in the rehearsal tree. Agent LeakAudit dispatched: inspect rows, teach lircheck refcount semantics, bisect a35c36310..a84219f42, fix real ones. The rehearsal binary is not trusted until the verdict.

Root cause narrowed (NativeObjectMem, 22:45): straight-line `first = [Int]{..}` drops the old list, but the same write inside a LOOP emits no drop: lower_release_write_drops never marks the loop write (the old value is the loop-carried slot block param). lircheck BLIND SPOT: reports 0 LEAK because the list is an inline stack aggregate whose buffer pointer escapes to memory, so the static leak gate cannot see this class -> the leak gate needs the runtime check (RSS/tracker) as well; NativeObjectMem adds an RSS runtime check and, if cheap, teaches lircheck to track escaped aggregate buffers.

SYSTEMIC LEAK found by NativeObjectMem (22:40): a whole-root WritePlace of an owned list does not release the old value (Lower.jet lower_release_write_drops never marks it). Native probes built with r29g stage 1 (a35c36310), 20k iterations/round, max RSS at 100 vs 400 rounds: `x = [Int]{...}` on an outer list local 130 MB -> 505 MB; `current = rest` (local moved into outer local) 130 -> 505 MB; `rows[i] = fresh` (owned list element overwrite) 130 -> 505 MB; controls flat (~5 MB): loop-local fresh, struct field holder.items = fresh, String reassign, Int element overwrite. This leaks in every compiled Jet program and is the main cause of the native.object memory blow-up in stage 2 (66% of page faults in x64_allocate etc., code that reassigns list locals per instruction/value/block). Probes: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/overnight/nativeobjmem/leak{,2}/ (leakrun.sh <dir> <jet>). Systemic fix in lowering assigned to NativeObjectMem on the rehearsal tree a84219f42, for the final clean chain; validated with these probes as fixtures + lircheck. The leak gate (0 LEAK) cannot pass without it.

Harness: calibrated baseline unchanged; 18 enum cases + probes 0 issues; lircheck cases LEAK 164 -> 60, DOUBLE 0, UAF 0 (remaining DOUBLE/UAF rows are a Slot:close lircheck artifact, identical on r29). NOT in r29d, untested: b788d6a7b on e286e96bb (a value defined in the block where its lowering started stays releasable after the lowering branches; fixes HostCall Result-box leaks in the Core files routes). Test: export from $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/leakint/wt (export exists at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/leakint/src-e), then W=$JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/leakint/src-e T=-e bash $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/leakint/harness2.sh; include in the clean second self-host if clean. cards.title: Context parity with Jai: readable context, typed keys, scratch storage, assertion handler
cards.body:
## Outcome

Decision D-JAI-CONTEXT1. Jai passes an implicit context (allocator, logger, temporary storage, assertion handler, stack trace, print style, thread index; #add_context, push_context). Jet has the D-CTX1 `#Context(...) { }` block for allocator, logger and deadline. The earlier context-extension card #3502 is frozen by the owner pending what context adds; the owner's 2026-10-16 direction (every Jai feature) supersedes that freeze for this decision. Audit rows: F01-F13, E24, E34.

The ballot carries the full design; this card holds the vote and, once ratified, the delivery plan.
cards.plan: Owner 2026-10-29: moved up; no longer sequenced after the speed goal. 1) #5030 done (C1). 2) Context reads (allocator, logger, deadline, scratch, on_assert, print, thread, trace) plus the Context read effect in sema (C2). 3) #ContextKey typed keys and task-owned context inherited by spawned tasks (C3). 4) Scratch storage and the assertion/print/trace hooks (C4). 5) Correct the spec overstatement #5892 (C5). Any exact spelling D-JAI-CONTEXT1 leaves open goes to an owner ballot before step 2. Proof per step: executable example with goldens on O0/O1/O2, UI snapshots for new diagnostics, one shared runtime meaning (I9).

log.text: ContextOnStop o2 intermittent internal compiler error: new evidence. On the batch 38 stage-2 compiler (dev b872a051a81), 'jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter ContextOnStop' run alone hit the o2 ICE (exit 101) in 1 of 2 runs, with no suite load; o0 and o1 passed both times. The full batch 38 golden run also hit it. Because it reproduces in isolation, a recorded run under jet debug --record of the o2 build is now practical, replacing the earlier inference that only suite load triggers it. Next step: record repeated O2 builds until one fails, then read the ICE's fault and backtrace in the replay. The golden row stays an open defect; it is not a batch regression.

Defect (found by batch suites): Examples/Concurrency/ContextOnStop.jet at o2 fails now and then with an internal compiler error (exit 101). It failed on batch 30, passed on batch 31 and hit the ICE again on batch 34. On the batch 34 compiler, 'jet build -O2' passed 3/3 and 'jet run -O2' passed 5/5 with the golden output, so the failure depends on timing or load. An intermittent ICE is an I2 defect. Next step: reproduce it under suite load with 'jet debug --record' on the compiler, then fix the nondeterminism at its root.

D-CONTEXT-THREAD1 posted: what context.thread reads in Jet code running outside the task pool (the Ctrl-C dispatcher running on_interrupt handlers, a realtime stream callback). The context-thread fix (Errors3202-context-thread-index.r2, landed p382 as 01d4c42a88) made pool indices dense from 1 and gives every other thread -1 as the interim; it found that every runtime helper thread drew from the carrier counter. The interim stands until the vote.

2026-11-15 TowerKeeper-1: c10, c11, c12, c16 and c20 met with G3Core commits and passing cases on dev a652c3674b (gate-p141). Still failing there: the context/context_allocator_* cases, context_scratch_block_rewinds_and_moves_what_leaves (ICE) and Examples/Memory/Allocation/ContextAllocator (served by the allocator: false), so c2 (allocator field), c4, c21 and c22 stay open.

c2 allocator field: no ballot needed (Main, 2026-11-12). Ratified D-CONTEXT1 types the field as `allocator: mem.Allocator`, and D-ALLOC-TRAIT1=A makes mem.Allocator a trait whose calls go through one trait-value slot with no box. So context.allocator reads as a borrowed mem.Allocator trait value. Arena, Bump, Pool and Fixed implement the trait, and #Context(allocator:) accepts any implementer, user allocators included, in place of the hard-coded four-name list. G12Docs-4 builds it as G3Core-c2-ctxalloc on G3Core-c2-ctxreads.

Main 2026-11-12 (c2): context.scratch reads as a borrow of the task arena, which is a mem.Arena view. Dropping it frees nothing, escaping it is E0631 and use after reset is a located stop, as D-JAI-CONTEXT1/D-CONTEXT1 state; no new type. context.allocator has no ratified value form for the current allocator: mem.Allocator is a trait, and only mem.Heap, mem.System and mem.Counting are named as package.jet allocators. That one field goes to ballot D-CONTEXT-ALLOCATOR1 (Main drafting). G12Docs-4 builds c2 for the other seven fields with goldens at O0/O1/O2.

G3Core-ctx8-r2 (c5) cut the spec status notes. Unbuilt parts it names: allocator routing in #Context blocks (new criterion c21) and context.allocator, .scratch and .print reads (already c2, c8 and c10).

Unlanded work, recorded 2026-11-12 (dead-lane sweep, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/deadlanes/REPORT.md). The G3Ctx lane has no agent. Only G3Ctx-1 (1e1fff240f) and G3Ctx-15 (a32aeb5757) are on dev. Unlanded and staged in Main/inbox: G3Ctx-2 (c3), G3Ctx-3 (c2), G3Ctx-4 (c8), G3Ctx-7 (c6), G3Ctx-8 (c5), G3Ctx-17/17b (c4 partial). G3Ctx-18 (c4 with #6314 c3) is only work in progress, saved as $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sweep/deadlanes/G3Ctx-t9.patch, with its draft message at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G3Ctx/g3ctx18.msg. The source tree is kept at lanes/G3Ctx/t4 (t7 is its worktree). All of it predates D-CONTEXT-EFFECT1=F (ratified 2026-11-12), so each SUB is re-checked against F and its review conditions (c16-c20) and rebased on dev before landing. Owner: G12Docs-4 (G3), after #5971.

Adversarial review of F, G12Docs-66 (Docs/audits/context-implicit-input-review-2026-11-12.md): F holds only on conditions, namely the local-value fold, module values, the #Memo key, the C-callback clause and the pure wording, each now a criterion on this card. c14 (a passing review) stays open until the spec closes those gaps and a second review passes. Decided within scope: locals that reach context stay run-time code, and module values that reach context keep E0643. The C-callback clause needs an owner ballot.

D-CONTEXT-EFFECT1 ratified F on 2026-11-12: context is an implicit input to every function, as in Jai. c2 and c13 now state F's build, and the new last criterion is F's cross-family review, which goes first.

Conflict found 2026-11-11 (G8Scope-3 sweep): c2's slice 1e1fff240f added `Context` as a 13th effect root (Compiler/Prelude Effect enum, generated EffectRoots.jet). Ratified D-EFFTYPE-KERNEL1 lists 12 roots. An effect root is user-visible language surface, so this goes to an owner ballot: ratify Context as a 13th root, or carry context reads under an existing root or a sub-effect. Until it is ratified, c2 cannot close. The ballot is drafted by G8Scope-3 and reviewed by sol-reviewer.
Correction to the previous log: the new criteria are c8 (the hooks) and c9 (the paired perf cell), not c7 and c8.

Owner asked 2026-11-10 ~21:20 where the Jai/Odin-style implicit context stands. Main probe 2026-11-10 on the t17a compiler (dev c2cecce162): `#Context(allocator: …)` blocks run, but `context.allocator` and `context.scratch` give E0107 (no `context` name), `#Context(frame_index: 3)` gives E0761 (only allocator, logger and deadline exist), and `#ContextKey` is not recognized (E0357 casing on the constant). The design is ratified (D-JAI-CONTEXT1=A 2026-10-17, D-CONTEXT1=A 2026-10-29, D-ALLOC-SITE1=A on #6314), but the card had no goal, so no agent picked it up after 2026-10-29. It is now under G3 (Core library completeness); c4 was rewritten to D-CONTEXT1's contract, and c7 (hooks) and c8 (the paired perf cell) were added.

D-CONTEXT1 is added and ready. It folds and replaces D-CONTEXT-NAME1, KEYS1, ALLOC1, FIELDS1 and SCRATCH1, which are deleted (originals in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots/backup38/). It passed Main's adversarial pass after revision 2 (older-container growth, exits, deep-move cost, the contiguous-reservation address test, the expert way out). Once ratified, amend D-JAI-CONTEXT1 SCRATCH/HANDLER/KEYS and D-CTX1 as its detail lists.

NixTmp-ctx0 landed as 36825b7a15. #ContextKey typed keys: packages declare keys, #Context(name: v) sets them for a region, context.get(name) reads them, and spawned tasks inherit the task-owned context; goldens and UI snapshots. D-CONTEXT1=A scratch blocks: `#Context(allocator: context.scratch) { … }` (or any mem.Arena) sends every allocation in the block, including in libraries, to the task's scratch arena (one contiguous reservation per task, pages committed on touch). Block exit rewinds to the entry mark, and nested blocks are nested marks. `&arena.reset()` inside the block is E0204. A value that leaves the block (a store into older data, return, a task hand-off or an escaping closure) first moves into the destination's own allocator, found by the one subtract-and-compare address test, and an older container grows from its owner's allocator. No reset call and no mark are user-visible, and dropping a scratch value frees nothing. Goldens on O0, O1 and O2 through the one shared runtime, plus UI snapshots for E0204. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Context/ScratchBlock` on O0, O1 and O2 and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0204`.

`context.trace` reads an owned list of SourceLocation records (D-JAI-SITE1), innermost first, from the same frame source as panic and fault reports, and prints the same text on every supported target; golden on o0, o1 and o2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Context/Trace` on O0, O1 and O2.

The context hooks take effect: context.on_stop (D-CONTEXT1=A: `on_stop: fn(debug.Stop)`, the handler a failed assert or panic reaches), context.print and context.thread are readable, on_stop and print are settable through #Context, and a replaced stop handler runs on a failed assert. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/Context` (ContextOnStop, ContextPrintStyle, ContextPureReads) on O0, O1 and O2; all 24 rows pass on dev a652c3674b with gate-p141.

The escape cost the D-CONTEXT1 claim rests on is measured: a paired two-program perf cell (scratch block against plain allocation) for a frame-style workload (and a second program that uses scratch differently) shows the address test costs nothing measurable outside scratch blocks and that scratch beats the plain form inside them, recorded in the canonical manifest (AGENTS.md, Performance gate). Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry context-scratch` and its manifest row.

cards.title: C source import: translate C into editable safe Jet, keep the rest behind the checked binder (c2v lesson)
cards.body: Source: mine-for-jet V report (Docs/research, 2026-10-16). V's c2v translates whole C and C++ projects to V through Clang's JSON AST (vlang/c2v README:1-86; DOOM and Doom 3 demos) and is V's main on-ramp for C codebases. Jet has no C source importer: Docs/spec/reference/migration-tier-map.md:28 keeps C binder-only by D-ADOPT-TIER1=A. The owner wants C compatibility as an on-ramp for new users (2026-10-16). V's model has two defects Jet must not copy: translated files relax the language rules (@[translated]: globals, pointer writes without unsafe, C scalar conversions; doc/docs.md:10990-11014), and vlang/doom still links the C platform layer and has broken sound (doom README:5-9). Jet already ratified one Clang declaration extractor for C and C++ (D-CBIND-UPSTREAM1=A, D-CIMPORT1=A, #4174), so a body importer can extend the same extraction instead of adding a parser. D-CSRC-IMPORT1=A (ratified) settles whether Jet translates C source into editable Jet, and so the C row of the tier map.
cards.plan: 1. Owner ratifies D-CSRC-IMPORT1. 2. If A: extend the shared Clang extractor from declarations to function bodies; translate each function into safe Jet when every construct maps (pointers to views/indices, arrays to fixed lists, unions to enums when tagged); leave the function in C behind the generated binder otherwise, with JT0101 naming the construct, span and reason. 3. Differential oracle per translated function against the original C (D-MIGRATE-SRC1). 4. Corpus: zlib, sqlite3 subset, Chocolate Doom src/doom; report translated/left-in-C counts per file.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): weeks. C-to-Jet import of zlib, sqlite and doom with differential fixtures.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): body reworded; the text waited on an owner answer that ratified decisions already give, or on a choice within ratified scope; it is recorded as decided (Main's operational authority) and nothing waits.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

cards.body: Owner direction 2026-10-16 (chat, mine-for-jet V session): 'the jet doom port would go in a separate project so that the license doesnt conflict. jet stays MIT but jet doom would be whatever license is needed. i also want as much as possible to be jet not leaning on c ffi/interop for most of it.' Doom's source is GPL-2.0 (id Software release; Chocolate Doom, doomgeneric, gore are GPL-2.0), so the port lives in its own repository under GPL-2.0; nothing GPL enters the Jet repository. Evidence: vlang/doom is a c2v translation of Chocolate Doom's src/doom only, linked against Chocolate Doom's C platform objects and SDL; its README lists inlined #define constants and broken sound effects; last push 2024-07 (vlang/doom build_whole_project.sh:10-36, README.md:1-9). Feasibility: game logic (~45k C lines in Chocolate Doom src/doom plus the shared engine files) is fixed-point integer code, tables and a software renderer, all expressible in safe Jet with fixed-width wrapping arithmetic and fixed lists; the only OS edge is the Core platform layer (#5035). cards.title: Compiler session protocol: jet.session.v1 NDJSON, `--listen=-` on check/build/test/run/dev, `--serve` owners and attach
cards.body:
## Outcome
One session protocol for every external client, per the ballots ratified 2026-10-17. D-SESSION-WIRE1=A: newline-delimited JSON `jet.session.v1`, UTF-8, one message per line. Reports are the D-REPORT-MACHINE1 object unchanged, build events come from the `compiler.Event` registry (D-COMPILER-EVENT1=A), the first line is `hello` with the toolchain identity, a mismatch refuses the attach (the CLI runs fresh and explains under --verbose; Jetpack reports E1227), lines are capped at 1 MiB, and artifacts never cross the wire. D-SESSION-ENTRY1=C: `--listen=-` on `jet check|build|test|run|dev` serves the protocol on stdio, with no hidden verb. D-SESSION-OWNER1=A: `jet dev --serve` and `jet self lsp --serve` may own the workspace endpoint. The first owner holds the lock in `.jet/session` and the other attaches as a client. This amends D-BUILD-SESSION1 (`dev --serve` only), and D-JPK-NODAEMON1 holds because both are foreground processes.

This card also carries the real work of #2529 (D-BUILD-SESSION1). That card is `done` without code: there is no `--serve`, `--session`, socket or tests/cli_dev_session.rs at 161cf85cc (finding F1).

## Plan
1. T2 codec: CompilerService.jet's tagged-value/CtValue codecs become the session JSON codec; `foundation_parse_protocol_json` stays the reader; the narrow diagnostic codec is deleted and the D-REPORT-MACHINE1 writer used.
2. `--listen=-` flag row in CLICommands.jet next to --threads/--trace; Front.jet parsing for the five verbs; session loop over the S1 session; per-verb `update` per the ratified D-SESSION-UPDATE1 table.
3. `--serve` on `jet dev` and `jet self lsp`: endpoint security as ratified (0700 per-user dir, symlinks rejected, peer credentials, nonce from .jet/session, one owner per workspace by lock); `--session=auto|off|required` attach on build/run/test; `invoke` envelope; Ctrl-C cancels the client's request.
4. Docs/spec/reference/cli.md section for --listen and --serve; help snapshots regenerated in the same commit.

Identity set: Compiler/ only, so this lands after a0_004.

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15: every criterion has a proof; c1 drops warnings (D-NO-WARNINGS1=A).

criteria.text: An attached `jet build` equals a fresh build for every corpus program across success, error and ICE: the binary SHA-256 is identical, and stdout, stderr and `--json` lines are identical except for observation fields (timestamps, durations, RSS).

`jet check|build|test|run|dev --listen=-` each answer hello, update, cancel and exit on stdio, with the ratified per-verb meaning of `update`. A malformed line gets a report line and the session continues, and `--listen=<addr>` other than `-` is refused with a UI snapshot.
A toolchain-identity mismatch on `hello` refuses the attach, and the CLI runs fresh and says why only under --verbose. A line of 1 MiB plus 1 byte is refused with a report.

With `jet self lsp --serve` running, `jet build` attaches (no second compiler process), and a later `jet dev --serve` attaches as a client. Closing the owner leaves no endpoint, and the next `jet build --verbose` prints the fresh-process note.
A foreign client (another user, a wrong nonce or a symlinked endpoint) is refused, and an edit made while no session ran is picked up by the next attached build.
The adoption receipt, comparing fresh-process and attached overhead on the #2859 corpus, is recorded. Proof: a committed measurement under Docs/Audits with both timings and the commands.

Proof: `jet test Jetpack/EnvModel` and `jet test Jetpack/ProjectEntry`, and `git grep -n __jetpack -- Compiler Jetpack` prints nothing.

cards.title: Scripting ergonomics ballots B1-B10 (list +, slot +=, char-index find, write, top-level statements, fail, Match.named, is_executable, Path.script_dir, Regex lint)
cards.body:
# Script ergonomics ballots (final; for Main to file on Tower)

One entry per proposed new API or syntax. Each names the exact spelling, the semantics, a
before/after taken from the four idiomatic tool rewrites
(`$JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/ScriptErgonomics/idiomatic/{TestShards,WebBundleCheck,LexerKeywordRows,Lifecycle}.jet`),
and the saving counted with `count.sh` (program lines / whitespace tokens: no blanks, comments,
`#Test` blocks or `package {}`). A saving marked [INFERENCE] is read off the before/after text,
not measured on a rewritten file.
Not ballots (bug fixes, no new surface). Landed: `pad_start`/`pad_end` link, `remove_prefix`/`remove_suffix`
methods (efbc29643), web baseline (17537755c). Patch ready, not landed (see lane report): the prelude
rows below and the collecting-loop propagation fix.
- readable prelude names `eprint`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `file_exists`, `keep`, `Clock`,
  `Instant`, `Date`, `Duration` resolve without `use` (Spec.md:305-317, D-CORE-PRELUDE1/2);
  `Date.today()` reaches `LocalDate` statics; `files.read`/`read_file` take `String | Path`
  like `write`; `.or_err(...)`/`keep(...)` no longer ICE (core.prelude loads);
- integer selectors of every width (`{i64:Hex(8)}`) and `Pad`/`PadLeft` of any displayable value
  (`{n:PadLeft(2, "0")}`), as codegen already lowered them;
- `"x".pad_start(n, f)` / `pad_end` link (they share the `rjust`/`ljust` runtime routes);
- `s.remove_prefix(p)` / `s.remove_suffix(p)` are methods (String.jet already had the bodies);
- `Int.parse` (any fallible call) inside a collecting loop propagates like the statement form
  (former draft B9).

---

## B1 — List concatenation with `+`
- Spelling: `a + b` where `a: [T]`, `b: [T]` → new `[T]`; operands unchanged (read, not moved).
- Semantics: eager copy of `a` then `b`. `View<T>` operands are E0108 (write `.copy()`); maps and
  sets keep their own operators (none). No new token: `+` widens its operand set, which is
  language surface, so it needs ratification.
- Beginner path: `all: header + rows`. Expert path: `xs.extend(ys)` (in place, no copy).
- Alternatives: (a) `xs.concat(ys)` method only; (b) status quo
  `out := xs.copy(); loop y in ys -> out.push(y)`.
- Before (Lifecycle.jet:62): `text: "{HEADER.join("\n")}\n{(loop row in rows -> "{row}\n").join("")}"`
  After: `text: "{(HEADER + rows).join("\n")}\n"`.
- Before (LexerKeywordRows, 2 sites): `values := m.get(k) ?? [String]{}` / `values.push(v)` /
  `m[k] = values` — After: `m[k] = (m.get(k) ?? [String]{}) + [v]`.
- Saving: −4 lines in LexerKeywordRows, −0 lines/−9 tokens in Lifecycle [INFERENCE].
- Trade-off: `+` hides an O(n) copy; the L0501 copy-in-loop lint covers the hot case.

## B2 — Compound update of a list slot (`xs[i] += n`)
- Spelling: `xs[i] op= v` for `xs: [T]` (mutable binding), `i: Int`, every compound operator that
  exists for `T`.
- Semantics: one bounds check, then read-modify-write of the slot; an out-of-range index stops
  before any write, so no partial update exists. Maps keep E0164 (a missing key has no value
  to update); maps get no sugar in this ballot.
- Today: E0164 "Compound assignment can't target an indexed slot".
- Before (TestShards.jet:44): `loads[lightest] = loads[lightest] + row.weight`
  After: `loads[lightest] += row.weight`.
- Saving: 0 lines, −2 tokens per site.
- Alternative: keep E0164 (explicit total update).

## B3 — `String.find` / `rfind` return a character index as `Int?`
- Spelling (changed signature, same names): `s.find(needle) -> Int?`, `s.rfind(needle) -> Int?`.
- Semantics: the character (Unicode scalar) index of the first/last match, `None` when absent, so
  it composes with `slice`, `len` and `regex.Match.start/end`, which already count characters.
  Byte search stays available as `s.bytes().index_of_seq(n.bytes())`.
- Today: `find` returns a UTF-8 byte offset (Core/Text/String.jet:83) and `-1` when absent;
  `"héllo // c".slice(0, "héllo // c".find("//"))` prints `héllo /` (probe r1.jet).
- Before (LexerKeywordRows literal port): `at: line.find("//")` +
  `code: if at < 0 -> line else -> byte_slice(line, 0, at)` plus a `byte_slice` helper.
  After: `code: line.slice(0, line.find("//") ?? line.len())`.
- Saving: the byte-helper family in every text port (PortReview counted 103 lines across ports;
  −1 line per site [INFERENCE]).
- Changes a ratified API: one cutover migrating every caller.
- Alternatives: (a) keep bytes, add `slice_bytes(a, b)`; (b) only document `split_once`.

## B4 — Ambient `write(text)` (stdout without a newline)
- Spelling: `write(text: String)` in the readable prelude, beside `print`/`eprint`.
- Semantics: writes `text` to stdout unchanged (no newline), same `IO` effect and flush rules
  as `print`; `#NoPrelude` hides it like `print`.
- Today: `print` always appends `\n`; raw text needs `out := term.stdout()` +
  `out.write(text).drop("...")`; `term.stdout().write(t)` is E0111 (a plain call cannot change a temporary).
- Before (Lifecycle.jet:64-66): `else if args[0] == "--print" {` / `out := term.stdout()` /
  `out.write(text).drop("lifecycle text")` / `}` — After: `else if args[0] == "--print" -> write(text)`.
- Saving: −3 lines in Lifecycle, and its `use core.term` line once B4 lands (−1).
- Alternatives: `print(text, end: "")` (labelled argument on an existing builtin); allow `&` on a
  temporary handle for one call.

## B5 — Script entry without `fn run()` (top-level statements)
- Spelling: a loose file (or `#!` script) with no `fn run` may contain statements at top level.
- Semantics: those statements, in order, are the body of an implicit fallible `fn run()`;
  `fn`, `struct`, constants and `use` stay items; a file that has `fn run` and top-level
  statements is an error. Authority and package rules are unchanged.
- Today: "Ordinary files execute only their explicit `fn run` body" (Examples/features/script_mode).
- Before: `fn run() {` … `}` (2 lines + one indent level). After: the body alone.
- Saving: −2 lines per script (TestShards, WebBundleCheck, Lifecycle, LexerKeywordRows: −8).
- Trade-off: two entry shapes (I8), mitigated because the implicit form desugars to exactly
  `fn run()`. Coordinate with lane ScriptMode (`#!`, `-A`).

## B6 — `fail(message, code)` for expected failures
- Spelling: `fail(message: String, code: Int{1}) -> Never` in the readable prelude.
- Semantics: writes `message` and a newline to stderr, runs scope guards, exits with `code`.
  Unlike `panic` (program bugs, E3001 frame) it prints no frame.
- Before (all four rewrites): `fn fail(message: String) -> Never {` / `term.eprint(message)` /
  `process.exit(1)` / `}` (TestShards names it `usage` with code 64).
- After: `fail("...")` / `fail("...", 64)` at the call sites; no helper.
- Saving: −4 lines per script (−16 over the four), and `use core.process` where only `exit`
  used it.
- Alternative: `#Error struct` + `return Err(...)` from `run()` (exists; prints a framed report).

## B7 — Named regex groups on `Match`
- Spelling: `m.named(name: String) -> String?` on `core.regex.Match`.
- Semantics: the text of the named group `(?<name>…)` in this match; `None` when the group did
  not participate or the name is not in the pattern (the pattern is known: a `Regex{…}` literal
  makes an unknown name a compile error).
- Today: groups are positional (`m.groups[2]`); named groups parse but have no accessor on the
  source engine path.
- Before (Lifecycle.jet:45-49): `kind: m.groups[0]`, `name: m.groups[2]`,
  `m.groups[3].trim()`. After: `m.named("kind") ?? ""`, `m.named("name") ?? ""`, …
- Saving: 0 lines; removes index bookkeeping (readability only).

## B8 — `files.is_executable(path)`
- Spelling: `files.is_executable(path: String | Path) -[FS]> Bool` in `core.files`.
- Semantics: true when `path` names a regular file the current process may execute; `false` for
  a failed probe, like `is_file`.
- Before (WebBundleCheck.jet:39): `if (process.cmd(["test", "-x", "{root}/{JET_ENV}"]).run() ?? fail(...)).code != 0 -> fail(...)`
  After: `if !files.is_executable("{root}/{JET_ENV}") -> fail(...)`.
- Saving: 0 lines, −8 tokens, and no `Exec` authority for the probe.

## B9 — `Path.script_dir()`
- Spelling: `Path.script_dir() -> Path` (static on the prelude `Path`).
- Semantics: the directory of the entry source file of the running program (the file `jet run`
  was given), canonicalized; for a built binary, the directory recorded at build time.
- Today every ported tool assumes cwd = repository root; the originals computed it from
  `import.meta.url` / `BASH_SOURCE`.
- Before: `root: files.cwd()` (wrong when run from elsewhere).
  After: `root: Path.script_dir().join("../..")`.
- Saving: 0 lines; fixes a behavior difference from the originals.
- Trade-off: one more ambient read of the entry path; must be defined for `jet build` output.

## B10 — Lint: constant `re.compile("…")` should be a `Regex{…}` literal
- Spelling: new lint code (next free L-code) "this pattern is a constant; write `Regex{…}`",
  with an auto-fix that rewrites the call and un-escapes backslashes.
- Semantics: fires on `re.compile(<string literal>)` / `compile_with(<literal>, flags)` with no
  interpolation; the literal is compile-checked and needs no `?? panic`.
- Evidence: the four ports re-implemented 873 lines of scanners (PortReview) and no port used a
  `Regex{}` literal; rewrites with literals were 0.7–1.1× the originals.
- Saving: per site, −1 `?? panic(...)` and doubled backslashes.
