cards.title: Build D-LINK-MODEL1=A: each linked part has its own linkage, shown by jet inspect
cards.body:
## Situation
Jet native programs are fully static Linux executables today: the runtime pack carries a private musl libc (used only for pthread, getaddrinfo DNS, and libm math) and no dynamic loader. The code already marks musl as interim (Compiler/JetRuntime/imports.list:10 "musl until glibc dynamic linking"; Thread.jet: "interim pthread imports die when musl leaves the pack"; raw clone/futex already written). D-JPK-VARIANT1=D ratified `runtime/libc` and `linkage` as native variant axes with context-derived defaults, but no decision says which default applies when.

The owner wants Jet-native raylib (#5086) that works out of the box. The GPU is only reachable through the vendor driver the user's OS ships (Linux: libGL/libEGL/libvulkan + libX11/libwayland-client, built against glibc; macOS: Metal/libSystem; Windows: d3d/opengl32/kernel32). Those must be loaded from the user's system at run time by the platform's own loader. A static musl process cannot load a glibc-built driver (the driver expects glibc's loader, TLS and allocator).

Other languages: C, C++, Rust, Jai link the platform libc dynamically by default (Jai: `#system_library "d3d11"`, OS loader, no custom loader). Go and Zig build fully static binaries with no libc for pure programs and switch to dynamic platform-libc linking when a program needs system libraries (cgo / linkSystemLibrary). macOS and Windows effectively require dynamic system libraries for every program.

## Same program under each option
```jet
// tool.jet (CLI)        // game.jet
fn run() {               fn run() {
    print("hi")              window := game.open(800, 600, "demo")
}                            ...
                         }
```

### A. Static by default, dynamic when the program needs OS libraries (recommended)
- tool.jet -> one static file, no libc (musl removed: Jet's own threads/DNS/math), runs on any Linux of the same architecture.
- game.jet -> dynamically linked against the platform libc (glibc on Linux), GPU/window drivers loaded by the OS loader. The compiler decides from what the program reaches (graphics/windowing Core APIs, `#Import(c)` of a system library); no annotation needed.
- Expert path: `jet build --linkage=static|dynamic` (the D-JPK-VARIANT1 axis) to force either; forcing static on a program that needs drivers is a diagnostic.
- macOS/Windows: always dynamic against system libraries (the platforms require it); static only on Linux.
- Trade-offs: two link modes to maintain and test (I9 parity runs both). Dynamic Linux builds inherit glibc version skew: build against an old-enough glibc baseline (as Go/Rust release builds do) so binaries run on older distros.
- Edge cases: a static program that later adds graphics silently becomes dynamic (shown in `jet build` output and `jet inspect`); plugin hosts (#5087) stay static (the WASM interpreter needs no OS library).

### B. Always dynamic (C/Rust/Jai model)
- Both programs link the platform libc dynamically. One mode, simplest mental model, drivers always reachable.
- Trade-offs: no "copy one file to any Linux box" for CLI tools and servers (glibc skew; containers need a libc); slightly slower start; musl still leaves.

### C. Always static, with a Jet-written loader for driver libraries
- Listed for completeness, not recommended: vendor GPU drivers (Mesa, NVIDIA) are glibc-built and depend on glibc loader internals and TLS; a custom loader in a non-glibc process would have to reimplement glibc's ABI. Impractical and fragile.

### D. Keep today's model (static musl, no graphics without dlopen)
- Raylib stays headless-only natively; contradicts the owner direction in #5086.

## Related owner directions (2026-10-21)
- HarfBuzz is removed: core.font shapes with Jet's own shaper only (correct for Latin/Cyrillic/Greek; complex scripts wrong until a Jet-native OpenType GSUB/GPOS shaper exists - Rust's rustybuzz and Go's go-text are pure-language precedents).
- musl leaves the runtime in every option (Jet-owned threads, DNS resolver, math).

log.text: Board burndown 2026-10-22: the open decision in this card is drafted as owner ballot D-LINK-MODEL1 (draft for Main to file). The card text is background, not the decision.

Owner amendment (2026-10-21): linkage is decided PER LINKED ITEM, not only per program, and is controllable in the package's fn build settings. Each linked item (Jet runtime and libc, a system library such as libGL or libX11, a bundled C library, a foreign closure) carries its own linkage (static or dynamic); option A's rule supplies each item's default (pure Jet and bundled C sources static; OS driver and system libraries dynamic, which makes the executable dynamically linked against the platform libc). The build function can override linkage per item (and the CLI flag --linkage stays the whole-program expert override). A request that cannot work (static linkage for a system driver library, static libc on macOS/Windows) is a diagnostic. To ballot before implementation: the exact build-settings spelling, the per-item defaults table, and how jet inspect reports the resulting linkage per item.

Owner selected option A (2026-10-21): static by default, dynamic when needed. CLI tools, servers and scripts build as one static file with no libc (musl leaves the runtime: Jet-owned threads via raw clone/futex, DNS resolver, math). Programs that reach graphics/windowing Core APIs or import a system C library build dynamically linked against the platform libc (glibc on Linux, with an old-enough baseline for portability) so OS drivers load through the platform loader; macOS/Windows always link system libraries dynamically. Expert override: jet build --linkage=static|dynamic (the D-JPK-VARIANT1 linkage axis); forcing static on a program that needs drivers is a diagnostic. Also owner directions: HarfBuzz removed (core.font shapes with Jet's own shaper; a Jet-native OpenType shaper is the later path), Jet-native raylib (#5086), WASM-interpreter plugins after D-ARCH-IR1 (#5087).

criteria.text: D-LINK-MODEL1=A: each linked part has its own linkage (pure Jet and bundled C static; OS drivers and system libraries dynamic), `fn build` can change any part, and `jet inspect` lists each part with its linkage and source.
The declared native package and module closure feeds linker inputs and missing-library errors, including the canonical z package key for -lz, proven by link execution on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Web target on JetIR: a new IR to JS/Wasm backend (A4)
cards.body: The Jet compiler has no live web path: no Jet CLI route constructs JetDriverCompileTarget.Web; web builds today run only through the Rust driver (crates/jet-driver MIRWeb emitter) and Bootstrap/Host/Native.rs, emitting MIR to JS (JetCodegen Emit/Web, 167 functions over 7 files) and MIR to Rust source to rustc for the Wasm bucket. JetIR/JetBackend have no JS or Wasm emitter. A6 S4b deletes Emit/Web with the MIR pipeline, and R7a deletes the Rust driver, so the 113 --target web cases stop running until this lands. Scope: an IR to JS backend (or IR to Wasm replacing rustc), move the JS/Wasm partition facts (web_marker/bucket, on MIR functions today) to checked facts or IR, keep the JS preludes (DOM, game, harfbuzz, timezone). I9: web must carry the same meaning as native. Acceptance: the --target web examples and UI cases pass on the Jet CLI.

cards.title: Supply-chain security: exact advisory matching, targeted grafts, capability diff on update, verified reproducibility and a declarative audit trail
cards.body: Jetpack knows every input a package is built from (lock and closure). Match security advisories against that exact graph, down to the version and build options, so "am I affected?" is an exact query instead of a guess, and the security lane knows exactly what to update.

log.text: Owner order 2026-11-22: JetOS is removed from the project entirely.
Board cleanup: one stream; #5458, #5459, #5460 and #5462 merged here, every criterion tagged (was #N cK).

criteria.text: jetpack answers "is this package affected by advisory X?" from the exact lock and closure, down to version and build options. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Advisory/exact_match_affected_and_unaffected` on a fixture graph with one affected and one unaffected path.

Whether grafts are allowed is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15); if they are, a graft is recorded in the declaration, applied without rebuilding dependents, and reconciled by the next full build. Proof: `tower decision show <id>` ratified, then `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Graft/recorded_applied_reconciled`.

Updating a dependency whose new version adds an effect (for example Net.Connect) or a `#Unsafe` block reports each widened effect with the dependency function that needs it, at update time and on the next run (D-AUTH-DEFAULT1=A); `--locked` refuses the update with a registered error, and a written authority row is a ceiling. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter CapabilityDiff/widened_effect_on_update` against a fixture registry.

Two independent builds of each published package from the same inputs are bit-identical, checked by the release gate, and each build attestation is appended to a transparency log anchored at the trust root, so a silently re-published package is detected.
An imperative change to a package writes back into its declaration, and drift from the last good state is reported.

The final generated security report and its canonical evidence are committed, and the report lists exactly the 134 original candidate IDs, each with one final disposition. Proof: the committed report under Docs/Audits/security-final-<date>/, with a count of 134 unique IDs and 134 dispositions.

The security-scan procedure is a committed Jet tool under Tools/ (the deleted scripts/agent/security-scan.mjs is not restored, by the greenfield rule), and its finalize step at the integration HEAD exits 0 with zero unresolved reportable findings, zero deferred items and zero open questions, and publishes Docs/Audits/security-final-<date>/. Proof: the tool's finalize run on a clean checkout, recorded in the report's gate section.

Each release ships a compliance bundle: an SBOM, SLSA provenance and an air-gap install runbook, generated by the release gate. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter release_compliance_bundle` and the bundle files in the release receipt.

Reached-code diffs on update (owner-approved greenfield proposal item P28, 2026-11-25): a dependency update lists every changed function the project can reach, with its source diff and the call path that reaches it, beside the capability diff. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Tests/Cases/JetpackEngine/update_lists_reached_changed_functions_with_call_paths`.

cards.title: Compile speed: 30M lines per second, with per-phase lines/s budgets
cards.body: Owner asked 2026-10-23 for the theoretical maximum compiler speed. Self-compile input: Compiler+Core non-test = 1,263 files, 576k lines, 38.9 MB; output ~55-63 MB. Today about 30 s wall / ~120-150 CPU-s (about 90,000 cycles per token). Reference per-core targets (Carbon toolchain goals): lex+parse 10M lines/s, semantic analysis 1M lines/s; direct x64 emission (no LLVM) can plausibly match about 1M lines/s at O0. Applied: about 1.2 s single-core, about 80-100 ms on 16 cores with near-linear sema/codegen scaling, plus output write/fault cost. Physical floor (memory bandwidth plus a few hundred cycles per token end to end) is tens of ms on 16 cores. Levers: data-oriented compiler data (index-based SoA IR, arenas, no per-node RC or atomics), interned symbols (no string_compare), hashed maps, parallel sema/codegen per function, SIMD lexing, direct emission without a link step, huge pages for output. Work: add per-phase lines/s to the trace report; set phase budgets; card each gap.
cards.plan:
Owner-ordered speed program (owner 2026-11-12). This plan is the one ordered home for compile speed, run speed and the related size work. Work runs in this order. A step starts when its predecessor's criteria land, except where a track is marked parallel. Every step's proof is in its criteria.

Step 0. Measure and guard (prerequisite, small).
- #5479 c1: a throughput cell for a million-line corpus.
- #5479 c5: the train speed gate (+10% fails).
- #5479 c2: per-phase lines/s budgets that add up to 30M.

Step 1. Cut the work. This is the top priority now: 1a, then 1b.
- 1a, #6328 c22: checked Core and Prelude ship precompiled inside the jet binary. The owner ruled this part of the toolchain, not a compile cache (2026-11-08, restated 2026-11-12: option B of the exec-tiers comparison). Owner: G11Speed-4. It follows Docs/proposals/precompiled-libraries-2026-11-05.md section 8 and uses the RecordCodec format (auto-derived Encode/CBOR, no hand-written codec). Slices, each its own SUB:
  S1. check Core and Prelude alone as one closed graph; `jet devtools core-record --check` reports counts; a Core read of a per-program fact is refused.
  S2. a census in Docs/audits of every sema and IR read of Core AST or registration state while handling user code; it fixes what the record holds.
  S3. the jet.core/v1 writer and reader (header with compiler identity, target and Core digest; modules; decl and registration rows; comptime values; checked bodies; the AST S2 names). A round-trip test; two builds give identical bytes.
  S4. a core-record step in Compiler/build.jet, embedded in the jet binary, with no file I/O per compile.
  S5. the cutover: the loader and sema seed every <corelib>/ module from the record, lazily per item. The Core parse and the demand-driven Core body check go in the same change, with no flag and no fallback path. The D-CORE-LAYERS1 impl-reach rule (1b S1) stays, and is applied to the record's impl rows.
  S6. comptime and IR read Core constants and bodies from the record.
  S7. Core machine code at O0, O1 and O2 is built with jet and linked by reach.
  S8. proof: goldens, ui and cases byte-identical before and after; PortBars and #6759 c9 timings before and after; strace -c of hello.
  Known risk, measured in S1: near-name suggestions and errors in Core code no program reaches can differ.
- 1b, #6759 c10 (moved from #6281 c162): D-CORE-LAYERS1=A. Owner: G11Speed-4, after 1a (slice plan written by G6Meta-4). Slices, each its own SUB:
  S1. the reach rule: a Core trait impl is a lazy row, reached only when its type and its trait are both reached (compiler-implied traits such as Display, Equatable and Comparable count as reached). It is written as one function over impl rows (type module, trait module) that CoreReach calls today and the 1a S5 record loader calls after the cutover. Proof: the c03 probe (core.time zoned+now: 33 units, 113 MB, 0.55 s on seed-b13, pulled in through ZonedDateTime's impl Decode) before and after, plus decode and display cases.
  S2. the layer table in Core/package.jet, and a registered sema error for an upward core.<area> name under `jet check Core`, with a ui snapshot.
  S3-S5. Core moves that remove the 67 upward references in 12 pairs (census at 4bb64588): encoding to files 27, crypto to files 20, data to db 6, net to http 3, data to files/sys 2+2, encoding to archive 2, and one each of crypto to tasks, encoding to db, meta to compiler, rt to time and sync to text. Git and Target get layer rows. `jet check Core` is clean.
  S6. the proof SUB with traces.
- 1c, #6759 c1, c5, c2, c4 and c9: one comptime child per compile, and load, finalize and memory proportional to the code reached. Then #6759 c8 and c3, and #6527 c10: the PortBars speed bar for cold tool twins.

Step 2. Use the machine.
- #5479 c6: modules stream through the pipeline, comptime runs in parallel, at least 24 of 32 threads busy.
- #6328 c23: small programs compile on the calling thread.

Step 3. Data-oriented core.
- #5479 c7: interned u32 ids, flat columns, per-phase arenas.
- #5910: self-compile under 1 GB, with no per-node heap allocation or RC.

Step 4. Fused per-function pipeline and a direct executable image writer (#5479 c8).

Step 5. Front-end primitives and budgets.
- #5910 c6: a SIMD lexer at 1 ns/byte or less.
- Every phase within its #5479 c2 budget, each overrun with a named root.

Staffing (owner 2026-11-12 evening: "do steps 0-5 right now with 1-2 agents"; G6, which ranks above this program, keeps G6Meta-4): steps 0-5 run now with one agent, G11Speed-4. Order: step 0, 1a, 1b (G6Meta-4 handed over its S1-S6 slice plan and the 67-reference census), 1c, then steps 2, 3, 4 and 5. When a probe wait blocks one item, the agent writes the next independent slice.

Step 6. The compiler compiled well (#5479 c9). Not now: it starts only once the language is mostly stable.

Exit: #5479 c3, `jet build` of the million-line corpus at 30M lines/s or faster, with identical output.

Not in this program (owner 2026-11-12 evening): "finish the rest of the goals before we try to get to perfect codegen." Run speed against the hand-written machine-code ceiling is hill-climbing work under G13 and starts after the other goals are done: #6414 (kernel catalog and gaps; measured gaps 3.7x-244x cycles, binparse 12.5x, Doom kernels 2.5x-8.6x) and #6461 (ceiling references). Binary size (#6328 c2-c6 and c25-c30) stays in G11 and is not part of steps 0-5.

Ruled out by owner rulings: an interpreter or JIT tier (D-EXEC2=A stands; jet run stays native O0); incremental compilation; and any cross-run cache. Precompiled Core is toolchain, not cache.

Owner direction 2026-10-23: every improvement that takes the compiler to 30M lines/s must also be applied to codegen, so all code Jet generates is as fast as physically possible without taking control from experts. Rule for the throughput work: each slice is tagged GENERAL (a runtime, codegen or Core mechanism any Jet program gets automatically) or COMPILER-ONLY (a data-structure choice inside the compiler). Prefer GENERAL: implement it once in codegen/runtime/Core and let the compiler benefit as an ordinary Jet program (I8 one mechanism). Examples: non-atomic RC unless shared (#5475), frozen immortal constants (mapfreeze), no reclamation at process end (#5478), escape-proven bump/arena placement (Goose lesson), small-Int fast paths, tag compare (#5473), Shared/queue primitives without futex waits on hot paths, the work-stealing task scheduler, hashed Map instead of binary search (#5474), COW uniqueness at every place (#5480). COMPILER-ONLY wins (interned ids, SoA AST/IR) are each followed by a ticket asking how codegen or Core can give user programs the same (for example Columns<T>/SoA layout, an interned Symbol type, or arenas via escape analysis). Experts keep control via the existing explicit surfaces (layout attributes, #Region, #Unsafe, explicit allocators); defaults stay safe.

Owner clarification 2026-10-23: the goal is that 32 hardware threads beat 16 where the workload allows, not just an explanation of why 32 loses. Pareto v1 (RustOut, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/RustOut/tp/pareto.md): stages S0 28 s → S1 ~10 s (contention/wait-free) → S2 ~2 s (interned ids, cheap RC, arenas, RSS 9.8→2 GB) → S3 ~0.5 s (flat SoA compiler data) → S4 ~50 ms (fused per-function pipeline, direct image writer) → S5 ~20 ms (30M lines/s). Measured 6→12 threads in a 12-CPU slot: instructions +1.6%, cycles +21% (IPC 3.18→2.67), futex ×3.4, EAGAIN ×6.8, contention in ir.x64/ir.opt/sema.check/comptime (Shared guard claims, allocator locks). v2 adds an SMT-positive track with per-stage acceptance (32 threads ≥15–25% over 16) and a full-machine 16/32 A/B.

criteria.text: Plan step 1, use the machine: average parallelism goes from about 5 to at least 24 of 32 threads. Modules stream through the pipeline as soon as their dependencies are checked (no phase-wide barriers), comptime runs in parallel, work queues are wait-free, and the allocator keeps per-thread arenas so threads take no global lock. 32 threads beat 16. Gate: at least 400K lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens). Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median).

Plan step 2, data-oriented core: every compiler name, symbol, type and function is an interned u32 id (no String keys in maps). AST, types and IR are flat struct-of-arrays columns, compiler data lives in per-phase arenas freed in bulk, and compiler data carries no reference counts. Peak RSS falls under 1 GB (#5910). Gate: at most 5 µs of CPU per line and at least 5M lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens). Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median).

Plan step 3, fused per-function pipeline: each function goes parse -> check -> lower -> select -> encode while its data is still in cache, with no whole-program intermediate copy, and a direct executable image writer replaces the object-then-link path. Gate: at most 1.5 µs of CPU per line and at least 20M lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. criteria.text: Plan step 4, the compiler compiled well. Starts only once the language is mostly stable (the major syntax, semantics and Core churn is done), so tuning isn't wiped out by later cutovers: Jet's own release code generation (register allocation, inlining, bounds-check hoisting, SIMD selection) and a SIMD lexer at 1 GB/s or more close the gap to hand-written machine code on the compiler's five hottest loops, each with an asm-parity ceiling cell (Tools/Perf/AsmParity). x64 instruction selection is linear in a function's forward jumps: at dev ba5711569a (2026-11-21), ir_x64_end (Compiler/JetIR X64Select.jet, lines 3916-3927) scans every pending forward jump at each block end, so a function of deeply nested branches spends quadratic time in the ir.x64 phase. Measured with the gate-p413 compiler on generated bodies (by Ballots3 for D-PLUGIN-ENGINE1): ir.x64 took 2.56 s at 25,000 nested levels and 10.74 s at 50,000 with branches, against 0.23-0.30 s at 50,000 for the other shapes, and a ~1 MiB body took 21.5 s at O0 and 22.0 s at O2. Each block keeps its own pending jumps (or the pending set is indexed by target), so the phase is linear. Proof: the same generated nested-branch bodies at 25,000 and 50,000 levels take ir.x64 time within 2.2x of each other (linear), and a second program with many small functions shows no ir.x64 regression.

cards.title: New GPU and accelerator support arrives as a library: a public device-provider interface
cards.body:
Jet should run fast on any chip, including chips that do not exist yet. Today each GPU family Jet knows (CUDA, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU) is wired into Core, so supporting a new accelerator means changing Jet itself. Mojo shows the better model: a hardware vendor ships a library that teaches the language a new device. This card makes Jet work that way.

Owner direction 2026-10-28: replaces the audit's "restore AI/ML / re-scope #3955" proposal. The shape is ballot D-ACCEL-LIB1, hosted here.

Builds on ratified decisions: D-CORE-BOUNDARY1=A (CPU chip instructions are Core library entries, #4565), D-HOST-CAPS1=A (packages add hardware kinds, #4195), D-GPU-PACKAGING1=A, D-COMPUTE1=D and D-COMPUTE-BACKEND1=D (Core owns the compute contract with a CPU reference). Related: #3026, #3028, #4731, #4762, #3955.

log.text: Frozen by owner direction (2026-11-01): cross-platform work is frozen for now. Remaining criteria need CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, Android and iOS device providers.

Merged #3028 "GPU provider matrix and actual cross-target dispatch" into this card (GPU and accelerator providers as a library); its 14 open item(s) are carried as "(was #3028)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T25: KernelIR + DeviceProvider proposal (D-KERNELIR1 and its epic card) folded here by owner direction; no separate ballot or card. Four layers, no MLIR: typed device facts (D-HOST-CAPS1) replace the string devices in Core/Compute/Solve.jet:83-84; #Kernel stays the restricted subset with a CPU reference (D-COMPUTE-KERNEL-SURFACE1=B); a provider implements caps, lower, load, launch, alloc and copy over a public, versioned kernel IR; Core.Compute tensors, autodiff and tiles target that interface. First providers are mined from the Rust-era backends #1144-#1146. Shader stages (#3027) use the same interface.

criteria.text: A package outside Core adds a test accelerator (a provider that runs kernels on the CPU through the provider interface) with no compiler or Core change; device selection finds it from the package's hardware description and runs the CPU-reference conformance suite against it.
The existing CUDA, Vulkan, Metal and WebGPU providers use the same public interface; no provider uses a private path.
A provider that fails the conformance suite is refused at selection with a named failure and is never used silently.

core.compute selects a device by a typed `Device` value built from the hardware description; the string device names in Core/Compute/Solve.jet are gone, and an unknown device kind is a compile error with a registered UI snapshot.

Providers lower from one public, versioned kernel IR (a subset of the compiler IR; no MLIR dependency); `jet inspect` prints a kernel's IR and its version, and a provider that declares an unsupported IR version is refused at selection with a named error (test).

The CUDA, Metal and Vulkan/WebGPU providers are ported from the Rust-era backends of #1144-#1146 (code mined, not re-authored) and pass the CPU-reference conformance suite where the device exists; without the device, selection reports unavailable and never falls back silently.

(was #3028) The existing provider family runs authored compute and graphics across all required Linux/Windows/macOS/browser/Android/iOS routes without adding HIP or a second public API merely for vendor coverage.

(was #3028) Supported NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple and Android mobile GPU routes have actual device execution/readback or presentation evidence. Every required platform has a successful supported route; hardware absence does not count as completion.

(was #3028) CUDA is correctly compute-only; Vulkan, Metal and browser WebGPU carry the matching graphics routes. Receipts identify the actual provider/device/program/profile rather than a generic GPU label.

(was #3028) All adapters consume the same checked program, resource and numeric facts. F32Strict/Reproducible compute and the graphics contract agree with their references across applicable execution tiers.

(was #3028) Loader/capability absence, unsupported precision/format, device loss, queue/allocation failure and invalid lifetime produce bounded typed failures. No implicit CPU/headless replacement or fabricated success occurs.
(was #3028) Existing Tensor .Auto, provider-issued unsafe contracts, system-loader trust, backend lifetimes and I6 dependency boundaries remain intact.

(was #3028) The canonical matrix records exact applicability, source/binary/device identity and focused results. Unsupported but required cells remain open; later broad campaign proof does not replace this card's complete matrix.

(was #3028) [#3207] A 16-op chain on resident F32 input reports exactly one allocation, upload and readback (compute_residency test). There is no hidden f64 roundtrip. Kernel-only and end-to-end timing are reported separately.

cards.title: Lockfile: committed, machine-independent, and outside the disposable `.jet/` folder
cards.body:
A lock file pins the exact dependency versions so every machine builds the same thing. Today the lock lives in `.jet/lock`, which `jet new` tells git to ignore, and it stores a build timestamp, so it would churn on every commit. This card makes the lock reproducible and places it where ballot D-LOCKFILE1 (hosted here) decides.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-02, LAY-06): generated .gitignore = `.jet/build/ .jet/lock .jet/cache/` (Host.jet:1478); `[build.stamp]` in the lock. Related: D-LOCK1 (spec), D-GENERATED-STORAGE2=B, #3421.

log.text: c1 checked on dev b66642b8bc: the jet_new cases pass (9 of 9 in the a0.0.046 admit run), but Tests/Cases/Pkg/cli_jet_new_creates_project_structure.case still asserts myapp/.jet/lock, and D-LOCKFILE1=A puts the lock at <root>/jet.lock with a one-line .gitignore of .jet/. Not met: jet new and the case still use the old place.
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 2 criteria from archived #2218: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: `jet new` writes the lock where D-LOCKFILE1=A puts it, plus the .gitignore it specifies. Proof: a jet new case (`jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jet_new`).
The lock holds no per-machine state: building the same project on two machines gives byte-identical locks, and build stamps live under `.jet/build/`.
The spec lists every `.jet/` subpath and whether it is disposable, and files meant to be committed live outside `.jet/`.
A lock change prints a changelog-shaped diff with version moves, added and removed counts and the net size change, and `jetpack lock diff` shows the same on demand.

A channel dependency update writes the exact lock and a build then uses it offline, a channel build with no lock is E1271, and `jetpack outdated` lists channel refs with newer releases. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackEngine/channel_update_writes_exact_lock_and_build_uses_it_offline` and `--filter jetpack_engine/channel_build_without_lock_is_e1271`.

A clean prepared environment runs a script with its recorded dependency and source hashes, missing or changed material is an error with no registry fallback, and lifting the script into a package keeps its dependency identity.

cards.title: Tables for data analysis: a dataframe type over Arrow column batches
cards.body:
Destination: Core ships a lazy table type over the shared Arrow column batches (D-DATA-FRAME1=A, ratified 2026-10-28: dataframe in Core): read a CSV into a frame, filter, group, join, sort and select by column name with compile-time column and unit checks, through the shared compute operations, and show and plot frames in `jet notebook` with no package install.

Why it matters: data analysts expect a dataframe; Jet has none.

Decisions: D-DATA-FRAME1=A, D-COMPUTE1=D (frames integrate through the compute operation family), D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1, D-DATA-READER1 (scan into column batches).

Evidence: audit 2026-10-28, DOMAIN gaps.

cards.title: One manifest per project: fold env.jet and workspace.jet into package.jet sections
cards.body:
A manifest is the file that describes a project. Jet projects can carry package.jet, env.jet and workspace.jet, and a user must learn which setting goes where. Removing the legacy pkg.jet is already decided (D-JPK-LEGACY1=A, #5075). Whether the remaining files become sections of package.jet is ballot D-MANIFEST-ONE1, hosted here.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-05). Related: D-CONF-NAME1 (members live in package.jet).

log.text: Test finding (DeclTypes-3, w22-wave cases, q/sg/cases-w22-wave.txt): 3 env_hook cases FAIL with 'capture prefix line missing': export_changed_definition, export_failed_reload and export_unchanged_directory. A 'module env.dev {prompt}' counts as a typed env (EnvironmentHash.jet:115, environment_names > 0), so an untrusted non-tty export prints 'env.jet here is not trusted' and emits no JETPACK_ENV_HASH line. Whether a prompt-only env needs trust is a trust-law question for this manifest card, not a small fix. The other 16 env_hook rows pass once a jetpack binary is present.

Merged #5980 "Map: Package model: workspaces, lockfile, one manifest, environments" into this card (one manifest per project and the package model); its 1 open item(s) are carried as "(was #5980)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

D-MANIFEST-ONE1: FutureAudit 2026-10-28 (FUTURE.md "Votes on audit ballots", T22): a `commands:` section of the one manifest also answers the Make and just task-runner pains (Make.5); no separate task-runner ballot.

criteria.text: D-MANIFEST-ONE1=A: a project with environments and workspace members has only package.jet at its root, env.jet and workspace.jet are no longer read, and every in-repo project is migrated in one cutover. Proof: `git ls-files '*env.jet' '*workspace.jet'` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Manifest/one_file_members_environments`.
Package dependencies imply a prepared environment (D-DEPS-ENV1=A): each battery example compiles after `jet env --prep` with no env.jet.

Every remaining per-package or cwd-relative `.jet/` writer (build/deps, lock unless a ratified package-scoped lock, cache/api, cache/schema, codemods, game-*, jobs, state/jobs.db) writes to the one workspace root, and shared cache goes under ~/.cache.

After build, test and run inside each member of a three-member workspace, exactly one `.jet` directory exists, at the workspace root. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter ProjectRoot/workspace_has_one_state_dir` (counts with `find . -name .jet -type d`).

One function returns the project state directory (the workspace root, else the package root), and no other code joins a `.jet` path by hand. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter project_state_dir_single` over Compiler/, Core/ and Jetpack/.

Tracked fixture inputs that lived under nested `.jet` directories are migrated with their consumers, so no tracked file sits under a nested `.jet` and no canonical source silently disappears. Proof: `git ls-files '*/.jet/*'` lists only files under the workspace root `.jet`, and the consumers' cases pass.

cards.title: Scripts may read the file you name on the command line, and use a private temp folder, without a prompt
cards.body:
When you type `./wc.jet notes.txt`, you have already said which file the script may read. This card lets that act count as the permission: a `#CLI` field of type `Path` grants reading exactly the path you passed, and a private per-run temp folder (`files.temp_dir`) needs no prompt. Everything else still asks once, as owner ruling #5949 says. Ballot D-SCRIPT-DESIGNATE1, hosted here, decides; this card builds the winner.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T11 items 2 and 3 (the powerbox model: a file picker grants the file the user picked). Writes are not designated; they keep the #5949 prompt.

Related: #5949, D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1=A (#3705), spec.md "Command registry and typed inputs" (`Path` is a supported #CLI scalar), core-library.md `temp_dir`.

cards.title: Run-time checks for #Unsafe code and foreign edges: the hardened profile (D-MEM-HARDEN1=A) and every aliasing and undefined-behavior class, like Rust's Miri
cards.body:
Rust has Miri: a slow interpreter that catches memory mistakes the type checker missed, such as reading past a buffer inside unsafe code. Jet should have the same safety net. This card adds an opt-in checking run at O0 that tracks extra state for every value and stops with a named error on any aliasing, bounds, release, race or uninitialised-read mistake, including inside `#Unsafe` blocks and at foreign edges.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T06 ("new card for the O0 checking mode if #4726 does not cover it"; #4726 lists results, not a checker).

Related: #4309 (static IR ownership verifier, a compile-time check; this is its run-time partner), #4620 (memory model), #4726 (defined-behavior ledger), D-MEM-HARDEN1=A (shipping run-time checks for unsafe islands and foreign edges).

cards.title: `jet test` tries many task orders: seeded schedules over the replay recorder find races and deadlocks
cards.body:
A concurrency bug often appears only in one rare order of task steps, so a test passes a thousand times and fails in production. Rust needs extra tools (loom, shuttle) to search those orders. Jet already records task message and lock order for exact replay (D-REPLAY-ORDER1=A, built in the Rust era as #4252). This card lets `jet test` run a concurrent test under many seeded orders and print the seed of a failure, so it replays exactly.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T07 and T21. The Rust-era replay recorder is a capability row on the not-built census card and must be ported first.

Related: #3239 (task outcomes), #4637 (fair turns), #5468 (stop edges in tasks).

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15: D-TEST-SCHEDULES1=A is spelled out across c2, c3, c4 and c8, and c1 merged into c8.

criteria.text: A concurrent `#Test` can ask for schedule exploration with a run count (spelling recorded in Docs/spec); `jet test` runs it under that many seeded task orders and reports the result per seed.
criteria.evidence: Merged into #6012 c8: the run-count spelling and its recording in the spec are the D-TEST-SCHEDULES1=A spelling criterion

criteria.text: Under `reruns:`, each rerun picks a different task order at the pause points (task start or join, lock, channel send or receive, shared read or write, yield). A test with fewer possible orders than its count runs each order once, depth-first, and says `all N orders`, and reruns run in parallel on virtual time. A planted lost-update race and a planted lock-order deadlock each fail within the default count. The report prints the rerun, its order number, each step with its source line and the replay command, and a deadlock or suspected livelock names who holds what and who waits.
`jet test FILE "name" --seed=<n>` replays exactly the printed order through the replay recorder, reproducing the same failure three times in a row.

The `reruns:` spelling lands with its Data/Syntax registry row, a syntax-decisions.md log entry, editor grammars regenerated by `jet self devtools grammars` and re-blessed snapshots, and the deadlock text in spec.md (lines 2872-2888 on 2026-11-06) is updated.

D-TEST-SCHEDULES1=A spelling: `#Test("…", reruns: N)` takes a whole number N of at least 1, and a value below 1 is a registered compile error with a UI snapshot. `reruns:` in a TestProfile, `t.reruns(n)` in fn test and `--reruns=<n>` set it for a run, in that order, and change only tests that ask for reruns. A property test with `reruns:` is a compile error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter test_reruns_` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter TestSchedules/reruns_settings_order`.

D-REPLAY-ORDER1=A on the self-hosted toolchain: task message and lock order is recorded in .jetproof-replay at the scheduler, channel, lock and join boundaries, and a two-task race recorded under `jet run` replays identically under `jet run` and a built binary.

`jet run --record` is built, and the prim-receipts-G2 probe that found the defect passes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Prove/run_recorded_alias_time_receipt_replays_without_execution`. (was #6418 c115)

cards.title: Registry publish policy: short-lived identities instead of stored tokens, and a runnable example per public function
cards.body:
Two rules decide what it takes to publish a package. First, how the publisher proves who they are: in 2025 a worm spread through npm by stealing long-lived publish tokens, and trusted publishing replaces them with a short-lived identity from the CI job. Second, what a package must contain: pages with only type signatures leave users guessing, so each public function could be required to ship a tested example. Ballots D-TRUSTPUB1 and D-REGISTRY-EXAMPLE1, hosted here, decide; this card builds the winners.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T15 and T20. Already ratified and not reopened: the transparency log, TUF metadata and transactional publish (D-JPK-REGISTRY1=D), signing (D-PKGSIGN1), the trust root (#2199).

cards.title: Remote builds and shared cache work with existing build farms
cards.body:
Big teams speed up builds by running steps on a shared farm of machines and sharing a cache of results. Jet has ratified who may use a remote builder and how it is bound (D-JPK-REMOTE1=D: `build.remote` grants, `jet remote bind`), but not the wire protocol. Ballot D-REAPI1, hosted here, decides between the open protocol existing farms speak and a Jet-only one.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T22.

criteria.text: With a remote builder bound by `jet remote bind`, `jet build` runs actions on a stock Remote Execution API server and its cache through the farm adapter (D-REAPI1=A), and outputs are byte-identical to a local build. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter RemoteBuild/reapi_adapter_byte_identical` against a containerised server.
Remote use still needs the D-JPK-REMOTE1=D grants: a project can neither force remote execution nor name an endpoint.
Local and remote action identity, inputs, outputs, worker platform, sandbox, signatures, provenance, cache publication and the consumed build result mean the same.

Corrupt or mismatched entries, malicious workers, lost connections, cancellation, timeout, replay, partial upload and sandbox failure never become local truth or publish partial outputs. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter RemoteBuild/hostile_remote_`, one case per failure.

The remote scheduler picks a builder by capability and fails over in order, an ineligible builder falls back locally when allowed, and remote execution identity binds the complete action request (the Rust tests remote_scheduler_selects_capabilities_then_fails_over_in_order, remote_ineligible_builder_honors_local_fallback and remote_execution_identity_binds_the_complete_action_request).

cards.title: Infrastructure as typed Jet: a first-party package where the plan is a value tests can check
cards.body:
Teams describe servers, databases and networks in tools like Terraform, then apply that description to a cloud. Those tools have their own languages, keep secrets in a state file, and make plans hard to test. A first-party Jet package could describe infrastructure in typed Jet, with the plan as a value that tests assert on and apply running only under Net and Secret authority. Ballot D-INFRA1, hosted here, decides whether to build it and whether to reuse Terraform/OpenTofu providers.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T24. Sequenced after the HTTP client and server (audit card 3: #3665, #4957), hence `later`. Fleet and OS deployment are epoch e9 and out of scope.

The adversarial review (BallotReview2, GPT family; Docs/Audits/ballot-redesign-r5-review-2026-11-18.md, submitted as Main-audit-ballot-redesign-r3-r5) verdict is that it holds within stated limits. Its build work first proves every LIMIT row in the review's SERVICE-CURRENT1 table and closes the PREREQ rows (#3645 c14-c16, #6048 c9, #6923 c11) before support is claimed.

Parked 2026-11-18 (DeclTypes moved to #6841 by owner order). c2-2-fallout and c2-4a are in p288. c2-4b to d (38 non-handoff .worker( files, list in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/DeclTypes-6-1/c24b.list) are not started. The 26 handoff files and c2-4e wait on D-SERVICE-CURRENT1, which is being reworked.
Owner 2026-11-18: D-SERVICE-CURRENT1's recommended option is insufficient. It is being redesigned (no consumed message on Stale, no refresh/send race), then re-reviewed and reposted.

c2 cutover: re-resolving a typed endpoint after a handoff needs a public shape that no decision gives (27 cases do handoff_generation, directory_resolve, send, receive). Ballot D-SERVICE-CURRENT1 is being drafted: (A) tree.current(endpoint) at the current generation, (B) typed endpoints carry no generation, (C) shapes that add no new name. Meanwhile c2-4a (the tree ops take Endpoint) and the other case migrations go ahead; the 27 cases and the String-form deletion (c2-4e) wait for the ballot.

Main decision (c2, durable half; within D-SERVICE-WORKER1=A, which removes tree.receive, and D-SERVICE-DELIVERY1=D): durable receipts reach a typed worker by push. send_durable needs a message type that is Encode + Decode, and the authority log stores its JSON. The tree pushes the decoded pending receipts into the worker's mailbox at start(), on each send_durable and on retry. A handler that succeeds marks the receipt Delivered; one that fails leaves it Accepted for retry. The existing retry entry point keeps its current name and spelling, and only its effect changes (push instead of re-queue for receive), so no new public name is added. The ServicesRuntime fixtures are rewritten to observe through handlers.

Decision (Main, within D-SERVICE-IDENTITY1): directory resolution is tree.directory_resolve<T>(name) -> Endpoint<T>. Sema passes T identity as it already passes handler_name, and Core refuses a mismatch with the registered worker message type (ServiceError.Unknown). The ratified rule that directories hand out typed endpoints already covers this. cards.title: Mutation testing and coverage-guided fuzzing for jet test
cards.body: Split from #6035 by owner answer 2026-10-28 (Q4: own card). The best-in-class evaluation (Audit/drafts4/BEST-IN-CLASS.md) lists mutation testing (peers: cargo-mutants, Stryker, PIT) and coverage-guided fuzzing (peers: libFuzzer/cargo-fuzz, Go native fuzzing, AFL++) as axes where Jet's test system has nothing. Both should climb the same test ladder and use the one settings table, without a second mechanism. Ratified fuzz rows that the CLI refuses today (Front.jet:1023-1027) are built under #6035 S3; this card covers coverage guidance and mutation.

log.text: Moved from G1 to G15 (testing toolkit) by owner order 2026-11-06: G1 keeps only hand-off and durability.
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 4 criteria from archived #2343: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: An owner ballot fixes the surface for mutation testing and coverage-guided fuzzing on the test ladder.
criteria.evidence: D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1 A ratified by the owner 2026-10-30: both on by default; mutate: changed|all|off with stock changed; grade: generated is coverage-guided with a corpus under testdata/fuzz/<test>/.

criteria.text: Mutation testing and fuzzing each run on an example package with golden output, and their results are rows in the `jet test` report.

D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1=A mutation: `mutate` is a row of the one test settings table (`changed` by default, plus `all` and `off`). By default only functions whose IR changed are mutated. All mutants share one build (mutant schemata), each runs only the tests that reach it (last killer first), and the kill matrix is cached in the #6035 store.

D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1=A equivalent mutants: a mutant equal to the original after canonical-IR folding is dropped unrun. An effect-free survivor is proved equivalent by the solver, or reported with an input that tells it apart (fuzzing is the fallback), and an effectful survivor is reported as unchecked. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter mutate_survivor_outcomes`, one row per outcome.

D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1=A fuzzing: `grade: generated` steers generation by branch coverage and keeps new-branch inputs and shrunk failures under the corpus directory (testdata/fuzz/<test>/ by default), and later runs replay them as ordinary rows.

A reviewed must-kill catalog names one exact mutation and the layer expected to reject it for every critical silent-data seam class. Proof: the catalog is committed under Docs/testing, and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter must_kill_catalog` runs every entry.
The mutation score and survivor list come from the catalog and immutable result bundles, and a manual exemption, hidden skip or stale target commit fails the run.

A coverage-guided fuzz run of a parameterized #Test finds a planted crash in a parser fixture within its time budget and saves the crashing input as a regression case that later plain `jet test` runs replay.

Optional independent-condition coverage evidence uses witness pairs. Branch reports keep their meaning, short-circuiting is unchanged, and bitmask coverage never claims independent bits. Source versus object scope and the build and target identity are recorded, and release gates do not change.

jet test runs with a named profile, --set values and coverage compile and execute their assertions with no ICE in the generated status and history JSON parser, which uses the canonical Foundation JSON contract.

cards.title: Memory checks accept every safe program: no over-strict rejections
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: if a program is memory safe, Jet must accept it. Checks must be neither over-strict nor under-strict; only `#Unsafe` blocks opt out.

Known over-strict case: E0221 rejects a type that could form a strong loop at its declaration. It rejects a plain linked list (`next: Shared<Node>?`) and a tree with weak parent links and strong `kids` (probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/ballots2/probe/family2.jet). A strong loop can only close when a strong field of an existing shared value is written with a value that reaches it. Building by construction (prepend, a new child) never loops.

Scope: every memory, ownership, borrow, aliasing and resource diagnostic.

log.text: Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: respelled for D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A and D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A; the soundness rule is unchanged.

Merged #6200 "Over-safety audit: every hard error protects soundness, every restriction names its expert way out, and no sealed floors" into this card (memory and safety checks accept every safe program); its 3 open item(s) are carried as "(was #6200)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

Landed 6e013d30c9 (SmallGoals5-g7): immediately called lambda no longer reports E0217; UI row local_cell_guard_immediately_called_lambda_reads PASS. Partial; remaining items unchanged (E0204 nested call, E0212 payload window, E0219/E0220 blocked by #5677, linear-guard Fn lambda E0121).

2026-10-29 Main: landed 3a2f6b469d (SmallGoals5-g5): a non-escaping lambda may read a Cell guard (E0217 only for escaping lambdas). UI test _5 is rewritten to an escaping lambda, and a new test proves the non-escaping capture checks clean. C3 and C4 stay partial; the remaining items are in land/SmallGoals5-g5-cards.tsv.

criteria.text: A census of every memory, ownership, borrow, aliasing and resource diagnostic lists, for each, safe programs it rejects today (probe files with expected output) and unsafe programs it must keep rejecting. Proof: the census is committed under Docs/Audits, and each probe is a case: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter MemoryCensus/`.

E0221 fires only where a strong loop can actually close (a write of a strong field of an existing shared value whose new value can reach it), never at a type declaration; a strong linked list built by prepend and a weak-parent tree with strong kids compile and run on O0 and O1.
criteria.evidence: Landed cb59b8f072 (E0221 at the write site). On dev cb59b8f072 base jet: tests/ui/shared_weak_parent_tree.jet prints 'Ada has 2 kids' rc 0 under jet run, --optimize=none, --optimize=basic and the built binary; golden Examples/features/memory/shared_graph_building.jet (prepend list + weak-parent tree) PASS o0/o1/o2.

criteria.text: Every other over-strict rejection in the census is fixed in sema, or carded with a ballot if the fix needs new syntax; every unsafe probe still fails with its diagnostic. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter MemoryCensus/` passes, with every safe probe accepted and every unsafe probe refused with its code.

Each active error row in Compiler/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet carries a safety class (soundness: refusing it prevents a memory, type, aliasing or resource fault; or opinion: the program would run safely) and a one-line reason. A Jet tool generates a dated audit under Docs/Research from those fields, and its `--check` fails when an error row lacks a class. It may land in slices by code range. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter diagnostic_safety_class` passes with every active error row classified.

Every sealed floor (a soundness refusal that neither #Unsafe nor another ratified expert opt-in can lift) is listed with its code, its sema location (file:line) and the expert path to the same program, or "none" with the reason, in the audit c5 generates. Proof: the generated audit's sealed-floor section, reproduced by the c5 tool's `--check`.

Soundness U1 (Prep 2026-11-04, probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/c3836/s64.jet): an escaping lambda that captures a list window of a local that dies owns a materialized copy, so the probe prints 2000|true| on O0, O1 and O2 instead of reading freed memory. The fix is in IR: ir_lambda honors sema's materialized and cloned captures. Sema keeps accepting the program. A case pins it on every tier.
criteria.evidence: dev 7567ee4508 (G10Safe-lambda-owned-window, g10-fold2 cmds 39-44, all rc 0, on that fold jet): ir_lambda honors sema materialized and cloned captures. Case view_copy_semantics/an_escaping_lambda_owns_the_window_it_captures pins the probe on every tier, and the whole view_copy_semantics/, closures/ and core_and_closures/ filters plus CodegenCeiling --check pass.

criteria.text: Wrong result L1 (Prep 2026-11-04, probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/c3836/s36x.jet): writes inside a loop in a non-escaping lambda reach the captured variable, so the probe prints 3|6|3 on O0, O1 and O2 instead of 3|3|0. A case pins it on every tier.
criteria.evidence: dev c7d8c0291b (G10Safe-lambda-loop-write, g10-fold2 cmds 50-53, on that fold jet): case closures/a_lambda_write_inside_a_loop_or_branch_reaches_the_captured_variable gives PASS 1 (O0, O1 and O2). The whole closures/ filter gives PASS 40, FAIL 0, KNOWN-FAILING 2 (the existing #5454 rows). The ui effects/iterable_loop_charges_its_cursor_effects gives PASS 1, and the Ownership/Checks.jet check is rc 0.

criteria.text: (S1, I1 soundness) A refill write 'self.r = next(self.r)' (next takes &&) on a &self receiver, where next can stop (panic), never closes the moved value twice. Today both the callee frame and the caller's owner close it: probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/bal2/p/stop_refill.jet prints 'close a' twice before E3001 on -O0 and -O1 (refill-move path, Checking.jet:583-584). Rule: while a write place is empty, nothing that can stop may consume the moved value; sema rejects it or the place is refilled before any stop. The probe becomes a Tests/Cases case that closes once on O0/O1/O2, and the 8 repo sites of 'x.f = g(x.f)' (g takes &&) (CheckProgram.jet:5580/5581/6385/6529/7346, Host.jet:2553, Review.jet:282, Loops.jet:177) check clean or are migrated. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/stop_refill_closes_once` on O0, O1 and O2, and `jet check` over Compiler passes at the 8 sites.

Probes are under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/ until they become repo cases. D-TASK-WINDOW1 A: a task in a `task.group` may capture a read view or a write window into storage whose owner outlives the group. The capture is a loan held until the group's join. Two live tasks holding overlapping windows, where either writes, are refused with the group-loan diagnostic E1101 (ConcurrentCaptureNotOwned), the one code the existing group-loan rule uses. So is any use of the owner inside the group. The element type must be sendable, and IR holds the window by address (BuildExpr.jet:6297-6300). Proof: prep/c6066/bal/task_a.jet prints 6 on O0, O1 and O2; today it is E0631 at 9:17 and 9:27 (Lambdas.jet:2171-2184). prep/c6066/bal2/task_overlap.jet (both tasks write window `a`) and task_owner.jet (`print(v[0])` inside the group) are refused, each with a UI snapshot. All three become tests/cases cases.
criteria.evidence: Built in e9bb4a3dbe (a group task may capture a window into an outer owner as a loan held to the join). on batch compiler p155 (dev 49836bd978), 2026-11-15 01:48: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter concurrency_boundaries/a_group_task_can_write_through_a_window_into_an_outer_owner PASS 1 (split O0/O1/O2 and ranges O0/O2 print 6, read O0/O2 prints 10 and 1; overlap refused with E1101 ConcurrentCaptureNotOwned at overlap.jet:6:21; an owner read in the group refused at owner.jet:6:16); --profile ui --filter taskgroup_window_ PASS 2 (taskgroup_window_lent_to_two_writing_tasks, taskgroup_window_owner_read_inside_group). The prep probes became these cases.

criteria.text: Probes are under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/ until they become repo cases. D-MAPSLOT-WINDOW1 A: `&map[key]` at a `ViewMut<V>` destination is a one-value window over the entry's value, read as `w[0]`. IR builds the header from the entry's value address with length 1, as ir_list_window does. A missing key stops exactly as `map[key]` does. Adding or removing entries while the window lives is refused by the existing loan check (today that is E0220 at slot_grow.jet 8:5). Proof: prep/c6066/bal/slot_a.jet prints 1 on O0, O1 and O2; today it is E0108 at 2:5. prep/c6066/bal2/slot_grow.jet is refused at 8:5, with a UI snapshot. prep/c6066/bal2/slot_missing.jet stops with `the map has no entry for key "z"` on every tier. All three become cases.

Probes are under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/ until they become repo cases. D-INDEX-COMPOUND1 A: `xs[i] op= v` and `map[key] op= v` mean the long form, with one lookup. - E0164 is retired: Prelude/Diagnostics.jet:157 becomes a retired row, and the Statements.jet:5835 refusal is removed. The Dyn-path refusal at Statements.jet:5961, which shares the code, moves to its own registered code with the same text. - Proof: prep/c6066/bal/idx_a.jet prints 2 then 2 on O0, O1 and O2. - prep/c6066/bal2/idx_missing.jet stops with E3001 `the map has no entry for key "z"`. idx_range.jet stops with E3010 `the list has 2 items, so position 5 doesn't exist`. Both match their long forms, idx_long_missing.jet and idx_long_range.jet. - tests/ui/compound_index_target becomes a run case. - The E0164 text is amended in spec.md:1449-1452, syntax-decisions.md:264-265 (S17) and architecture.md:834-835. - The comments at Statements.jet:6158 and :6221 are corrected, and so is the fixture comment at tests/cases/l0503_behavior/…/prefer_compound_assign.jet:20. L0503 itself does not change.

criteria.text: Definite initialization accepts a fixed array `[T#N]{ uninit }` that a counted loop fully writes before any read; today it reports E0420. The census covers each fill shape (counted loop, while with index, fill call) and each lands as a case. Found by the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation (dev 0ccdff27ea). cards.title: Upgrades need no hand edits: every breaking change ships a `jet fix` rewrite, and last release's code builds on the new one
cards.body:
Scripting audit 2026-10-28 (row D28). `jet --version` on commit 8fbf094 prints "release readiness: not-ready" and "1.0 compatibility policy: future-1.0 (planned; not active)". Go 1 (compat promise plus `go fix`) and Perl 5 are best in class: old code keeps running. Python 2 to 3 took twelve years because most changes needed hand edits.

Design that beats them. Jet keeps greenfield freedom (AGENTS.md) but makes every break mechanical: a change that makes accepted source fail `jet check` must register a `jet fix` rewrite in the same change. CI proves it on the previous release's Examples/ and on a fixed corpus of scripts. Go fix covers a subset of changes; Jet's rule covers all of them, so users never hand-edit to upgrade. No card owns this: #5071 removes editions and retired forms but does not gate migrations. Map: #5982.

log.text: BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Owner 2026-11-06: not scheduled before v1 release preparation. c6 moved to #3720 (D-TEACH-RECONCILE1=A and the greenfield order remove retired-spelling paths now); c7 and c8 moved to #5950. For Main: tests/cases/onboarding_recovery/entry_recovery_covers_missing_ambiguous_legacy_and_stale_layouts expects jet run to migrate main.jet to run.jet, which the greenfield order (2026-11-06) forbids; drop its legacy arm and repoint its known-failing row to #5950.
Examples concept-area cutover (2c3e68a70b) moved paths this card's criteria cite. Read each cited path as its new home: c1: Examples/features -> Examples.

Owner 2026-11-06: until v1 release preparation no retired spelling, API or library path gets a teaching error, snapshot or jet fix rewrite; this card is where migration support is established during v1 release preparation. Not scheduled before then.
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 5 criteria from archived #266, #679, #1727: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

criteria.text: A blocking release guard checks out the previous release's Examples/ and a fixed corpus of 200 scripts (the ScriptBench programs plus Examples), runs `jet fix --all` and then `jet check` with the new toolchain, and fails on any error.
A change that makes previously accepted source fail `jet check` without registering a `jet fix` rewrite fails the guard (a planted-break test).

`jet fix` applies every rewrite added since the toolchain in the lock, or since `--since <version>`, and prints one line per rewrite kind with a count (D-LANG-MIGRATE1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jet_fix_since_lock` and the UI snapshot `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter jet_fix_since_summary`.
Across every release since the guard turned blocking, moving the corpus forward needs 0 hand edits, logged on this card per release. Proof: the per-release log entries citing the guard's receipt.
The `1.0 compatibility policy` line of `jet --version` reads from Docs/Spec/release-policy.md, and the policy names the release in which the guard became blocking.

cards.title: Port the Python bridge and the PyPI/npm providers to the self-hosted toolchain: `use py.X` in a loose script, each foreign package fenced by its grant
cards.body:
Scripting audit 2026-10-28 (row D06, ecosystem size). Python has 600k+ PyPI packages and JavaScript 3M+ npm packages; Jet's own registry has no public content, so Jet loses on reach by count. The ratified design already answers this. D-FFI-PY1=A (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:4166): `use py.X` talks to a supervised sidecar CPython with a typed message boundary and the `-[FFI.Py]>` effect; `py@embed` is the opt-in in-process mode. D-JPK-EXTPROV1=A (:4185): PyPI, npm and SwiftPM are first-class providers, fetched, hash-pinned and offline after the first fetch. D-DATA-BRIDGE1=A (:5964) reserves the `py.*` and `r.*` roots. Both were built in the Rust era (#180, #937 done) and never ported: probe on commit 8fbf094, `jet run -A b/pyuse.jet` with `use python.numpy as np` gives E0603 "The imported module is not present in the package source snapshot". No open card owns the port (#5984 is a map with no criteria).

Why this beats every peer rather than tying. Reach becomes a superset: PyPI plus npm plus Jet packages, where Python reaches only PyPI and Node only npm. Safety is better than at home: a PyPI package runs in a sidecar whose OS access is fenced by the script's grants, so a package that reads ~/.ssh is refused unless FS.Read for that path was granted. pip, uv and npm run package code with the user's full authority. Mojo also imports Python modules but runs them in-process with no fence.

Scope: the self-hosted `py.*` binder (sidecar default, `py@embed` opt-in), the PyPI and npm providers in the resolver behind #4833's fetch path, typed stubs from `.pyi` files where present, and the authority wiring. The R bridge (D-FFI-R1) follows the same sidecar path and is out of scope here.

criteria.text: A loose script with `use py.numpy as np` and `print(np.mean([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))` prints 2.0 under `jet run`: the first run fetches and hash-pins numpy from PyPI, and the second works with the network disabled (today E0603).

Reach census: at least 90 of the 100 most-downloaded PyPI packages import and pass a one-call smoke test through `use py.X` on Linux x86-64, with the script and table checked in and each failure listed with its reason. Proof: the checked-in census table and the committed receipt of its script's run.

A fixture PyPI package that opens ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 at import is refused with an authority error naming FS.Read and the path unless that grant was given, while the same package under `pip install` and `python3 -c 'import fixture'` reads the file (paired test).
The #5949 first-run prompt lists `FFI.Py` and the Python package names when a script first uses `py.*`, and a dependency update that adds a Python package asks again (#5459 rules).

With `py@embed`, 100k calls of a small pure Python function take less than 1.5x the same calls inside CPython, and with the sidecar default the median round trip is under 20 microseconds. Proof: a committed benchmark receipt per release.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6957 c17

criteria.text: A manifest dependency in the D-JPK-EXTPROV1 form (`leftpad: npm@"1.3.0"`) fetches, pins and is called through its typed first-party stub package, and the second run works offline.

The first run of a loose script with one dependency, on a cold cache, is faster than `uv run` of the PEP 723 equivalent and `deno run` with one `jsr:` import of similar size (median of 5, Jet/peer < 1.00). Proof: the committed hyperfine receipt.

cards.title: Benchmark Jet's build and package system against Nix, and beat it
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: Jet's build and package system must be lightning fast, substantially faster than Nix, more powerful, and easier to use, audit and reason about. Nix is a required peer for the build, package and configuration cells.

Compare like with like: the same project or package set built hermetically by both, on the same machine, cold and warm. Nix evaluation and store operations count, and so do Jet's check, store and cache.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): weeks. Nix peer cells, gates and a note.
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed card: G11 by the owner's 2026-11-09 ruling (speed and size are G11).

KitSpeed first receipt 2026-10-28 (5 samples, interleaved; Jet/Nix medians with the SemanticIndex O(n²) fix): eval 0.77, noop 20.4, incremental 4.87, cold_cache 5.21, scratch 3.88 — all lose. Causes: 73% build-plan query (whole-package Interpreter check, eager ProgramInfo, third Doc-mode recheck); no build stamp or artifact cache (JET_CACHE_DIR unread); Core rechecked per process (~150 ms). Fix plan: build stamp, plan cache + per-module interface/object caches, CAS under JET_CACHE_DIR, build-program closure scoping + one shared check + lazy ProgramInfo, persisted Core interface. Receipt: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/land/kitspeed-nix-peer-receipt.txt

criteria.text: The canonical performance manifest lists Nix as a required peer with paired cells: config evaluation (`nix eval` against `jet check` of the build program), no-op rebuild, one-file incremental rebuild, cold build from a populated cache or substituter, and a from-scratch hermetic build of the same medium project; each cell has a harness and committed receipts. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs` passes with the Nix rows.

Every Nix cell meets the gate (Jet/Nix below 1.00), and the evaluation, no-op and incremental cells reach Jet/Nix of at most 0.25; losses stay on cards with their cause. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry nix-build` shows no loss.

A side-by-side note shows the same project in Nix and in Jet: lines and concepts a reader needs, how each declares and audits inputs and effects, and reproducibility (bit-identical output on two machines or two clean stores). Proof: `git ls-files 'Docs/**/nix-vs-jet*'` names the committed note.

Store verification and hashing fan out across OS threads through a task group (D-TASKRUNTIME1=A), and the store verify and hashing performance cells record the speedup (frozen #3598 item 2 holds the original). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Store` (the parallel verify case) and the perf cells in the measurement manifest.

The same app's start time, peak memory and artifact size are measured against its wasm and OCI builds in a paired perf cell recorded in the canonical manifest. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Tests/Cases/AppFormat/app_format_is_measured_against_wasm_and_oci`.

cards.title: `Set` is a sorted array with a memmove per insert
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R3 (cells: w13 wall/CPU). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `Set` is a sorted array (`Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildSets.jet:1-7`). Each insert shifts the tail with memmove (`ir_set_insert_body`, `:65-95`, memmove `:77-88`). Building a set of 2 M lines is O(n²) moves.

Evidence: perf: `jet_rt_mem_move` 80.0 %, `jet_rt_string_compare` 5.8 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 18,666 ms vs PHP 733.1 ms, Python 1,363.8 ms.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): days (perf). ScriptBench w13 beats every peer.

ScriptBench receipt on the p391 batch compiler (dev 55614ffe3b), `jet Tools/Perf/Scriptbench/Bench.jet --only w02,w05,w13`, quiet machine (loop paused), 3 rounds x (2 warmup + 5 runs), receipt in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/bench/out-p391-w02-w05-w13/cells.tsv. c2 NOT met. w13 release binary (jet-bin, 27 cells) loses 8: peak RSS 187 MB vs luajit 76 (2.45), lua 84 (2.21), php 86 (2.17), python 94 (2.00), ruby 150 (1.25), perl 151 (1.24); php also wins wall 1.22 and cpu 1.23 (Jet 201 ms, php 165). The RSS gap is the main root to chase: the Set or its input holds about 2x the peers' memory.

HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).
BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from G4 to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

W13 root (CardClose-1, perf on a 200k-line subset, base s1 release): jet_ir_set_insert → jet_rt_mem_move is 88.5% self, string_compare 4.0%. Set<String> is a sorted array (Compiler/JetIR BuildSets.jet:65-95, ir_set_insert_body). Each new key is binary-searched, then the tail is memmoved, so n distinct keys cost O(n^2) shifting: 200k keys take 3.5 s, 2M lines 87 s. Fix: a hashed Set index like BuildMaps' hash/capacity, or insert-then-sort for bulk adds.

ScriptBench w13 on dev 69a987b5a6, wave-21 s1 (CardClose-1, sbench/w13-dev.json): LOSS against every peer. jet-bin 86.9 s wall, 79.1 s CPU, 220 MB RSS. Wall ratios: 249x python, 78.6x ruby (the closest), 241x php. jet run 56.5 s; that run may have overlapped other jobs, so it is not yet evidence of an inversion. The root is not profiled yet.
