cards.title: Each generator yield is a scheduler task park and wake, about 20 us per value
cards.body: Measured by IrTypes-3 2026-10-31 (IrTypes-25b timing): a generator pull hands off through the task scheduler (park the consumer, wake the producer, and back), about 20 us per yield. The iterloop kit case does 3M yields plus 1.28M channel pulls and takes 79 s. A generator that runs on the consumer thread needs no scheduler: a direct stack switch or a compiled state machine costs nanoseconds, and C/Rust/Zig iterators cost one call or less. This is a structural cost on every program that iterates a generator. Related: #6089 (lazy pulls charging comptime fuel through a global mutex).

log.text: Ruling on c3 (2026-11-24): SchedulerTests.jet compiles only inside the composed runtime unit, and its C host (scheduler-fixture.c) passes 7 callback addresses, so no unit-leg package can run it on a host without cc. Approach: one general runtime-dialect intrinsic yielding a named function's code address (no fixture-specific rows in ir_runtime_intrinsic_specs); an #Export(c) main in SchedulerTests.jet replaces the C host, which is deleted with the case's cc/as steps; a JetBackend/Tests #Test composes, lowers and links the unit and runs it at 1, 2 and 8 carriers and in root-panic mode. The cancel assertion counts as fixed at its root: 96a924e9f3 aligned the test with spec.md:4401-4406 (cancellation unwinds at the next wait point or check). Proof: JET=<batch jet> jet test Compiler/JetBackend/Tests --filter 'the scheduler fragment'.

a0.0.46 admit (dev c137227f92, 2026-11-21): FiberLiveness/tasks_start_within_one_futex_wake_of_their_spawn FAILs with the parallel wake (5799f50925) in: causal fixture 4000 starts, 99th percentile 1328 us after spawn; fan-out 7500 starts, 509 us; one futex wake 29 us. c2 stays open; the release carries the row as a disposition naming this card.

HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c1 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

criteria.text: A generator pull that stays on the consumer thread costs under 50 ns per value (a direct switch or a compiled state machine, no scheduler park and wake), measured same-run on the iterloop kit case and a 10M-yield microbench, with every generator golden unchanged on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Generator` and the committed microbench receipt.

A task the scheduler can run starts at once: in plain `jet run` of the causal fixture (Perf/causal_profile_predicts_speedup), 4-22% of rounds start a task more than 100 us late, some waiting on a parked carrier's wake (100-1000 us) and others queued behind a sibling on one carrier (~1050 us) while other carriers idle; the share varies run to run, so the case's hand-measured truth varies with it. The wake and placement path is fixed in the runtime scheduler for every program, with no special case for the fixture. Proof: a case that measures task start latency against the spawn (p99 under a stated bound derived from the futex wake cost on this host) on the causal fixture and on a second spawn-heavy program, plus Perf/causal_profile_predicts_speedup passing when run alone.

The scheduler unit tests run and pass in the suite: on dev a8df17dfb5 the Scheduler unit (SchedulerTests.jet) did not compile (a 2-argument scheduler_timer_schedule call, fixed in IfHole-6-1-scheduler-own-wake), and once compiled it exits 1 at the poll/propagate-after-an-ordinary-cancel assertion. The landing suite reported units 0 failures throughout, so this unit is not in the units profile. Proof: the units profile selects SchedulerTests.jet and it passes; the cancel assertion is fixed at its root.

cards.title: stdin reads one byte per syscall: cat-style programs run ~3,300x slower than Rust
cards.body: Floor-1 same-run measurement on df84 (2026-10-31, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Floor/out/pareto-speed.md): the cat cell is about 3,300x Rust by task-clock, because terminal/stdin reads go one byte per read syscall (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/RouteTerm.jet:19-51). stdout writes need the same check. Fix the root in the one shared runtime: buffered stdin and stdout with correct flush semantics (line-buffered for a TTY, block-buffered otherwise, flush at exit, flush before reading interactive input), with one meaning on every tier.

log.text: c2 progress: 6444-c2 landed (dev 7583396c60). Owned-main print goes through the shared stdout buffer. On the batch 15 compiler, cases PrintBranchTiers/print_writes_numbers_into_stdout_with_the_text_a_string_has and BuildEntry/package_lint_import_silent PASS, and golden shows no new failures. c2 stays open until its named proof runs: strace -c on a 3M-print owned-main loop into a pipe shows at most one write per 64 KiB, and the same-run bench against Rust with a BufWriter gives Jet/Rust < 1.00. That measurement waits for the heavy slot.

Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): 1d. c1's Runtime/stdin_buffered_reads already PASSes on batch12; it still needs the committed same-run cat receipt against Rust (perf host). c2 is the owned-main stdout buffer in the runtime: hours, plus a strace proof.

c2 not met on gate-p419 (tip 24356fa7b8): an owned-main 3M-print loop (Main: program-owned), built --release, writes 37,888,890 bytes into a pipe in 4626 write calls (8 KiB each) against the bound of one write per 64 KiB (578). The non-terminal stdout buffer must grow to 64 KiB; sent to the implementer with the cases that encode 8192.

Same-run cat on the p403 batch compiler (dev 236298d8c0, 2026-11-21; $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/probe-6444/bench.sh, 2M lines / 93 MB on a pipe, hyperfine -N 30 runs interleaved, jet build --release against rustc -O). Reads are fixed: jetcat makes 1,427 read(0) calls averaging 65,487 bytes (rscat makes 11,409 of 8,191), and both outputs are byte-identical to the input. Speed still loses: wall 132.0 ± 5.8 ms against 117.6 ± 3.8 ms (Jet/Rust 1.12), user+sys 131.1 against 116.8 ms (1.12). c1 stays open: the remaining cost is past the read path (per-line handling or the write path), for E24.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match the AGENTS.md Performance gate (Jet/peer < 1.00 with no Rust band, then the asm-parity ceiling).

Main-34 folds print's LF into host_stdout_write (one locked write per print line). cat cell vs rust-O3, perf stat medians: HEAD 7c67280960 runtime 435M cycles / 94.3 ms task-clock (Rust 395M / 89.3 ms: 1.10x cycles, 1.056x task-clock); with Main-34 430M / 93.3 ms (about -1.1%). Output byte-identical; cases --filter stdout|print match the HEAD baseline; golden suite adds no new failures versus HEAD (18 missing-stream rows are #6538, stack_overflow o2 tier-split is pre-existing at HEAD). Rejected: a 16-byte unroll of stdin_line_scan (+3.8% cycles). Remaining gap per profile: sync_sole_enter about 14% (about 15 cycles per elided call), copy about 14%, SWAR scan about 10%, stdout write about 22%; mostly runtime codegen quality (stack spills) and call overhead. Card stays open: the gate requires Jet/peer < 1.00.

Main 2026-11-01 09:05, dev 367eaf8f0d base jet, release build of Floor cells/cat/run.jet on a 200,000-line (10.7 MB) pipe input: output byte-identical. strace shows 165 stdin reads (64 KiB each) and 1,398 stdout writes (about 7.6 KiB each), so the one-byte read root is gone. hyperfine -N, 40 runs, load average 18: Jet 33.2 ms (user 25.7), Rust O3 20.1 ms (user 9.8), C gcc O2 3.9 ms. Jet/Rust is 1.65, down from about 3,300. Criterion 1 is still open. The remaining cost is per-line user time: lines() makes one String per line, UTF-8 is checked per line, and print adds its own work. Next: a borrowed line view or a bulk copy for the lines-to-print path, still with one meaning on every tier.

AsmPar-1 2026-11-01 01:05: the one-byte read root is fixed on wave 18 (strace of the cat cell: 1,086 reads of 64 KiB for 71 MB). The cell is still 3.3x Rust in cycles (0.78G vs 0.24G); the remaining gap is a per-line alloc/free in the lines iterator plus stdio_checkpoint.

Landed on dev at undefined in AsmPar-13 (patch row: criterion/count 2): AsmPar-13 (partial; criterion stays open): cat's final string drops skip the lock. Locked instructions retired 3.535M -> 3.303M (-6.6%, release); the remaining locks are retains and shared drops.

Landed on dev at undefined in AsmPar-12 (patch row: criterion/count 1): AsmPar-12 (partial; criterion stays open): the cat cell's per-line UTF-8 validation no longer calls rt_text_valid_width for each ASCII tail byte. cat: 2581.4M -> 2453.6M instructions (-5.0%, release, r15 vs r16 s1).

Landed on dev at undefined in IrTypes-31 (patch row: criterion/count 1): PARTIAL, criterion NOT met (card stays open): IrTypes-31 drops the line's trailing LF/CR inside jet_stdin_line_raw (in place, after the UTF-8 check), and Core read_line no longer round-trips each line through [U8] (stdin_chomp removed). Floor cat cell, jet --release: 6,485 M instr / 252-312 ms -> 3,963 M / 150.6 ms task-clock; matched Rust peer (cells/cat/main.rs, now BufRead::lines + BufWriter) 752 M / 58.8 ms, so Jet/Rust is 2.56x (the raw block copy moved to cells/catblock). CRLF transcript byte-identical to the old chomp on 5 inputs, default and --release; 88 stdin/terminal/prompt/io_/print cases have the same status as on IrTypes-30. Left: per-line Result/Option boxes and the String alloc in the lines iterator (codegen, sent to Codegen-1).

Landed on dev at undefined in IrTypes-30 (patch row: criterion/count 1): PARTIAL, criterion NOT met (card stays open): IrTypes-30 buffers stdin (one shared 64 KiB buffer under the stdin lock) and stdout (print flush 0: line-buffered on a tty, 8 KiB blocks otherwise; flushed before stderr, every stdin read, children, exit). Floor-1 cat cell: jet --release 35,612 ms -> 252 ms task-clock (wall ~= task), rust-O3 10.2 ms, zig 9.3 ms same run, so Jet/Rust ~24x, not <= 1.05. strace: stdin reads max 65,536 B, mean 65,424 B (1,086 reads; was 1 B each); stdout 9,198 writes (was 833,335). Every stdin/stdout/prompt/terminal/print/io_/no_args/runtime_stop_goldens/build_option_ case has the same status as the pre-patch jet (cases/repl/ differs only by the harness's E2104 stdin-write race); terminal/stdin_lines_emit_before_eof and stdout_write_bytes_ordered_with_print pass by hand on default and --release. The remaining ~300 ns/line is the per-line String (Core StdinHandle.read_line: checkpoint, jet_stdin_line_raw copy, stdin_chomp's [U8] round trip, alloc/drop), which needs a borrowed line view in the lines loop to reach Rust's raw 64 KiB copy.

Main 2026-10-31: IrTypes-30 (wave 11) buffers stdin/stdout: cat cell 35.6 s -> 252 ms, 64 KiB reads, corpus 52/52 identical. The Floor-1 Rust peer was an io::copy block copy, so it was not matched. Against a matched BufRead::lines + BufWriter Rust (64 ms, 752M instr), Jet is 4.2x in time and 8.5x in instructions (7,894 vs 928 Ir per line). Roots: Core stdin_chomp round trip 30%, jet_stdin_line_raw 27% (UTF-8 validated twice), per-line lazy_line_next boxes 18%, print 8%, String drop 5% ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/IR/IrTypes/c6328/d44/cg/ATTRIB.md). Next: runtime strips CR/LF (IrTypes-31); per-line boxes and String alloc go to Codegen-1. Criterion 1 is not met yet.

criteria.text: The cat cell is faster than Rust same-run (Jet/Rust < 1.00) by wall time and task-clock, strace shows reads of at least 64 KiB per syscall on a pipe, and every stdin and stdout golden and interactive REPL case is unchanged on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Runtime/stdin_buffered_reads` and the committed same-run cat receipt.

A program that owns its main prints through the same stdout buffer as every other program: block-buffered when stdout is not a terminal, line-buffered on a terminal, flushed at exit and before a read from stdin, as this card states. Found by Rivet profiling the cat cell on the p403 jet (2026-11-21): an owned main prints with jet_term_write_stdout_line_direct, one writev per print with no buffer, so a 3M-print loop made 3M writev calls and ran 18x Rust with a BufWriter. Proof: strace -c on a 3M-print owned-main loop into a pipe shows at most one write per 64 KiB, its golden output is unchanged on O0, O1 and O2, and a same-run bench against Rust with a BufWriter reads Jet/Rust < 1.00.

Printing or interpolating a Float costs at most what Rust's shortest round-trip formatting costs per value: FloatShortest gains a fast path (Ryu or an equivalent shortest-digits algorithm) and falls back to exact arithmetic only where the fast path can't decide; today every Float takes the exact arithmetic path, about 500 ns per value (G2Regressions, 2026-11-24, batch 13 compiler). Proof: a cases row printing 1M varied Floats with output identical on O0, O1 and O2 to the current digits, plus a same-run receipt against Rust showing Jet/Rust below 1.00 for wall time and peak memory.

cards.title: The web app layer leaves Core: pages, forms, router, store, tables, live queries and browser storage go to a first-party `web` package
cards.body:
Move card for #6146 (D-WEB-HOME1=A, ratified).

- Moves Core/Web (pages, forms, router, store, tables, live queries, browser storage) to the first-party battery Jetpack/Provider/Batteries/web/. It ships with Jet at its version, and `jet add web` writes the one dependency line.
- core.http and core.net stay in Core.
- The sema web rows become markers and traits in the package (Core gets no private powers).
- `use core.web` is removed with no teaching error, snapshot or `jet fix` rewrite (owner order 2026-11-06; migration support is set during v1 release preparation, #6068).
- One greenfield cutover: every in-repo caller, example, golden and doc moves in the same change.

log.text: c5 (one serializable transaction per write method) is being built now as a G9 dependency. Four G9 criteria wait on it: #6820 c3, #6825 c1, #6800 c3 and #6813 c5.
Correction (owner order 2026-11-15 ~12:50): GoalsB-5-2 stays on G9 and owns c8 then c5. The earlier routing log is void.

Routing (Main, 2026-11-15): GoalsB-5-2 moves to G6 #6846; c4 (app.caller, E2815) and c3 (Remote reaches only marked methods) are submitted and land next batch; c5 and c8 are unowned until G9 work resumes.

Handoff (GoalsB-5-3 stopped, agent cap): c2's moves are on dev; SUB web-sync-live-key (core.web.sync/storage gone, sync rule keyed on app, world cell app.live) is in census222. c2 still needs: (1) a #WebApp marker on web.app(), with the CLI WebGraph.jet/Entry.jet name matching re-keyed onto it; (2) the openapi lookup at Calls/Http.jet:808 uses the literal core.web instead of SEMA_WEB_MARKER_MODULE; (3) the __app_port/__app_dev env reads at Pipeline.jet:6072 and Effects/Checks.jet:4047 are still keyed on core.web; (4) the grep proof, which needs c1. c1 also needs D-HTTP-HANDLER-ENTRY1=A built first (server.listen, static_dir, serve_once, RoutePattern), because Web.jet calls 15 private http_server names. c9: native Remote works; on web it ends in CallError.Unreachable (sockets return ENOSYS). Planned seam: a jet.runtime.web fetch binding through a host-provider leaf wrapped in WebAssembly.Suspending, with promising run/click.

Decisions (Main, 2026-11-14, within D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A), for the Remote transport (G5DevX2-app-remote-transport). (a) #App.SignedIn endpoints answer 401 (CallError.SignedOut) until App sign-in lands (c4), so the call fails closed. (b) CallError.Invalid carries [FieldError] (Core's existing FieldError{path, reason}), decoded from the 422 body, so server field errors (#6831) need no second form. (c) Every Remote<S> call, direct ones included, has CallError in its type and -[Net, Time.Wait]>, so screen code is the same on every target. Web leg: JSPI (WebAssembly.Suspending and promising), with events queued while a call is suspended. G5DevX-2 checked the support: Chrome and Edge 137, Firefox 153, Safari 27 (MDN browser-compat-data); Node on by default from 25.0.0 and 24.20.0; local node v24.21.0 ran a round trip unflagged.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-13, within D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A): a screen gets its app.Remote<S> from one Core constructor, app.remote(service). The ratified example takes `crew: app.Remote<Crew>` as a parameter but names no constructor; this is the smallest one, a Core struct API with no new syntax. Only methods marked for remote calls are callable on it (E2812 jet.ServerOnlyMethod otherwise). The client transport is a separate c3 item.
Owner question on D-HTTP-HANDLER-ENTRY1: rework to the best greenfield design versus all ecosystems, with downsides engineered away (G3Core-2).

G9Web retired (team cut to 6, 2026-11-13).
Staged in g9-route1, after G9Web-6055-stack-r3: routetable, concurrent-serve-r2 and inline-battery (tree 4d154ca7).
Unstaged WIP: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G9Web/wip-6445c2-form-columnof.patch.
- #Form is done there: E2474, six callers migrated, plus a ui test.
- #ColumnOf crashes the compiler as a parameter marker (sema totality ICE "unsupported program form applied rules"), so either sema accepts parameter markers first, or #ColumnOf becomes a function marker.
- #WebApp is not started.
The handoff is at lanes/G9Web/handoff.md. The orphan worktrees g19, g20 and g21 left by G9Web-1 were removed after their diffs were saved as lanes/G9Web/saved-g19-a0222b38e4.patch, saved-g20-34da8adfd2.patch and saved-g21-78d3db56d8.patch.

Ballot D-HTTP-HANDLER-ENTRY1 posted (v2, after the adversarial review). It decides the public call the web package uses to serve once core.web leaves Core. Part E and c1 wait on it; the #6055 trio restack and the other #6445 parts continue.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06 (owner ruling): no teaching errors, snapshots or jet fix rewrites for retired spellings, API or library paths until v1 release preparation (#6068).

criteria.text: core.web no longer exists in Core; Examples and tests that used it import the `web` package and their goldens pass on O0/O1/O2; `use core.web` fails as an ordinary unknown module, with no teaching error, snapshot or jet fix rule (owner 2026-11-06). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter web` on O0, O1 and O2 importing the `web` package, and `git ls-files Core/Web` prints nothing.

D-WEB-RUNTIME-API1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). core.web.browser becomes core.browser, members unchanged. core.web.on and core.web.value become core.browser.host.on and .value, and core.web.storage.local/.session become core.browser.storage.local/.session (get, set, remove, clear). Live<T, E> and app.live, subscribe, push, invalidate, state and live_stats move into Core's app module with their signatures, and the jet.runtime.web bindings stay priv under app. web.openapi(site) returns String OpenAPIError! (no E2805 stop). The compiler rules key on four markers the battery declares (#Form, #RouteTable, #ColumnOf, #WebApp), not on module names. Every caller moves in the same cutover. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Browser` on O0, O1 and O2 and `git grep -n "core.web" -- Core Compiler Examples` prints nothing.

A method of a mounted service is reachable from app.Remote<S> only when marked #App.SignedIn or #App.Public: a client call to any other method (job, webhook, signing key, unmarked) is a compile error naming the method (Appendix A probe probes/cl1_server_only.jet).
criteria.evidence: batch compiler p187 (dev 9860836a00), 2026-11-15: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/remote_has_only_marked_methods 1/1 PASS (landed 5a023c36a2)

criteria.text: app.caller() is accepted only on paths that start at an #App.SignedIn endpoint or a test's app.as_caller; a path from #App.Public, a webhook, a job or a schedule is a compile error naming the path; app.maybe_caller() is the Public form.
Each method that writes runs in one serializable transaction, retried on a serialization failure up to a cap; two concurrent move_task calls on one version give one Ok and one Conflict.
criteria.evidence: p204 batch compiler (dev 686cdaaee7): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/write_method_is_one_serializable_transaction gives n=1, bad=0 (commits e19632601d and 79075a3365).

criteria.text: Only the package that builds the shared graph calls .screen: a .screen call in an entry package (one an output names) is a compile error; push open:, mail link: and app links resolve through the one route set.

A handler of kit.button, icon_button, swipe_action, file_button, native.item, ui.drop_zone, the tray and menu bar builders, native.background's run, native.lifecycle's on_resume and native.drop_files's on_drop has type fn() app.Notice!: its error type must convert to app.Notice. The frame shows the notice at the handler's destination (beside the control, a disabled menu item, the resumed window, or the drop target), announces it, and rolls back a refused predicted write. A failed native.background run joins the app's notice list, kept until dismissed, and is logged.

app.live's closure must be one call of an app.Remote endpoint with codable arguments, so the subscription is keyed by the method and its arguments; anything else is a compile error with a registered diagnostic.
criteria.evidence: p238 batch compiler (dev 5bea729463), full collect-all suite: cases WebApp/live_takes_one_remote_call PASS.

criteria.text: A web client reaches a mounted service through app.Remote<S>: the web host gains a network leg that fetches through the same suspension mechanism web tasks already use to wait, never a synchronous XHR on the page's main thread. Proof: a case builds a client for web and native, calls one #App method of a running server on each, and prints the same result and the same app.CallError for a refused call.
The web store is one generic impl over its state type in the `web` package, not per-type copies.

Exactly one module exports live, subscribe, invalidate and sync (the `app` package of D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A) and one exports the auth surface (the `auth` package); every caller migrates and Core/Web/Query.jet's live, subscribe and invalidate are gone. Proof: `git grep -n -E '^(live|subscribe|invalidate): fn' -- Core` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/` passes. (was #3709 c8)

A dated parity audit in Docs/Audits lists every element of the reference frameworks named in the body, the best framework for each element, Jet's current state cited by code path and executable example, the gap, and each known downside of the best implementation with the Jet design that removes it. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*web-framework-parity*"` names the dated audit. (was #6552 c1)

Every owner choice the audit raises is on a Tower ballot with same-program alternatives, and every ratified choice has a child card under this card. Proof: each audit row names its ballot ID and child card. (was #6552 c2)

Every audited element at parity or better has an executable example with golden output on every applicable tier, and the audit row cites it. Proof: each parity row of the audit names its example, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter web` on O0, O1 and O2 passes on every applicable tier. (was #6552 c4)

Every claim that the Jet framework or any of its elements is better than an existing framework is backed by a passing adversarial review in Docs/Audits, and every downside that review finds is engineered away and re-reviewed before the element is presented to the owner or built (AGENTS.md, Adversarial design review). Proof: each better-than claim in the audit names its passing adversarial review under Docs/audits. (was #6552 c6)

Routes, data queries, forms, tables and stores run on one reactive app runtime: one example app uses all five, and its golden passes on O0, O1, O2 and web. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/AppSuite`. (was #6552 c7)

One app package serves web, desktop and phones (D-ONEAPP-MODEL1=A): one example app builds for web and Linux desktop from the same source, and both goldens pass. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/one_source_web_and_linux`. (was #6552 c35)

A screen calls a marked server method like a plain function (D-SERVER-FN1=A, in the D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A form of app.Remote<S> and #App.SignedIn): the call crosses to the server with typed arguments and comes back with a typed error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/remote_call_typed_errors`. (was #6552 c36)

The client-safe app graph of D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A is built in the app package as the proposal's 1 and 3.3 spell it: app.new(title:) with .api<S>(path), .screen(path, view, signed_in:) and .offline(.Queue); one graph serves the route set, the screens and the Remotes, with no second registration path. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/app_graph_builds_screens_and_api` on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: tui leaves Core for the first-party `tui` package (D-TUI-HOME1=A): managed run loop, widgets, styles, key bindings and a typed test driver
cards.body:
Move card for #6147 (D-TUI-HOME1=A, ratified).

- Moves Core/Tui (layouts, widgets) to the first-party battery Jetpack/Provider/Batteries/tui/; `jet add tui` writes the dependency line. Printing, keys and raw mode stay in core.term.
- Deletes the #Live syntax-registry row; core.term declares `Live` as a library marker (struct Live implementing the marker API), spelled `#term.Live`.
- ANSI text lands in core.term.
- `use core.tui` becomes a registered error naming `jet add tui` (what/why/fix and a UI snapshot); `jet fix` rewrites imports and #Live uses.
- One greenfield cutover of every in-repo caller, example, golden and doc.

log.text: Cleaned 2026-11-15: criteria restated with proofs; c6 merged into c9; c9 and c10 came from #3551.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match the Rust-free toolchain (Jet suites and tests/cases rows replace cargo tests and .rs sources).
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 7 criteria from archived #2467, #2470: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

criteria.text: core.tui and the #Live registry row are gone; tui examples and tests import the `tui` package and #term.Live, and their goldens pass on O0, O1 and O2; `use core.tui` fails with the ordinary unknown-module error (no teaching error or snapshot). Proof: `git ls-files Core/TUI` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter TUI/` passes.
A tui program declares a typed model, routes keyboard, resize, timer and I/O events through update, runs asynchronous commands, and renders its view without blocking redraw.
A widget and a stateful widget receive typed geometry and state, and nested constraints give deterministic layouts at narrow and wide terminal sizes.
The same ui node tree (D-UI-HOME1=A, the `ui` package) renders through the tui backend in the `jet dev` terminal host and in a user TUI, with no second widget implementation.

Styles pick ANSI16, ANSI256, truecolor or ASCII from terminal capability, visible-width measurement keeps Unicode blocks aligned, and NO_COLOR stays plain (ANSI text itself is core.term's, D-TUI-ANSI1=A).
(was #2467 c5) Normal return, error propagation, panic, and interrupted input restore terminal state and leave no raw-mode residue, proven by a tests/cases row.
criteria.evidence: Merged into #6446 c9: terminal restore on every exit path is part of the managed run criterion

criteria.text: Remapped key bindings drive dispatch and generated help from one typed declaration, including a narrow-terminal help layout.

TUI interaction, headless frame capture, readiness waits, cursor movement, click dispatch and recordings work on typed element ids, hit regions, a semantic cursor and target-owned readiness, never by parsing rendered text.

The `tui` package publishes only the managed `tui.run`: it takes the typed model, update, view and adapt callbacks and returns the owned final model; commands are children of the structured task scope; the terminal guard is the only raw-mode boundary and leaves no raw-mode residue after normal return, error, panic or interrupted input; a non-TTY paints one frame and returns NonTty. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter TUI/RunTasks` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter tui_run_pty_`.

`ui.UiNodeId` is the public identity in the `tui` package's controls: TuiListState drives list and table, UiTextEditorState handles editing, mouse press, drag and scroll are typed events, stale layouts are dropped, malformed input records give TuiError.Input, focus is restored by id, and NO_COLOR keeps interaction.

D-TERM-COMMANDS1=A is built: `term.execute(...)` takes any number of `term.Command` cases (.ClearBuffer, .EnableRawMode, .EnterAlternateScreen, .HideCursor, .MoveTo, .Print and the rest of the research list) and writes them at once; every lasting setting records its undo, run on return, exit, panic, stop and SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT, on Linux, macOS and Windows. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Systems/Terminal/Execute` on O0, O1 and O2 through a pseudo-terminal, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Term/raw_mode_restored_after_panic`. (was #6315 c3)

D-CORE-TERMSTDIN1=A and D-TERM-INCREMENTAL1=A are built: the input, output and error handles answer `is_terminal()` (is_tty is renamed at Core/Term/Term.jet:62,129,149), and `term.keys()` returns a Receiver<Key> giving one whole key per receive, with `read_key` (Term.jet:427) deleted. Proof: `git grep -n -E 'is_tty|read_key' -- Core` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Systems/Terminal/Keys` passes on O0, O1 and O2 through a pseudo-terminal. (was #6315 c4)

cards.title: Function-local Result/Option boxes from runtime routes stay heap-allocated (binparse 25% alloc/free)
cards.body: binparse run builds a jet_rt_alloc(16,8) Result box around each reader route (4 per record in the loop) that never leaves run. perf on the register-return build: free_8 12.4% + alloc_8 8.8% + alloc 4.3% = 25.5% of 257M cycles (~66M). The register-return pass does not reach these boxes. Fix: escape analysis in JetIR: a function-local box used only by Load/Store at offsets, the unique test, free and Drop becomes a stack slot, and scalar replacement then puts it in registers. General: applies to every non-escaping small heap allocation. Full text: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/IR/IrTypes/c6328/d53/CARD-REQUEST-local-box.md.

cards.title: Cross-package IR inlining of small Core bodies (runtime-routed Core leaves are opaque to OptInline)
cards.body: Runtime-routed Core leaves (jet_std_math_*) are prebuilt in the runtime pack, so OptInline never has their IR; OptInline also refuses cross-file callees holding located (stop-capable) ops because the trap site is tied to the source file. Ship the IR of small Never! runtime leaves with the runtime pack (or compile them from Core source into the module), and carry the source file per located op so an inlined cross-file op keeps its trap site. Measured motive: fft/tensormap still call Core fabs via to_bits/from_bits after the ir_leaf_route table (-9.1% instead of 12-16%). Full text: wave/16/in/Codegen-1-27.msg.

log.text: Ruling on c3 (2026-11-24): 'no slot for x' means x costs nothing at run time: no frame place, no store and no load. At O1 and O2 the IR keeps only the debugger's declaration 's1 local x: Int', which ir_x64_variables locates as X64DebugLocation.Constant, with no frame place and no code. Deleting it would remove x from an O1/O2 debugger and gain nothing (AGENTS.md: never remove a feature to meet a cost). The case asserts both facts.

cards.title: Hoist constant Regex{} construction out of every evaluation
cards.body: sema_expression_typed_literal_regex (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/Constructors.jet) lowers every Regex{"…"} literal to a runtime core.regex.compile(pattern) on each evaluation, although the pattern is fixed and checked at compile time. Build each constant Regex once per program (comptime constant: Regex values already materialize, see comptime_diff/reusable_regex; or a once-initialized global). cards.title: Register allocator: live-range splitting so density-based spills keep hot loop values
cards.body: IrTypes-37 (floats in xmm2-15) found that a pure density spill rule wins nbody (1.65G -> 0.62G cycles) but evicts collatz hot loop variables for short temporaries (6.97G -> 10.82G instructions). The landed safe rule (evict only lighter ranges) keeps collatz exact but gives nbody only -36% (1.64G -> 1.05G). Split long live ranges around hot loops so the density rule can keep both. Proof: nbody at or under 0.62G cycles and collatz at or under 6.97G instructions in the same s2, every other ceiling cell flat or better, s2 chain + FULL cases.

cards.title: Pareto census: profile every cell, attribute every gap to a root, and plan each root
cards.body: Owner order 2026-10-31 20:00: binary size and speed are still far from the hand-written ceilings. Profile every cell (not cherry-picked): every asm-parity ceiling cell, every gauntlet cell against every peer, and a seeded random sample of programs from the example/workload corpora with peer versions. For each, record cycles, instructions and bytes as ratios to the ceiling and to each peer, plus perf hotspots and a size breakdown by symbol and section (runtime, glue, user code). Attribute every gap to a root (e.g. startup, RC/locks, bounds checks, spills/regalloc, missing loop opts or vectorization, inlining, allocation, runtime size, dead code). Rank the roots by total gap mass across cells. Separately, compare the JetIR/backend pipeline with the LLVM O2 pipeline (SROA, GVN, LICM, InstCombine, SCCP, jump threading, loop unroll/vectorize, inliner cost model, register coalescing, shrink-wrapping, tail dup, code layout, LTO dead stripping) and list the missing ones with their expected reach. Output: a dated audit under Docs/audits with the TSV, and one Tower card per root with an owner, proof terms and the cells it moves.

criteria.text: An empty program (`fn run(){}`) image is at most 8192 B in release and 10240 B in default, with identical output (baseline 360e470044: 21168 and 23064 B).
The empty image links no allocator (jet_rt_alloc and free absent) and no fault-report text tables, and any cell that cannot fault or allocate gets the same by liveness, not a flag.

The hello asm-parity cell image is at most 12288 B in release, with identical output (baseline 360e470044: 25.6 KB). Proof: `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate --cells hello --modes default,release`.

Runtime startup and print pull in only what the program uses: a program that never spawns tasks, allocates or formats links none of that machinery, by liveness and lazy initialization, with one meaning on o0, o1 and o2 (I9) and no change to panic or error behavior. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Size/runtime_pay_for_use` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #6328 c2)

Jet's default build (jet build, no size flags) of hello and of every required perf workload is strictly smaller than each peer's smallest output for the same program (Zig ReleaseSmall stripped, C musl static -Os stripped, Rust opt-level=z stripped, Go -ldflags=-s -w, Odin -o:size), measured on the same machine; o0 (jet run/jet dev output) and --release are smaller still or equal, never larger. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs` binary_bytes column shows Jet strictly smallest in every required cell, O0 and --release included. (was #6328 c3)

The size win comes from the root design (pay-for-what-you-use runtime, lazy runtime initialization, liveness through every runtime and Core layer, no unconditional startup machinery), with no hello-world special case, no per-program flags, no stripping or compression tricks that peers are denied, and no change to panic, error, safety or I9 behavior; the receipt shows the same mechanism shrinking a non-trivial program. Proof: a committed receipt showing the same mechanism shrinking hello and a non-trivial program. (was #6328 c5)

For every program in the size corpus (hello, one program per required perf cell, and every landed #5072 tool twin, each with a hand-written, optimized x86-64 assembly reference committed beside it that delivers the same features, fault reporting included), the default jet build holds only the code the program reaches: its size is at most the assembly reference size (Jet/ceiling at most 1.00 in bytes). Every byte category above the reference is listed with the root that keeps it and the card that removes it. (moved from #6836) GauntletTower probe 2026-11-13 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/GauntletTower/csize/probe.txt, probe2.txt): Jet hello is 109,976 bytes unstripped and 95,552 stripped, all static. C hello is 15,888 dynamic, 16,512 static and 13,352 static stripped. Jet/C is 6.0 to 7.2 under every fair pairing, so this is a real loss on the binary-size floor. The cause is the runtime, which links 76 KB of code and 11 KB of unwind tables into every program, used or not: jet_rt core 17.2 KB, allocator 13.2, production receipt 6.5, trap and fault report 5.7, helpers 5.0, scheduler 4.5, host 4.3, sync/vDSO 3.5, plus threads, sentry and comptime-stop. General fix: the runtime links by reach, as Core does, so a program pays only for the runtime parts it calls. The scheduler, threads, sentry and receipt come in only when used. Features that every program genuinely needs (fault report, trap) stay, minimized and never drop — Criterion: The runtime links by reach: a hello program links no scheduler, threads, sentry or production-receipt code, and every runtime part it does link is called on its path. Proof: `nm --size-sort` of the batch-jet hello build lists no jet_rt scheduler, thread, sentry or receipt symbols, and a second program that spawns a task does link the scheduler and prints the same output on o0, o1 and o2. (was #6328 c34)

cards.title: Beyond the hand-written ceiling: survey optimizations that beat expert asm (Goose language claims, whole-program specialization, superoptimization, data-layout transforms)
cards.body: Owner order 2026-10-31: once every program meets the hand-written asm ceiling in cycles and bytes, the next goal is to BEAT it. Survey with sources: the Goose language (its claimed speedups over Rust and C, what mechanisms produce them, which are verified, and which fit Jet semantics and I9), whole-program specialization and monomorphization budgets, superoptimization of hot blocks, automatic data-layout transforms (AoS/SoA, field reordering, small-value packing), allocation elision and region inference, comptime evaluation of input-independent work, and cache-aware code layout without PGO. Output: Docs/research/beyond-asm-ceiling-2026-10-31.md ranking each idea by expected gain across ALL programs (not one example), implementation cost and semantic risk, with cards proposed for the top items. No claim without a source or a measurement.

That maximum is not only optimized machine code, but the best result the problem allows, reached by rethinking phasing, ordering, logic and advanced techniques. For real-world cases, hit the real-world maximum. The owner chose "Record it": every required cell gets a written, reviewed theoretical bound; reports show Jet against the peers, the hand-written reference and the bound; the gate stays peers plus the reference; the design targets the bound. criteria.text: The survey lists every technique known to beat expert hand-written assembly (Goose-style stack-based execution, whole-program specialization, superoptimization, data-layout transforms and others), each with sources and a runnable probe. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Research/*beyond-the-ceiling*"` names the survey, each technique with its sources and probe.
Each technique that wins its probe gets a card with a paired two-program cell under the performance gate rules. Proof: each winning row of the survey names its card and paired cell.

End metric: required cells beat their asm-parity ceilings (Jet/ceiling below 1.00 in cycles and bytes) with identical output, and every cell that does not is on a card. Proof: `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate` ceiling columns below 1.00, each other cell naming its card.

Every required gauntlet and ScriptBench cell has a written theoretical bound per metric, derived only from the workload's stated contract: wall time from the critical path (unavoidable latencies and dependency chain); CPU time from the larger of bytes moved over memory or disk bandwidth and minimum operations over machine throughput; RSS and bytes from the minimum working set and image. The derivation is committed beside the cell and reviewed adversarially, so a bound cannot be made easy. Proof: a bound derivation committed beside each required cell, each with its adversarial review.

The performance reports show, for each cell and metric, Jet against the best peer of each tier, Jet against the hand-written reference, and Jet against the theoretical bound, on the binary and on `jet run`. The bound ratio is the design target and never relaxes the gate (every peer below 1.00, the reference at most 1.00). Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/standings.test.mjs` with the tier, reference and bound columns.

The survey covers the schedule-level techniques that move Jet toward the bound and that typical runtimes do not apply by default: effect-aware early I/O (sema-known opens, DNS, connects and fetches issued at process start); concurrent execution of effects sema proves independent, longest expected chain first; syscall batching (io_uring, writev, readahead) and zero-copy; elimination of unread outputs and stage fusion; compile-time initialized startup images; speculation limited to repeatable effect-free reads. Each gets a probe, a paired two-program cell, and observable behavior preserved (output, the order of visible effects, workload limits such as "at most 32 in flight"; no caching of results the program must compute). Proof: the same survey, each schedule-level technique with its probe and paired cell.

The Goose and Lobster mining run of 2026-10-23 ($JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/mine/goose-2026-10-23: 349 claims, 242 Goose and 107 Lobster; recall audit 3 at about 77%, with 65 misses not re-mined) is committed as a Docs/Research note with one prior-art row per source, as the mine-for-jet hand-in rule requires. Each claim that names a mechanism Jet could adopt (data stacks with bump reservation, bounds-check elimination, packed and narrow layouts, whole-program inlining) names its card or is marked as not fitting, with the reason. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Research/*goose*"` names the note, and every claim id in it resolves to a card or a not-fitting reason.

Why it matters: today the only board is a record of strings (Jetpack/Provider/Batteries/embedded/embedded.jet), registers are untyped U32 fields, and there is no interrupt registration seam.

Decisions: D-HW-DECLARE1=A, D-TARGET-SURFACE1, D-TARGET-MEMORY1, D-TARGET-LINKER1, D-HOST-CAPS1, D-CORE-BOUNDARY1=A.

criteria.text: An SVD reader package turns a vendor SVD file into a typed chip value with volatile register blocks, and interrupt and DMA ownership rows keep exact profile, channel and type identities on O0, O1 and O2 (D-HW-DECLARE1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Embedded/SVDChip` and an emulator run.
MMIO volatility is distinct from synchronization: a volatile register access implies no fence, and a fence needs its own call.
DMA and interrupt buffers are bounded and their cancellation is safe: a cancelled transfer releases its buffer only after the hardware stops.

A target rejects hardware its chip lacks at compile time, and unused hardware dependencies are left out of the build. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter hw_target_lacks_peripheral` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Hw/unused_dependency_excluded`.

Jet tests cover what the retired target_machines tests checked: the selected target machine, a no-OS machine refusing dev explicitly, an MCU firmware build writing ELF, map, audit and size budget, and the target provider fact matrix for present, missing and malformed facts.
Typed target capabilities and validated provider source cover MMIO, clock, entropy, scheduler, byte sink, allocator, panic and startup (D-TARGET-SURFACE1=A, D-HOST-CAPS1=A).

Chip knowledge lives in Core (D-CORE-BOUNDARY1=A): typed instruction entries (chip feature, Jet codegen encoding, plain Jet body checked against the chip before a bundle ships) are Core declarations marked by the instruction marker (its spelling registered in the syntax registry and ratified with #4570's jet_builtins work); Core is versioned against one kernel number; kernel-only Core functions expand at the call site; the compiler keeps only the kernel, targets, calling conventions and register kinds, migrated per Docs/Research/compiler-corelib-boundary-2026-10-04.md. A new chip entry lands as a Core change with no compiler edit, and Core loads lazily. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Hw/chip_entry_is_a_core_change`.

(moved from #6847 c14) Comptime on native O0 handles DMAStart and DMAWait, or refuses them with a registered #run stop (E3010 family, with its UI snapshot), in the same change that first makes a DMA channel reachable from a program (a board.<profile> import and a TargetMachine with hardware.dma_channels). Proof: a Comptime/ case that reaches dma.start and dma.wait at build time.

cards.title: Service supervision: one Service record, readiness, bounded restarts, a declared restart policy, and pipeline values
cards.body:
Destination: a service tree is supervised from declared data. One Service record (D-SERVICE-WORD1=A) covers the beginner run form and the expert fields; the supervisor separates start from readiness and bounds every restart and watch loop; restart policy is a field on the tree or worker line, not the `set_restart` setter (Core/Service/Service.jet); and `tasks.pipeline(source)…` builds a dataflow value whose pure stages run in parallel.

Why it matters: supervision today is a setter with a tree-wide strategy and no intensity, and Core has no pipeline value.

Decisions: D-SERVICE-WORD1=A. The restart-field and pipeline spellings are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Research: Docs/research/declarative-jet-2026-10-31.md section 3.6 (card #6513).

criteria.text: One Service record (D-SERVICE-WORD1=A) covers the run-only beginner form and the expert fields: readiness probes, restart, watch, ports, sockets, dependencies, shutdown, logs and limits.

The supervisor separates process start from readiness, reserves ports and sockets before release and reports a conflict as a typed error, and refuses dependency cycles. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Service/supervisor_readiness_` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter service_dependency_cycle`.
Restart budgets, backoff, watch debounce, readiness transitions, generation identity and failure states are bounded: each has a case that drives it past its bound.

Service start and stop order, process-tree cleanup on stop and cancel, and the D-JPK-SERVICEAUTH1 failure path run on task groups and core.process, and plans, logs and receipts use the existing log and receipt types, with no second scheduler.

A pipeline value: `tasks.pipeline(source).map(f).filter(p).sink(g)` builds a value whose pure stages run in parallel and fuse, and whose writing stage runs on one task; the spelling is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/Pipeline` on O0, O1 and O2.

Restart policy is declared, not set: `restart: .OneForOne(max:, within:)` is a field on the tree or worker line with an intensity budget, and `set_restart` (Core/Service/Service.jet) is deleted in the same cutover; the spelling is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: `git grep -n set_restart -- Core Examples` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Service/restart_intensity_`.

D-SERVICE-WORD1=A is built: one Service record type, whose run field takes an argument list or an output reference (Service{ run: packages.api }, the D-ECO-DECL1 form), so a package's own built output runs as a supervised service. Proof: a jetpack case declares Service{ run: outputs.api } and the service starts that output, plus a UI snapshot for a run reference that names no output. (was #6523 c12)

cards.title: Startup cost: dynamic symbol binding, setlocale and env capture dominate short programs (hello 8.8x, taskfile 22x asm)
cards.body: asm-parity on dev 45ab3b5ef5 (perf record cycles:u, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/asmpar-45ab/hot.sh): hello's cycles are ld.so symbol binding (do_lookup_x 24%, _dl_lookup_symbol_x 23%, _dl_check_all_versions 15%) and glibc tunables init (24%). taskfile spends 14% in check_match, 13% in _nl_intern_locale_data (a setlocale/locale load), 12% in jet_rt_host_env_capture, 12% in strcmp and 12% in record_in. Every cell pays this startup cost. Within the current dynamic-libc model (static linking is the owner ballot #5088): import only the libc symbols the program reaches, avoid eager binding of unused imports, don't load locale data the program never uses, and capture the environment lazily (#6493 is in wave 22). Proof: asm-parity hello and taskfile cycles columns drop, no cell worse in bytes or cycles, and output is identical.

CORRECTION (Codegen-1): the ld.so, tunables and locale rows in Main's hot.sh came from the taskset wrapper (perf record -- taskset BIN profiles taskset's own dynamic startup before exec). The asm-parity binaries are static, with no dynamic section and no libc. Real hello cost: 7,212 cycles:u / 2,642 instructions, about 1,200 of them the JET_CHECKED_ALLOC env scan that environment.md requires; the rest is syscalls and page faults (TLS, 12K stdout buffer, 256K sigaltstack, 4 sigactions, ioctl). taskfile: host_env_capture (#6493), alloc/free, stop_poll and thread_attach. The scope of this card is now those real startup costs. The long-running cells' profiles (fft, wordfreq, nbody, binparse, tensormap) are unaffected; taskset is negligible there.

criteria.text: The asm-parity hello and taskfile cycles:u and instructions columns drop against dev 45ab3b5ef5 (instructions, plus the median of at least 21 interleaved runs for cycles), no asm-parity cell is worse in bytes or cycles, and output is identical. Proof: `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate --cells hello,taskfile --runs 21` and then the full cell set.

End metric: startup is as fast as physically possible: exec-to-exit cycles and instructions of the hello and taskfile cells match their asm-parity references within noise. Proof: `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate --cells hello,taskfile`. (was #6414 c57)
taskfile-cli carries no state between invocations. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry taskfile-cli` passes with a fresh-state check between runs. (was #6954 c8)

A program's first task spawn costs no more than a steady spawn plus the unavoidable thread creation. Measured on p372 (-O2, idle CPUs, n=41): a first spawn and join takes 196 us median, against 12-14 us for the second. About 58 us is the pool sizing on the spawner's critical path: scheduler_worker_count, then cpu_available_parallelism, does 7 opens, 12 reads and 1 stat of cgroup and sysfs files, and JET_SCHEDULER_THREADS=8 drops it to 138 us. About 125 us is carrier start-up, mostly kernel time and 40-50 extra first-touch faults: the 256 KiB fault stack and its sigaltstack, the zeroed TCB, the guarded stack's mmap, mprotect and madvise, and the allocator's first per-thread use. Fix it generally (size the pool once, off the critical path and without the cgroup walk; make the first-touch work lazy or smaller), measured with jet perf. A Perf case asserts the first spawn costs at most 2x the steady spawn plus the thread-create floor measured in the same run.

cards.title: jet repl: evaluating 1 + 2 takes 3.6 s and 691 MB peak RSS; suite REPLs reach 5 GB
cards.body: Measured by Main 2026-11-01 08:15 EST with the wave-24 tree (a34ef0affd content), stage s2. The input file is the two lines '1 + 2' and ':quit'; run as jet repl < input with JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY set. Result: '3 : Int', 691,148 KB max RSS, 3.55 s wall. cards.title: Function-value copy: does f.copy() of an escaping closure share its captured state, give an independent copy, or get refused?
cards.body:
Question (owner/ballot): spec.md:889-905 ("Captures and escaping lambdas") says an escaping lambda owns its captures. Copy values are copied at closure creation, clonable values are cloned, and owned non-clonable values move. It never says what a *function value* does when it is copied (`alias: counter.copy()`) or bound twice.

Witness: tests/cases/run_regressions/shared_and_closure_owner_topology_is_preserved.case, fixture tests/fixtures/shared_owner_topology.jet:82-87.
  counter: make_counter(live)   // returns `(value: Int) -> { bucket.values.push(value) ... }` over a `:=` Bucket it owns
  alias: counter.copy()
  print(counter(1)); print(alias(2)); print(counter(3))
The ORACLE-LITERAL output (run_regressions.rs:174, never re-bless) is 102 / 202 / 302. bucket.values.len() grows 1, 2, 3 across counter and alias, so the alias **shares** the one captured environment, as a refcounted closure would.

Today: sema refuses with E0211 "`fn(Int) -> Int` can't be copied" (360e470044).

Alternatives:
- A: A function value is a cheap handle. `.copy()` (and implicit copy) shares the captured environment, as `Shared<T>` handles do (spec.md:1426-1431). Matches the oracle 102/202/302. Needs closure env refcounting in IR/runtime and a spec sentence.
- B: `.copy()` deep-clones the captured environment, so each copy has its own state. Requires every capture to be clonable, or E0211. The oracle would become 102/102/202 (re-blessing an ORACLE-LITERAL needs owner sign-off).
- C: Function values that own mutable captured state are not copyable (today's E0211). The spec gains that sentence, and the case's alias line is removed with owner sign-off (oracle lines 11-12 change).

Acceptance: spec.md "Captures and escaping lambdas" states the chosen rule. The fixture then runs on every tier with the decided output, and shared_and_closure_owner_topology_is_preserved passes (or is rewritten per C with a cited spec line).

Related fixture repairs already staged by CardClose-1 (CC-66 follow-up, not yet landed because this blocks the run):
- bare-block scopes become helper fns (S6-R, syntax-decisions.md:3949)
- `fn(Int) Int` becomes `fn(Int) -> Int` (spec.md:857)
- `String!` becomes `Err!` (E2417)
- untyped-lambda `return x` becomes the tail value
- SharedSnapshot `.value` becomes `.value()` (Main ruling, SharedOwner.jet:429)
- `!= .None` now type-checks (CC-66 sema fix, D-FLOWTYPE1)

cards.body:
## Outcome

Build the ratified D-REACT-REF1 outcome. The design and its claimed advantage are in Docs/proposals/memory-model-foundations-2026-09-27.md, section "Using the language level to replace stack layers".

## Gate

No implementation starts until criterion 1 is met (AGENTS.md, Adversarial design review). The ballot authorizes the direction, not the claim that it beats existing solutions.

React virtual DOM and memo, Solid and Svelte signals, Vue reactivity, MobX.

fine-grained update cost versus signals, lists and keyed reordering, derived and async state, effects and cleanup, cross-component and cross-task data, data reached through collections and foreign values, devtools visibility, and compile-time cost on large apps.

cards.body:
## Outcome

Build the ratified D-SECRETEDGE1 outcome. The design and its claimed advantage are in Docs/proposals/memory-model-foundations-2026-09-27.md, section "Using the language level to replace stack layers".

## Gate

No implementation starts until criterion 1 is met (AGENTS.md, Adversarial design review). The ballot authorizes the direction, not the claim that it beats existing solutions.

## Strongest existing solutions to judge against

Next.js server-only and taint APIs, SvelteKit $env/static/private, Remix .server modules, framework log scrubbing.

## Attack points the review must cover at minimum

derived values (hashes, lengths, error text), implicit flows, foreign calls and serialization, logging libraries, deliberate declassification, false positives that push users to bypass it, and side channels the type system cannot see.

log.text: Owner order 2026-11-14: paused and frozen cards are removed from their goals so they do not block closure; they stay tracked here. It was in goal G9; relink it on unpause.

criteria.text: A dated adversarial review in Docs/Audits attacks every claimed strength of D-SECRETEDGE1 against Next.js server-only and taint APIs, SvelteKit $env/static/private, Remix .server modules, framework log scrubbing: it states each peer's best case fairly with sources, covers at least derived values (hashes, lengths, error text), implicit flows, foreign calls and serialization, logging libraries, deliberate declassification, false positives that push users to bypass it, and side channels the type system cannot see, checks claims by code, probe, or measurement where possible, and gives each claim a verdict (holds, holds within stated limits, or fails). Every failed claim is redesigned and re-reviewed, and every gap has a card or ballot, before any implementation starts. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*secretedge1*"` names the dated review, with a verdict per claim.

The design as reviewed is implemented, with an executable example and golden output on every applicable tier (I5, I9), and a UI snapshot for each new diagnostic (I4). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/SecretEdge` on every applicable tier and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter Web/secret_edge`.

Each automatic choice follows choose, explain, pin: it is visible through jet inspect or an LSP hover with the fact that drove it, and an expert pin fails compilation when the program no longer satisfies it.

Before the design is presented to the owner as the solution, every downside the adversarial review finds is engineered away in the design and the redesign passes the review again; any downside that cannot be removed is named with its cost and best mitigation (AGENTS.md, Adversarial design review). Proof: the re-review section of the c1 audit lists every downside as removed, or named with its cost and mitigation.

cards.title: Leak freedom is structural: safe Jet cannot leak
cards.body: Owner rule, 2026-11-05: Jet never leaks memory. Leak freedom is part of the memory-safety guarantee (I1); only an expert #Unsafe block may leak, so the language must structurally prevent leaks rather than fix them case by case. On 2026-11-05 three lowering families leaked in safe code (c8a 5037b3ce72: a reassign after a move; c8b 2d712dd94a: a field read off a fresh call result; c8c: a loop over or an index into a fresh List or Map), found only because jet repl grew 6.2 GB over 9 turns. This card makes such a defect impossible to ship: the compiler checks its own output, and the suites fail any program that leaks.
cards.plan: 1. An ownership verifier pass after IR lowering. 2. A leak gate in the golden and cases suites, plus the compiler itself, using the checked allocator. 3. Fix every leak the two find, by lowering family. 4. An audit of every construct that could leak in safe code (shared values and cycles, tasks parked at exit, channels, globals, closures) with a structural rule for each, or an owner ballot where the rule is a language choice. 5. I1 in AGENTS.md states leak freedom.

log.text: Leak found and fixed under #6999 B (6999-B-move-params-a, batch 41): five Core.rows rows (core.files.__mkdtemp_raw, __temp_dir_raw and __temp_file_raw; core.net.__ip_from_bytes and __socket_from_parts) marked an argument as moved (&[false]) while the runtime export only reads it and never frees it, so every call leaked the argument. On dev, the new case Tests/Cases/MemorySemantics/core_host_rows_free_the_arguments_they_lend measures 29776 kB of RSS growth over 300k temp_dir calls and 93844 kB over 1M socket_addr_parse calls. The fix marks the rows lent, and the runtime_leaf_exports guard now refuses a row mask that disagrees with its binding. Gap for this card: no program can read an allocation counter, so leak cases fall back to VmRSS, which is coarse and platform-bound. A Core-readable live-allocation count (in core.mem or the testing kit) would let leak cases assert exact zero growth.

Golden leak-gate census, 2026-11-05 on dev 02602250cc (s1 with the checked allocator; runtime process roots tagged; under --checked-alloc the runtime runs the entry's drops instead of the exit shortcut): about 1170 of the golden programs leak (o0 1164, o1 1162, o2 1161 rows; about 100 more rows leak on only some tiers). On o0, 610 rows leak only runtime init roots (jet_rt_*_init, TLS keys), so the runtime frees or tags those at shutdown; 507 have real library or user leaks. Leak-gate rows: 3492 of 4715. Starting point for c2 and c3 when G19 is worked.

c3 progress (invariant fixes), f2ba7d34bf: the fresh-temporary-never-dropped family. loop x in make(), make()[i], make_map()[k], every non-mutating Map/Set builtin on a fresh receiver, and Set.from(make()) (buffer) now end the temporary. Before: 100-520 MB VmRSS per 40,000 rounds per shape on O0 and O2. Three new cases FAIL->PASS, one guard case PASS on both; every shape clean under --checked-alloc on O0 and O2; chain FIXED_POINT; golden A/B 267 = 267; cases A/B over 284 ids. Probe audit of the flat shapes (match, if pattern, struct method, String chains, ?. and ??, slices, tuple fields) is in the guard case.

criteria.text: After IR lowering, a verifier checks that every owned value, temporaries included, is dropped or moved exactly once on every path out of its scope, outside #Unsafe. It runs on every compile at O0, O1 and O2; a violation is an internal compiler error (exit 101), never a user diagnostic. A negative-control case shows it catching each of the 2026-11-05 leak shapes when the matching fix is reverted.

The golden and cases suites run their programs with the checked allocator and fail any row whose program exits with a live owned block allocated outside #Unsafe, at o0, o1 and o2. The compiler itself passes the same check: jet check and jet build over Core and over the compiler's own sources end with zero leaked blocks, and 9 jet repl turns of repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins stay flat. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden` and `--profile cases` with the leak gate on report zero leak rows at O0, O1 and O2, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Repl/repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins` stays flat over 9 turns.

Every leak the verifier or the leak gate finds is fixed at its root, per lowering family, each with a case per shape; the full suites then run with the leak gate on and show zero leak rows. Proof: with the leak gate on, `jet test Compiler --profile golden` and `--profile cases` report zero leak rows, and each fixed family has a `--filter leaks/` case.

An audit, committed under Docs/Audits, lists every construct that can keep memory alive in safe Jet (shared values and reference cycles, tasks or generators parked at exit, channels, globals and caches, closures and captures) and states the structural rule that prevents a leak for each, with a case; any rule that is a language choice goes to an owner ballot. Proof: the audit is committed under Docs/Audits, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Leaks/structural_rule_` has a case per construct.
AGENTS.md I1 states that safe Jet cannot leak memory (only #Unsafe may), and Docs/spec/philosophy.md's memory-safety guarantee says the same.
criteria.evidence: 520bfbfa0f: AGENTS.md I1 says memory safety includes leak freedom: safe Jet cannot leak memory, and only code inside an #Unsafe block or function may. Docs/spec/philosophy.md design priority 1 says safe Jet cannot leak memory: every value it allocates is freed, and only #Unsafe code may leak.

criteria.text: jet repl does not keep every turn's compile in memory (Repl.jet:338-348 held 773 MiB at 1 turn and 5.6 GiB at 9 on 2026-11-04). Memory per turn stays flat: 9 turns of repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins stay under 1 GiB (also #6543).
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6543 c5

criteria.text: A run-time leak and double-drop witness proves leak freedom per program. On 2026-11-12, JET_MEMORY_LEDGER recorded only unsafe sentry events, and the counting allocator cap did not trip on String allocations (a 32 MB copy ran under a 48 MB cap, #6677). A safe-Jet program run under the witness reports 0 live allocations at exit and fails on any double drop, on O0, O1 and O2. jet test and jet dev print the same witness (live allocations, unreleased foreign handles and Shared cycles, with their sites), and release builds carry no tracking.

D-EXIT-TASKS1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). When run returns, the runtime cancels every live task, with no OBSERVE_TASK_CAP limit, and drains until none is queued, ready or running, or until 1 s of monotonic time has passed, then exits with run's status. A waiting task unwinds at its wait and runs its cleanup. E3013's exit report is retired (registry row, explainer and the runtime_e3013 ui snapshot, which becomes a case exiting 0), and the leak witness names each abandoned task. spec.md states the rule. Proof: cases for a waiting task that cleans up and a busy loop that is abandoned after 1 s, on O0, O1, O2.

D-RETAIN-BOUND1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). The no-leak promise covers memory nothing can reach; data a live global, cache or task still reaches is the program's own. jet audit retention (also jet inspect audit retention, with --json) lists every store that can grow without a bound: #Memo(bound: none) caches and module Shared globals holding growable data, both exact, and loops that never end by themselves and keep appending, marked "may grow". Each row gives place, kind, name and type. help, man, completions and cli.md list it. Proof: a golden on the ballot program showing exactly its 2 rows, a --json golden, and a program with only bounded stores printing no rows.

cards.title: JSON event reader drains a document about 10x slower than parse
cards.body: Measured by GoldenRoots3 on dev aeeb2c479c (golden serde/json_selective, 1.05 MB document, --release): draining every event from the JSON reader takes 1.37 s against 80-123 ms for parse, and decode<Small> builds the whole Dyn tree before projecting (129 ms, 84 MB peak vs 67 MB for parse). Bring the event path to at least parse speed, let typed projection skip unselected fields without materializing them, and add a paired cell with a ceiling reference per the performance gate.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): 3d+ (perf). JSON event reader and parse beat every peer.

HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). These criteria stay open and unworked: c1 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c); c2 (owner order 2026-11-11 (no micro-optimization until the language is mostly stable; #5479 c).

Main 2026-11-08 03:35: reader speed slice by G1Lead, landing now. On the 1.09 MB 20-field doc (CPU time), the reader drains in 51 ms against 52-72 ms for parse; it started at 1110 ms. Per kind, reader vs parse: ints 24/36 ms, strings 30/40, objects 88/94. Remaining plan, set aside for cheaper G3 criteria per the pareto order: (a) typed projection, about 2-3 h. A compiler-private intrinsic encoding.__decode_keys<T>() gives the generated Decode its demanded wire keys, wired through CoreSignatures, CoreCallRows, the Sema backing gate and JetIR lowering. __decode_typed then skips the other root fields with a validating, non-materializing skip. (b) the paired performance cell. A gauntlet entry (e.g. formats.json-kernel) with a fixture, expected.out, and peers in rust, c, zig, go, python and node, plus a hand-written Tools/perf/asm-parity ref.S ceiling, about several hours.

criteria.text: Draining every event from the JSON reader is at least as fast as parse on the 1.05 MB serde/json_selective document, typed projection skips unselected fields without building a Dyn tree, and a paired perf cell records it against its peers (Jet/peer below 1.00; the ceiling ratio is reported only). Proof: the cell's row in Tools/Gauntlet/measurement-manifest.json and the gauntlet receipt.

cards.title: Every CLI flag must also be a setting: non-build commands (registry publish --force and others) have no settings home
cards.body: Standing owner order: every CLI flag is also a setting. The only flag↔setting table is JET_BUILD_OPTIONS (build profiles, fn build, pins), which only build, run and dev read. jet registry publish --force (CLICommands.jet:796; it also gates E1218 per #6600) and every other non-build command flag have no setting. First census every registered CLI flag against its setting home. Then ballot where non-build command settings live (e.g. package.jet publish: {…} vs a per-command settings table in jet settings), with same-program alternatives. Then build it, with one flag↔setting mechanism for all commands.

log.text: dev a95a9761d0: migrated 13 files (Land.jet, LaneCheck.jet, Chain.jet, CompilerRegistries.jet, CensusSnap2, Throughput.jet, Scaling/Gate, Scaling/Harness, orchestration SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, control_variables.jet) from control env vars to D-ENV-SURFACE1=A CLI flags (217/217 Tests/Guards, CensusSnap2 15/15, ScalingHarness 23/23, ScalingModuleLookupsProof 6/6, seed a0.0.46 verified); only Admit.jet:1242 -> Jetpack/Bootstrap/Check.jet:406 remains.

meet-6606 (seed-b8, dev cc09d22cb9, 29 lines PASS-only) credits c2 only. c1: the cases rows cover four families (keep-going, trace, opt-dump, fmt --check). c1 asks for a row per command family and a census of every registered flag; the full family list and a row for each are needed. c4: rows cover keep-going, trace and opt-dump. Still missing: the disable, verify and SSA-stress hooks, the GC trace, the phase counters and the memory ledger, plus proof that AGENTS.md, the skills and the repository tools use the flag rather than the variable. c6: the text and --json snapshots pass, but the redaction test (Controls.jet "a URL's user and password never show") wasn't among the lines, and the criterion's 'every registered variable that is set' needs a line without --command. Routed to ScriptAPI-2.

Edge the ballot did not cover: a relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME. ScriptAPI-50 refused it, which broke roots-sh (parity 0/11 on b8) and cache_cli_status. Decision: jet ignores a relative value and falls back to the default, as the XDG Base Directory specification requires. ScriptAPI-62 makes that fix, with cases.

Criteria c3-c7 added on the owner's order (2026-11-10 ~21:00, G5): environment variables become one registry in code, every behavior control becomes a flag or setting first, transport moves to one channel, one listing command is added, and the D-ENV-SURFACE1 ballot gates the public spellings. The census script is in Main's scratch (envcensus.mjs, envdoc.mjs).
Owner ruling 2026-11-09 (BoardPlanner C-G4-6): moved to G5 (one settings table). ScriptLead-15r, already built, lands; further work waits for G5 in the owner goal order.

D-CLI-SETTINGS-HOME1 posted for the owner after a CLEAN adversarial review (sol-reviewer, 2026-11-09): the flat commands: keys are added as A. It is a home-format vote only, not an implementation receipt. D-SCRIPT-LINE-HELPERS1 and D-RUN-TIER1 came back NOT CLEAN (a0_042 already promotes plain jet run, and the helper size claim loses to Perl) and go back to ScriptLead.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Q24 A): one registry. Every CLI command flag row gets a key <command>.<flag>, readable from package.jet settings and the user settings file; precedence flag, then package, then user (the JET_BUILD_OPTIONS mechanism). Destructive flags are marked not persistable and setting one is refused with a registered diagnostic. ScriptLead builds it.

Census (c1 first half), Main 2026-11-07, dev eb47eb7277 on seed a0_034. Method: jet help for all 49 commands and every action of the group commands (117 help pages), parsing each flag a usage line or flag row lists. A flag counts as homed when its long name is a JET_BUILD_OPTIONS row (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuildOptions.jet, 7 rows) and its command reads that table (build, run, dev). Result: 429 command-flag rows over 76 commands and actions. 21 are homed: build, run and dev each have 7 (backtrace, bounds, inline, libs, optimize, os, small). The other 408 rows (157 distinct flags) have none. The most common homeless flags are --json x52, --color x44, --quiet x44, --live x8, --verbose x7, --profile x6, --set x6, -p x6, --gate x5, --release x5, --target x5, --threads x5, --trace x5, --dry-run x5 and --allow x4. Rows per command: test 57, build 34, run 32, dev 26, inspect 26, new 17, cc 16, c++ 16, jobs 15, check 12, fmt 11, self 11, budget 9; registry has 7, including publish --force and --no-sign. Flags with a neighbouring but non-flag-keyed home (--allow/--deny to package authority, --target to package targets, --profile to build profiles) count as homeless, because none goes through one flag-to-setting mechanism. The census is regenerated on demand by $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/flags/{collect.sh,census.mjs} (scratch; the porting home is the CLI registry, not a committed table). Next: the ballot on where non-build command settings live, then one shared mechanism.

criteria.text: A census lists every registered CLI flag with its setting (or none); after the ratified ballot, every flag has exactly one setting through one shared flag-to-setting mechanism, with a cases row per command family proving that flag and setting have the same effect Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLISettings/flag_equals_setting_`, one row per command family.

Authority flags (--allow, -A, --gate, --token, --allow-unofficial) have no setting: the census marks them never persisted, and a package.jet or user settings key for one is refused with a registered diagnostic (owner 2026-11-09); a cases row proves the refusal.
criteria.evidence: Lander meet-6606 on seed-b8 at dev cc09d22cb9, each line judged PASS-only with its source printed. Line 8: tests/cases/cli_settings/permission_flags_are_never_settings.case, landed in fe4c65249b (ScriptAPI-66), shows that a package.jet commands block or the user settings file naming --allow, -A, --gate, --token or --allow-unofficial is refused with the registered E2117 before the program starts. Lines 19-20: the CommandSettings.jet census tests "no flag that gives permissions is a setting" and "a remembered destructive flag is refused as its CLI snapshot records" (ScriptAPI-49/50, 5263e2258c) mark them never persisted. D-ENV-SURFACE1 was ratified A on 2026-11-11.

criteria.text: Owner 2026-11-10 ~21:00: "seems like we rely heavily on env vars ... other languages just use build settings and build flags, not a ton of hidden envvars ... yes we need to fix that". Main's census on dev c2cecce162: code reads about 140 JET_/JETPACK_ variables (193 names in all), and Docs/Spec/Reference/environment.md, which calls itself the registry, lists 66 plus 3 wildcard families; 113 read names are on no list. One registry in code holds every environment variable that jet, jetpack, the runtime, Core or a repository tool reads. Each row gives the name, the owning module, its kind (user, automation, maintainer, transport between Jet processes, or test hook), its value type and default, and the flag or setting it overrides. A guard refuses a read of a name that has no row, across Compiler, Core, Jetpack and Tools. environment.md is generated from the registry, with a --check that the lane checks run. Zero unregistered reads. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter env_registry_covers_every_read`, and the environment.md generator's `--check` passes.

Every user, automation or maintainer behavior control is a CLI flag or a settings key first, and its environment variable only overrides that setting, through the shared flag-to-setting mechanism of c1. The controls include keep-going and its report and skip lists, trace file and trace detail, the optimizer dump, disable, verify and SSA-stress hooks, the GC trace, phase counters and the memory ledger. AGENTS.md, the skills and the repository tools use the flag, not the variable. A cases row per family proves the flag, the setting and the variable have the same effect. D-ENV-SURFACE1=A (ratified 2026-11-11): concise descriptive flags and the existing command-qualified setting names.

Transport between Jet-owned processes goes through one channel: argv, or one handoff file or descriptor that the parent passes to the child. It does not go through a separate environment name per value. The JET_FRONT_*, JET_DEVELOPMENT_RECEIPT_*, JET_DEVTOOLS_RELAY_*, JET_PROVE_*, JET_EVIDENCE_*, JET_TEST_SUITE_ROOT, JET_TEST_PLAN, JET_TEST_SETTINGS and JET_READ_SCOPE families are cut over in one greenfield cutover, with no old names kept. A launched user program inherits no Jet transport variable it does not own (a run case proves its environment). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Run/launched_program_inherits_no_jet_transport_vars`, and git grep finds none of the listed families in Compiler, Core or Jetpack.

D-ENV-SURFACE1=A: the env command group gains a pure vars listing, not a new environment manager. It prints every registered variable that is set, with its effective value and where that value came from (environment, setting, flag or default), redacts secret values, and has text and --json forms with UI snapshots, like `go env`.
