cards.title: core.ui renderer is the fastest 2D renderer: gauntlet cells against Blend2D, Skia raster, tiny-skia and cairo/pixman, with an asm-parity ceiling
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-09: 'we should be the fastest renderer especially since we have top to bottom full control over the whole language stack.' Today a 900x600 frame (a full gradient, ~15 shapes, ~7 text lines) takes ~140 ms at O0 and ~55 ms at O2. Under the AGENTS.md performance gate, core.ui's rasterizer (Core/Ui/Draw.jet and the font rasterizer) gets required cells in the GUI-applications area. For each workload, Jet/peer must be below 1.00 against every matched CPU 2D renderer (Blend2D, Skia's raster backend, tiny-skia, cairo/pixman), and Jet/ceiling at most 1.00 against a hand-written SIMD reference (asm-parity) doing the same work, on every tier (O0 included, since  is what users run) and in both cycles and bytes. The workloads: solid and gradient fills, anti-aliased paths and shapes (rects, rounded rects, circles, polygons), alpha blending (straight and premultiplied), anti-aliased glyph text, image blits and scaling, and full-frame redraw at 1080p and 4K. Use the whole stack: SIMD in the runtime or Core through vetted internals, compiler codegen (bounds-check elimination, vectorizing span loops) and data layout. Fix compiler-side gaps at their root in the compiler, not by hand-unrolled Jet. Semantics and pixels are identical on every tier.
cards.plan: 1. Gauntlet cells plus peer harness: same scenes, same pixels (compared as images), peers built at their best settings. 2. asm-parity ceiling references with the best known technique (AVX2/AVX-512 span fill and blend, analytic coverage rasterization). 3. Profile Jet per workload; split the gap into rasterizer algorithm, codegen and runtime. 4. Close the gap: algorithm first (span and coverage pipelines like Blend2D's), then codegen defects as compiler cards. 5. Gate: every cell passes both stages.

log.text: HELD by owner order 2026-11-11 (no small optimizations until the language is mostly stable; architecture and regression fixes go first, per #5479 c5-c8). WaylandLead3 numbers, 1080p best of 5, O0 before->after: clear 37.5->0.9 ms, fill_opaque 37.4->0.8, fill_alpha 108->44, gradient_v 333->0.96, gradient_h 417->0.99, circle_r300 9.8->6.0, rounded 13.2->9.1, triangle 26->16.7; owner demo frame 900x600 99->4.6 ms at O0 (3.9 at O2). AA Atkinson text: 7 lines in 344 us at O0. Byte-identical to the per-pixel reference. Remaining: span/coverage pipeline, translucent fill, a [U32] canvas, and gauntlet cells. Compiler defects are on a child card.

criteria.text: The canonical measurement manifest and Tools/Perf/AsmParity/cells.json carry renderer cells: fills, gradients, AA shapes, blending, AA text, blits/scaling, and full-frame 1080p and 4K. Each has an image-equality check against every peer (Blend2D, Skia raster, tiny-skia, cairo/pixman) and a hand-written SIMD ceiling reference. Proof: `node --test Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs` passes with the renderer rows, and each cell is listed in Tools/Perf/AsmParity/cells.json.

Every renderer cell passes the peer floor on every tier (O0, O1, O2): Jet/peer < 1.00 for every peer in cycles and bytes, with its Jet/ceiling ratio reported. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs` over the renderer entry of c1 shows no peer loss.

A native window redraws a full 1080p frame of the showcase scene well inside one refresh at O0 (jet run), measured by frame_stats with no missed frames over 60 s. Proof: a committed 60 s frame_stats receipt with zero missed frames.

core.ui GPU path (#6722): gauntlet cells pair the GPU path with the software path and with the peers named on this card, with a ceiling reference, per the performance gate. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry ui-gpu` shows no loss.

cards.title: Codegen: pixel-loop throughput (fill leaf through a &struct field place, slow U64 arithmetic at O2, O0 indexed stores ~3 ns/element)
cards.body: Found by WaylandLead3 while speeding up the core.ui rasterizer (#6718); the renderer lane's Micro.jet repro is gone, so the proofs are cases and the pixel-loops gauntlet entry. (1) The O2 fill leaf doesn't fire for stores through a &struct field place: 1.15 ns/B vs 0.07 ns/B for a local. (2) U64 arithmetic takes ~10 ns/iteration even at O2, no faster than O0. (3) An O0 indexed store costs ~3 ns/element, so per-pixel Jet code can't redraw 1080p in a few ms at O0 (jet run). Fix each at its root in the compiler (IR/backend), not with library workarounds. The same semantics on every tier (I9).

log.text: BoardPlanner review 2026-11-09 (dev 6a06b917cb). Speed or size card: moved from no goal to G11. Owner order 2026-11-09: all speed and size work is G11.

criteria.text: Stores through a &struct field place reach the O2 fill leaf, as stores to a local do. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter fill_leaf_through_a_struct_field_place` shows the fill leaf in the O2 IR of the field-place loop.

U64 arithmetic at O2 compiles to native 64-bit instructions with no per-operation call or check beyond Jet's overflow meaning. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter u64_arithmetic_is_native_at_o2` (the O2 IR of the loop has no runtime call).

An O0 indexed store costs no more than the bounds check plus the store, so per-pixel code can redraw 1080p in a few ms under jet run. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry pixel-loops` reports at most 1 ns per element for the O0 indexed-store row.

A loop that grows an Int geometrically through wrapping(...) or saturating(...), such as an FNV-1a hash `h = wrapping((h ^ byte) * PRIME)`, gets the L2511 ExactIntSpill tidy diagnostic naming the repair (I64 or U64, or a range-typed Int), because wrapping on an unbounded Int is its exact operator and never wraps (with a _quiet twin on U64 that stays silent); and the same hash written on U64 compiles to a machine multiply and hashes 1 MB in milliseconds at O0, O1 and O2 (a Run golden with a time bound).

cards.title: Games: Jet ships every primitive needed to build a full high-resolution 3D game (no engine)
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-09): Jet is to be the best language for making games, so it must be capable of rendering full high-resolution 3D games. Do not build a 3D rendering engine now, but ship all the tools and primitives needed to make one: GPU device, swapchain and presentation on the native window, buffers, textures, render passes and pipelines, shaders written in Jet (D-GPU-SHADER-SURFACE1), GPU compute, 3D math (vectors, matrices, quaternions, SIMD), image and mesh asset loading, raw and relative input, audio, frame pacing and GPU timing. Related cards: #c0ce571w (shader stages and pipelines), #c0li0kor (GPU kernels), #c084tcrl (device providers), #c0776o2m (game platform layer), #c0ba141x (linking model: GPU drivers need the platform loader). First step: a gap map against code, then ballots for every public API.

criteria.text: A dated gap map (Docs/Research) lists each primitive a high-resolution 3D game needs and, for each, what Jet has today, proven by code, an example or a probe, and what is missing, the dependencies, the owner gates and the related cards.
Every missing public API or new syntax has a Tower ballot that has passed adversarial review before it reaches the owner.

An executable example draws a lit, textured, depth-tested 3D mesh of at least 100k triangles at 2560x1440 through the GPU in a native window, using only shipped primitives and no engine code in Core, with golden-tested output (headless image hash) on every applicable tier.
Gauntlet cells measure the GPU path (frame time and draw submission cost) against C with Vulkan and Rust with wgpu, with an asm-parity ceiling reference, per the performance gate.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #4731 c3

cards.title: core.ui GPU acceleration in native Jet, with the same look native and in the browser
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-09, on the Showcase: 'it would also be excellent if it can be gpu accelerated - again with native jet support, not some additional dsl or sub language, but native jet', and 'we want this to look the same whether it is running in a native app or in a browser'. Standing direction: one unified GPU language built into core Jet (ratified markers: #Shader for graphics, D-GPU-SHADER-SURFACE1=B; Kernel for compute, D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1), working on any GPU out of the box, with no per-vendor or per-OS DSLs. Conflict: D-GPU-UI1=A keeps desktop defaults on software (a static single file, no driver loading), so a GPU default on desktop needs a new owner ballot that revises it, tied to the linking-model ballot #c0ba141x (GPU drivers need the platform loader). Open technical questions for the ballot: GPU rasterization isn't bit-identical across vendors, so 'same look' must be defined (bit-identical through the software path vs perceptually identical through the GPU), and how a static musl binary reaches the system Vulkan/WebGPU driver.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): BLOCKED. c1 is an owner ballot revising D-GPU-UI1; c2 and c3 follow it.

criteria.text: An adversarially reviewed owner ballot (revising D-GPU-UI1) decides the desktop and web GPU default for core.ui, the fallback, the driver-loading model, and what 'the same look native and in the browser' means, with same-program alternatives. Proof: `timeout 120 node Tools/tower/tower.mjs decision show` for the D-GPU-UI1 revision shows it ratified with its review.

core.ui draws through the GPU from native Jet code only (#Shader/#Kernel), with no shader-language source, per-vendor path or DSL in the repository, on Linux native and in the browser. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter UI/GPUDraw` on Linux native and web, and `git ls-files "*.wgsl" "*.glsl" "*.hlsl" "*.metal"` prints nothing.

The same Showcase program renders the same look native and in the browser, proven by headless checksums or a perceptual-difference bound the ballot fixes, on every applicable tier. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter UI/ShowcaseSameLook` on native and web.

cards.title: I1: values leak: boxed trait values are never dropped, and branch lowerings carry a move from one path onto the other
cards.body: ReplMem (2026-11-09): a trait-value row (Compiler/JetIR BuildTypes.jet:286) is a Pointer row with no drop and no clone, so a boxed trait value has no drop glue and its payload leaks. A strong_count probe leaks one per binding. In the compiler, Pipeline.jet's compiler_queries (a JetEvalCompilerQueryHost trait value) holds a Shared context whose eval_config.native keeps the whole JetEvalNativeSession (about 3.25 MB image plus the child) alive on every compile: the REPL residual of about 12 MB per turn. The fix gives trait values drop glue that dispatches on the payload's implementer, keeping today's observable copy and alias semantics as the spec states them, and handles move-receiver dynamic calls.

log.text: Closer ranking (orchestrator, 2026-11-24T10:07Z), smallest remaining work first: 1 #6901 (c10 fix in batch 22; proof only), 2 #5007 (c10/c11 fix in batch 22; proof only), 3 #6853 (c4 in batch 23; c8 needs c8b-fix, ~1h), 4 #4720 (all 5 open criteria have fixes in batch 23; proofs plus fixes), 5 #6727 (c4 per-turn REPL retention, root fix ~2-4h), 6 #6902 (5 open, completion work ~1 day). Closer A G1Facts-2: #6853, #5007, #4720. Closer B G2Editor: #6901, #6727, #6902. Epoch agents on G1: G1Generation-2 (#6851), TypeIDSlice3-3 (#6852).

cards.title: Peer floor, enforced structurally: Jet is faster and uses less peak memory than every other language
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-11 late. A Jet program must be faster and use less peak memory than the same program in any other language. Only highly optimized hand-written machine code is exempt, and Jet aims as close to it as it can. A loss to any peer on wall time or peak memory is a codegen, runtime or Core failure. It is fixed generally, structurally and robustly in the mechanism every program uses, never per cell, so that the result holds for programs nobody measured. The machine ceiling stays the hill-climbing stage (G13): its ratio is reported, but it holds no cell until the owner opens it.

log.text: Main 2026-11-12, found by G11Speed-4 measuring c3: the gauntlet's run tier reuses each compiled peer's binary-only row (rust, c, zig, go), comparing jet run (a cold compile plus the run) with a prebuilt binary. That is mismatched evidence, and it contradicts the ratified run-cell rule: jet run time-to-answer is gated, after an edit and on a repeat run, against lua, luajit, python3 and node; the hello cell must come within 0.5 ms of a minimal hand-written program; the first run after install is reported only. The manifest's report_contract.peer_measurement ratio_tiers [aot, run], which reuses peer rows for every Jet tier, is the defect. G11Speed-4 is fixing the manifest contract and run.mjs so run-tier ratios use only the interpreted peers and compiled peers gate aot and build time. The c3 census waits for that fix and runs on b12. Sieve smoke on b11: aot beats all 5 peers on wall and peak; jet run is 0.73 s / 271 MB, all front end over Core (load 280 ms, comptime.bodies 210 ms, core_demand 140 ms, finalize 130 ms), which is the #6759 root.

criteria.text: The perf gate encodes the peer floor: on the canonical manifest it fails every required cell where Jet/peer is at or above 1.00 on wall time or on peak memory for any matched peer, names the cell, peer, metric and ratio, and reports the asm-ceiling ratio without failing on it. A unit test plants one time loss and one memory loss and expects both refusals.
criteria.evidence: G11Speed-G40 landed on dev 6ca4d72969 (tool-only: Tools/gauntlet/harness run.mjs, status.mjs, measurement-manifest.test.mjs, matrix.json). The gate fails a cell at Jet/peer >= 1.00 on wall or peak memory for any matched peer, names cell/peer/metric/ratio, and reports the ceiling ratio without failing. Out: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Lander/loop/out/G11Speed-G40/{1..6}.out.

criteria.text: A loss census on the current compiler lists every cell, peer and metric where Jet loses. It groups the losses by root (the codegen, runtime or Core mechanism responsible), and each root is on a card with its general fix. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*loss-census*"` names the committed census, each root row naming its card.

Structural coverage beyond the cells: a generated or curated corpus of at least 30 programs that use the language's features in varied ways (the gauntlet programs and their peer twins) is measured against the peers on wall time and peak memory, and its losses join the census, so that a fix that only helps a measured cell is caught. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry coverage-corpus` measures all 30 or more programs against the peers.

The loss census is empty: on the canonical manifest and the coverage corpus, Jet beats every matched peer on wall time and peak memory, each fix proven on a second program that uses the feature differently. Proof: the census rerun on the canonical manifest and the coverage corpus lists no loss.

Peak memory is measured per program, not per harness. The gauntlet's peak_rss readings no longer inherit the timer's own high-water mark across exec: each reading is the measured process's own exact VmHWM, read at its exit, for every peer and Jet alike. Proof: the Jet hello binary reads under 1 MB through both the gauntlet timer and GNU time; coreutils true reads within 5% of its exact /proc VmHWM at exit; the timer's own overhead on wall time is reported for one cell; and the hello cell's rss is re-judged under the fixed timer. (Found 2026-11-12: timer.py's ru_maxrss gave every reading a floor of about 15.3 MB.)

ScriptBench peak memory is measured per program too. Its rss column comes from hyperfine's memory_usage_byte, which reads hyperfine's own high-water floor: Jet hello (exactly 0.19 MB) and coreutils true (exactly 2.47 MB) both read 3.66 MB, so every rss row under about 3.7 MB is the harness floor. Bench.jet reads each run's exact VmHWM at exit through the G51 launcher. Proof: the hello and true rows read within 5% of their /proc VmHWM, and the ScriptBench rss rows are re-judged.

cards.title: Cold compile of a small script is about 1-4 s, and comptime.bodies is its largest phase
cards.body: Measured by G4Ports-1, 2026-11-11, on seed-b9, from the #5072 port twins (PortBars runs each twin from source, so every case pays a cold compile). jetc-trace, a 148-line file: jet run 1063 ms, against a 3 ms run of the built binary and node's 24 ms. Its phases: comptime.bodies 0.29 s (4 comptime programs built and run), load 0.26, sema.finalize 0.19, register 0.07, ir.build+opt+x64 0.07, link about 0.01. run-cold-context: jet run -- --help takes 4108 ms against node's 40 ms. Its phases: comptime.bodies 1.26 s (31 programs, 381 functions), sema.finalize 0.80, load 0.60, ir.opt 0.40, register 0.23, ir.build 0.08, x64 0.08. The port bar measures exactly what the 30M lines/s cold-compile target is about: the cost is general compile cost, not twin code.

c10 known gap (Speed-3-2, 2026-11-15): core.rt stays in the system layer. Moving it to the prelude needs Instant (public core.time surface) below core.time, and no D-CORE-LAYERS1 row allows that; changing RealtimeStream.next_deadline() to a raw Int was refused as a public API change. Cost, measured on the p178 seed (median of 5): a core.rt-only jet check takes 108 ms / 86 MB, of which core.time is about 60 ms / 28 MB. Removing it needs a ballot that moves a monotonic clock type to the prelude layer.

c10 known gap (Speed-3-2, 2026-11-15): core.rt stays in the system layer, not the prelude row D-CORE-LAYERS1=A lists it in. Reason: RealtimeStream.next_deadline() returns core.time's Instant (data layer). No D-CORE-LAYERS1 row puts Instant or a monotonic clock type in the prelude layer. The only allowance is that helpers may sit one layer below their natural home, and Instant is public core.time surface, not a helper. Moving Instant down would change its home module and surface, and returning raw Int ns is a public API change (withdrawn c10-rt). Cost, measured on the p178 seed with jet check, median of 5 runs, shared JET_STORE_DIR: a program that imports only core.rt (tests/cases/corelib/fixtures/rt_next_deadline_without_time_import/main.jet) takes 108 ms at 86 MB peak and loads Core/Time/Time.jet (8.2 ms parse CPU). An empty program takes 38 ms at 55.5 MB. A core.time-only program (time.instant()) takes 100 ms at 83 MB. So core.time accounts for about 60 ms and 28 MB of each core.rt-only check. Only programs that import core.rt without core.time pay it. Closing it needs a ballot that either gives the prelude a monotonic instant type or changes next_deadline's result type.

Main 2026-11-15: A2a (6eb1df37a7) regresses the compiler build's load. Small Core-heavy loads get faster (102-126 ms to 73-108 ms). Root: jet_driver_core_restore_bodies re-lexes and re-parses each lazy module's whole text after the head parse, so a mostly reached module costs about 1.1 full parses, and the pass holds every restored source at once. The big load restores 2960 bodies and saves only 774 (9%). Decision (operational): restore parses only the kept bodies' byte ranges recorded by the head parse, frees each module's source after restore, and reports the tokens actually lexed. Proof: the same A/B no higher than without a2a, with the CoreInterface equality tests passing.

criteria.text: Cold script cost: `jet file.jet` for a script importing core.process compiles and runs from cold, with no reuse, in less wall time and peak memory than the original tool it replaces. Today (ScriptAPI-2, PortBars outputs, 2026-11-11) b4 pays 1.1-1.6 s and 355-388 MB per run, against originals of 37-1700 ms and 5.8-57 MB, so all 7 measured tool twins fail the speed and memory bars (e.g. census-snap2 21086 ms / 422 MB vs 1117 ms / 47.5 MB). Acceptance: a per-phase CPU and peak-RSS breakdown of that script on the batch compiler names each root (parse/import/sema/lowering/emit/link of Core modules the script does not reach, eager whole-module work, arena sizing); each root is fixed in the general path and proven on a second script; the PortBars speed and memory bars pass on the census-snap2 and roots-mjs entries with cold compile counted. Reuse is not the fix: the standing order counts cold compile time. Proof: `jet Tools/Gauntlet/PortBars.jet` speed and memory bars for census-snap2 and roots-mjs, cold compile counted. (was #6527 c10)

Peak memory: a small Jet tool's peak RSS is no higher than its original's on every PortBars entry. ScriptAPI-2 measured Jet at about 19-21 MB against bash's 7-12 MB on batch10, integrate10, streamb10 and verify-rows, and the cost is the runtime's baseline, not the twins. The fix goes in the general mechanism (runtime start-up, reserved heap or arena sizing, and eagerly mapped tables), and is proven on a second small program. PortBars shows peak memory PASS on all nine. Part 1 (ScriptAPI-3, image layout locality and the build key; it rides t16) took the warm small-script peak from 15.5 MB to 7.1-7.5 MB, and batch10, integrate10 and streamb10 still lose (11.8 against 10.6 MB, 12.9 against 8.6, 10.6 against 8.6), while verify-rows ties. Proof: `jet Tools/Gauntlet/PortBars.jet` shows peak memory PASS on all nine entries. (was #6639 c4)

An uncached `jet file.jet` (a fresh cache dir: compile from cold, link and run from memory) beats python3 and node on wall time and peak memory, with no script cache, result cache or incremental state serving the run. Measured 2026-11-11 with GNU time on hello world (seed-t21): uncached `jet hello.jet` takes 30 ms and 36-40 MB, a script-cache hit 20-30 ms and 8.7-10.7 MB, the built O1 binary 0 ms and 256 KB, python3 10 ms and 13.1 MB, node 20 ms and 60 MB. Name where the uncached 30 ms and 37 MB go (front end, sema, lowering, emission, link, runtime start), fix them in those general mechanisms toward the 30M lines/s compile target, and prove it on hello world and on a repository tool twin. Proof: a committed GNU time receipt for hello and a repository tool twin, with the phase breakdown. (was #6639 c5)

A body loaded from precompiled Core costs at most a tenth of checking it from text. Today it costs 28-85 µs per load against 4-7 µs per text check (x12-x20 on rcc and summarize, p202 core-interface receipt, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/c15-p201-p202/receipt.md). In the ballot program, `big.len()` of a folded 50 MB String folds to its constant, and the emitted IR holds no Unicode scalar count over it. Proof: jet inspect decisions shows the folded length, and a case checks the IR.

Bytes of a build-time value that no run-time code reads are not emitted. In the D-COMPTIME-SIZE1 program (two 50 MB repeats used only for their lengths), the --optimize=full binary holds neither run and is within 10% of the size of the same program reading its size at run time (136,272 bytes on seed-b13). criteria.text: D-COMPTIME-SIZE1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). One fixed storage rule applies to every emitted value at O0, O1, O2 and web, with no switch. A value of at least 64 KiB whose bytes repeat one pattern of at most 64 bytes is stored as pattern plus length, and an all-zero value as zero-fill. Item reads, length, loops, slices, comparisons, searches and hashing work on the pattern. print and file or socket writes stream from one reused 64 KiB buffer. A use that needs fixed bytes, such as a [U8] parameter or foreign code, fills it once under a guard into reserved read-only pages. jet inspect decisions lists each pattern value. Proof: identical output digests on every tier, binary size never above raw, the ballot program near 50.1 MB, and a racing-threads fill-once case.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #7039 c2

criteria.text: D-COMPTIME-SIZE1=A author path: core.archive.zstd compress writes real compressed blocks, not only stored blocks, and round-trips through zstd.decompress. `jet inspect decisions --estimate` prints each large raw value's stored size and its zstd-estimated size, running only when asked. Proof: a golden of --estimate and a round-trip test.

cards.title: Tests fail under machine load: a wall-clock step limit turns slow into failed
cards.body: Owner, 2026-11-12: a test that fails under load, rather than passing more slowly, is a reliability defect. In the a0.0.45 admit of dev 2844b04984 (run beside a train build, landings and probes), about 200 rows across candidate chunks 2-5 and 8 were TIMEOUT or ERROR. 82 golden, 20 ui and 59 cases rows passed only on retry. Five browser_bidi and web_app rows ERRORed with an empty 'free-port probe failed', because the probe's own wall-clock timeout was reported without its reason. The root: JetTestKit gives every step a 60 s wall-clock timeout (Compiler/JetTestKit/Source/Exec.jet KitOptions timeout: 60, process.cmd(...).timeout), so a loaded host's slowness is judged as failure. The admit retry masks it instead of fixing it.

log.text: Owner ratified D-BUILD-TARGETFACTS1=A, D-DERIV-READ1=A and D-DEBUG-PREP1=A (2026-11-24). Assigned: #5007 c7-c9 and #6848 c8 to G1Facts; #5007 c10-c11 and #6772 c15 to G1Generation-2 after the #6846 c12 family-Self fix.
Correction to the c13 evidence: across the 50 runs the 1-minute load ran from 25.4 to 246.4, with a median of 138.4, not 138 to 246. Every run was still during the p435 full suite.

c9 not met: WebBrowser/browser_test_ui_mode passed in the 9 full suites p400-p419, but it failed in p399 (11-21 01:32) with the same "`notes` failed on chromium after 2 attempts: browser protocol failed", after the late-reply fix dcee077542 (11-20) had landed, and nothing browser-related landed since. The streak is not a root fix; the wait or read that gives up under load is still to be found.

c5 case half passes: fe131e30c3 on dev, jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter build_entry/run_steps_stop_a_looping_step_at_its_cpu_limit gives PASS 1 with bwrap on PATH (gate-p66, 2026-11-14). The loaded jet build --profile dev Compiler half and the c3 load sweep are pending: they're Main heavy-slot jobs after the batch compiler.

criteria.text: A test step's limit judges the work, not the host's load: JetTestKit bounds each step by the CPU time of the step's process tree (unaffected by other load). The wall-clock limit stays only as a hang guard, set far enough out that a loaded host can't reach it on a working step. A hit on either limit reports TIMEOUT with the limit kind, the CPU and wall seconds used, and the step. A Core.jet #Test proves a CPU-bound step that exceeds the CPU limit is TIMEOUT (cpu) and that a step sleeping past its wall guard is TIMEOUT (wall).
criteria.evidence: f15ece1132 on dev. 2026-11-14 15:0x, gate-p66 jet on dev 6cd4312a1a: jet test Compiler/JetTestKit/Tests/Core.jet --filter 'past its CPU limit' gives 1 passed, 0 failed

criteria.text: Every helper inside a test step that has its own deadline reports a deadline miss with its reason, never as an ERROR with an empty message. This covers the free-port probe (kit_steps_free_ports, StepsTokens.jet) and any readiness or port wait in the case harness. A case forces the free-port probe past its deadline and checks the TIMEOUT reason.
criteria.evidence: f15ece1132 on dev. jet test Compiler/JetTestKit/Tests/StepsHost.jet --filter 'free-port probe past its deadline' gives 1/0, and --filter 'host-port cases hold' gives 1/0 (gate-p66, 2026-11-14)

criteria.text: Load sweep: the corpus rows that were TIMEOUT, ERROR, or passed only on retry in the a0.0.45 admit are run again while a load generator holds every core busy (for example stress-ng at 2x the core count). Every row passes, and each failure found on the way is fixed at its root: either the harness limit, or a product deadline. A product deadline in Jet's runtime or Core (a BiDi handshake, a service delivery wait, a readiness wait) waits on its event or uses the user's own deadline, never a fixed wall time that load can exhaust. The rows, the generator and the result are recorded. Proof: the recorded load-sweep result under Docs/Audits lists every row as PASS under the named load generator.

The release gate stops masking load sensitivity: a row that fails and then passes on retry is reported in REPORT.md as a flaky row with its two outcomes, and fails the gate unless it carries a disposition that names an owning card.
criteria.evidence: f15ece1132 on dev. jet test Tools/release/Tests.jet --filter 'passed only on retry' gives 1 passed, 0 failed (gate-p66, 2026-11-14)

criteria.text: A build action's time limit judges the action's work, not the host's load, the same as test steps (c1). It bounds the action by the CPU time of its process tree and keeps a wall-clock limit only as a far-out hang guard. Today, on G6Meta-7-r5's CHAIN line 13 (b14, 08:13), jet build --profile dev Compiler failed with E3505 'Build action runtime ran past its time limit of 600000ms' at a 10.9G peak while the deferred pass and a 30G probe loaded the host, while the unloaded base passed. Proof: that build passes with every core held busy by a load generator, and a case shows a looping action still stops at its CPU limit with E3505.

On O0, the `jet dev` step budget (E2202), `jet debug` (E2203) and the REPL (E1802) each have a working Jet implementation or an owner-ratified retirement. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E2202` (and the same for E2203 and E1802) shows the working path, or the decision ID is cited. (was #6418 c146)

The rows that failed only under full-suite load in cycles p220-p225 pass under that load, fixed at their root (a timing or resource assumption in the test or runtime), not by retry: Tests/Cases/HTTPServerLifecycle/plain_http11_keepalive_pipelines_in_order_and_closes_at_boundaries (tcp_shutdown write 'finish request write' panic in p225; passes 3/3 alone on the p225 batch compiler), the DeadlineContext o1 golden, the TLS dudect case, the FiberLiveness C toolchain unpack race and Tests/Cases/WebScaffold/jet_new_native_scaffold_builds_for_explicit_web_target (poll deadline exceeded in p226; passes 2/2 alone), Tests/Cases/FFIRust/rust_extern_build_killed_mid_way_leaves_no_workspace_behind (the same C toolchain unpack race, p227; Tests/Cases/Cffi/concurrent_bridges_share_one_target_publish_without_racing hit it in p229) and Tests/Run/Concurrency/ConformanceCapsule o2 (the shield printed past its cancel in p227; passes 3/3 on o0/o1/o2 alone). Proof: three consecutive full collect-all suite runs on batch compilers list none of them. p232: Tests/Cases/CoreLib/core_net_tcp_read_uses_scheduler_and_returns_typed_cancellation (server task failed under load; no p232 commit touches it). p233: Tests/Cases/TaskControlTiers/carriers_come_from_the_runtime_or_from_the_c_closures_libc (the same C toolchain unpack race).

RuntimeStops/stack_overflow_under_jet_run_stops_within_a_second_and_4_gib holds its one-second bound under suite load, or measures CPU time instead of wall time. It failed in the p282 and p284 suites and passed alone both times. Proof: it passes in 5 consecutive full cases suites.
criteria.evidence: On dev 24356fa7b8 (p419) and the batch compilers before it: RuntimeStops/stack_overflow_under_jet_run_stops_within_a_second_and_4_gib PASS in 5 consecutive full cases suites, p407, p410, p413, p417 and p419 (suite-pNNN/cases.out, the cycles with a full suite; the cycles between ended before their suite). It also passed in p400, p401, p403 and p406, so 9 of 9 full suites since p400.

criteria.text: WebBrowser/browser_test_ui_mode passes under full-suite load, fixed at its root, not by retry. It failed in 20 of 79 full cases suites from p303 to p399, each time with `a retried browser test records its trace` failing as `notes failed on chromium after 2 attempts: browser protocol failed` (p399 suite, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT-side log cases.out). Alone on the p399 compiler with the suite environment it passed 3 of 3 (2026-11-21). Find which browser-protocol wait or read gives up under load and bound it by the work, as c1 does for steps. Proof: it passes in 5 consecutive full cases suites.

The case runner never errors on a step whose child exits, as expected, before reading its stdin: in the p413 full suite (dev ba5711569a, 2026-11-21) Tests/Cases/Debug/stdin_file_is_the_program_s_input_while_the_console_reads_commands.case reported ERROR "stdin: closed during write `process stdin`: process stdin closed; child exited 2 without reading it" on the step `jet debug echo.jet --stdin=/dev/stdin`, whose expected result is exactly that exit 2 refusal before any read. It passed in p410 on the same refusal, so the outcome depends on whether the child exits before the write. Fix: a write to a child that has exited (EPIPE) ends the stdin feed and the step is judged on its exit and streams. Proof: a testkit unit whose child exits at once without reading a large stdin, run 200 times under load, always judged on its exit; and that case passes 50 times in a row under the cases suite.
criteria.evidence: Landed 3b3c3e0724 (p417, tip a495b97fee). On the p417 batch compiler, under the p419 census and suite load: Compiler/JetTestKit/Tests/Core.jet --filter "without reading its input is judged on its exit" (the unit loops 200 rounds of a child that exits 2 without reading 1 MiB of stdin, each judged on exit 2 and its stderr, no process failure): 1 passed, 0 failed. Tests/Cases/Debug/stdin_file_is_the_program_s_input_while_the_console_reads_commands.case through the cases runner (jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter): 50 of 50 PASS in a row, load average 13.8-25.0 on 32 CPUs ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/c6772-x50.out). It is in the p417 suite fixed list.

criteria.text: A case that copies jet and runs the copy never fails with ETXTBSY: in the p413 full suite (dev ba5711569a, 2026-11-21) Tests/Cases/CLI/compiler_aliases_run_the_compiler_verbs.case reported ERROR "spawn: I/O error during resolve `.../work/bin/jet`: Text file busy (os error 26)", so a write descriptor to the fresh copy was still open (in this process or a child forked meanwhile) when it was executed. Fix the root: the copy is written through a descriptor that no concurrently spawned child can inherit (O_CLOEXEC, closed before the spawn), or the runner retries exec only on ETXTBSY with that reason. Proof: a testkit unit that copies a binary and executes it while other threads spawn children, run 1000 times under load with no ETXTBSY; and the case passes 50 times in a row under the cases suite.
criteria.evidence: Landed 3b3c3e0724 (p417, tip a495b97fee). On the p417 batch compiler, under the p419 census and suite load: Compiler/JetTestKit/Tests/Core.jet --filter "a fresh copy of a program runs while other threads spawn children" (1000 rounds of copy-then-exec of /bin/sh while three tasks spawn 2000 children each; every round ran with no error, exit 3): 1 passed, 0 failed. Tests/Cases/CLI/compiler_aliases_run_the_compiler_verbs.case through the cases runner: 50 of 50 PASS in a row, load average 13.8-25.0 on 32 CPUs ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/c6772-x50.out). It is in the p417 suite fixed list.

criteria.text: Tests/Cases/Debug/first_print_nonentry_under_250ms holds under full-suite load, fixed at its root, not by retry or a wider bound: in the p417 suite (tip a495b97fee, 2026-11-21) it failed with "recv deadline exceeded after 258.69942ms", while direct timing on the same compilers gives a median of 18.6-21.8 ms (10 runs each, load 14-23), so a stall under load took the case 12 times its normal time. Its wall bound judges the debugger only when the debugger had the CPU: measure the debugger's own time to the first print (CPU time, or the stall excluded) or keep the 250 ms promise by design under load. Proof: the case passes 50 times in a row under the cases runner while a full suite runs.

FiberLiveness/fibers_past_the_pool_tear_down_in_random_order holds under full-suite load, fixed at its root. In the p420 full suite (dev 4f1f6c1c7f, 2026-11-21) its `jet run` step printed "threads unchanged false" after passing in the 9 full suites p400-p419; p420 changed no thread or scheduler code. The fixture (Fixtures/Teardown/main.jet) samples /proc/self/status Threads: after a fixed time.sleep(50ms) and again after a fixed time.sleep(100ms) once every task has joined, so a scheduler worker that starts or retires late under load changes the count. The comparison must wait on the runtime reaching its settled state (or compare against the bound the runtime promises), not on wall time. Proof: the case passes 50 times in a row under the cases runner while a full suite runs.
criteria.evidence: dev ae994a28ce, the p435 batch compiler (it carries the teardown fix 94bedff569 from p431): Tests/Cases/FiberLiveness/fibers_past_the_pool_tear_down_in_random_order.case passed 50 runs in a row (each `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter ...` rc 0, PASS), every run while the p435 full suite ran, at load 138 to 246 (2026-11-21, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/c13-50-p435.out). It also passed in the p431, p434 and p435 full suites.

criteria.text: Examples/Systems/Process/ProcessRunAllParentDeath holds under full-suite load. In the p435 full suite (dev ae994a28ce, 2026-11-21, load near 250) its o2 golden printed "job running after its owner died: true" after waiting 5 s for the killed owner's job to stop; it passed in the 15 suites before. Fix (Main-6772-parent-death-wait): the job sleeps an hour and the check waits up to 10 minutes, then kills a survivor. If it fails again with that wait, the parent-death mark really missed the job and the runtime is at fault. Proof: the golden PASS in 5 full suites in a row.

Compile-time code's step limit (E0952) counts deterministic steps, as ratified in D-PREP-FUEL1 (a step is a deterministic count, never wall time); it never measures time. Today SessionHost.jet:285-309 bounds the comptime child by the wall-clock wait on the monotonic clock (391-393), so a loaded host, or a debugger pausing the child, turns a working build into E0952, and Docs/Spec/Reference/metaprogramming.md:183 describes the time rule. Found by the D-DEBUG-PREP1 adversarial review, 2026-11-23. Proof: a case runs one compile-time loop just under its step limit and one just over: the first passes and the second stops with E0952 at the same step count under an all-cores load generator, and the spec line states the count rule.
criteria.evidence: On a compiler built from landed dev 6ab0b5a5c8 (tip20), run in an export of that commit: cases RuntimeStops/comptime_step_limit_counts_under_load; ui comptime_step_limit_; PASS 1/1; PASS 5/5; metaprogramming.md:183-186 says "Steps are counted, never timed"; SessionHost.jet has no clock wait

criteria.text: A `build: fn` that reads a constant marked #StepLimit compiles and runs on every tier; today it is an internal compiler error ("constant … without a declaration", found by G1Generation-2 on the batch 17 compiler while fixing c15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter build_fn_reads_a_step_limit_constant`.

cards.title: A lambda that moves a capture runs the move on every call
cards.body: Found by G9Web-1-2 (#6779 work, dev 46855ae09a, seed-b14). Sema accepts a lambda whose body moves a captured owner, even when the lambda is passed to a per-item callback. `[1,2,3].map(x -> consume(s.move()) + x).sum()` prints 33 and fold prints 27: the same owner is moved three times, a use after move (I1). Probe: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G9Web/probe6779/mapmove/main.jet. The safe fix needs no new syntax: refuse the move. A call-at-most-once parameter mark that would allow it for one-shot callbacks is a language choice and goes to a ballot.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): BLOCKED. c2 waits on the call-at-most-once parameter mark ballot.

D-CALLBACK-ONCE1 reposted as r6 on 2026-11-18, the owner-ordered rework with every downside engineered away or stated with its cost. The adversarial review (BallotReview2, GPT family; Docs/Audits/ballot-redesign-r5-review-2026-11-18.md, submitted as Main-audit-ballot-redesign-r3-r5) verdict is that it holds within stated limits. Its build work first proves every LIMIT row in the review's CALLBACK-ONCE1 table and closes the PREREQ rows (#3645 c14-c16, #6048 c9, #6923 c11) before support is claimed.

Owner 2026-11-18: D-CALLBACK-ONCE1's recommended option is insufficient. It is being redesigned to cover stored and async one-shot callbacks with the downsides engineered away, then re-reviewed and reposted.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c2 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

c3 is wider than written (CardCloser-3 probe on gate-p131, 2026-11-14): a lambda stored in a struct field (h: Holder{action: fn() { k += 1 }}) or in a list silently loses even a plain k += 1 on a := Int, not only a &self method call. A lambda bound with := or passed as an argument does write through. So the loss follows storing the closure in an aggregate: the capture is copied at the aggregate store instead of referenced. This is a silent miscompile (I1 type/memory-safety class), G10 priority. The fix needs one capture-mode rule in sema (by-reference for mutated := captures, or refuse storing a mutating closure in an aggregate) and its IR lowering.

criteria.text: Sema refuses moving a captured owner inside a lambda body whenever the lambda may run more than once (any lambda that escapes into a call or a binding), with a registered code, what/why/fix text (copy, clone or move the value in as a parameter) and a UI snapshot of the probe. The rule is swept over Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples and every tests/ tree first, and every hit is fixed in the same batch.
criteria.evidence: dev 499cb49813: E0121 'moves out of a lambda that can run more than once'; jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter lambda_move_capture_repeated_call: 1 PASS on batch compiler gate-p131 (dev 8d83659ef3), verified by Main on dev 529aba0d26

criteria.text: A one-shot callback may move a capture only through a call-at-most-once parameter mark, which is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15); c1's refusal lands first and does not wait. Proof: after the ruling, `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Closures/one_shot_callback_move`.

A stored closure (in a struct field or a list) that writes a captured `:=` local, by `k += 1` or a `&self` method call, either writes the original or is refused with a registered error; it never silently loses the write (gate-p64 prints 10; CardCloser-3 found the field and list forms on gate-p131). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter stored_closure_capture_write` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Closures/stored_closure_capture_write_` on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: dev 23be2f30cb (p268) and 2d5ee4ccc1 (p270). A stored closure that writes a captured := local makes every later whole or field read of that local the registered E0204 jet.UseWhileWriteActive, so the write is never silently lost. On batch compiler p270: cases Closures/stored_closure_capture_write_ 2/2 PASS (both forms run on O0, O1 and O2); ui stored_closure_capture_write PASS on p268, and the new field-read snapshot stored_closure_capture_write_field_read landed in 2d5ee4ccc1. Card2845StoredMutatingClosureTierParity and ReactiveCodegenClonesTheWholeRootBeforeRunning goldens pass on all tiers.

criteria.text: A lambda bound to a local reads the captured local's current value, or the program is refused. Today 'v := [1]; f := fn() { v.len() }; v.push(2); f()' prints the stale count (accepted on p267 and p268): the outer write is invisible to the lambda's copy, the converse of c3. Proof: a case in Tests/Cases/Closures where each tier prints the current value or the UI snapshot shows the registered refusal.
criteria.evidence: Landed 6683523959 (p271). On batch compiler p271 (6d6315d3bd): cases Closures/bound_lambda_reads_changed_capture PASS 1/1 and golden ClosureCaptureWrites 3/3.

cards.title: Data-oriented compiler core: interned u32 ids, flat columns, per-phase arenas, no RC, under 1 GB
cards.body:
Owner order (2026-11-13): "i want one slot working the data oriented core immediately. this should be done carefully, systemically, and cleanly. it should be a fast intelligent cutover." This card is the work home for #5479 plan step 3 (#5479 c7) and the memory half of #5910. #5479 c7 and #5910 stay as the gates and are met from this card's evidence.

What it is: every compiler name, symbol, type and function becomes an interned u32 id, with no String-keyed maps. The AST, types and IR become flat struct-of-arrays columns instead of per-node heap objects. Compiler data lives in per-phase arenas freed in bulk and carries no reference counts. Peak memory falls under 1 GB.

Why: G11Speed-5's 2026-11-13 profile (check RunColdContext on the core-b1 jet) has no symbol above 2.3% self time. The cost is spread across allocation, RC, string keys and copies, which this work removes. From today's numbers (8,510 lines/s on the c1 cell, about 5 of 32 threads busy, so roughly 590 µs CPU per line), the c7 gate of 5 µs per line is about a 100× CPU cut. The parallel pipeline (its own card) needs this card's arenas and ids to scale.

How: one slot (G11Speed-5). Design and census first, then slices in dependency order. Each slice is a whole cutover (greenfield: no parallel representation, no adapter layer, no flag) whose proof is identical output: the self-host chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases. The worker writes code and submits; Lander5 builds, runs the chain and lands. A slice that cannot be cut over whole is split by package boundary, never by keeping two representations.
cards.plan:
Census (G11Speed-5, base c490f18529; commands, census.awk and per-file.tsv in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G11Speed-5/6793/). Over the nine pipeline packages:
- 1333 `[String:` maps and sets (Sema 933, Driver 143, IR 103, Foundation 86)
- 393 `Shared<`
- payload node enums: Expr 51, Stmt 35, Item 24, TExprKind 77, NodeKind 99/95, Type 23/17
- peak: jet check of one Sema file is 4414 MB (seed-b14, 28 s), held across sema

Slices, each a whole cutover with no second form, proved by chain fixed point plus identical goldens, ui and cases:
- S0: census guard and ledger, plus Docs/spec/compiler-data.md
- S1: ModuleId
- S2: SymbolId
- S3: Names, String maps to 0 (c2)
- S4: flat AST (c3)
- S5: TypeId and flat checked bodies (c4)
- S6: IR and backend ids, no Shared
- S7: phase arenas, no Shared in sema (c4, c5)

Decisions (Main, 2026-11-13; all as proposed):
- F1: compiler data means the nine pipeline packages (Lexer, Parser, Foundation, Sema, IR, Backend, Driver, Eval, Wasm). Tool packages read it through accessors.
- F2: nominal type names become SymbolIds in S2; structural TypeIds come in S5, after the flat AST, so the Type tree is rewritten once.
- F3: the split is by id space across every package, because Foundation types are shared. A package split is used only for package-private data (S3, S6).
- F4: "no RC" means the only heap blocks are single-owner column buffers whose count word never moves after creation. There is no String, box, Shared or per-node block. Literal zero count words would need a language feature outside this card.
- F5: S1 comes before S2.

log.text: Batch 6 full suite done on the -O1 batch-6 compiler (c2k): golden 0 new failures, ui 0 new failures, cases 0 new failures vs batch 5 (4953 pass); long_chain_100000_terms_check_and_run passes again at -O1. c2k (0b62f91531) stands.

Batch 6 landed: 0b62f91531 (c2k, well-known TypeID constants), 3019343199 (Jetpack area check fixes: Parser Entry.jet unused binding, Federation TextReports.jet raw_line). CompilerData --check ok (300 text-keyed lookups); DiagnosticRows --check passed. Cases profile still running.

Landed c2a-c2j on dev (513255e576 through 5eb6938dec, ledgers 5eed140a7d): compiler text-keyed lookups fall from 1034 to 300. Tested in batch 4: golden, ui and cases show no new failure from them. long_chain_100000_terms failed only because the batch compiler was built at O0 (the Expr drop glue takes a 3.2 KB frame per level there); the same source built at O1 or O2 passes, so it is not a c2 defect. c2k (the TYPE_STRING rename that unblocks the Jetpack areas check) goes in the next batch.

Decision (c2): JetWasm Text.jet's 14 WAT name maps move to NameTable through a new path dependency jet_wasm -> jet_foundation. c2 requires zero String-keyed maps in compiler data from one interner per id space; a wasm-local interner would be a second mechanism. c2i staged for the next landing batch.

Wave 3B (dev ead79f56ba): adopted true columnar Rows<T> across X64Select.jet (eliminated last 2 .copy() calls, deleting X64Select.jet from copy_ratchet ceilings.tsv!), Image/Object.jet (zero-copy .offset/.size/.weight columns), and Driver/ForeignDeps.jet.

Wave 2B (dev c7b432d894): D-COLUMNS1 true per-field columnar SoA storage for Rows<T> landed in Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildRows.jet (24*k inline column lists, O(1) zero-copy table.field view dropping 50k-row column reads 49ms->0ms at -O0/-O1/-O2, strict I9 parity, proven live on compiler DeclTable.rows). Wave 3 streamlines Compiler/ tables onto Rows<T>.

Gap found 2026-11-14 while landing: Docs/spec/compiler-data.md says a parallel phase lends read-only tables to its workers, but the compiler has no mechanism to do that. A task's read capture copies the value (BuildExpr ir_copy_value), a lent parameter is E1102, and every parallel phase in Compiler/ uses Shared in a file whose row already counts it. So a new parallel phase (record take, Core body decode, O2 pass threads) either adds a Shared cell, which the ratchet refuses, or copies the whole input per worker. Withdrawn for this reason: Speed-2 6759-c2-core-record-take-parallel and 6759-c9-core-bodies-decode-parallel-r2. GoalsA-1's o2-*-threads and PrecompiledCore's parallel encode/pack are being reworked against the same constraint. Closing this needs a read-only lend for tasks, which is a language or Core surface and so an owner ballot.

Decision (Main, 2026-11-14), compile speed (build.plan): the build-plan query (RootRun "build", running a package`s build.jet plan) loads only the sibling members the build entry reaches, through the existing jet_driver_namespace_reach scan, plus their imports. Measured by G11Speed-5 on seed-b17: Compiler/test.jet pulls in jet_testkit (164 modules, a 574-function comptime closure) that build.jet never uses; `jet inspect graph Compiler/build.jet` 7.8 s with it and 1.78 s without; `jet check Compiler/build.jet` 4.48 s and 0.61 s. Chosen over moving test.jet into its own package, because that would tailor only the measured package, while every user package with build.jet plus test.jet pays the same cost. `jet check` and `jet test` still check every member, and target compiles still check what they compile; only the build script`s plan run stops loading unreached siblings. Proof: a case where the plan runs while test.jet has a type error that `jet check` and `jet test` both report; the win on a second user package; the cold self-compile row.

S1 boundary decision (G11Speed-5, 2026-11-13). Module identity text is also the prefix of every SymbolID key and is printed in IR names and goldens. So S1 moves module records, rows and lookups to ModuleID and one ModuleTable: the loader interns and the graph takes a copy. Symbol.module_name and key text stay text until S2 and cross at module_find. S2 moves Symbol.module_name to ModuleID together with symbol keys.

criteria.text: Design and census first. The card plan records, for Compiler/ by package: every String-keyed map and set, every heap-allocated node type, every RC-carrying compiler struct, and every phase's data lifetime, each with counts and a reproducible census command. It also records the slice order with each slice's files and its proof. A short durable design note goes in Docs/spec (for example compiler-data.md) with the contract: id spaces, column layout, arena lifetimes, and the rule that compiler data holds no RC.

cards.title: Parallel compiler pipeline: streaming modules, parallel comptime, wait-free queues, per-thread arenas (24 of 32 threads)
cards.body:
Owner order (2026-11-13): the parallel pipeline is tracked as its own card so it cannot be lost. This card is the work home for #5479 plan step 2 (#5479 c6), which stays as the gate and is met from this card's evidence. It is not staffed today: the data-oriented core (#6793) takes the speed slot, and this card starts once #6793's interning and per-phase arenas have landed. Lock-free per-thread allocation and contention-free scaling depend on them.

What it is: modules stream through the pipeline as soon as their dependencies are checked, with no phase-wide barriers. Comptime runs in parallel. Work queues are wait-free. Each thread allocates from its own arena and takes no global lock.

Projected ceiling (from today's numbers, not measured): about 5 to 24 busy threads, so at most about 5× wall time on its own with CPU per line unchanged. Its 400K lines/s gate needs #6793's CPU cut as well.
cards.plan: S1 (GENERAL): lift hard thread caps (IR_BUILD_MAX_PARTS=12, SEMA_FINALIZE_SIDE_EFFECT_PARTS=16, taint threads/4), shard Alloc.jet large-block/slab locks (words 216, 736), lock-free per-carrier work-stealing in Scheduler.jet, safe Atomic<Int> compiler queues (0 new #Unsafe). S2 (COMPILER-ONLY): fix Barrier #6 build.step/runtime (forward --threads in RuntimePack.jet:621, unify JetRuntime+Core thread pool in Request.jet:254, parallelize BuildExecute.jet:293 ready targets). S3 (COMPILER-ONLY): Tier-1 streaming Parse->HeaderRegister->HeaderBarrier->BodyCheck+CoreDemand with deterministic (pass_id, module_id, ordinal) diagnostics. S4 (COMPILER-ONLY): Tier-2 streaming ir_build(fn_id)->x64_patch(fn_id) after convergence checkpoint (sema.failure/effects/masked/#Inline(Always)/dead_code) + per-module flat arena munmap once #6793 c3-c4 lands. S5 (COMPILER-ONLY): parallel warm comptime pool K children (gated on DAG-width probe) + #6794 c3 32t scaling gate (>=24x, >=400K LOC/s).

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): weeks. A streaming parallel pipeline at 400K lines/s.

Landed on dev: 5fa9c6500c (guard fixes: closed_lists row for JetCLIBuildDone, the parallel parse moves instead of copying), 952ad6c16e (B1: b.jet_built_from, b.source_key, the source key), 929c537b86 (E1: on a same-source build the Core check takes the carried pack; its gain needs B2), 5050e48ec3 (S3: streamed load, -0.21 s on jet-bare's load). Tested in batch 4: golden, ui and cases show no new failure from them. B2 waits on a seed admitted from a compiler that includes B1. Per owner order (2026-11-23), architecture work stops here; the lane moves to G1.

Decision: S5 (parallel comptime batches) dropped. All comptime evaluation in jet-bare is about 0.76 s over 394 items; lane spawn and per-lane loading cost 0.2-0.55 s per batch against 0.05-0.10 s serially, so the best case is about -0.3 s; fixing its 6 case failures means removing the speculation it relies on. The atomics case's out-of-memory under the case cap is attributed to its lane children. The patch stays in the orchestrator's land directory as 6794-s5.dropped. Next for this lane: S3 rebased, B1, E1; B2 after a seed with B1; then parallel sema.finalize (3.88 s) and ir.build (1.87 s).

Correction to the batch-3 entry: the 2.19 s load delay was the runtime step's load, measured across processes by mistake. On jet-bare's own process, S3 shortens load by about 0.21 s (1.28 -> 1.07 s), and S5 lengthens comptime by about 1.5 s (3.25 -> 4.80 s) plus about 0.6 s in the build-step generator. S5 is the regression; S3 is resubmitted rebased; S3b is dropped.

Landed on dev 776eabec7a (S1r2 sharded allocator, S2 compiler threads shared with the runtime build, det fix) and ce4e8bb137 (S3a linear inline-always check, effect spans, TaskGraph). -O0 Compiler jet-bare byte-identical at threads 1/8/32 (dev before: 1 vs 16 differed). Batch 3 (S3 loader streaming, S5 parallel comptime, S3b Core-seal walk) not landed. Throughput O0 at 32 threads: wall 52.7 -> 55.5 s, CPU 120.8 -> 128.6 s. The load window ends 2.19 s later (S3); S5 adds 2.34 s of comptime CPU and fails 6 comptime cases (one ICE); S3b changes nothing measurable. Returned to the worker with the trace.

Decision 2026-11-23: the runtime pack overlaps the jet-bare compile (runtime-overlap note option B: the pack is lowered by the building jet, gated on its source digest). It is built directly, as one cutover of IDENTITY, E2105, provenance.json and the Gate, under the owner's standing order to implement the architecture without design-doc gating. Ranking from the s1r2 32-thread trace: runtime step 19.9 s after jet-bare ends at 17.82 s (up to ~18 s of ~39 s wall), then the Core check's comptime wait for the runtime image (~7.4 s), then load->sema streaming and the serial ir.build/ir.object remainders. Proof: c2 chain fixed point and byte identity at threads 1/8/32; c3 throughput.

Antigravity #6794 work folded into ParallelS2S3's slices, saved 2026-11-23: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/tmp/parked_arch/6794-taskgraph.tar (JetFoundation TaskGraph.jet + its test: dependency-driven node schedule with no phase barriers, from the earlier Speed-3-2 park; on no branch) and $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/tmp/parked_arch/6794_s1.patch (work-stealing scheduler + sharded allocator; S1r2 carries 156 of its 320 changed Alloc lines; the rest is to be folded or dropped with a stated reason).

S1 rev 2 (IR_BUILD_MAX_PARTS 12 and the quarter-thread taint-walk cap restored) measured 2026-11-23 on dev 03f1442ac1: Throughput --against the dev-tip compiler, O0, --threads 32, n=3: wall 39.33 -> 39.33 s median, cpu +0.3%, instructions -0.0%, ir.build cpu 15.66 -> 15.57 s (the S1 v1 regression to 29.5 s is gone), gate INCONCLUSIVE only on build.step spread. Neutral: no gain and no regression. S2 (two ready targets at once, the thread cap split between compiles and passed to child jets, Core leaves the pool while it waits on the runtime image) is frozen; S1r2+S2 is under A/B with thread-count byte identity. The worker's trace analysis: the c1 critical path is jet-bare (about 14 s) then the runtime step (about 20 s); Tier-1 load streaming can win at most 0.3 s and is parked; the jet-bare finalize tail is under 0.2 s; splitting the runtime unit (about 2 s) is deferred for its blast radius; the runtime-overlap option is written up in Docs/Audits/2026-11-23-parallel-pipeline-runtime-overlap.md and is not built: it speeds only the compiler's self-build and moves the pack identity contract, so it needs an adversarial review against the no-cell-tailoring rule first.

S1 test 2026-11-23 (S1's 15 files on dev c4b26fa3ac): self-host fixed point holds (s2 == s3); golden and ui no new failures; cases: one new abort under full-suite load, Atomics/d_atomic_width1_contract  -> 'memory allocation of 32 bytes failed' (Alloc.jet alloc_out_of_memory, never seen on the base; passes 3/3 alone). Throughput --against dev tip, O0, --threads 32, n=3: no wall gain (parallelism 3.1 -> 3.2), process CPU +10.4% FAIL, ir.build CPU 15.7 -> 29.5 s (+89%) FAIL after lifting IR_BUILD_MAX_PARTS. S1 is not landed; both findings went back to the implementer. Thread caps were not the wall-time limit: the phases are serial in structure, so S3 streaming is the lever.
2026-11-23 08:12: S1 resumed in worktree ParallelSched (detached at dev 93bd9dc289) with the parked part-A Alloc.jet patch applied; implementer CopyPatchO0.

Parked 2026-11-23 06:48 when staffing was cut to 2 agents: S1 part A (Alloc.jet sharding) diff at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/tmp/parked_arch/6794_s1.patch, base 93bd9dc289; Scheduler.jet part B not started; the baseline scheduler benchmark hung (task killed).

Landed Pillar 5 Slice 2 + 4B/6B (dev d2fc656a69, master ec68fd9d73, S2==S3 4e091ee4...): hardware SHA-NI link/embed (core-embed 2267->702ms, -69%), direct x64_link_runtime_image_objects (runtime.pack -22%), struct JetCLICoreLibraryIR (709MB drop gap 267.5->1.0ms), lock-free partitioned ir_opt_bodies + OptStops/OptSimplify/OptBuilder fast paths (runtime.core ir.opt -12.4%), parallel Core writes & 4-way IR drop. Full -O0 Compiler 33.51s->30.99s quiet (-2.52s), full -O2 Compiler 39.44s->37.89s, Peak RSS 4833 MB (sub-5GB!). All gates pass (CodegenCeiling 9/9, CompilerData 1093, UnsafeRatchet 1660, Tests/Guards 217/217).

Landed Pillar 5 Slice 1 + 4B (c022bb1d9c, 5 files): parallel comptime.prefetch (-129ms), parallel driver.prelower.owners (-98ms), overlapped driver.result (-111ms), 4-way detached release_aside (-143 MB at ir.build.program), overlapped ir_body_scan_collect, skipped O0 tail_calls (-58ms), flat ir_x64_reached_only (-88ms ir.object), pre-reserved x64_executable_debug_apart, overlapped core-embed facts check. Combined with P1-P4A: FULL jet build -O0 --threads 24 Compiler 40.69->33.51s (-7.18s, -17.7%; jet-bare 12.01s, runtime 16.36s, core-embed 2.27s), standalone jet-bare 12.13s, FULL -O2 --threads 12 Compiler 49.28->39.44s (-9.84s, -20.0% wall / -21.4% CPU), CodegenCeiling 9/9, CompilerData 1093 ok, UnsafeRatchet 1660 (0 outside kernel), 269/269 unit tests, Tests/Guards 217/217.

criteria.text: Design: a slice plan on the card covering the module dependency scheduler, removal of the phase barriers in the driver, parallel comptime children, the wait-free work queue, and per-thread arenas built on #6793's arenas, each with its proof. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*parallel-pipeline*"` names the design note and its passing review.

criteria.text: Streaming: a module enters sema, lowering and codegen as soon as its dependencies are checked, with no phase-wide barrier in the driver. Comptime evaluation runs in parallel. Output is identical: chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases. Proof: the chain fixed point, then `jet test Compiler --profile golden`, `--profile ui` and `--profile cases` on every tier.

Scaling: on the #5479 c1 cell (32 hardware threads, cold, n=3 median), average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) is at least 24, 32 threads beat 16, no global allocator or queue lock shows in a perf profile, and throughput is at least 400K lines/s. #5479 c6 is met from this evidence. Proof: the #5479 c1 cell receipt with a perf profile.

The known-failing row this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv: CLICompilerSpeed/parallel_check_matches_serial_check. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Copy-and-patch machine code for the O0 tier (jet run, jet dev, comptime)
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-13): idea 1 of Docs/research/2026-11-13-compile-speed-beyond-the-plan.md is planned. At O0, each IR operation is emitted by copying a pre-built machine-code template (stencil) and patching its holes (constants, frame offsets, jump and call targets), with no instruction selection or register allocation at O0. The stencils are built once with the toolchain, like precompiled Core, so they are toolchain, not a cache (D-EXEC2=A holds). Prior art: Xu and Kjolstad, "Copy-and-Patch Compilation", OOPSLA 2021; the CPython 3.13 JIT (PEP 744). O1 and O2 keep the optimizing backend. Sequenced after the data-oriented core (#6793) lands its IR ids (S6), because stencils are keyed by flat IR opcodes. Unstaffed today (speed ranks below goals).
cards.plan: S1: Add 6 missing x86-64 helpers to Compiler/JetBackend/Source/X64/Encoder.jet + build-time generator Compiler/Toolchain/X64Stencils/Main.jet (Compiler/build.jet x64-stencils step + LaneCheck --check per G4) emitting Compiler/JetIR/Source/X64StencilData.jet (~185 micro-stencil stampers, O0_STENCIL_COUNT/BYTES/DIGEST) + unit/case tests. S2: Greenfield unified 24B POD X64FlatReloc (deleting X64RelocTarget) across all 8 consumers (Emission, Object, DirectBind, X64Module, X64Stack, X64Select, X64Patch, JetDebug/NativeFix). S3: Zero-alloc 4-pass DropEarly (ir_drop_plan_into), zero-liveness X64Patch with Guardrails G1-G3 (complete p.starts/p.ends replacement, inline #FFI(asm) preserved, stack check for f.stack_check || frame+StackAddress > 32768), safe RFLAGS/rax/epoch const table, STD_CFI + fast debug_info=true emission, Tests/Cases/Backend/o0_stencil_emit.case (c2). S4: S2==S3 fixed point, inline_census 0 remaining #Inline(Always) (G4), jet debug tests, golden/ui/cases on all tiers (c3), committed cold >=10x backend CPU cut & <=1.5x runtime receipts on #5479 c1 + jetc-trace (c4).

The rename is with the #6793 lane. Defect recorded, not scheduled: a blocking registration error in a one-module unit unsettles that module (sema_registration_settle_modules), so sema_copy_nominal_has_impl reports known=false and every unmarked move-to-share of a nominal becomes a false UseAfterMove. Collect-all output should report the one root error, not 157 consequences.

Census on de08daf13a with a dev-built seed: check, build, runtime, selfcheck and core-tests clean. Landed c90bca2d19 (Jetpack sources.list gains TypeIDs, TypeIDOps and Chunks, which fixed the assembly pass and the drift in all 16 Jetpack areas; unsafe baseline line shift; seven compiler-data rows lowered), 6910a725bc (Executor JET_BUILD_THREADS through ENV_JET_BUILD_THREADS, the guard shard 4 failure) and the guard shard memory cap 4G -> 6G (measured peak 4.8G; the rc=143 kills). Still open for the receipt: the closed_lists and copy_ratchet guards (from S2 and S1, with the #6794 lane), and the Jetpack areas unit check, which already failed at c4b26: 152 UseAfterMove in the assembled unit that package checks don't report, with the #6794 lane; plus the TYPE_STRING duplicate (TypeID slice 3a), with the #6793 lane.

Census on dev de08daf13a: the build pass fails because core-embed reports 'cache entry exceeds its byte limit'. Root cause: the admitted seed a0.0.46 bounds every kept build output at 512 MiB (BUILD_MAX_ACTION_FILE_BYTES) even with no artifact store. Its own jet is 505 MB, and dev's -O1 jet has now grown past 536,870,912 bytes. Dev's executor already drops the bound when no store is open (bounded: reuse != None), so the fix is a seed bump. The builder is a compiler built from dev, because the a0.0.46 seed can no longer build dev at -O1. Also blocking the receipt: guard closed_lists (BuildExecute.jet JetCLIBuildDone, from #6794 S2) and copy_ratchet (Parser/Entry.jet 21 copies over 11, from #6796 S1), both sent to the #6794 lane; guard shard 4 was killed at the 4G cap (being measured).
Census false E0361 fix landed on dev 38a01f0a9c (operator hook recursion check matches the right-hand type). This unblocks the Land.jet census receipt that c3's chain needs.

Far from c4's >=10x: the base already emits most O0 functions through the Pillar 2 X64Patch emitter, so the X64Select-relative 10x projection does not apply to the live baseline. c4 stays open; c2 case passes on every tier; c3 has one regression (TailCalls/comptime_tail_walk_runs_in_constant_stack at -O0, StackOverflow) sent back to the implementer. Receipt: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/tmp/orch/c4/against.{log,tsv}.

Handoff 2026-11-23 07:56 (prior session stopped on quota at 07:40). Worktree GoalsOrder (base 93bd9dc289), uncommitted: S1 Encoder helpers + Compiler/Toolchain/X64Stencils generator + generated JetIR X64StencilData.jet, S2 unified X64FlatReloc across consumers, S3 DropEarly/X64Patch rewrite in progress; Backend/o0_stencil_emit case added and passing on all tiers after a block_release hole-offset fix. Live cold metrics: jet-bare -O0 -j24 14.15s (A/B 15.09->14.35s, -738ms, Peak RSS -203 MB -> 5160 MB), Hello.jet 20.7->18.8ms (-9.3%), full -O2 -j12 Compiler 49.02->45.47s (-3.55s).

Landed Pillar 2 Slice 1 (1d11568b1b): Copy-and-Patch O0 stencil emitter (Compiler/JetIR/Source/X64Patch.jet, all 52 IROps, zero regalloc/relax/dying, reusable per-worker scratch, O(N) suffix-shared stop edges, cache-line-padded chunked scatter, IRPatchColdKind deduplicated onto IRX64ColdKind). Verified Stage-1->Stage-2->Stage-3 exact SHA-256 fixed point, O0 -j12==-j24 determinism, I9 parity, CodegenCeiling 9/9, CompilerData 0 rises, UnsafeRatchet ok, JetBackend/JetIR/JetDriver/JetCLI 269/269, Tests/Guards 217/217. Interleaved A/B vs pareto-w6b-dist: ir.x64 CPU -40.3% (9560->5710ms), ir.x64 wall -29.2% (1052->744ms), backend total -20.5% (-4710ms CPU), jet-bare -O0 -1.16s (-7.1%), Peak RSS -181 MB, output binary -17.2 MB (-7.3%), .debug_jetline -24.7%.

criteria.text: O0 code generation emits every IR opcode by copying and patching a toolchain-built stencil, with no instruction selection or register allocation at O0. The stencil set is built by Compiler/build.jet and embedded in the jet binary, with no file I/O per compile.

cards.title: Parallel lexing and parsing inside one file
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-13): idea 3 of Docs/research/2026-11-13-compile-speed-beyond-the-plan.md is planned. A SIMD pre-scan finds top-level declaration boundaries in a file, and chunks are lexed and parsed on separate threads, then joined in source order. This matters because the compiler itself is essentially one large module, so module-level parallelism (#6794) cannot split it. It requires that lexing can restart at a top-level boundary. If that needs a language rule (for example, no raw newline inside a string literal), the rule goes on a ballot before the build. Sequenced with #6793 S4 (flat AST) and #6794. Unstaffed today.

cards.title: Shared generic code at O0: one compiled body per generic function, types passed as a hidden argument
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-13): idea 4 of Docs/research/2026-11-13-compile-speed-beyond-the-plan.md is planned. At O0, a generic function is compiled once and takes its type information (size, alignment, trait method tables) as a hidden argument, as Swift does for unspecialized generics and Go does with GC-shape stenciling and dictionaries (Go 1.18). O1 and O2 keep per-type specialization. Meaning is identical on every tier (I9): only the implementation strategy differs, and the proof is identical goldens, ui and cases on o0, o1 and o2. Per-type copies are the main compile-time cost of generics in Rust and C++. Sequenced after #6793 S5 (TypeId). Unstaffed today.
cards.plan: Sequenced after #6978 / #6793 S5 (TypeID). S1: Tagged IRDataReloc/X64DataReloc (.Data/.Function/.Runtime) + .data.rel.ro/.data placement in both merged and own_sections modes (L4) + data-reloc traversal in ir_x64_reached_only (X64Module.jet). S2: 72B IRTypeDesc (type_id, move_fn, close_fn) + Go 1.18 IRGenDict + tightened V1 eligibility (excluding Option/Result/Map/[T#N]/Rows/ZST/pop/first/last per L2) + pre-prologue stack-checked entry-hoisted dynamic frames (L1) + closure-box adapters & witness thunks + BuildRoutes.jet generic-stride list ops (0 new #Unsafe) + Backend/o0_shared_generic_body (c2, c3). S3: Cold uncached two-program -O0 compile/size/runtime receipt (c4, L5). S4: Full dated >4 KB tool-twin audit + general OptInline cold/growth caps, cold-stop outlining, and .rodata table lowering proved on two programs with CodegenCeiling 9/9 (c5).

criteria.text: At O0, each generic function is compiled once and receives its type information (size, alignment, trait method tables) as a hidden argument. O1 and O2 keep per-type specialization.

Output is identical before and after: chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases on every tier. Proof: the chain fixed point, then `jet test Compiler --profile golden`, `--profile ui` and `--profile cases` on every tier.

Measured: O0 compile time and code bytes for a generic-heavy program (for example Core collections used at 20 element types) against per-type specialization, plus a second program. Run-time cost at O0 is reported beside it. Proof: a committed receipt for both programs.

Per-function code size: no Core or generated function carries code its callers cannot reach or expansion a hand-written version would not. Measured by Main on seed-b13, 2026-11-12, default jet build: core_encoding_json_parse_string 21,323 B, __core_encoding_stream_jcs_number 37,759 B, core_regex_scan 35,189 B, unit_unicode_upper_mapping and lower_mapping 28-29 KB each, and MemorySafetyFuzz_run_memory_safety_fuzz_axis 58,080 B. A dated breakdown names, for each function over 4 KB in the tool-twin binaries, what the bytes are (inlined callees, unrolled loops, tables as code, checks) and the general codegen or Core rule that shrinks it; each fix shows the gain on two programs. Proof: the committed dated per-function breakdown, each fix with its two-program receipt. (was #6328 c29)

cards.title: Cheaper compile-time execution: one warm child per compile, fast O0 code, shared-memory values
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-13): idea 6 of Docs/research/2026-11-13-compile-speed-beyond-the-plan.md is planned. Compile-time code runs natively in a child of the compiler (I9). Today that costs process start-up, an O0 compile and value serialization per batch. The plan: start one child per compile and keep it warm for that compile only (nothing survives the compile, so D-EXEC2=A holds); compile compile-time functions with the copy-and-patch O0 path (its own card); and pass values through a shared-memory region instead of serializing them. Related: #6759 c1 (one comptime child per compile) and the re-finalize cost measured 2026-11-13 (1.19 s of the 2.86 s RunColdContext check). Unstaffed today.
cards.plan: S1: Native.jet sub-phase trace spans + zero-ELF x64_bind_comptime_batch (X64ComptimeCode) + defined_addr cache (preserving x64_bind_functions_at ELF parity, E3012, respawn, Comptime/one_warm_child_per_compile). S2: Scalar DONE fast path (Float/Float32 xmm0->rax, narrow masking, Int inline/boxed) + parent .rodata reads + sealed memfd/MAP_SHARED return window for flat shapes + CALL_BATCH (with stderr settle/replay, HOST-free eligibility, per-item fuel, STOP recovery, SessionHost #Unsafe consolidation <= 1654). S3: Wire #6795 c2 binary stencils + sound LocalSplice baseline reuse (JET_RECHECK_VERIFY=1) + comptime.precheck cuts + cold uncached c4 receipts.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): weeks. One warm comptime child on copy-and-patch O0.

Landed Pillar 3 (bf843c6d0b, 7 files): enabled fast_o0=true (X64Patch) on comptime stubs & batches, 4 MiB memfd/MAP_SHARED staging (SHM_TEXT/SHM_WRITE/single-round-trip SHM_LOAD), process_vm_readv zero-pipe value reads + last-page MRU + cached runtime symbol table + struct layout cache + X64Patch fused_slot reset after patch_stop_point. Verified Stage-1->Stage-2->Stage-3 exact SHA-256, O0 -j12==-j24 determinism, I9 parity, CodegenCeiling 9/9, CompilerData 1115 ok, UnsafeRatchet 1660 (0 new, 0 outside kernel), 269/269 unit tests, Tests/Guards 217/217. Live cold A/B vs pareto-p2s2-dist: comptime.load 391->236ms (-39.6%), comptime.eval 696->513ms (-26.3%, host CPU -31.9%), comptime total -301ms (-10.9%) / -1.02s CPU, jet-bare -O0 -j24 13.94s (build.jet step 13.48s), full -O2 -j12 Compiler 45.47->43.39s (-2.08s).

criteria.text: A design note and a passing adversarial review in Docs/Audits (per AGENTS.md "Adversarial design review") cover this card before any build SUB. The review names the strongest existing implementations and checks the claimed gain against a runnable probe. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Audits/*comptime-child*"` names the design note and its passing review.
criteria.evidence: dev 40e3ec0b6f: Docs/Audits/2026-11-23-comptime-child-design.md (Rev 3) and Docs/Audits/2026-11-23-comptime-child-review.md (PASS after 3-pass fresh-context review by 11e9f2d8); covers strongest peers (Zig comptime, rustc CTFE/Miri, Copy-and-Patch, Linux sealed memfd/MAP_SHARED), two-process N=500 IPC probe (5.315ms -> 2.744ms DONE -> 0.008ms CALL_BATCH+MAP_SHARED), live f3b6b8f4f7 baselines for RunColdContext/JetcTrace/CompileThroughput, and S1-S3 slice plan.

criteria.text: One compile-time child runs per compile, stays warm for that compile only, and exits with it. Compile-time functions are compiled on the copy-and-patch O0 path (#6795), and values cross through a shared-memory region with no serialization.

Output is identical before and after: chain fixed point plus goldens, ui and cases on every tier. Proof: the chain fixed point, then `jet test Compiler --profile golden`, `--profile ui` and `--profile cases` on every tier.

Measured: compile-time cost (comptime.bodies plus the re-finalize) of check RunColdContext and jetc-trace before and after, each showing the gain. Proof: a committed before-and-after receipt for both programs.

The native compile-time child's exchange with the compiler is deterministic: `jet build --release Examples/Concurrency/ContextOnStop.jet` gives exit 0 on 50 of 50 runs, with no internal error. Today about 1 run in 6 ends in exit 101, on both the batch-42 and batch-43 compilers, with one of three messages: 'the comptime child answered command 4 with frame 4', 'the comptime child ended during SHM_TEXT (status 0)', or 'the compiler read the child's memory through a word that is not an address'. That points to a race in the shared-memory command/frame protocol. Golden's o2 tier for ContextOnStop fails intermittently from it. Proof: a 50-run loop of that command, plus a stress witness case for the protocol. Diagnose with jet debug --record on the compiler (the AGENTS.md dogfood rule).

Dispatching a heard call to its check rule costs at most D-CORE-CHECK1's 1 µs budget per call, measured as the marginal cost of one more heard call: (time with N heard calls − time with one heard call) / (N − 1), N = 20000. The one-time cost of a module's first heard call (building and running the rule program) is reported beside it and is at most 25 ms. TypeIDSlice3 measured about 46.5 µs per heard call on the batch 12 compiler, G1Facts about 49 µs on batch 20 (2026-11-24). Proof: the rule-dispatch probe named in Docs/Audits/2026-11-23-d-rule-typeargs1-review.md plus its one-heard-call variant, rerun on dev, report at most 1 µs marginal per heard call and the fixed cost.

Build-time evaluation costs no more than running the same code: building the D-COMPTIME-SIZE1 Collatz table at compile time takes at most the time and peak memory of running it plus the compiler's own floor (seed-b13: 12 s and 4.1 GB against 1.24-1.29 s and 596 MB). Proof: a committed receipt measuring `jet build` and `jet run` of the ballot program on one machine.
