criteria.text: The desktop output writes an AppImage and a Flatpak on Linux, signed with the identities named in outputs:. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter BuildEntry/desktop_output_writes_signed_linux_packages` (it checks the structure and the signature of each package).
The updates: feed is signed. A client refuses an update whose signature fails or whose version is lower than its own, and applies a delta update when one is offered.
A client below the server's min_client gets the typed UpdateRequired (section 4.12) and is offered the update.

`jet package` builds a real, deterministic desktop bundle from the checked package plan, with installer metadata, signing hooks, an updater artifact and a byte, digest and mode receipt, with no placeholder archive and no second bundler.

D-INSTALL1 is ratified and the install page documents only the channel it picks. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter install_page_single_channel`. D-INSTALL1 is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). (was #5950 c1)

On a clean Linux x86-64 container with no Nix and no Jet, the documented install command installs `jet`, and `jet new hello && cd hello && jet run` prints the greeting; the release gate runs this on every release. Proof: the release gate's committed install receipt for the release. (was #5950 c2)

`nix run github:<org>/jet -- --version` prints the release version: flake.nix exports `packages.<system>.default` built from the pinned seed release asset (D-SEED-DIST1=A). Proof: `nix flake show` lists `packages.x86_64-linux.default`, and the release receipt records the `--version` output. (was #5950 c3)

The install page is generated from the tested install script, so no page names an install command the release gate does not run. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter install_page_generated`. (was #5950 c4)

The installed `jet` runs `jet run hello.jet` with JET_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT and JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY unset, because Core ships inside the binary or the install root. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Install/runs_without_toolchain_env`. (was #5950 c5)

A freestanding aarch64 program runs under QEMU in the release gate and prints its expected output. Proof: the release gate's committed receipt of the QEMU run (waits for hosted CI, which returns with a pinned native seed release; owner ruling 2026-11-08). (was #5950 c8)

The install, scaffold, run, check, test and edit commands named in the getting-started docs are the same on every supported Linux beginner host, and each runs as documented. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Onboarding/beginner_path_`. (was #5950 c12)

A missing entry, an ambiguous project, an unsupported host, an install failure, invalid code and offline state each give a registered error with a tested next step; retired entry layouts get no migration (owner order 2026-11-06), so the case's legacy-layout step is removed. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter OnboardingRecovery/entry_recovery_covers_missing_ambiguous_legacy_and_stale_layouts` with its known-failing row removed. (was #5950 c13)

A published toolchain channel lists the Linux releases with digests; `jet self` resolves, verifies, installs beside the running binary and swaps; a corrupt or mismatched release is refused with a registered error; the keyless tier needs an explicit override. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter SelfUpdate/`. (was #5950 c14)
The app's ui.asset files are packaged into the Linux desktop bundle. (Moved from #6816 c2.) Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter BuildEntry/assets_are_packaged_per_target` on Linux.

cards.title: Streaming server rendering: the page shell first, then each loading region as its data arrives
cards.body: Gap card for #6792 c6/c7 (owner order 2026-11-13: one cohesive package covering everything a web app and a native app need, with styling far better than HTML and CSS). D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (ratified 2026-11-13) governs this card; the examples/*.jet and crewboard/* paths name the programs in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md. Its criteria are written from the ratified shape and from the matching example in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md (key G14).

log.text: Dependencies (Main, 2026-11-15, from GoalsB-5-2's preflight): under D-STREAM-REGION1=A a region is the screen code that matches on one app.state read. Finding it needs three things that don't exist yet: screens as ui.Node rendered to HTML on the server (web.App pages are WebPage{title, body: String}, and no UINode-to-HTML renderer exists); the renderer marking an app.state match's node as a region root; and the app graph's .stream(after:)/.screen (#6445; web.App.stream() today is only a mode label). So c1/c2 wait on #6445 and #6447, and c2 also waits on #6556 (D-RESUME1, owner-paused). No work is lost: GoalsB-5-2 moved on to #3709 c7/c8/c27/c28.

Main 2026-11-14: streaming per region needs screens as ui.Node with server-rendered Loading branches (#6447) and an app stream API on the #6445 graph, and no decision covers either. Ballot D-STREAM-REGION1 is to be drafted by GoalsB-4 after D-DB-TABLE1.

criteria.text: With .stream(after: 50ms), the server sends the shell with each still-running read's Loading branch after 50 ms, then each region's HTML as its read finishes. A page whose reads finish within 50 ms is sent whole. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/stream_sends_the_shell_then_each_region`. Where a page splits into regions follows open decision D-STREAM-REGION1.

Streamed regions resume (D-RESUME1) with no hydration replay. A read that fails after the 200 status is sent renders its region's error branch. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/streamed_region_errors_render_their_error_branch`. Where a page splits into regions follows open decision D-STREAM-REGION1.

Accessibility checks: a lint checks each text paint against its background in both themes, and under increased contrast, against WCAG 1.4.3 (section 6.5 row b8). The preview tests of section 6.4 (three widths, two text sizes, both themes) report the four measures of section 6.5.

Fonts belong to the graph's theme (D-THEME2): `.theme(ui.theme(tokens, font: ui.font("Inter", files: [ui.asset("fonts/Inter.woff2")])))` exists in Core, the web build bundles each ui.asset's bytes under a hashed URL, and the first screen's theme fonts get preload hints. criteria.text: `kit.Form<T>` exposes one typed field per member of T, so `f.text(f.title, ...)` is checked, and the form runs T's validate block as the person types. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/FormTypedFields` (a kit.Form over a struct with a validate block prints its field errors as typed input arrives) on O0, O1, O2 and web.
Every view in the D-VIEW-SET1=C standard set ships with an executable example whose golden passes on every applicable tier (O0, O1, O2 and web).

One struct-declared rule set (its validate block, D-VALIDATE1=A) gives the same field paths and reasons for JSON decode, `T.validate` and form submission, and a field's error clears on the next valid submit. cards.title: Typed tables: db.Table<K, T> with declared keys and read and write sets
cards.body: Gap card K9 from the #6792 r2 proposal (Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md) and review round 1 (Docs/audits/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape-review.md). D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (ratified 2026-11-13) governs this card; the examples/*.jet and crewboard/* paths name the programs in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): BLOCKED. c5 waits on typed service state (another lane).

Main decision (c6/c7 interplay): a scoped query is refused only when it names a table outside the scope. A query that names no table (select 1, select now()) runs under any scope, as c6 requires, and one that names another table is refused with the registered diagnostic, as c7 requires. The table set comes from the parsed SQL, not from text matching. No ballot is needed; this applies the two criteria together.

D-SQL-SCRIPT1=A ratified: keep the direct Store methods (query/query_one need DB.Read, execute needs DB.Write, through the all_rows Driver path) as trusted owning-code convenience. with_policy returns another scope and doesn't narrow the Store. DBScope is not a security boundary today; c7 tracks that gap. c6 is built to this outcome.

c6 code landed in dev 136c4759d9 (Store implements Driver: query/query_one need DB.Read and execute needs DB.Write, with no row policy; a policy scope allows select 1). Both proof cases PASS on the p252 batch compiler. c6 is NOT met: its text names the no-policy default as ballot D-SQL-SCRIPT1, which is not posted or ratified. The landed behavior is option A of that ballot, and the owner may keep it or revert 136c4759d9. On Main's morning ballot list.

batch compiler p187 (dev 9860836a00), 2026-11-15: c2's TableMigration golden passes 3/3, and tests/run/CoreDB/TypedTable.jet passes; TableSecretField and TableSecretMigration fail at o0/o1/o2 with E0737, because the derived #Codable branches on a #Secret field. GoalsB-5-2 owns the fix.
c2 split (Main, 2026-11-15): the table half is built (GoalsB-5-6822-c2-table, lands after c1-db on a seed with c1-sema); the service half is its own criterion, waiting on typed service state.

Decision for c1 (Main, 2026-11-15): the #Secret storage codec is a real codec, a new serde handle op (stored encode/decode) through the existing THandleOp/BodyHandleOp path. Default Encode/Decode methods cannot carry it, because .encode() is a handle op and builtins have no impls. Rejected: a sema-supplied per-type secret-field list beside the codec, which would be a second mechanism and a compiler-known name. The wire codec skips #Secret fields in place of today's E2411. Planned as four SUBs from GoalsB-5-2 after #6869: seed a (Prelude rows and the new op), ir lowering, sema and derive bodies, then Db Table and the golden. Landed for c4 and c3: queued in the next batch.

Handoff (CardCloser-3 stopped, agent cap; no code written yet): c1 needs a compiler-derived storage codec and a change to E2411 for #Secret fields; c2 waits on #Table; c3/c4 need db.Table/Store exports in Core.rows (compiler rebuild) plus read-set tracking in app.state. Implementation choices to settle under D-DB-TABLE1=A: whether DBConnection is renamed to Store, and whether DBError becomes an enum.
Cleanup 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2): c1 split; read and write sets are #6822 c3, the DB.Write effect error is #6822 c4. blockedBy D-DB-TABLE1 (open ballot).

Main 2026-11-14: no ratified decision pins db.Table<K, T>: its constructor and binding, key declaration and method signatures exist only in the proposal (D-DBMIGRATE1 and D-DBPOLICY1 cover SQL and policy; D-QUERY-RETAIN1 retired a public Table<T> carrier). GoalsB-4 is drafting ballot D-DB-TABLE1 after #6830 slice 2. #6445 c5 and #6820 c3 wait on it.

criteria.text: A typed table stores #Secret fields with a storage codec that never reaches the wire codec. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Data/TableSecretField` (a db.Table<K, T> holding a #Secret field prints its stored and wire forms, the secret absent from the wire) on O0, O1 and O2. The table declaration form follows open decision D-DB-TABLE1.
criteria.evidence: p238 batch compiler (dev 5bea729463), full collect-all suite: golden Data/TableSecretField PASS on o0, o1 and o2.

criteria.text: D-DATA-EVOLVE1=A, table half: a typed table's stored rows upgrade through the row type's one migration block (reads decode old rows through it, Table.upgrade() rewrites them, #Secret rows through the storage codec), and a stored table upgrades across one schema change. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Data/TableMigration` and `--filter Data/TableSecretMigration` pass on o0, o1 and o2. The table declaration form follows open decision D-DB-TABLE1.
criteria.evidence: p238 batch compiler (dev 5bea729463), full collect-all suite: golden Data/TableMigration and Data/TableSecretMigration PASS on o0, o1 and o2.

criteria.text: get, put, insert and query on a typed table record read and write sets for D-INVALIDATE1, so a query's read set invalidates a live query after a write. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter web_app/table_read_set_invalidates_live_query`. The table declaration form follows open decision D-DB-TABLE1.
criteria.evidence: batch compiler p185 (dev b6b255de57), 2026-11-15: cases --filter web_app/table_read_set_invalidates_live_query 1/1 PASS (landed 143bcde2e8, case fixed in f1a25b1980)

criteria.text: get, put, insert and query carry DB.Read and DB.Write: a put in a function without DB.Write is an effect error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter table_put_without_db_write`. The table declaration form follows open decision D-DB-TABLE1.
criteria.evidence: batch compiler p184 (dev 61b4ee98a7), 2026-11-15: ui --filter table_put_without_db_write 1/1 PASS (landed d95870d428)

criteria.text: D-DATA-EVOLVE1=A, service half: the D-SERVICE-UPGRADE1 migrate function derives from the state type's one migration block. Waits on typed service state: today service state is untyped String records with a hand-written migration class, so no typed handoff exists to drive it. Proof: a golden in which a service upgrades its typed state across one schema change through the derived migrate function, on o0, o1 and o2.

A script can run `db.open("notes.db").query(SQL{"select …"})` with no row policy, joining tables or touching none, with `query` needing DB.Read and `execute` DB.Write so the #5949 prompt shows read-only versus writing, while a row policy stays available through `with_policy`; and a policy scope no longer refuses a query outside its one table such as `select 1`. Today `c.query(...)` is E0102 and a script needs `db.policy`, `with_policy` and `migrate` first (Core/DB/DB.jet:697-727). The default without a policy is the ballot D-SQL-SCRIPT1, on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DB/script_query_without_policy` and `--filter db/policy_scope_select_1`. (was #6277 c12)
criteria.evidence: Holds on dev eba6f39612 (136c4759d9) and matches the ratified D-SQL-SCRIPT1=A: DB.jet query/query_one are -[DB.Read]> and execute -[DB.Write]>, and with_policy returns a policy scope. On batch compiler p270: cases DB/script_query_without_policy PASS (a script queries db.open(...) with no row policy) and DB/policy_scope_select_1 PASS. The card's second filter, db/policy_scope_select_1, matches nothing because filters are case-sensitive; DB/ is the right spelling.

criteria.text: A DBScope is a confinement boundary: code holding a scope cannot rebuild the whole Store from public scope.state, and a scoped query cannot read or write tables outside its scope (today DB.jet:753-762 passes other-table queries through unchanged). Otherwise no doc, ballot or spec calls it one. Proof: cases rows for the scope-escape probe (Store rebuilt from scope.state is refused) and for an other-table query from a scope (refused with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot).
criteria.evidence: p288 batch compiler (dev 21bf9d76c7, Speed-3-3-6822-c7-scope-confinement landed 37e191e50b): cases db_scope_cannot_rebuild_store, db_scope_other_table_refused, policy_scope_select_1, script_query_without_policy and db_scope_enforces_policy_on_query_insert_and_live (2 rows) all PASS; ui db_scope_other_table_refused PASS; the full p288 suite shows no new failure from it.

cards.title: app and auth: the account lifecycle and outgoing mail
cards.body: Gap card N3 from the #6792 r3 proposal (Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md, section 4.7; crewboard/Web/web.jet, Logic/crew.jet invite and accept_invite). D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (ratified 2026-11-13) governs this card; the examples/*.jet and crewboard/* paths name the programs in Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md.

log.text: Cleanup 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2): c1 split into one criterion per builder (#6826 c6, #6826 c7, #6826 c8, #6826 c9); c5 split, membership is #6826 c10.

criteria.text: auth.Accounts.verify_email works end to end on the test host: a new account cannot sign in before it confirms its address.
kit.account_flows adds the sign-up, confirmation, reset, passkey and two-factor screens to the one route set on every target.
auth.verified_email returns an address only after it is confirmed; Crewboard's invite and accept_invite pass end to end, and an account with an unconfirmed matching address cannot accept.
app.mail sends through the .mail(transport, from:) of the server entry; a mail queued in a job is retried with the job.

Invitations: accepting an invitation deletes it; an invitation lapses after its expiry and a nightly job deletes it; the members policy refuses a member insert from a lapsed invitation; auth.verified_email returns the lowercased address.
auth.Accounts.reset_password works end to end on the test host: a reset link is single-use and expires in an hour.
auth.Accounts.passkeys works end to end on the test host: a WebAuthn passkey signs in.
auth.Accounts.two_factor works end to end on the test host: once turned on, a TOTP code is required, and recovery codes sign in.
auth.Accounts.limit_sign_in(per_minute:) works end to end on the test host: the sixth failed sign-in in a minute for one address waits.
Membership: set_role, remove_member and leave keep at least one owner (LastOwner); a removed member's open live queries re-run and are refused; jobs that push check membership first.

The `auth` package verifies tokens per D-AUTH-TOKENPOLICY1=A: JWT verification requires a named nonempty audience, exp and a matching aud (the empty-audience bypass is gone), HS256 only with constant-time comparison, and the selected PASETO mode. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Auth/TokenPolicyHostile` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #6448 c13)

Each mail a job sends gets its own Message-ID, made from the run key, the recipient and the send open: or link: value, hashed to fit the header, and app.mail passes it to the transport. A retried run repeats each Message-ID even when its query returns rows in another order, and two different mails from one job never share one. (Moved from #6825 c10; needs c4.)

The known-failing row this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv: CoreLib/core_auth_strict_jwt_and_paseto_hostile_matrix. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.body: Gap card N7 from the #6792 r3 proposal (Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md, section 8.1 observability row). log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): days + BLOCKED(c6 public metric names on Main's ballot list). c1 and c2 are trace spans and request IDs.

Main 2026-11-14: an App's spans export through the standard OpenTelemetry environment variables (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT, then OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT), read at serve, as batched OTLP/HTTP JSON off the request path, and the W3C traceparent header joins a Remote's trace. criteria.text: Every endpoint call, job, webhook and live-query re-run is a trace span with the request ID, the method, the caller's account ID (never a #Secret value) and the database statements it ran, exported over OTLP; the client's request ID matches the server span.
app.Problem.id in the error view is the trace ID of the failed request.

c21 rulings (Main, 2026-11-14) for the ProhibitedEffectReached reds (app handler rows and route cases). Root, from G6Meta-4: jet_driver_package_effect_rows (Pipeline.jet:5419-5475) follows the value edge from App.__route and __action (Core/Web/Web.jet:210,253) into Core-built dispatch lambdas, and so charges route() registration with the whole request path (__body_reader -[FS.Read, Time.Wait]>, Http.jet:967). (1) A Core-built lambda`s effects are charged where it can run, at app.serve(), and no longer at registration. app.serve() must still carry FS.Read, Net and Time.Wait, so a serving program`s main row is unchanged. A case pins both halves. A user handler`s value edges still count. (2) app.serve()`s reads of JET_APP_PORT and JET_DEV (__app_port and __app_dev, Web.jet:528-542) are toolchain reads, like the CLI-parse exemption (Pipeline.jet:5437), scoped to exactly those two names; a user env.get still charges Env.

Registering a route charges only what registration runs. Sema folds a lambda`s effects and call edges into the function that writes it (sema_effect_merge_lambda, JetSema Effects/Checks.jet:2605, called at :3370), so App.__route`s call_edges contain __app_page_response, and route() with a pure handler reaches FS.Read, Net and Time.Wait through the spooled body reader (Http.jet:967). Interim (2026-11-14): the send_fn_lowering and app-handler fixtures declare those effects, with a comment, which is sound because serving needs them. Fix: a TEffectFacts field that keeps edges from lambdas filling closed-row slots apart from a Core function`s own calls, charged where the lambda runs (app.serve()), not at registration. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Effects/route_registration_charges_only_registration` (route() with a pure handler reaches nothing; serve() reaches FS.Read, Net and Time.Wait), and the send_fn_lowering and app-handler fixtures drop their interim effect declarations.

A from return is a real loan at run time: a function returning T? or T from a borrowed owner (fn(item: X) -> T? from item with a read parameter, and a method -> T? from self, called directly or through trait dispatch) carries a pointer into the owner's payload, with no new cell, no byte copy and no retain, on O0, O1 and O2. Two cases must stay safe first: (a) an argument converted at the call (a Point passed where a union is expected) lives in a temporary cell that is released right after the call (op 16 in the IR, probe z04), so the loan must keep that temporary alive for the result's life, or the call is refused; (b) a body that returns a fresh value, or a copy of another parameter, on some path under from item (probe z05) has no owner to point into, so that path either stays a copy that jet audit reports or is refused. Today the from form and the same function without from emit identical IR at O0 (a 24-byte optional cell, a byte copy and a retain), and jet audit counts only the one without from (p207-p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 reviews 6 and 7, probes y12_from_val_copy_audit.jet with its .ir.out in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview6/probes, z01, z01b, z04 and z05 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview7/probes). Proof: a cases row whose IR or jet audit shows no copy for each form, a case or UI row for (a) and for (b), and a paired size/speed cell against the copy form. Before lowering, two more cases must be checked (D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8): a view captured by a lambda (c50) and a view of a Shared field written through any handle (c51); c46 lands only after both. Review 9 found more carriers: c46 lands only after c50, c51, c54 and c56 (struct field, enum payload, list, defer, method value, Shared to task).

Also stored and returned lambdas that capture a view outlive the owner's move today (review 9, probes e02 and e03 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview9/probes). Stored lambdas clone their captures, so the capture stays a loan: moving or rewriting the owner while the lambda lives is E0212 (D-PRIM-ANY1 ballot ¶48 at round 10: every holder keeps the owner borrowed).

A from view read out of a Shared field is checked against writes to that field, through the same handle or a second one: the write is refused while the view lives, or the view is not a loan. Today the view survives the write, and in the IR the value it was read from is released right after the call (op 70) (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8, probes a03 and a03b with IR in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview8/probes). Safe today only because the view is a copy; c46 must not lower this case to a pointer until it is checked. Proof: a UI snapshot and a cases row for each handle form.

E0305's suggested fix for a same-named pair compiles when applied. Today it spells the file's own type as <filestem>.Point, which fails with E0119 and then an E0108 that contradicts itself (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8, probes a04 and a04c in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview8/probes; c47 covers the named-case form). Proof: a UI snapshot of the corrected fix text and a cases row applying it. E0307's fix has the same defect: it spells the package's own member as filestem.Point (review 9, probe f06 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview9/probes); fix both.

An arm refused with E0305 still declares its binding (with an error type), so its uses add no cascade E0107: one root, one report. Today each use of the binding adds an E0107 (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 8, probes c1, a04, a08 and o8f in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview8/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot showing E0305 alone.
criteria.evidence: dev bb5f0f28a0 (6839-c53): ui --filter union_refused_arm_binding_is_one_report PASS on the batch 13 compiler (dev bb5f0f28a0); E0305 alone, no cascade E0107.

criteria.text: A loan keeps its owner through every carrier: a view (a from result or an arm binding) stored in a struct field (e01, against control e01b, which is E0212), an enum payload or nested binding (e07, against e07b), a list built in a loop (e05), a defer (e06), a method value bound to it (e08), or a Shared cell handed to a task (e09, which bypasses E1102) keeps the owner borrowed: moving or rewriting the owner while the carrier lives is E0212. A plain arm binding escapes the same way today (e10), and rewriting the owner leaves the view reading the old value (e11). Safe today only because views are copies; #6839 c46 must not lower views to pointers until this holds (p209, dev a1c3325a65, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 9, probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview9/probes). Proof: one UI snapshot per carrier, plus a cases row of each legal carrier use. Also a tuple field, pair: (view: got, tag: 1) (h02), and a map value, m["k"] = got (h05): each lets the owner move and reads the old value today (D-PRIM-ANY1 review 10, probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview10/probes).

Two instances of one generic type in a union (Box<Int> | Box<String>) have defined arms, and no diagnostic suggests or accepts the compiler's internal names. Today the bare .Box(b) arm is E0305 with the wrong text ('doesn't belong') (f01); the else is E0641 (f01b); and E0641's fix suggests .M_Box_Int_ | .M_Box_String_, which compile and bind (f01c, f01d), although the internal identity tag is refused elsewhere (a08). Internal names are never user spellings (p209; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 9, probes f01-f01d in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview9/probes). Proof: UI snapshots of the corrected E0305 and E0641 text, and a case showing a mangled-name arm is refused. The same holds with one instance: E0641 over Int | Box<Int> offers .M_Box_Int_ (m33), and .M_Box_Int_(x) binds boxes.Box<Int> beside kit.Box (m31b) (D-PRIM-ANY1 review 11).

A from result or an arm binding chosen by a value-producing if or table keeps its owner borrowed: with got: pick(item), w: if flag -> got else -> None (h06), the call itself in a branch, w: if flag -> pick(item) else -> None (h09), the same view in both branches (h08), a table's value (h10) or an arm binding (h11), moving or rewriting the owner while w lives is E0212, as it is for a second local (h01) or a relay through a from function (h03). Today each compiles, the move prints the old value, and rewriting the owner leaves w reading 41 (h12). spec.md:2057-2058 keeps invalidation through control-flow joins and 2068-2069 unions branch sources (dev 7f902dd915). Safe today only because views are copies; #6839 c46 must not lower views to pointers until this holds (p209 and p210, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 10, probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview10/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot per form and a cases row of the legal use.

A bare generic name in type position (fn(b: Box) with Box: struct<T>) reports E0104 alone: one root, one report. Today it adds an E0112 at the call, '`show` wants `Box` for argument 1, but this is `Box`<Int>', whose type text puts the type arguments outside the backticks (p209, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 10, probe t03 in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AnyReview10/probes). Proof: a UI snapshot showing E0104 alone.

criteria.text: A user trait implemented for a library trait type (impl lib8.Shown.Back {}) is refused with E0301 at the impl, as impl Shape {} is (spec.md:924-925), since a trait names no type to implement it for; or it works. Today it is accepted and inert: a Shown value has no point() (E0311, m44), and a Shown value at a T: Back bound gets E0904 'No trait named Back is in scope for the bound on T', naming a declared trait (m47) (p210, O0/O1/O2 alike; D-PRIM-ANY1 review 11, probes fm/m44, fm/m44b, fm/m47). Proof: a UI snapshot.

The JetCLI unit tests pass. On batch compiler p325 (dev e6ddae4d43), run as the suite runs them (JET, JET_BIN and JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY set), two fail: jet test Compiler/JetCLI 48 passed, 1 failed: "code suite rows sort, a repeated id fails, and a stopped suite adds a failing row" (Source/CLI/TestProfile.jet:743 expects "suite `perf`: ..." and gets "Suite `perf`: ..."); jet test Compiler/JetCLI/Tests 189 passed, 1 failed: "the settings census lists every command family and every flag with its setting or why it has none" (CommandSettings.jet:231). No per-cycle suite ran compiler unit tests until now. Proof: both commands report 0 failed on the batch compiler, and the landing suite runs every Compiler/<Pkg> and Compiler/<Pkg>/Tests package each cycle.

cards.title: Exceptional built-in debugging and profiling, built on Jet's reflection and metaprogramming (Jai-style)
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-14), high priority, on G5: Jet ships exceptional built-in debugging and profiling, done early so the team dogfoods it to fix Jet itself. As in Jai, much of it should come cheaply from the reflection and metaprogramming Jet already has: type facts drive value display and watch expressions, and compile-time code that sees every function can insert profiling spans or checks without a separate tool. Today: jet perf (run, test, attach, view, compare, export; source sampling, memory counters, .jettrace) works; jet debug (lldb and DAP) is weak on the self-hosted toolchain (#6730 has 24 open criteria, and Compiler/JetDebug no longer checks); no metaprogram instrumentation exists; whole-program compiler events are still being planned (#5009). Depends on #6730 and #5009.

log.text: Worktree saves from 2026-11-21 still partly off dev af651a6949 (share of added lines present): $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/wt-save/Lens-6841-1522.diff 74% (Image/Loader, CLI/Perf/Counts, Outside, Session), $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/wt-save/Rivet-6841.diff 70% (CLI/Perf/SourceSampling, Tests/Perf, JetDebug/NativeDump, JetRuntime/PerfSamples), $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/wt-save/lens-stash1.diff 75% (CLI/DebugDump, InspectCompiler, Perf/Outside, Perf/Session), $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/wt-save/lens-stash2.diff 52%, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/wt-save/Rivet-c113.diff 74% (Docs/Spec/Reference/core-library.md, Docs/Spec/safety.md). The missing lines may have been rewritten rather than lost; the next worker on this card checks each file before writing new code.

Handover 2026-11-21 20:40 (owner paused this stream for an uninterrupted compiler-performance session). c94: Rivet-6841-c94-attach-window landed as 5c61361976 (p438, dev d643d1e71a). On the gate-p438 jet, `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Perf/attach` passes 11 of 12; Perf/attach_samples_a_command still fails at its unchanged hot-function check ("% total · unit.rt_text_append_owner"), because the comptime child's samples are unnamed (#6995 c11). That root is Lens-6995-c11-comptime-names.r1, landing in p439; once it is on dev, rerun the Perf/attach filter and meet c94 if all 12 pass. c39 stays open: the review's verdict does not hold on every axis yet (Docs/Audits/2026-11-19-debug-profile-best-in-existence.md). c108 waits on its ballot for the Canvas Debug panels. A stale worktree (IfHole-6-1, base 50b6fec6e7) held an uncommitted, earlier version of the c95/c106 disassembly work that landed as c0e8fae53e and 04181acf9c (its cases pass on a0.0.46); it was removed, and its diff is kept at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/handover/IfHole-6-1-uncommitted.patch.

Worktree audit 2026-11-21 (dev 938d4d84f8): the IfHole-6-1 worktree (base 50b6fec6e7) holds unlanded work. When a call is inlined, OptEntry.jet and OptInline.jet copy the caller slot_formal, so an inlined frame lists its function parameters at -O1 and -O2. Native.jet adds a test for it, and observability.md text says an inlined frame locals lists its parameters "with the value passed where the code still holds it, else <Unavailable> with why". Every other added line in that tree is on dev. Its diff is saved at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/wt-save/IfHole-6-1.diff. The tree stays until a worker rebases and submits this or it is judged superseded.

c116 not met: on gate-p419 (tip 24356fa7b8), Tests/Cases/Perf/overlapping_zones_attaches_share_the_window failed 28 of 30 cases-runner runs (window_wall_ns 1.956e9 against >= 2e9, load 11-28); it passed once in the p419 suite. Sent back to its implementer.

c115 cause (Rivet, 2026-11-21): jet perf run spawns jet run --observe (Perf/Session.jet:197-199), whose jet_rt_observe_link route is not root-free, so ir_entry_own keeps the process root and the profiled program is a rooted main, not the shipped owned main. Decided within this card's scope: an observed program keeps its owned main, since a profiler must measure the shipped program. c114 decided: one load and branch before each runtime syscall (the host_call gate), measured inside noise against at least 210 ns per syscall (20M getppid, p407 O2); perf's own and signal-handler syscalls stay ungated; the #6444 cat bench gates it.

c94 checked, left open: zones (Perf/attach_turns_zones_on), flight ring (Perf/attach_drains_flight_ring), alloc (Perf/heap_snapshot_types_retention_and_diff) and outside (Perf/attach_samples_a_plain_jet_process) each assert the real window in their headers; the browser family (perf_attach_drives_real_devserver_browser_lifecycle) is KNOWN-FAILING under #5931 (known-failing.tsv, devserver E2104), so c94 waits on #5931.

c89 checked, left open: on the gate-p392 jet (probe axis p3, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Lens/c89-p3-gate-p392.txt) a `jet perf attach --source live.jet --zones=500ms` header reads window=live run_wall=847040249ns run_cpu=52288977ns: the window's real wall and CPU, no longer 1443ns/0ns, and Perf/attach_turns_zones_on asserts it (window_wall_ns >= 500 ms and <= took, cpu > 0). Not met: c89 asks for about 500 ms for a 500 ms window, and the window ran 847 ms, because it opens at the writer's next 250 ms publication after the request and closes at the next one after it is removed (observability.md, zones). Also open: the view still prints `Sample wall 1683ns` for the live snapshot's own sample. To close: open and close the zones window on the request itself (not the publication cadence), or bound the overshoot in the case, and make the snapshot's sample line say what it is.

c105: ballot D-PERF-OVERHEAD-BOUND1 (drafted by Lens, reviewed by Main) is posted to the owner. Option A bounds the runtime's share at 1% and reports the kernel's share as an estimate from timed samples, which may read low (1.85 us/sample charged vs 2.3 us probed). A fixed 4 kHz default was weighed and excluded by c68's 8 kHz parity. The overhead row stays failing until the ballot is ratified and built; no bar was relaxed.

c104 not met: in p392's proof run and units profile, JetDebug an_optimized_stop_never_shows_a_scattered_list_as_empty fails at -O2 ('Can't evaluate items: this session has no compiler'). OptScalar --filter scattered passes. Root: Native.jet evaluate skipped an <Unavailable> local and fell through to compiling the name, which a session with no evaluator (the unit test, a dump) refuses. Fix filed as SUB Main-6841-c104-print-unavailable (print refuses an unavailable local at once: 'local items has no readable value at this stop'); passes at -O1 and -O2 on the p392 compiler in a scratch tree. c104 is met when p393's proof run passes it.

c104: root confirmed by JET_OPT_DISABLE=scalar. With scalar replacement off, the same -O2 stop shows items = [0, 3, 6, 9, 12]. When the storage is lent, OptScalar keeps it for the loan, but its bytes hold the fields only around each loan, while the address slot still located the variable. Fix submitted as Main-6841-c104-scattered-list: IRFunction.scattered marks those address slots, ir_x64_variables gives their variables no location (shown unavailable), and every slot-renumbering pass carries the list. A JetIR unit test fails without the marking. The JetDebug test from the criterion (-O1 and -O2; accepts the true list or unavailable, refuses []) fails on the p391 jet and runs on the next batch compiler. Showing the true value from the field slots (DW_OP_piece) is possible later work, not needed for c104.

c104 root, found by `jet debug` disassemble at the stop (p390 batch compiler, -O2 prog.jet): early(5) folds to a constant list in rodata (0x41b008) and later() is inlined into run(). The optimizer splits the list header into registers (r14 = word 0, r13 = the data pointer, the length at [rbp-0x48]), but the DWARF location of `items` stays `[rbx]`, the original stack slot at rbp-0x60, of which only the length word is written. The debugger reads that slot faithfully and shows []. The defect is in the backend debug-location emission: once an aggregate local is split into registers, its location must follow the pieces (DW_OP_piece per register) or end, so the debugger shows it as unavailable. Owner: the backend debug-info path, not JetDebug.

Owner order 2026-11-20: speed and size work goes to E24 (G11) or E25 (G13) unless the owner says otherwise. Moved the lldb speed bar (old c70) to #6960, the zone cost under 27 ns (old c87) to #6958, and the task start latency (old c100, the per-carrier wake root and its proof design) to #6440.

Perf/task_clock_nominal_matches_kept fails in suite p387 (nominal 335 > kept+1 = 327), and stays failing until fixed. The case premise "the kernel share of the spin is under a period" is false. Under exclude_kernel the task clock counts both modes and the kernel skips an overflow that lands in kernel mode, so nominal minus kept is the period ends that fell in the kernel, the second runtime thread's syscall time included. Measured on gate-p387: 408/413, 350/358, 389/399, 4611/4646, 10739/10866, a 1.2-2.8% gap that grows with run length. At perf_event_paranoid 2 no counter separates user time. Decision: no bound widening. Samples carry the task clock count (PERF_SAMPLE_READ), so the dropped period ends D are counted exactly, and the case asserts nominal == kept + D. This lands in one samples-file format bump with the stack-id cites (Lens).

Sampler overhead, correction to the earlier log: the 0.75% of R2(d) was the POSIX-timer sampler at 1 kHz or less; the rise to about 3% followed the 8 kHz rate (6dda4bf451), not the kernel ring. Per-sample kernel cost on this host, 5 runs: ip-only 1.10 us (the floor, 0.88% at 8 kHz), callchain-only 2.06, current callchain+512 B 2.29; a STACK_USER copy large enough for Jet stacks costs more (16 KiB 2.89, 32 KiB 4.63) and still truncates 95% of compiler samples (deeper than 32 KiB), so drain-time unwinding is rejected. Decision: the 2% budget at the default rate stands (2.5 us/sample all-in at 8 kHz). Keep the callchain; shrink STACK_USER to the largest frameless-leaf frame so the leaf caller recovery stays; cut the handler/drain cost; calibrate from interleaved on/off pairs. The default rate (8 kHz vs 4 kHz) is user-visible and goes to ballot D-PERF-RATE1.

Sampler overhead finding (receipt_reports_measured_overhead, suite p383-p384). The case fails quiet and loaded alike: overhead_ns is 56-60 ms (2.8-3.0%) on burn.jet against the 2% budget (40 ms). The run_delay subtraction works: a run-queue wait 3x the run time leaves the receipt at its quiet value. Cause: 64c616649f moved sampling to the kernel ring with sample_type IP|TIME|CALLCHAIN|REGS_USER|STACK_USER (512-byte copy), and the kernel FP callchain write costs 2.7-3.2 us per sample at about 30 frames. Docs/Audits/2026-11-18-best-debugger-profiler.md:917 R2(d) "0.75%" comes from Probes/sampler-overhead.log (d3fbbe5cb4), measured on the earlier SIGPROF sampler, so it is stale for the current sampler: the switch raised overhead about 4x. Decision: the 2% budget stands and the bound does not rise. The cut is to drop CALLCHAIN and unwind FP+CFI inside one larger STACK_USER copy at drain time, marking deeper stacks truncated, with calibration from interleaved on/off pairs. Proof in a quiet window: jet run Tools/Perf/SamplerOverhead/Main.jet -- --jet jet --runs 9 --bar 200, which also re-measures R2(d) on the current sampler.

Decision (defect fix within scope; suite p383 row JetPerfTracePartsCaptureRun/perf_run_short_program_has_repeatable_source_attribution): a profile has one shape whether or not CPU samples land. (a) Samples in compiler-emitted shims such as the entry shim count as outside the source, like helpers, never as a source row. (b) The run wall observation row is kept beside any CPU sample rows instead of being swapped out. The case asserts the stable shape. Also under measurement: at 8 kHz on task-clock, a 0.5 ms program should collect about 4 samples but records 0 in nearly every run, so short programs may lose samples at arming or at the final drain.

c94 on p355 (dev a05d321392): 3 of 4 attach lens families report the real window and pass: point/flight ring (Perf/attach_drains_flight_ring), zones (Perf/attach_turns_zones_on, window_wall >= 500 ms), alloc (Perf/heap_snapshot_types_retention_and_diff, the 500 ms --lens=alloc --zones=500ms step). The browser relay family (JetPerfTracePartsBrowser/perf_attach_drives_real_devserver_browser_lifecycle) is KNOWN-FAILING under #5931 (Compiler/JetDevServer does not compile, so jet dev --target=web is refused E2104); its window lines are added to that case now and c94 is met when #5931 lands and the case passes.

Idle cores clock down while the long narrow line runs, a real speedup shortens the idle gap, and a virtual speedup cannot. Decision: the lens samples core clocks and flags its gains when idle cores clock down past a stated share (the same pattern as the contention refusal), and the case compares only clock-steady runs. 153 rounds are woken-late (begin 718 us late). The runtime wake is a single FUTEX_WAKE_PRIVATE right after unlock, with no polling or floor, so the delay is the CPU leaving deep idle. A bounded spin before an idle carrier parks (about 50 us, checking workSeq, as Go and Tokio do) would trade CPU for wake latency. Finding for the scheduler performance work; not needed for c55.

Decision (c47 gap 4, Core #Profiled handler): option (a). c6 root, part 2 (Main, objdump of the gate-p305 -O2 ProfileOverhead arms): the plain arm runs under a program-owned main (EntryOwned.jet ir_entry_own: host startup, jet_rt_main_owned_start, the entry), while any core.perf use keeps the process root (main calls jet_rt_main), because jet_perf_zone_open/close, jet_perf_frame and jet_perf_plot are not in IR_ROOT_FREE_ROUTES. The root links +18.5 KB of scheduler-root code (jet_rt_main, deadline parse, world_now, stop polls, root publish, env index) and runs it at startup, so more 64 KiB text windows fault in: with env -i, the zoned image has 172/172 KB text resident against the plain image 108/148. Just listing the perf routes as root-free would drop attach: only jet_rt_main runs the observation start (Main.jet observe_start_code), which opens the flight ring that jet perf attach needs. Fix design: an owned main whose module links observation calls the observation start itself (x64_object_main, after jet_rt_main_owned_start), and the perf routes join the root-free set (their off paths read only perf_zones_on; their on paths write rows and need no root). Proof: profile-overhead pair peak_rss_kb even, plus Perf/attach_turns_zones_on and the zone cases unchanged. The -O1 wall +2.4% is to be rechecked after it, since the root also adds stop polls to every loop.

c65 decision (Main): the precise branch is provable on this host (Ryzen 9 7950X3D, kernel 7.2.8, perf_event_paranoid=2). IfHole probe: ibs_op (type 11) per thread with exclude_kernel=1 and config2 bit 0 (sysfs format swfilt, the kernel software privilege filter) opens and gives about 2590 user-IP samples in 0.3 s; ibs_fetch the same. ibs_op user-only without swfilt gives EINVAL; with no exclude gives EACCES; cycles precise_ip=1/2 gives EINVAL (AMD forwards them to IBS without swfilt); precise_ip=3 gives EOPNOTSUPP. Reading of the criterion: "perf_event_paranoid at most 1" is met where the kernel permits a user-only precise event, as IBS swfilt does at paranoid 2. Design: try ibs_op swfilt in cycle-count mode, then cycles precise_ip=2 (PEBS), then the CPU-time timer signal; one per-thread mechanism and one sample record; the perf receipt sampling object names the pc source and each refusal errno. criteria.text: c39 P1 rate parity with Superluminal (8 kHz, full stacks): Linux expires CPU-clock timers (timer_create CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID) only from the scheduler tick, so that sampler is capped at CONFIG_HZ (1000 or 250 Hz). Where the kernel lets a process profile itself (perf_event_paranoid at most 2, the upstream default), jet perf run samples each thread at up to 8 kHz with whole stacks through perf_event_open, at the existing rate setting, and four fib tasks at -O2 keep at least 90% of the nominal samples at 8 kHz; where it may not, the CPU-timer sampler runs at the tick and the receipt states the cap and its reason. The overhead bar of c44(d) holds at the default rate. Proof: a Perf case asserting the receipt's source, rate and kept share at 8 kHz, plus a case forcing the timer path that asserts the stated cap.
criteria.evidence: p324 batch compiler (dev 6dda4bf451, IfHole c68-default-8khz landed): Perf/task_clock_keeps_eight_khz PASS (receipt source perf_event task-clock, rate 8000 Hz, kept share >= 90% for four fib tasks at -O2) and Perf/timer_fallback PASS (forced timer path, receipt states the CONFIG_HZ cap and its reason). Overhead at the 8 kHz default, m68 harness ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/IfHole-6-1/m68/m68.sh, 38 runs x 5): 1894 samples, handler 331 ns + delivery 1753 ns = 2080 ns per sample, measured overhead 1.24% (cost projection 1.66%), under the c44(d) 2% bar. criteria.text: Owner order 2026-11-19: the debugger is never slower than lldb, with no fork or evaluation-cost excuse, since Jet controls the compiler, runtime and stack. Every measure of `jet run Tools/Perf/DebugLatency/Main.jet -- --functions 20000 --runs 5` is at most lldb's on the same image and host: first_stop, print_place, print_first, second_eval, per_step, print_again, watch_per_stop and condition_per_hit. On p330: print_first 60.9 ms vs 7.4, second_eval 27.9 vs 1.2, condition_per_hit 2.9 vs 0.7, watch_per_stop 10.5 vs 8.3. The tool's bars become "at most lldb's" for every measure, and the fix is general (the evaluation path every expression, condition and watch takes), with a second program proving the gain. Proof: the DebugLatency run prints every bar met against lldb.

criteria.evidence: Landed on dev as 130fffbf6a (cycle p394). Causes named: (1) the canvas client read its first answer with a 5 s deadline, but on the native tier that answer waits for a whole `jet build -O0` of the entry (1.0-1.6 s measured at load average 214-235), so a loaded machine pushed it past the deadline; the client now reads without its own deadline, bounded by the case step timeout, and canvas-protocol.md states the first request builds first. criteria.text: Regression of c67: `Perf/receipt_reports_measured_overhead` fails again under suite load. In p387-p391, overhead_ns reached 43-66 ms against the case's 40 ms bar (p391: 50262488). Quiet, it is 34.9 ms (1.74%). Lens's root: at 8 kHz with whole kernel callchains, the kernel's ring write is about 1.85 us a sample (30.1 of 34.9 ms), and under load the kernel's own perf-interrupt time climbs. No ratified decision sets the 2% bar, so the fix is either engineering that cuts the kernel's per-sample cost while keeping c44 whole stacks and c68 8 kHz, or the D-PERF-OVERHEAD-BOUND1 ballot (Lens drafting); never a looser bar without a ruling. Proof: the case passes in 3 consecutive full suites (suite-pNNN cases.out), under whatever bound is ratified.

criteria.text: The debugger evaluator returns the right value for a call that returns a list. Found by Lens on gate-p420 (dev 4f1f6c1c7f, 2026-11-21): with `build: fn(i: Int, items: Int) -> [Int] { out := [Int]{}; out.push(i); loop k in 1..<items -> out.push(i + k); out }`, stopped at a line inside main, `jet debug main.jet --break main.jet:33 --do continue --do "print build(3, 2).len()" --do "print build(3, 2)"` prints `.len() = 0` and `build(3, 2) = [3533934837823998284, <Unavailable>, … 140737488319240 more]` instead of 2 and [3, 4], while `print [Int]{3, 4}` is right. So the evaluator reads a returned list from the wrong place: its result slot or the list header is not where the call left it. Fixed at the evaluators call-result path for every growing value (list, text, map), not for this call. Proof: a Debug case that prints a called list, text and map result and their .len() on O0, O1 and O2, with the expected values.

cards.title: Generated code: the Compiler value, Meta effects, generation rounds and rollback
cards.body:
Destination: a program that generates or rewrites code does it through one passed, root-created `Compiler` value whose actions are Meta effects checked like any effect, and generation is deterministic, provenanced and all-or-nothing. Why: generated code must be as trustworthy and debuggable as hand-written code, and nothing above marker expansion may happen by import alone.

Governing decisions: D-META-LADDER1=A (Meta effects follow the rule of every effect; compiler control is one passed value; macros stay out), D-META-OPTIN2=A (a checked package opt-in suffices for above-level-five operations), D-HOOK-STAGES1=A, D-ADDSTRUCT-TYPE1=A (meta.add_struct names a field's type with a TypeId). Spec: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md.

Carried decisions: the org policy file accepts the same `authority: { deny: [...] }` record as package.jet (D-EFFBUDGET1), applied as an outer rung that only narrows (Main 2026-11-11). `#build`, `#program`, `#package` and `#phase` are spelled with `#` and cannot be shadowed (D-META-HASH2=A, landed 00a2b37a42..53805444ba). Sizing (owner 2026-11-11): each Compiler-value slice is at most one hour of code and one hour of tests. Background: the Compiler value needs a build session alive through application checking and closures called on each checked-function event; see the G6Decl notes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G6Decl/BLOCKED.md.

Carried from #3526, #3520 and #4276 (closed 2026-11-14).

log.text: c12 scope decision: c12 is met by S2 (the standard sizes are Prelude aliases of the three generic families, generated into the parser and number-kind tables) and S12 (an impl on a family expands to one impl per size; Core's per-size impls become one per family), once golden Basics/ passes on O0, O1 and O2 and git grep shows one family definition per kind in Core. S4-S11, which collapse the compiler's internal per-width representation, are not required by c12's text and overlap #6851's type identity work.

c12 S2b decision: the parser keeps binding the standard size names (I8..F64) to the number types through a table generated from the Prelude alias declarations (checked against them by a generator check or guard), and leaves a Named type wherever the file declares, imports or type-parameters that name, so a shadowing type stays the user's; Sema resolves other aliases of a family through the alias. Chosen over a full Sema pre-resolution audit (about 850 JetSema and 300 JetIR sites, untestable before a build, self-host miscompile risk).

Batch 9 landed c8f, c6r, c10r, c5r, c7 (dev 9597797b1b). Held: c1 (ui meta_ladder_marker_cannot_rewrite_without_a_compiler_value snapshot lacks the closing summary lines), c14 and c2 (cases meta_events_hear_marked_functions and meta_events_hear_resolved_calls passed in batch 7 and now stop with ArithmeticOrBoundsFailure). c10 stays open: generate_cancel_midway_leaves_no_partial_module fails (ComptimeFuelExhausted then UnknownFunction second_value).

c12 S1: the private float storage is builtin.FloatWord<exponent, fraction> beside builtin.Word<bits>, because Core.rows type exports and the Core owner maps key on bare names and a jet_builtins Float export would become the bare owner of Float.

c12 S1 decisions: (1) the private integer storage in jet_builtins is spelled builtin.Word<bits> (floats builtin.Float<e, f>) because Bits is already the public bitset collection and Core types are bare-named; jet_builtins is Core's private door (D-CORE-BUILTINS1), so this is not user surface. (2) E0324 AliasWithoutParameters admits a parameterless alias whose target is an applied generic in any package (its own rationale: aliases shorten generic spellings), so I8: Signed<8> needs no Core-only exception; an alias of a plain non-generic type stays E0324.

c12 plan (D-CORE-NUMFAMILY1=A), ranked by site share (1557 Type.IntN/Float32 sites, 236 name-string sites): S1 Core families Bits<bits>/Float<e,f>, Signed/Unsigned/IEEE plus aliases and foundation_family_type (~3%, UI snapshot shows U8 for Unsigned<8>); S2 names resolve through Core aliases, width arms and IntegerKinds deleted (~8%); S3 from_<source> conversions from one family rule (~4%); S4 Foundation representation collapse to Type.Apply with accessors type_fixed_int/type_ieee (234 sites); S5-S8 Sema (~215 each); S9-S10 IR (323); S11 remaining packages (~140); S12 Core per-width impls to one impl per family. Proof each slice: golden Basics/ at o0/o1/o2 plus touched package unit tests. F16/BF16/I128/U128 stay on the paired card. Batch 7 landed c8r (b7986f520d), c9r (6bcfb66b1f), add_struct wording (d8063248ea); c6r and c10r fixture failures went back to the worker, c5r/c7 held behind them.

Rebased the Antigravity c11-c13 patch onto dev and split it. c11 (Toolchain/CompilerValueMethods.jet generator, its build.jet step and JetEval test; generator output equals the committed file) is in batch 3. c13 (generated modules load under jet check and jet run: InspectBuild.jet, Request.jet jet_cli_compile_prepared, EntityBuckets.case, build_fn_generated_modules_load_across_run_check_and_build) is held as $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/tmp/orch/land/6846-c13.patch. It regresses 5 cases: jet_cli_compile_prepared now runs the entry package's build fn for every check, fix and explain, so the build fn's reports and pinned fetches fail  (program_info_effects_tell_the_written_row_from_the_solved_row, program_info_groups_a_two_module_package_into_one_package_record, program_info_uses_qualified_collision_free_type_function_and_method_identities, keep_going_trap_keys_failed_function_references, explain_effects_reaches_comptime_inputs; A/B: pass without it, fail with it). Fix direction: under check, fix and explain, fold in only the modules the build fn generates, without making its reports or input fetches the check's outcome.

Unlanded Antigravity work, saved 2026-11-23: c11-c13 patch $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/tmp/parked_arch/parked_g1_6846_c11_c13.patch (InspectBuild, Request, JetEval CompilerValueMethods, build.jet, EntityBuckets case; conflicts with dev af651a6949, 7% present, needs a rebase) and its new files $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/tmp/parked_arch/6846-untracked-goalsorder.tar (Compiler/Toolchain/CompilerValueMethods.jet, JetEval/Tests/CompilerValueMethods.jet, Tests/Cases/BuildEntry/build_fn_generated_modules_load_across_run_check_and_build).

criteria.text: A metaprogram action above marker expansion (adding declarations outside a marker, rewriting a body, making a type from text) needs a `Compiler` value, and each action checks its Meta cases (`Generate`, `Include`, `Rewrite`, `Types`, `Raw`) like any effect: denied by written code, otherwise allowed; without a `Compiler` value it is refused with a registered diagnostic and UI snapshot.
criteria.evidence: jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter meta_ladder_: 11 PASS, 0 FAIL on the batch 11 compiler (dev 431de10934 + batch-11 stack; landed on dev as ea939e9553..7578d807e7, a1267a9894). Snapshots cover the Generate, Rewrite, Raw and Types denials and E0774 for a marker without a Compiler value; Meta.Include has no action on dev, so it has nothing to check.

criteria.text: Standard mode allows complete read-only reflection and explicit checked generation and refuses operations above level 5 unless the package opts in (D-META-OPTIN2=A); `#run` runs at every tier, fn build runs only for artifacts, and a built artifact never re-runs `#run`; a pure cache hit keeps every observable effect (print count and order).
criteria.evidence: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter meta_ladder_levels: 2 PASS on the batch 11 compiler (dev 431de10934 + batch-11 stack; landed on dev as ea939e9553..7578d807e7, a1267a9894) (meta_ladder_levels_run_build_artifacts_and_cache_hits pins #run at check, test, run and build, fn build only for artifacts, no #run re-run in a built artifact, and #Memo cache hits keeping print count and order; compile-cache reuse is off by default).

criteria.text: `meta.add_struct` takes each field's type as a TypeId (D-ADDSTRUCT-TYPE1=A, ratified 2026-11-13); the String form of CompilerField.type is gone in one cutover, and a computed name is still refused with its registered code.
criteria.evidence: 6e387d3e3b: CompilerField.type is TypeId (CoreRecordRows.jet); BuildEntry meta.add_struct cases (4/4) and meta_ladder_ UI snapshots (7/7) PASS

criteria.text: Each generated declaration and rewrite carries a stable identity and its full producer and Compiler-handoff chain in `jet inspect`, `jet explain`, the editor and the CLI; diagnostics name the caller, handler, output or missing producer separately.
criteria.evidence: Landed on dev in c6d9e746f2 (the editor names what made a generated module, from .jet/build/receipt.json; its message records that inspect, explain and the CLI already carried the producer and handoff chain). Checked 2026-11-14 on dev 72a8142651 with the gate-p136 jet: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter meta_ladder_missing_producer` PASS 1.

criteria.text: Each generation round, source identity, collision check, dependency edge, lock fact and rollback result is deterministic and source-provenanced: two runs, and runs with permuted, cold, warm and parallel schedules, give byte-identical output and provenance.
criteria.evidence: Landed 01869d94a5 (c5r). Batch-9 -O1 compiler (dev 2541ece0b1 + 13 submissions), landed on dev 9597797b1b: cases generate_rounds_deterministic_across_cold_warm_parallel_and_permuted_runs PASS (with bubblewrap, no SKIP); Compiler/JetBuildSession/Tests/BuildGraphRules.jet --filter=generation_schedule 7/7; Compiler/JetCLI/Tests/InspectBuild.jet --filter=inspect_build 9/9.

criteria.text: Shadowing, duplicate output, self and multi-node cycles, round exhaustion, outside-root paths and materialization failure each leave no partial module and report their registered code with what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot; each test fails if the code, span, message or cleanup path is bypassed.
criteria.evidence: Landed afb50bc93c (c6r). Batch-9 -O1 compiler (dev 2541ece0b1 + 13 submissions), landed on dev 9597797b1b: cases generate_refusals_leave_no_partial_module PASS; ui --filter BuildGenerated 7/7 PASS and the Generate snapshots PASS (the one other FAIL is the pre-existing ForeignMetaCheckedBindings jetpack row); InspectBuild.jet --filter=inspect_build 9/9.

criteria.text: `generate {}` helper values and inline `b.generate` are one mechanism with byte-identical output and source maps; handwritten code uses the generated items; a collision reports at the helper's line; opt-in in-tree materialization fails on drift; raw source strings are refused.
criteria.evidence: Landed cbb8501201 (c7). Batch-9 -O1 compiler (dev 2541ece0b1 + 13 submissions), landed on dev 9597797b1b: cases generate_helper_ 4/4 PASS; BuildGraphRules.jet --filter=generation_schedule 7/7.

criteria.text: Generation follows a dependency-aware schedule (declared inputs, rounds, typed barriers, promised outputs); cycles and duplicate outputs are detected with registered codes.
criteria.evidence: Landed 82406dbdd0 (c8f) on the c8r base. Batch-9 -O1 compiler (dev 2541ece0b1 + 13 submissions), landed on dev 9597797b1b with bubblewrap on PATH: cases generate_schedule_orders_producers_before_consumers and generate_schedule_refuses_cycles_duplicates_and_round_exhaustion 2/2 PASS; cases failed_step_report_shows_its_stderr PASS.

criteria.text: When a promised generated output is missing, the error names its producer and its consumer, and an unrelated unknown name is not reported as a generation promise.
criteria.evidence: Landed 6bcfb66b1f (c9r). Batch-7 -O1 compiler (dev 3019343199 + stack): jet test Compiler --profile ui passes Tests/UI/generate_promise_missing_names_producer_and_consumer.jet; ui suite 0 new failures from c9r.

criteria.text: Cancelling generation midway, or exhausting memory or steps during it, leaves no partly published declaration and no stale checked fact; the next run starts clean.
criteria.evidence: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter generate_cancel_: 1 PASS on the batch 11 compiler (dev 431de10934 + batch-11 stack; landed on dev as ea939e9553..7578d807e7, a1267a9894) (generate_cancel_midway_leaves_no_partial_module).

criteria.text: The Compiler value's method list is generated from Core declarations: Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerValueMethods.jet no longer lists records and fields by hand, so a new field on `CompilerChecked` appears with no evaluator edit.

On a dev-built compiler at de08daf13a: 'jet Toolchain/CompilerValueMethods.jet --check' (from Compiler/) prints 'compiler value methods check passed'; 'jet test JetEval/Tests/CompilerValueMethods.jet' 2 passed, 0 failed, including 'generated compiler value methods accept CoreRecordRows fields and project values'. build.jet's compiler-value-methods step regenerates the file from CoreRecordRows on every jet build Compiler, so a new Compiler record field needs no evaluator edit.

criteria.text: Each number family has one generic definition that compile-time code expands to the needed widths (D-CORE-NUMFAMILY1=A), replacing one hand-written type per size. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Basics/` on O0, O1 and O2, and `git grep` shows one family definition per number kind in Core. The frozen #4570 holds the original item.

On a dev-built compiler (dev 1422e2ebd7 + this patch): Tests/Cases/BuildEntry/build_fn_generated_modules_load_across_run_check_and_build.case PASS (one module added by a package's build: fn loads the same way under jet run, jet check and jet build), Examples/Metaprogramming/Reflection/EntityBuckets golden PASS at o0/o1/o2, and the program_info_*, keep_going_trap_keys_failed_function_references and explain_effects_reaches_comptime_inputs cases PASS; golden, ui and cases show no new failure from it.

cards.title: One fact registry: typed rows, one query, uniform flow joins and one gate ledger
cards.body:
Destination: every compiler fact a user can see (marker rules, knowledge planes, rights, build facts, gates, send-safety, failure attribution) lives in one registry of typed rows, read through one public query, so tools and libraries see the same facts the compiler uses. Why: today facts live in several tables with several readers, so tools drift from the compiler.

Governing decisions: D-META-REG1=A (one registry substrate, told apart by attachment), D-META-REG2=A (one public `compiler.query`, ratified 2026-11-11), D-LEDGER1=D (three lifetime-separated stores behind one typed query), D-FACT-FLOW1=A, D-FACT-GATE1=A, D-FACT-HOME1=A, D-FACT-OWN1=A. How a fact is declared is D-DECL-TYPES1=A (field-less structs implementing Fact), built on the declarations card. Spec: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md.

Carried from #4276 (closed 2026-11-14).

log.text: All criteria met with recorded batch-compiler evidence; closed in the near-done sweep. Batch 23's full suite rechecks every named row.

Owner ratified D-BUILD-TARGETFACTS1=A, D-DERIV-READ1=A and D-DEBUG-PREP1=A (2026-11-24). Assigned: #5007 c7-c9 and #6848 c8 to G1Facts; #5007 c10-c11 and #6772 c15 to G1Generation-2 after the #6846 c12 family-Self fix.
