cards.title: jet fmt --simplify: guard clauses, single-use temporaries and one corpus migration
cards.body:
Destination: `jet fmt --simplify` rewrites code to the ratified simplest forms, the repository is migrated once with it, and style points are rewritten, never reported. Plain `jet fmt` keeps its one default style. Why: style should cost nobody attention; Jet has no warnings (owner, 2026-11-09 language review), so anything a tool can fix it fixes.

Governing decisions: D-FMT-SIMPLIFY1=A (plain jet fmt unchanged; the rewriter runs only with `--simplify`; teams canonicalize a repo in one deliberate run). Spec: Docs/spec/reference/cli.md (jet fmt), Docs/spec/spec.md (formatter).

Carried from #4276 and #6637 (2026-11-14).

log.text: Speed stopped. c5 unlanded: plain fmt comparison 0 diffs of 4321, guards and patch not yet run; c2 corpus migration not started (plan in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Speed-3-3/HANDOFF.md).

criteria.text: The in-repo corpus is migrated once with `jet fmt --simplify`, in one mechanical commit, and stays migrated: `jet fmt --simplify --check Compiler Core Jetpack Tools Examples tests` exits 0, and a plain `jet fmt` run leaves code it did not format unchanged. Proof: `jet fmt --simplify --check Compiler Core Jetpack Tools Examples tests`

`jet fmt --simplify` rewrites a nested if/else into guard clauses (early return) without changing behavior and never reports it; it is applied across Compiler/, Core and Jetpack in one mechanical change, `jet fmt --check Compiler Core Jetpack` passes, and the self-host chain reaches its fixed point.
criteria.evidence: dev 930090f78c8 (batch 44), run on the batch-44 compiler (its suite build also held #6852 p1/p2a, which this landing excludes; the landing tree passes all 240 guards without them): cases fmt_simplify_guard_clause PASS.

criteria.text: `jet fmt --simplify` inlines a needless temporary (an immutable binding used once, on the next line) only when evaluation order is unchanged, and never reports it; a fmt case pins an order-sensitive negative that is left alone.
criteria.evidence: p295 batch compiler (census build of dev 3f4dd54f21), landed Speed-3-3-6850-c3: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter fmt_simplify_inline_temporary PASS (with the order-sensitive negative); jet check Formatter.jet rc=0

criteria.text: `jet fmt --simplify` rewrites the old arm-table shapes (adds an explicit `else` arm, removes redundant returns and fallback tails), keeping comments, bindings, order, effects and spans, and reports nothing; plain `jet fmt` leaves them as written.  proof: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter fmt_arm_table_rewrite
criteria.evidence: dev 8ba69b5418, batch compiler p329 full suite: cases Fmt/fmt_arm_table_rewrite_adds_else_and_drops_redundant_returns PASS (plain jet fmt keeps the shapes and prints nothing; --simplify rewrites, reports nothing, a --check second pass keeps it; the program prints the same before and after).

criteria.text: Tests/Cases/Fmt has one AST-equality and second-pass stability case for every enabled simplify rewrite, and fmt_project/simplify_mode_is_stable_across_a_project exists. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Fmt/fmt_simplify_` and `--filter fmt_project/` pass.

cards.title: Core gets no privilege a package lacks: host-leaf gates, per-domain call checks, Core-only constructs, #Unsafe and lexing
cards.body:
Destination: Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use (Docs/spec/philosophy.md, pillar 5). Today sema lets Core do things a package cannot: it gates host leaves on the caller's module name, keeps a hand-written checker per Core domain, accepts constructs only in Core files, exempts Core from the #Unsafe secret rules, and lexes and parses Core with its own rules.

Why it matters: a third-party library must be able to do what Core does, and every privilege is a second rule that tools copy and drift on.

Sources: findings F02, F03, F07, F08 and F14 of Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md (line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Split from #6151, which keeps the Core-declaration and twin-table work. D-HOST-LEAF1=E (runtime is an ordinary library, #6615). Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4).

Ballot: package-private `__` helpers (the lexing criteria) are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

log.text: Decision (orchestrator, within scope) for n6 Data.jet: Dyn is a language-owned type with no Core declaration (like TaskGroups), so its checks (indexing, members, conditions, literal variants, get/has/keys/remove/len, the field/at/int/text accessors, decode/encode) move unchanged to Sema/Expressions/Dyn.jet: sema keeps owning language checks (I3). The domain checkers in Data.jet (csv/json to_string, data.query, Query/Stream methods, args.decode, db/env decode, SQL schema) move to Core declarations and rules, and Data.jet is deleted, as n6 states.

Decision (orchestrator, within ratified scope) for n6: sema's hardware call checks (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Hardware.jet: dma.start/.wait and board.<profile>.BLOCK.REG read/write/set/clear, the scope transfer tables and the hardware calls in Frames.jet) are removed as unratified compiler-privileged surface with no spec, test, example or snapshot. Their replacement is #6518 under the ratified D-HW-DECLARE1=A and D-CORE-BOUNDARY1=A: typed register blocks and DMA ownership as Core declarations (#6518 n1, n3, n7, n8). No ballot needed. The Loader's board-import exemption for targets stays.

D-CORE-LASTROWS1 posted for the owner's vote (two adversarial passes; the second, LastRowsReview2, verified the first's 10 findings and fixed 11 more). Rec A: tls.client keeps the ratified stream spelling, the host/port form becomes tls.connect, term.take becomes take_bytes. n18's last two rows (core.term take, core.net.tls client) wait on it.

c3 route: S2-S4's handler typing and the OpenAPI contract are not open questions. D-RULE-REWRITE1=A (the contract as a per-call #run parameter default) and D-RULE-BODYFACTS1=A (#Recorded calls in FunctionInfo) are ratified, and their builds are now criteria 39 and 40. Call-site rewriting stays ruled out (D-RULE-REWRITE1 whyNot B; no macros, syntax-decisions.md). The only unowned gate is REWRITE1's fifth, the typed-handler adaptation to one request; its ballot D-HTTP-HANDLER-DECODE1 is being narrowed to that after review (HandlerDecodeReview: the draft re-balloted REWRITE1 and BODYFACTS1).

c7: G1Checkers found and fixed the root of release and hardened builds dropping Core check rules. Lazy Core restore counted a marker check that held only the parser-appended None as non-blank, so every lazily loaded Core rule ran as { None }. The fix is jet_driver_core_body_blank in JetDriver CoreInterface.jet, with the DeclaredCallChecks golden (o0/o1/o2) and the case expiring_force_is_rejected_on_the_release_and_hardened_profiles. It goes in batch 45; o0/o1 already pass on the batch-44 compiler. c3/c5 finding: the remaining TimeHandles, StreamHandles, ProcessHandles, UIHandles and HTTP checks aren't rule moves. They type compiler-built handle types that Core doesn't declare, so c5 first needs those types declared in Core with ordinary Core functions. HTTP forms/E2411, StreamHandles E0904 and Geometry E2521 wait on criterion 35 (D-RULE-TYPEARGS1=A build), which G1Checkers takes next.

Three ballots posted after two Opus adversarial review rounds (r1 and r2 reviews in the orchestrator's ballot notes): D-PROCESS-BUILDER-RECEIVER1 (c5 ProcessHandles), D-SERVICE-SHAPES1 (c4 Services; option E was probed and found to need three missing language features) and D-RULE-DISPATCH-BUDGET1 (n=22; recommends moving n=22 unchanged to #6798, which owns the dispatch work). c4, c5 and n=22 wait on them. Independent work continues on c3, c5's other files, c6 and c7 (G1Checkers).

Adversarial review 2026-11-25 (Orchestrator, fresh) of the three draft ballots: D-PROCESS-BUILDER-RECEIVER1, D-RULE-DISPATCH-BUDGET1 and D-SERVICE-SHAPES1. All are rejected for revision. PROCESS-BUILDER: the share is Jet's general unmarked-owning-position law (Ownership/Checks.jet:3634), not a ProcessSpec privilege. Options are missing (the general law applied to receivers; mutate in place), the Rust comparison is wrong (Command takes &mut self), and the count of reuse callers is missing. DISPATCH-BUDGET: A's new card breaks the follow-up-as-criterion order, the 15 µs is a projection (15-20), and the cost against the 30M lines/s target is missing. SERVICE-SHAPES: an option is missing, one generic Core worker that picks its form by compile-time #if over the handler's reflect() (G1's own a79988747df), which keeps every spelling and meets c4 as written. Findings are with the author, G1Generation-2.

Defect found in batch 44, c6 Data: a collecting-loop lambda inside a generic body's #run, e.g. `names: #run (loop field in T.reflect().fields -> field.name)` within `#if schema_record(TypeId{T})`, fails at comptime.bodies with E0107 'Nothing named `T` exists here' (repro: Core/Data/Data.jet:1654 of the land/6851-c6-data-c-schema-b44 patch, stage-44c compiler). data-c-schema-r2 works around it with `fields: #run T.reflect().fields` and builds the columns at run time. The compiler gap stays open under c6: T must be in scope in every #run of a generic body, lambdas and loops included.

Correction: my earlier note on 'c20' (core_lower_entry_roots has no case) concerns the D-CORE-LOWER1 entry-half criterion. Earlier meets used list positions; they are corrected (n=18, 32, 38 reopened; n=19, 34, 39 met; n=33 re-evidenced).

c20 sweep (batch 43): the four SelfhostTerminators jet_lexer cases that had turned the ffi and export lines red now pass. But the named proof, cases --filter core_lower_entry_roots, matches no case. No Tests/Cases file covers the root kinds yet, so c20 needs one case per root kind (job, C export, CLI command, callback, other roots): each proves the root is kept and an unreached entry function has no lowered body (IR or symbol listing). Queued for the next free G1 implementer.

c6 Data, decided: data.schema moves into Core on TypeIds, with no new surface. A non-record row is one value column named by TypeId{T}.name, and Decimal/Fraction/Complex are matched by TypeId equality, so no builtin TypeInfo is needed and the drafted ballot D-TYPEINFO-DOMAIN1 is withdrawn unposted. Two implementation pieces under the ratified typed-reflection rule: TypeId{T} answered per instance in generic bodies, and a T.reflect() in an untaken #if arm builds nothing and reports nothing. data_schema_requires_typed_container keeps its code and text through a Core check rule.

Batch 43 defects in #6851 slices. Fixed in the batch tree: (1) c13 print style typed context.print as the filler's whole return type, PrintStyle Never!, which broke 2 goldens and 2 cases; ContextKeys now uses the success type. (2) c13 vault moved pbkdf2_hmac, so CryptoErrorRun's snapshot line was updated, and WrappedVaultKey's CoreSurfaceInventory source moved from static: to type:, since the builtin static rows are gone. (3) c34-a carried a decision citation in a CheckRules.jet comment, which is removed. Open: c34-a fails its own case check_rule_hears_written_parts on its own stage compiler (Misheard: a non-bare hole {record.id} is heard as 'hole - 2'), sent to G1Generation-2.

c6 blocker, decided as an implementation choice: `T.reflect()` inside a generic fn body fails (UnknownName T), because a generic body is checked once and a #run site is staged once. The ratified meaning is in metaprogramming.md, Typed reflection, item 2: T.reflect() reads the same in ordinary code and is a constant in the running program. So this is a defect, not new surface. Chosen fix: sema enumerates each generic fn's instances and lowers a T-dependent reflect read to a TypeTest chain of compile-time TypeInfo literals, which IR already folds per instance (one mechanism). A caller-site fold was rejected because it would give one read two meanings. Builder: G1Generation-2, in items of an hour or less, with a bounded-cost plan first; data.schema stacks on it.

Batch 42 landed eb7aaf51a8b: the template_paste_core_dunder_call snapshot points at line 11 and passes in batch 42's ui run (c39, one of its three snapshots; the other two are in batch 43). Batch 43 carries c9, c13 slices 1-2 and role slices (CBD 66 to 12), c19, c33 and c34 (D-RULE-WRITTEN1=A parts a and b).

Correction to the c34 entry above: no new ballot is needed. D-RULE-WRITTEN1 was ratified A on 2026-11-24: CompilerArg.written: [CompilerWrittenPart]? with CompilerWrittenPart: enum { Text(text: String), Hole(name: String?, span: SourceSpan) }. It is not yet built (absent from Docs/Spec and code on batch43). c34 is an unbuilt piece of that decision, assigned to G1Generation-2 to build as ratified. The template: String? shape is dropped.

c13: the old proof filter `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_declarations` matched no test (that guard is the package Tests/Guards/CoreDeclarations). The proof now names the package and core_builtins_door's CBD_CEILING reaching 0. The ceiling is 66 on dev, and 63 with the c13 slice-1 patch queued in batch 43.

c34 needs a ballot. The ratified CompilerArg surface (label, type, value, function, span) cannot tell an interpolated String literal such as "/users/{id}" from a String known only at run time: both are heard as type String, value None, function None, and neither SourceSpan nor call.source carries source text. Shapes found: (A) CompilerArg gains `template: String?`, the written text with each hole as {name}, set only for a literal with at least one hole whose value the build does not know; (B) `interpolated: Bool`, which cannot rebuild the quoted pattern for E2805's message; (C) `written: String?` for every argument, which exposes syntax for all arguments; (D) a template Dyn inside value, which breaks the rule that value != None means known. The ballot record is being drafted. c19 and c33 held on dev and their tests are in batch 43.

Sweep on dev e128950680d: the snapshots ui http_route_path_type and http_route_invalid_literal pass, but c33 and c34 are not met: the route checks still come from Sema/Calls/HTTPRouting.jet (the 'brace interpolation is not allowed in route patterns' message at line 463), not from a Core check rule, so the snapshots do not prove rule ordering or the interpolated-literal fact. The c9 (core_construct_ordinary_visibility) and #6852 c2 (declared_copy_resource_typestate_facts) filters match no test yet. c9 is assigned to G1Generation-2.

ContextOnStop o2 (batch 29 and 30 golden): it passes at o0, o1 and o2 in isolation on the batch 30 compiler (jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter=ContextOnStop, 3/3) and in two standalone jet builds. It fails only under the full suite's load, where the native compile-time run of core.files ReadOnlyHandle's marker check (Core/Files/Files.jet:427) returns no result and the compiler reports it as the user diagnostic Jet.InvalidStatement ('returned neither a value nor an explicit control result'). A compile-time child that ends without a result is a compiler or host failure, not a user error: under I2 it must not reach the user as a diagnostic. Open: find why the child returns empty under load (resource limit, timeout or crash) and report that cause instead.

Defects found while fixing the batch 29 regressions (G1Generation-2): (a) a marker rule declared in one module never hears calls from another: Core's StaticRoutes rule never sees App calls, so c37-b-r2's move of compile-time Jet.AmbiguousRoute into Core lost 6 UI snapshots. 6851-c37-b-fix reverts it and rides batch 31; c37-b re-lands once (a) is fixed. (b) An unhandled '(E | WebFormError)!' from FieldRef validate is reported as 'Jet.MissingDisplay: Never has no Display implementation' at the wrong span instead of an unhandled-failure diagnostic. 6851-c38-fix (dev 57dc273725) handles the failure in Examples/Apps/Web/JetWeb/run.jet; the sema misreport stays open.

Batch 29 regression, L0517 (Tests/UILint/path_containment_string_prefix.jet emits no lint): c5-stream-b5 moved Path's methods into Core (impl Path in Core/Files/Files.jet) and rewrote sema_stmt_note_normalized_path_text (Statements.jet) to match a TExprKind .MethodCall named to_string over a .MethodCall named normalize, with receiver.ty == Type.Named{name: "Path"}. Under the batch 29 compiler the binding is never marked, so the Core inherent call is checked into another shape (kind or receiver type). The types display as Path. Next step: dump the checked kind of b.normalize() and match it there. The c5 stream's author is no longer running, so the orchestrator holds this.

Batch 29 suites (batch 29 compiler, compared with batch 28): golden 5169 passed, 7 failed, 1 error, 3 timeouts (batch 28: 25 failing rows); ui 3145 passed, 12 failed (batch 28: 54); cases stopped early to free the slot. Fixed since batch 28: 21 golden and 50 ui rows. New: (1) c37-b-r2 removed the sema route checker, so 6 ui snapshots lose Jet.AmbiguousRoute (http_route_ambiguous_overlap, http_route_custom_method, http_route_mixed_duplicate, web_app_page_handler_clash, web_app_route_collision, web_app_routes_same_words); (2) c38: Examples/Apps/Web/JetWeb/run.jet fails with Jet.MissingDisplay `Never` at o0, o1 and o2; (3) Examples/Concurrency/ContextOnStop.jet has an ICE at o2; (4) Tests/UILint/path_containment_string_prefix.jet emits no lint; (5) Tests/Run/Foundations/Text/run.jet times out at 600 s at every tier (passed in batch 28). Sent to the lane agents. The Taint snapshot (&& left by the write-mark migration) is fixed on dev at 28aacd56ce.

Parked for owner-ordered cleanup #6999 (2026-11-24 12:00): c13 leaf step B (f32 bits callers) and the Time __duration_* roles slice (9 names; CBD 70 counts them) are unwritten; c36-05c-r2 (derive #if conditions must fold without the comptime image) and c36-06 are parked with TypeIDSlice3-3; c18 continues under #6999 B. Queued for batch 30: c13 string/service/math-precise r2, math-f32-roles, f32-bits-leaf, c18-guard-priv, c18-a.

c18 proof command: the guard's proof is `jet test Tests/Guards/CoreDeclarations`. A `--filter core_declarations` run matches no test. The guard was red on dev because the Core declaration checks missed `priv __x: fn` lines (176 false problems); 6851-c18-guard-priv fixes that and is queued for batch 30 with c18-a (core.compute, 59 dispatcher rows).

c13 decision: core.math's by-name helpers (64 of the 123 CBD rows left: precise math built as __{type}_{op}, F32 as __{member}_f32) move to roles next, ahead of the 26 Core-only rows, because they carry the largest share of the remaining gap. They use the one existing mechanism, a plain #Builtin.Role case per helper ({Type}{Op}, {Member}F32, about 93 cases), and PreciseBind and the F32 lowering look the role up the way every other family does. No parameterized role form is added.

Batch 27 landed on dev (e7155486f3), one commit per submission: c36-02 one maker graph 689cc79e4f, c36-03 in-sema makers 91d3a32bb0, c5 time-b2 72a593f2e2, c13 stale rows 865e858f05, c13 units roles 307c05de2f, c13 compute roles 0ed47ff071, c5 time-c1 3eab75d0b7, c30 CompilerCall type c584d98f05. Merged into master 9ddc0975d6. Batch 27 suite against batch 26: golden 66 and UI 54 new failures, grouped into roots for the fix sweep (Duration ledger, mark texts, compute role item, three still unexplained).

c13 Args decision revised (orchestrator): A replaced by A'. CLIEntry builds its role-to-helper table at compile time (#run over the #Builtin.Role markers in Core/Args/Args.jet). Compiler source spells only role names, and a missing filler fails the compiler build. Member lookup is unchanged, so user code naming a role stays an ordinary unknown member. Generated wrapper calls to priv helpers pass through the one existing generated-code visibility path.

c13 Args decision (orchestrator, under D-CORE-BUILTINS1=A): generated CLI entry text names the role, not the helper (e.g. __jet_cli_args.CLIValue(...)). In compiler-generated code only, member resolution maps a missing member of a Core module alias to that module's filler of the role of that name, through sema_core_role_function. User code naming a role gets the ordinary unknown-member error, which a UI case proves. A missing filler reports CoreRoleMissing. Args leaves the guard list.

c13 implementation decision (orchestrator, under D-CORE-BUILTINS1=A): Core helpers that generated code calls (Args __cli_*, Units __measurement_*, Data __query_*/__group_*, Compute __ad_*) are found by role, through #Builtin.Role markers (the compiler markers that the ratified jet_builtins module holds), not moved into jet_builtins. The ratified module holds only what the compiler alone can provide. The helpers become priv. Generated callers pass visibility through the one existing generated-code path (Items.jet, c14b). Each family leaves Core.rows, and the guard ceiling drops with each family patch.

c13 size (G1Facts-2 census, 2026-11-24): 268 compiler-known Core names sit outside jet_builtins (guard ceiling 268). Sema also builds names such as __{member}_f32 and __{owner}_* (Calls/Core.jet:1033, PreciseBind.jet:27), which appear only in Core.rows. Closing c13 means moving each family behind the door, with sema finding it by role, one family per patch, the largest first, after #6852 c8 (which moves the decode, lines and precise-math families).

Staffing, 2026-11-24 (owner order: finish G1 now; all three agents on G1, LSP latency and non-G1 fixes parked). TypeIDSlice3-3: c36 (interned TypeId), then c6, then c24. G1Facts-2: D-DECL-FACTS1 review (for #6852 c1/c2), then c39, c14, c13, then #6852 c8/c9. G1Generation-2: #6998 steps A and B, the c37 split, c38, c5, c4. In batch 25 now: heard-args-r4 (c30, c31) and c29. Next as agents free up: c3, c7, c9, c18, c19, c21, c22, c33, c34.

Correction to the dead-tail log: on the batch 16 compiler, marker_check_rules_hear_calls now passes its tidy step (the dead-tail fix holds). criteria.text: D-RULE-TYPEARGS1=A is built: TypeId is a small handle into the compile's one interned type table, keyed by the checker's canonical key; every maker (reflection builders, the TypeId{T} literal, type_id_of, derive templates, marker arguments, settings, variant payloads) interns through one sema maker; fn build reads a frozen copy of the table carried by its snapshot; identity names package and path, name prints leaf names (qualified only where ambiguous or foreign); entries carry generic_bindings and signature once. Proof: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Reflect/ and --filter Metaprogramming/ pass, including a new case where a rule reads Transform<Screen, World>'s bindings, and the deleted text round trips (BuildAdapter find_type/add_struct text rows) are absent from source.

D-RULE-ACROSS1=A is built: a rule may declare row: fn(self, call: CompilerCall) -> String? beside check: fn(self, call: CompilerCall, first: CompilerCall?), and the compiler pairs each call with the earliest earlier call on the same table with an equal key (same binding/field path with no assignment between, or one builder chain; both calls in one block or the earlier one in an enclosing block); reject gains also: and label:, and a clash is reported beside the call's own errors. Core's route rule writes the key as method plus route shape, and the sema route-table checker is deleted. Proof: jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter http_route_ambiguous_overlap passes pointing at both routes, and a package router declaring the same two members gets the same clash (new case under Tests/Cases/Packages).

D-FORM-FIELD1=A is built: Prelude declares FieldRef<Model, T> (only the compiler builds one); where FieldRef<M, T> is expected, a bare .name checks name against M's visible stored fields and unifies T with its type, an unknown name is Jet.UnknownField at the selector listing M's fields, and a chain, payload or upper-case selector is refused; web.form(Model, …) returns WebFormTyped<Model>; validate, set, blur and focus take FieldRef; inside a binding-less loop .name still reads the loop item and the error names the loop binding; forms.typed<Model> refuses an unknown name at run time with WebFormError.Missing. Proof: golden Examples/Web forms example passes on o0/o1/o2 and new ui snapshots for the unknown field and the loop case pass.

A user marker template cannot paste a reserved `__` name. Fresh review (G1Generation-2, 2026-11-24) found that on tip23 a user template can declare and call `#{hook}` with hook `__hidden_hook` (prints `reached the hook`), and can call Core's `args.#{hook}("42")` with hook `__cli_is_int` (prints `true`): Items.jet:1443-1449 gives Core `__` items visibility 2 for any generated code. The `#code` paste already refuses `__pasted_hook`. Pasted names are user-written, so E0067 applies to them: one diagnostic for both paste doors; only Core's own templates may paste a `__` name; and a non-Core impl may not define a Core trait's `__` member. Proof: UI snapshots for both refusals, from the probes in the review (d1_template_dunder.jet, d3b.jet), at O0, on a batch compiler.
criteria.evidence: batch 43 (dev 70ff64f2288, master 911872e93df), run43d on the batch compiler built from that tree, O0: ui PASS for the review's probes: Tests/UI/template_paste_dunder_member.jet (#{hook} = __hidden_hook, refused), Tests/UI/template_paste_core_dunder_call.jet (args.#{hook} = __cli_is_int, refused), Tests/UI/template_paste_core_trait_dunder_member.jet and Tests/UI/core_trait_dunder_member_user_impl.jet (non-Core impl of a Core trait's __ member, refused).

criteria.text: D-RULE-BODYFACTS1=A is built: Core marks HTTPRequest.json, server.json, server.response and server.empty_response #Recorded; each function's FunctionInfo lists its calls of recorded callees as CompilerCall values (recorded), and a second list holds those whose value a return path returns, following local aliases (returns). A check rule reading handler.recorded and handler.returns sees a 404 returned through a local alias, which today's body walk drops. Proof: a cases/Metaprogramming case whose rule prints a handler's recorded and returns lists passes on o0, o1 and o2.

D-RULE-REWRITE1=A is built: a parameter's default may be #run over earlier parameters, evaluated at each call with those parameters bound to the call's argument facts; a call may write that parameter only by forwarding its own caller's parameter with the same default, and any other written value is refused with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot. The route contract reaches each route call this way, and a handler used on many routes is computed once. Proof: a cases/Metaprogramming case for the per-call default and its forwarding, and the UI snapshot for the refusal, pass.

A #run const may decode a #Codable enum, with the same meaning as at run time (I9). Today 'SHAPE: #run { json.decode<Shape>(json.to_string(Shape.Circle(7))) ?? Shape.Dot }' with '#Codable Shape: enum { Dot, Circle(Int) }' fails with Jet.TraitNotImplemented '`Shape` does not implement `Decode`', while the same decode in a runtime body works. A case pins both and prints the same value on every tier.

A rule's CompilerArg.function is a FunctionInfo for a lambda written in place and for a module-qualified function (pages.show), not only for a bare function name. A lambda's FunctionInfo has an empty name, the identity <module>.fn@<offset>, its parameter and result types, its recorded calls and its returns. This is a D-RULE-REWRITE1=A landing gate (the c30 met evidence covers only named functions).

cards.title: Copy, resource, typestate, effect, sink and layout facts come from declarations, not Core names
cards.body:
Destination: the checker reads copy, resource, typestate, effect and sink facts, and IR reads runtime-handle layout, from the declaration of a type or function. No compiler file keeps a list of Core type or module names to decide them.

Why it matters: a package type declared the same way as a Core type must get the same facts, and every name list drifts from Core (census F1 found Core/Jobs/Jobs.jet `queue() -[DB, Env, FS, Time]>` reduced to Effect.DB).

Sources: findings F06, F11 and F12 of Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md (line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f); D-CORE-LOWER1=A (lowering). Split from #6151.

Starting point for the taint criteria: an unlanded, unreviewed rework saved from lane TlsLead-3-6151 (on 73739ba7c3) at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/tls-unlanded/TlsLead-3-6151.patch (35 files: Sema/Taint.jet, ProveReplay.jet, CoreSourceRows.jet; deletes JetFoundation/Data/Syntax/Sinks.jet).

Ballots: the declaration-facts criteria and the layout criterion are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

log.text: Ballot D-MEM-POOL-NAME1 posted (A: the allocator becomes mem.SlotPool, recommended; B-F alternatives). The review added F (keep both spellings, separate declarations) and showed by probe that `use core.mem.Pool` hides the ambient store, so F needs a new import rule. n=16's separate declarations proceed meanwhile (TypeIDSlice3-3 on c16); only the final spelling waits on the ballot.

D-FALLIBLE-CLOSE1 posted, after a fresh Opus adversarial review (one revision: option A was added after finding that TCP and Unix close duplicate shutdown(.Both)). Until it is ratified, TCPStream, UnixStream, TLSStream and WsConn stay resources through one Core-identity row in Ownership/Copy.jet. The other eight Core resources (FileReader, FileWriter, FileLock, FileScope, Arena, Bump, Pool, Fixed) get empty impl Close in TypeIDSlice3-3's part 2. c1/c2 are met only after the ballot's cutover removes that row. Part 1 (#MoveOnly, #Local on types) is in the batch-44 rebuild.

Correction to the previous entry: D-DECL-FACTS1 is ratified with option A. It is the ballot c1/c2 waited on, so they are unblocked. Build A: `#MoveOnly` joins the prelude marker registry as a field-less Type-site marker beside SingleUse. The `Local` marker gains the Type site (its values never leave the thread that made them). `#SingleUse` goes on Task (join or detach exactly once). Resource types keep their declared Close. The ten undeclared carriers get arity-only Core declarations. The name lists in Ownership/Copy.jet, Ownership/Crossings.jet and Typestate.jet are deleted. Assigned to TypeIDSlice3-3.

Orchestrator decision 2026-11-25: c1/c2 need no new ballot. Each fact already has a declared mechanism. Resource (closed once, never copied): an `impl Close` in the type's declaration (Close trait, Compiler/Prelude/Traits.jet:251), which sema_copy_nominal_close already reads for user types. A one-duty value: the `#SingleUse` type marker (Ownership/SingleUse.jet). Typestate: declared state types. Work: the 12 names in Ownership/Copy.jet sema_copy_named_is_builtin_resource (FileReader, FileWriter, FileScope, FileLock, TLSStream, TCPStream, UnixStream, WsConn, Arena, Bump, Pool, Fixed; none declares impl Close today), the Pool/KeyRef/Rotation/View facts and sema_copy_apply_is_noncloneable in sema_copy_apply_facts, Crossings.jet:150 and 352 (core.mem Arena/Bump/Pool; Task, Receiver, Sender) and Typestate.jet:19 SEMA_STATE_TASK move onto those declarations in Core, and the name lists are deleted. Proof c2: Tests/Cases declared_copy_resource_typestate_facts (a user type declared the same way gets the same facts). Queued to TypeIDSlice3-3 after #6999 D's last 16 lists.
6852-c8-reach-paths landed on dev 939fda3b63.

2026-11-24: c1 and c2 wait on D-DECL-FACTS1. It was drafted but never reviewed or posted, so the owner could not vote on it. G1Facts-2 is reviewing it now, and the orchestrator posts it for the owner when the review passes. c8 and c9 have been build work since D-FORMAT-TRAIT1, D-ITERATOR-FAIL1 and D-BUILTIN-METHOD1 were ratified (2026-11-18); G1Facts-2 takes them after its #6851 items.

Owner questions open (2026-11-24): D-IMPL-STRUCTBOUND1 'Why does this syntax look so odd and repetitive? Is there a better way?' and D-IMPL-CONCRETEHEAD1 'Engineer away downsides'. Assigned to TypeIDSlice3-3: rework both ballots (verified against spec, code and a probe), each with a dated adversarial review audit; the Orchestrator then updates the ballots.

D-IMPL-STRUCTBOUND1 posted for the owner's vote (recommendation A: impl [T]<T: D>.D, [T#N]<T: D, N: Int>, T?<T: D>, [K: V]<K, V: D>). Adversarial review passed after three rounds: Docs/Audits/2026-11-24-d-impl-structbound1-review.md (dev d3162bdc91). Bounded structural heads and the element-bound Decode impls wait on the vote; unbounded heads are in batch 17 as 6852-c8-structural-heads. The concrete-head question ([U8].Decode, the __decode_* helpers) goes on its own ballot, D-IMPL-CONCRETEHEAD1.

c8 math part, profiled with jet perf on the batch 16 compiler (G1Generation-2). A 1/3 program builds in 35.7 ms without core.math and 127.1 ms with it, +91 ms: load +19 (Math.jet parse, 417 bodies), sema +44 (core_demand 45 by-name roots and 178 jobs, 133 trait-impl bodies checked up front, 89 comptime constants), lower +22 (380 Core functions lowered for a program that needs 2). Root: ir_precise_source_target, ir_core_lowered_by_name and jet_driver_core_lowering_roots root every precise family member, the abs/pow role fillers and the unit helpers by name. Fix: bind '/' and the precise families through the public arithmetic trait impls, rooted by reachability. That removes the by-name roots, CoreReach's helper names and the load cost together. Assigned to G1Facts.

c8 precise-math part: on the batch 16 compiler, binding '/' through core.math for every program raises a 3-line build from 38 ms to 130 ms. Loading core.math costs about 92 ms, which is a compile-speed defect in Core module loading. A module-identity lookup of the jet_fraction_* helpers would still name helpers, so it would not meet c8. The math part stays open until it binds through public trait impls with the load cost fixed at the root. Profile requested via jet perf.

c10d ruling (orchestrator, 2026-11-23): Core Build wrapper methods take at: SourceLocation{#caller}, the ratified caller-location spelling, and pass it to the jet.build import. The build session resolves it to the call expression's exact byte span from sema's recorded call sites, so diagnostics point at the user's b.run(...) with byte-identical carets. Rejected: #Import on bodyless methods (new surface) and line/column-only spans (they move carets).

c10 slice 3 ruling (orchestrator, 2026-11-23): Build, BuildPlan, BuildTarget and BuildStepHandle become Core structs wrapping the host handle word (priv handle: Int), with methods that call the jet.build imports. This is the same representation #6853 c9b5 gives the net handles (TCPStream: struct { priv handle: Int }). The evaluator and the host make and read the struct instead of the bare word, through the same path as the net handles. ir_host_value_name's Build words are removed in the same patch. One handle representation for every host type.

c10 ruling (orchestrator, 2026-11-23): methods on compiler-made handles (b.add_executable, meta.add, and the rest) need no new surface and no ballot. They are ordinary Core methods on Core-declared Build, Compiler and BuildPlan types, and their bodies call #Import(jet.build|jet.compiler, symbol:) free functions with the handle as the first argument, the jet.runtime pattern Core.Net and Args already use. D-COMPTIME-HOST1=A covers this. The draft D-COMPTIME-HOST-METHODS1 (#Import on methods) is not posted.

c10 plan (orchestrator, 2026-11-23), under D-COMPTIME-HOST1=A, implemented by G1Facts. (1) Provider split: each Build, BuildPlan, BuildStepHandle, BuildFile, Code and Compiler host operation becomes one named handler; BuildAdapter becomes transport; binding is one symbol-to-handler row table, so both BuildAdapter closed_lists rows leave. (2) Core declares those symbols, and Sema and IR carry the declared symbol, not owner.method text (bootstrap two-step: compiler half, then Core half). (3) The table is generated from the declarations; JetBuildSession becomes the public jet.build provider and Sema's hand-written contract table (Calls/Build.jet) is deleted in the same patch. c10 is met only once all three hold. c7: G1Facts reports that the route tables are gone on batch 12; patch 6852-c7 removes the last Core name (Sender) from RouteHandle.

Decision (c7, Reader/Cursor family): Reader.read_*/peek/seek/skip/take and Cursor.take_until move into Core declarations and fail with Err instead of a plain String. The ratified rule E2417 (a failure domain must be an error type) already forbids the String domain, which existed only through the compiler-owned path, so this is a defect fix under the greenfield cutover, not a new surface; every caller migrates to err.message in the same cutover. ReaderTakePattern and CursorTakePattern are match-pattern lowerings and stay in IR. Args family (26 variants) goes first; E1301-E1304 retire and become ordinary method-arity errors.
Owner ratified D-ITERATOR-FAIL1=A, D-FORMAT-TRAIT1=A and D-BUILTIN-METHOD1=A (2026-11-18). The ballot-blocked criteria are now build work, queued to the next free implementer.

D-RUNTIME-HANDLE1 is withdrawn as a duplicate. The ratified D-CORE-LAYOUT1=A already sets the rule: ordinary carriers with private typed handles, Close/Shared ownership, refusals, and delivery gated row by row. A package type follows the same rule. c5 (IR runtime-handle layout without <corelib>/ key-prefix tests) is no longer ballot-blocked: build it to D-CORE-LAYOUT1. From the review: privacy is module-scoped, and a cleanup demo does not prove foreign-resource ABI, so production porting meets the existing per-object/tier gate.

D-HOST-CALLBACK1=A and D-COMPTIME-HOST1=A ratified: checked managed-provider imports (#Import(jet.runtime, symbol:) through the extended checked foreign-provider carrier) and phase-checked provider declarations (#Import(jet.compiler, symbol:) and jet.build), where provider policy decides phases. This unblocks c7 (host-leaf declarations) and c10 (core.build on the public compiler library).

c7/c10 spellings needed (DeclTypes): (1) RouteBuiltin String/Bytes/List/iter rows need a way for Core to declare methods on the built-in String, [T] and Bytes types; (2) RouteHandle event rows need Core declarations for the generic Event/Hook handle types plus host leaves that take closures; (3) c10 needs a declared host-leaf spelling for compile-time compiler services (only #Import(c) exists) so Build/BuildPlan methods bind by declared symbol. The c7 precise-math slice is being submitted. The FileReader/FileWriter intercept removal is feasible, moves no baseline row, and is kept as a pending c7 slice.

c8 waits on ballots: format selectors and decode are ballot-gated by c8's own text, and the line loop needs a fallible-iteration trait (Iterator.next is Never!) that no decision gives. The precise-math part can land as a slice once those ballots are decided; alone it cannot empty CoreReach.jet. DeclTypes moved to c7.

c5 slice 1 (BuildTypes prefix tests via module_is_core, Pin matched by declaration, 14 -> 6 corelib sites) is in p253. Slice 2 waits on the runtime-handle-layout ballot already on c5 (Main's ballot list): Core handle types (HTTPRequest, Point2, TaskStatus) are plain structs/enums found only through IR_RUNTIME_HANDLES keyed by Core identity, so a package type needs a declared 'carried by runtime handle X' spelling. The key-row cutover patch is parked unlanded at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/DeclTypes-6-1/c5slice2/patch.

c11 design decided (Main): source-owned Core calls carry no effect set of their own; sema and jet inspect read the effects from the Core declaration, which is already the checked row (E0740 names them). This is one mechanism, so nothing can drift, and the build does not embed and scan the 5.4 MB of Core sources. Adapter rows (no Jet declaration yet) replace effect_kind/effect_leaf with an effects set from the hand list until c7 gives them host-leaf declarations; at that point the hand list is deleted. The c11 proof shows jobs.queue's full effect set through jet inspect and E0740.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c1, c2, c5, body reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: Copy, resource and typestate facts come from declarations: Sema/Ownership/Copy.jet (298-307, 597, 697), Sema/Ownership/Crossings.jet (225) and Sema/Typestate.jet (67-68, Task join and detach) hold no Core type-name lists. Declaration facts are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: those lists leave Tests/Guards/closed_lists/baseline.tsv and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter closed_lists` passes.
A user type declared like a Core type gets the same copy, resource and typestate facts. It depends on the same ballot (Main's ballot list, 2026-11-15).

A Core call's effects and credential-sink class come from its declaration: sema_taint_core_effect and sema_taint_credential_sink (Sema/Taint.jet:240-300 at 25f9dee58f, also read by Cli/ProveReplay.jet) are deleted. Proof: `git grep -n -E 'sema_taint_core_effect|sema_taint_credential_sink' Compiler` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter Taint` passes.
criteria.evidence: p223 batch compiler (dev a8b53c68d8): git grep -n -E 'sema_taint_core_effect|sema_taint_credential_sink' Compiler prints nothing; jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter Taint PASS 46/46 (e45ca214e6)

criteria.text: `jet inspect` shows the same effects for a Core call and a user call with the same declaration.
criteria.evidence: p225 batch compiler (dev 1b2c2d0a54), commit 493d3e1ead: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter inspect_effects_core_and_user_match PASS 1/1; suite p225 0 new failures from this commit.

criteria.text: IR decides runtime-handle layout without `<corelib>/` key-prefix tests (BuildTypes.jet, about 14 sites, for example lines 33, 399, 547, 561, 598 and 3384), so a package type gets the same layout rule. Runtime-handle layout for package types is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: `git grep -c 'corelib>/' Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildTypes.jet` prints 0 and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Types` passes.
criteria.evidence: Landed in 0099c1cc87 (dev, p279). cards.title: Open vocabularies: the compiler reads Core members as trait impls, never by name (D-EXTEND-ARCH1)
cards.body:
Destination: every compiler list that holds a Core member becomes a Core trait that any package implements with `impl Member.Trait` and trait constants (for example `impl TOML.Format { name: "TOML" }`). Core impls are pre-generated (D-OPENTABLE1); package impls are read once per build, only when imported. No compiler file recognizes a Core member by name.

Why it matters: a third-party database head, file format, unit or protocol must get the same powers as Core's without a compiler release.

Decision: D-EXTEND-ARCH1=A. cards.title: Build tools and package sources are package providers
cards.body:
Destination: a foreign build tool and a package registry or service preset are each one package implementing a provider trait or declaring rows, not an edit to the build session or Jetpack.

Why it matters: today Session.jet:664 names cmake, make, gradle, npm and cargo; Jetpack's ServicePresetKind has 43 presets and its provider list sits in four places that disagree (#6217).

Decisions: D-EXTEND-ARCH1=A, D-CORE-PROVIDER1, D-INFRA1. Design: Docs/research/2026-10-29-extensibility-every-layer.md sections 4.24, 4.25, 4.29 and 6.2 (`b.toolchain`, `b.action`, a Jetpack provider trait).

criteria.text: A Meson provider package implements `b.toolchain` and builds a Meson project from `fn build` with no build-session change; Session.jet names no foreign build tool.

Provider leaves are written in Jet source using the ratified F4/F5 facilities.

cards.title: Jet has no warnings: jet fmt rewrites style, tidy errors never stop run or dev (D-NO-WARNINGS1)
cards.body:
Destination: Jet prints no warnings. A style point `jet fmt` can rewrite is rewritten and never reported; everything else that matters is an error. Tidiness errors (an unused binding, an unused import, unreachable code) never stop `jet run` or `jet dev` and are not printed there; `jet check` and `jet build` list every one and exit non-zero, so the list works as a todo list.

Why it matters: the final-return and positional-Bool lints print thousands of lines when Jet's own runtime compiles, which hides real errors.

Decision: D-NO-WARNINGS1=A (ratified 2026-11-10). Related: #4624 (member liveness findings follow the same rule) and #6326 c4 (state-machine lints L0529, L0302, gated on that design).

Source: #6281 c129 (split here 2026-11-14).

A marker application counts as a use of its import, so it raises no false unused-import error, while a genuinely unused import is still reported as the registered tidy error (listed by jet check, never stopping jet run). An unknown or qualified marker gives one E0927 per site whose Why and Fix match D-META-USER1 and name the declaring import. A parse error in an imported file renders with that file's path, line and text. Proof: UI snapshots for all three under `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter marker_import`. (was #3720 c50)

A namespace needed by a used dotted, grouped or forward-alias member import is never reported unused, and no safe fix removes it, while a genuinely unused namespace still gets the unused-import tidy error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter unused_import_`. (was #3720 c51)

The devserver test package checks: JET_KEEP_GOING=1 jet check Compiler/JetDevServer/Tests reports 0 errors (on fa4be89 it reports 543 in about 30 files, stale Rust-port bodies: 244 UnknownFunction, 82 UnknownName, 50 ClosedSetElse, 41 UnknownType; 2e3eb65bf0 left them to their own change). Each stale test is ported to the current API or removed with its reason. #6841 c19 and c37 prove through this package. Proof: JET_KEEP_GOING=1 jet check Compiler/JetDevServer/Tests rc=0, then jet test Compiler/JetDevServer/Tests/LiveInspect.jet and jet test Compiler/JetDevServer/Tests/Canvas/DebugSourceGit.jet pass.

cards.title: Module variables belong to the main task; a task that touches one is refused (D-MODULE-VAR1)
cards.body:
Destination: a plain module variable is owned by the main task. Each function type carries its touch set (the module variables it reads or writes) as a deny-only fact; a task spawn requires an empty touch set; functions may write module variables (the E0111 function-write ban goes); borrow exclusivity holds across calls that touch the same variable.

Why it matters: module state is easy for beginners and stays race-free without locks or annotations.

Decision: D-MODULE-VAR1=A (ratified 2026-11-10). Each refusal is a registered error with what/why/fix and a UI snapshot; the example runs the same at O0, O1 and O2.

Source: #6281 c158 (split here 2026-11-14).

criteria.text: A function type carries its touch set (the module variables it reads or writes, transitively) as a deny-only fact, and `jet inspect` shows it.
A task spawn whose function touches a module variable is refused with a registered error naming the variable and the touching call.
A function may write a module variable: the E0111 function-write ban is removed. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Basics/ModuleVariables` passes on o0, o1 and o2.
Borrow exclusivity holds across calls: a call that writes a module variable while a borrow of it is live is refused.
A mutable module variable in a generic module body checks and runs as spec.md 'Generic modules' allows; today it is refused with E0003 (Lens probe in SUB Lens-6841-debug-eval-proposal.r4).

Each test starts with its own copy of every module variable and every module Shared holder, as D-MODULE-VAR1=A point six and D-CORE-GLOBAL-STATE1=A promise: today `jet test` runs a file's tests one after another in one process and nothing resets a global between them (JetRuntime TestHarness.jet:148-156; module Shared holders are Process sites never reset, JetIR BuildSharedSites.jet:62-90). Proof: two tests that write one global pass in either order and in parallel.

A function changes a module variable in place like a local: `enemies.push(e)`, `frame[i] = v` and lending it to a `^` parameter work (today `frame[i] = v` is refused with E0111 and the wrong text "is a constant", and `push` with E0223), and E0223's refusal of every non-#Persist changeable module root (Ownership/StaticCells.jet:1-62, callers Ownership/Checks.jet:2409, 2538, 3471-3477, 5008) is removed; Tests/Run/Comptime/MutableGlobalStartsFromComputedValue.jet then edits its [U8] without #Unsafe.

A #Persist global follows the same task rule as any module variable: today a #Persist global can be written from any function and any task with no check, and the D-MODULE-VAR1 probe m05 compiled and ran such a race. Proof: the m05 program is refused with the registered task error.

The touch fact is the one record of module reads and writes: TEffectFacts.module_writes (JetFoundation Facts/Declarations.jet:36-40) records reads too, and the second read scanner sema_comptime_tree_module_state (JetSema ComptimeItems.jet:847-863, callers ComptimeItems.jet:841-843 and JetDriver Pipeline.jet:1711-1716) reads that fact and is deleted.

A C callback that touches a module variable is refused with a registered error, as a callback that reads the context already is (E3218, JetSema Calls/Checking.jet:486), because C picks the thread the callback runs on.

Diagnostics and teaching match the rule: the E0338 registry row says it covers module-value cycles, which ComptimeItems.jet:1809 already reports under it (Prelude Diagnostics.jet ~5490 says computed fields only); a public function's touches appear in its docs, as D-MODULE-VAR1=A says; and the language reference gains a page on module variables, which none teaches today.

cards.title: Library promise changes show in jet check, and publish computes the minimum version (D-API-SURFACE1)
cards.body:
Destination: a package records its public promises (signatures and effects) in package.api. `jet check` reports a changed promise and tells the author to accept it; `jet registry publish` computes the minimum semantic version from the promise diff, and the author may raise it but never lower it.

Why it matters: users can trust a minor release, and a new required effect on a released function is never shipped as a patch.

Decision: D-API-SURFACE1=A (ratified 2026-11-11). Related: #5459 (capability diff on dependency update).

Source: #6281 c179 (split here 2026-11-14).

criteria.text: `jet check` compares a package's public promises with its recorded package.api and reports a changed promise with a registered diagnostic (what, why, fix) that tells the author to accept it.
`jet check --accept-api` rewrites package.api to the current promises.

`jet registry publish` computes the minimum version from the promise diff: an unchanged API is a patch, an added function a minor, and a released function newly needing Time a major; an author raise is kept and a lower version is refused. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter publish_minimum_semver` covers the four cases.

package.api records each public function's failure set: infallible to fallible, or a new member in a closed set, is a major change that `jet registry publish` refuses below a major version without acknowledgment (D-FAIL-PUBSIG1=A).

`jet registry publish` has a Jet public-API producer (PublicAPIItem from the checked package, structs included): `#CLI struct Config { port: Int{3000}; required: Int }` freezes as `struct Config { port: Int; required: Int [positional 0] }`, so a typed default is not frozen as positional.

Every deleted pkg.rs public-API test has a Jet Publication #Test over the public-API producer: v2_snapshot_upgrade_matches_duplicate_inline_leaves, public_effect_metadata_preserves_symbolic_rows, public_trait_effect_contract_drift_is_breaking, soft_public_names_are_not_semver_promises and inferred_public_effect_drift_is_breaking.

Physical-unit APIs freeze with canonical dimensions: physical_unit_api_freeze_and_semver_share_one_canonical_signature and physical_unit_trait_methods_use_canonical_dimensions pass as Publication #Tests.

cards.title: TLS host reads are effects: clock, entropy and CA bundle reads show in the effect row and obey denials (D-NET-HOSTREADS1)
cards.body:
Destination: every host read TLS makes (wall clock, OS entropy, CA bundle files and directories, and the other ingress leaves the review lists) is an ordinary inferred effect on the TLS and HTTP calls that reach it. A denial of FS, Rand, Env or one CA file refuses the program with the registered effect diagnostic, and a denied override never falls back to another bundle.

Why it matters: an effect row that hides host reads is a false promise; a sandboxed HTTPS client must be able to deny entropy or its CA file and know it holds.

Decision: D-NET-HOSTREADS1=A (ratified 2026-11-12), with its adversarial review (sol-reviewer, 2026-11-11). Probes: the seed-b5 probes (a local HTTPS client denying FS, Rand and Env; a scoped denial of its CA file; a server denying Rand).

Source: #6615 c12, c14, c15 (split here 2026-11-15). Related: #3418 (one effect-policy model).

criteria.text: Each TLS host-ingress leaf (wall clock, OS entropy, CA bundle files and directories, and the rest the review lists) is an inferred effect on every TLS and HTTP call that reaches it, carried through TLS and HTTP errors, callbacks and tasks, with the caller, registry and docs cutover in one change (D-NET-HOSTREADS1=A).

A local HTTPS client denying FS, Rand and Env, a scoped denial of its CA file, and a server denying Rand are each refused with the registered effect diagnostic, and a denied CA override never falls back to another bundle. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter tls_host_reads` (the seed-b5 probes as cases).
A dependency's TLS use under a dependency sandbox that denies one of its host reads is refused at the dependency boundary (sandbox intersection).

On a target with no clock, no entropy source or no filesystem, a TLS call that needs it is refused at check time with a registered error, and the host-read cases pass on O0, O1, O2 and web where applicable.

An embedded or file-free CA configuration never removes the conservative effects by itself: file-free sandboxed TLS uses separate precise entry paths or a complete provider API with a lifetime design.

cards.title: Typed data loaders: deterministic snapshots, exact invalidation, no leaked credentials
cards.body:
Destination: a typed data loader (`file<T>(path, format, limits)` and the archive, parameter and provider forms) yields one canonical snapshot with provenance and schema identity, is invalidated by exactly its inputs, and never exposes credential-sensitive metadata.

Why it matters: notebooks, apps and data scripts all read data through loaders; a loader that caches wrongly or leaks a credential into public state breaks every one of them.

Decisions: D-DATA-READER1=A (Arrow reader behind the format boundary), D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1. Spec: Docs/spec/core-library.md (data loaders). Related: #5968 (dataframes), #6619 (notebook).

Source: #5985 c9-c12 (archived #2448 c1-c4, re-added by the 2026-11 precut audit as unproven).

criteria.text: Loading the same input twice gives the same canonical snapshot content, provenance and schema identity, and the result is marshalled into the declared type T, on O0, O1 and O2.
A change to the loader's input file, archive member, parameter or authority invalidates its cached result, and a change to anything else does not.
Credential-sensitive loader metadata never appears in public loader state or output, and a provider payload the loader's authority does not cover is refused with a registered error.
Loader preview, status and cleanup read and remove only the state of their own invocation; an app or notebook using a loader goes through the same loader, not a second copy.

cards.title: Endpoints: one checked contract drives dispatch, the typed client, schema, form and OpenAPI
cards.body:
Destination: an endpoint is declared once (a marked method or route) and its contract derives dispatch, the typed client, the JSON schema, the form and the OpenAPI document; all of them agree with an independent HTTP client.

Why it matters: hand-kept clients and schemas drift from the server; one derived contract removes that whole class of bug.

Decisions: D-ENDPOINT-SHAPE1=A (contracts derived from typed handlers), D-ROUTE-ONE1=A, D-HTTP-ROUTE-EXPOSE1=A (route markers on struct methods, added with one call), D-FOUND-COREAPI1, D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A.

Source: #6552 c20, c28, c29, c34 (from archived #2962, #3304, #2852). Parent: #6552.

criteria.text: A typed endpoint is admitted, lowered to one descriptor, invoked, and encoded through the native and web codecs, with goldens on O0, O1, O2 and web.

Renaming a public input changes the derived client, schema and form in one place, and an independent client (curl) sees the same typed errors, auth requirements and HTTP statuses as the typed client. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter endpoint_contract_replay` on O0, O1 and O2.

Malformed path, query or body input is refused before the handler, private result fields never cross the public boundary, and optional, nested, enum, list and recursive schema references appear only where the endpoint declares them.

web.openapi(app) derives one deterministic OpenAPI document from the route table (D-ROUTE-ONE1=A): stable operation IDs, typed input, success, failure, auth and status, and no internal or visual routes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/AppOpenapi` on O0, O1 and O2.

Route markers on struct methods are added to the app with one call (D-HTTP-ROUTE-EXPOSE1=A): a jokes API with GET and POST routes serves identically on O0, O1 and O2, `web.openapi` renders both routes, and a bad path parameter is a compile error with a UI snapshot.
criteria.evidence: p150 (dev cb824d0276; JokesAPI landed 0fec89bfa1, renamed a147a156e6): jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/JokesAPI: PASS 3 FAIL 0. The criterion's filter Web/JokesApi predates the rename and matches nothing; the example's name is JokesAPI.

criteria.text: An action's security policy runs before any mutation: malformed, oversized, CSRF, unauthenticated and forbidden requests never mutate, authenticated-but-forbidden differs from unauthenticated, the duplicate JSON member policy is explicit, and no secret appears in a response. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/WebApp` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/action_security_policy_runs_before_mutation`.

A request body read under ?? (request.json<T>() ?? return ...) stays in the route contract and web.openapi. Proof: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter openapi_request_body_survives_a_decode_fallback.
criteria.evidence: p149 (batch compiler from dev 413cddeab5, 2026-11-15 00:20; GoalsB-5-15 landed c979f70f49): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter openapi_: PASS 3 FAIL 0, including openapi_request_body_survives_a_decode_fallback; --filter auto_derived_http_inputs: PASS 1 FAIL 0.

criteria.text: A failed route, context or operation check names its source construct and causal dependency, and the machine facts match the human error, with no new graph store or debug endpoint. Emit, check and repair fidelity is measured. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Web/WebApp` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter route_check_names_cause`. (was #3186 c9)

`json.schema<T>()` emits JSON Schema draft 2020-12 from Codable metadata (required, optional and default fields, renames, variants, recursion), represents custom codecs honestly, and its dialect is explicit and reused at app boundaries. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONSchema`. (was #3236 c13)

Published-schema add, remove, change and rename migrations work with examples, and computed-text typed JSON dispatch is integrated. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/SchemaMigration` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c29)

A method call on a Remote held in a field (client.notes.publish(doc)) checks exactly as the same call on a plain variable (notes.publish(doc)); today the seed refuses the field form with a misleading E0204 'already shared in this call'. Proof: a cases entry calling one Remote both ways, passing on O0, O1, O2 and web, plus the E0204 UI snapshot unchanged for a real double share.

cards.title: Offline write queue: request keys, row versions, shared tabs, session expiry and refused-write notices
cards.body:
Destination: an app's writes made offline are queued, replayed exactly once, never conflict with the device's own earlier edits, survive tabs and session expiry, and a refused write is never lost silently.

Why it matters: local-first apps (Linear, Convex) win on writes that just work offline; a queue that double-applies, conflicts with itself or drops a refusal loses user data.

Decisions: D-SYNC2=A (typed local collections that work offline and sync), D-SYNC1=A (CRDT values), D-WEBAPP-SHAPE1=A (shape: Docs/proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md). Gaps K1 come from the #6792 review round 2.

Source: #3709 c6, c11, c14-c17, c23, c26. Parent: #3709.

log.text: p222 (dev 961427a575): c10's native leg landed; WebApp/device_store_keeps_queue_and_notices_across_restart PASS on O0/O1/O2. c10 stays open for the web leg (waits on #6445 c9 and #6866).

c10 split (Main): the native leg ships now (B1: data_dir on Linux/macOS/Windows; B3: jet_rt_device_load/replace, temp+fsync+rename under data_dir()/<package>/; the entry package name is an image fact the runtime exposes, not a sema rewrite of one call). c10 stays open for the web leg, which needs #6445 c9 (the web Remote network leg) and a jet test browser harness with IndexedDB across a reload (#6866). B2 dropped: #package.name already gives the entry name at compile time, and server: meets no criterion here.

Plan (Main, from DeclTypes): SUB A = server: field (JET_APP_SERVER under jet run), the Unit-write queue with drop-plus-notice rollback, app.pending(), drain on reconnect and before the next call, c1 case sync_two_clients on o0/O1/O2; queue and notices in process cells. B1 = Core/Sys data_dir made correct on Linux/macOS/Windows through one runtime symbol, which the device cell reuses (no second helper). B2 = the driver embeds the entry package name and server: as a compile-time fact of the image. B3 = jet.runtime.device load/replace (atomic; a truncated file loads empty) under both cells, plus the c7 restart case.

Decision (Main): the device store is a runtime-owned cell (jet.runtime.device load/replace), effect-free in Core like the World store and NOTICE_CELL, so remote calls keep -[Net, Time]>. core.db is unusable here (it imports app) and a core.files store would add FS and Env to every remote write. Native is keyed by package name under the platform data dir, written through atomically. Web IndexedDB persistence is a criterion on this card.

Decision (Main, within approved scope): the offline write queue is built to the approved contract for writes whose result is Unit; each such write is queued and returns () at once. c1 rollback of a Unit write drops it and posts the notice; c7 rebases queued Unit writes. Value-returning writes keep the current offline behaviour (.Unreachable, as on the web) until #6555 c2 (prediction, gated on D-PREDICT-JOB1 and D-PREDICT-PIN1) lands; they get no separate path. c1, c3 and c7 proofs use Unit-result writes; queueing of value-returning writes is completed under #6555 c2.

c1, c3 and c7 need the client graph (new #6445 criterion: app.new/.api/.screen/.offline), app.Notice with its list (#6445 c7) and prediction (D-OPTIMISTIC1, #6555 c1 review then c2/c7). DeclTypes-6-1 builds them in that order. No stopgap web.App.offline: it would be a second, unratified mechanism (I8).

Rulings (Main, 2026-11-16 06:00). The offline queue surface is the proposal's .offline(.Queue) on the client graph; no app.offline_queue(path) free function (a second spelling, I8). c4-c7's client half waits on the graph and its card (Speed-3-2 to name it). c5 waits on #6818: the queue sends no session until #6818's native session design exists. Marking an ID type (Core app.ID with a bare UUIDv7 codec, or a marker on a distinct String) is new public API: an owner ballot that Main files, with neither spelling built meanwhile. Built now without a ruling: c6's server half (app.new_id() UUIDv7; Table.add answers Exists only when the caller may read the taken row, otherwise Denied). Queued for p215: c2 request keys (Speed-3-request-keys) and the server-side signed-in caller (Speed-3-signed-in-caller, a dependency of c5-c7).

State on dev 78f4541780 (Speed-3-2 survey): c9's grep matches Docs/research/2026-11-15-sync-partial-bootstrap-and-local-only.md, but the note is a fifth draft whose own status needs a fifth adversarial review before anything is built, and review 4, which it cites, is not in Docs/audits; c9 stays open. c1 and c3-c7 are blocked by no ballot but need unbuilt parts: the offline client queue (.offline(.Queue)); a signed-in caller over HTTP (#App.SignedIn endpoints answer 401 today); a browser runtime with IndexedDB and Web Locks; and the frame's notice list. c2 (request keys) is in progress (Speed-3-2).

criteria.text: Two clients: one edits offline, reconnects, the server refuses one of its writes and that client rolls it back, on O0, O1, O2 and web.
criteria.evidence: p220 batch compiler (census build of dev 17c073989d): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter sync_two_clients PASS

criteria.text: Every queued or retried remote write carries a request key; the server keeps (account, key) -> result for 24 hours and answers a replay with the stored result. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/replayed_write_returns_stored_result` (the first response is dropped).
criteria.evidence: dev b66642b8bc, the a0.0.046 admit's candidate suite run (s2 compiler, evidence rows-candidate.json): `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/replayed_write_returns_stored_result` → 1 of 1 PASS.

criteria.text: A second queued edit to one row carries the version the first edit predicts, so a device never conflicts with itself.
Browser tabs of one origin share one queue (IndexedDB plus a Web Lock), and the queue replays once.
When the session expires offline the queue is held, never sent under another account, and resumes after sign-in as the same account.

A client-made UUIDv7 ID lets an offline create open its row at once. An ID type's decoder accepts only UUIDv7 text (422 otherwise; a test sends "t1"). Table.add meeting a taken key answers DBError.Exists when the caller can read that row and Denied when it cannot, and the queue reports it.

A refused queued write whose screen is gone, or which is refused after a restart, adds a notice to the app notice list, kept until dismissed. Edits rebased on it replay with the row version each was made against, so one whose row changed since answers Conflict; each is judged on its own checks with its own notice.
criteria.evidence: p227 batch compiler (dev eab1677096), commit d87ae00329: jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/refused_queued_write_without_a_screen_becomes_a_kept_notice PASS 1/1.

criteria.text: Network partitions, concurrent merges, duplicated or reordered operations and reconnects keep every replica convergent: a seeded property test of random schedules over two and three replicas ends with equal state.
criteria.evidence: Already holds on dev 78f4541780 (found by Speed-3-2, rerun by Main on the p213 batch compiler): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter sync_crdt/partitions_converge -> PASS tests/cases/sync_crdt/partitions_converge.case, 1 passed, 0 failed.

criteria.text: The sync design covers partial bootstrap for large workspaces and a local-only mode with sync switched off (the parts Docs/Proposals/2026-11-13-web-app-framework-shape.md does not cover; it already covers the client cache, rollback, socket fan-out and the offline queue), as a reviewed design note. Proof: `git grep -n -i -E 'partial bootstrap|local-only' -- Docs/Proposals`. (was #3709 c1)

The device store that keeps queued writes and the notice list across restarts has one meaning on every tier: native writes through atomically to the platform data directory keyed by the app's package name, and the web target persists the same cell in IndexedDB through the same runtime load/replace symbols; a reload in the browser keeps the queue and notices exactly as a native restart does. Proof: a golden app case that queues a Unit write, restarts (native) or reloads (web), and prints the same queue and notice list on o0, O1, O2 and web.

cards.title: Lists edited in place: retain, drain, extract_if, splice and fixed-array init
cards.body:
Destination: Core List edits in place with exact ownership: retain keeps only some items without a new list, drain, extract_if and splice own their ranges even when dropped early, a live drain excludes other access, and fixed arrays initialize slot by slot.

Why it matters: ports of Vec::retain, drain and splice otherwise allocate a second list or do quadratic removes, and an early-dropped drain that leaves the list half-edited is a silent data bug.

Decisions: D-LIST-RETAIN1=A, D-ARRAY-INIT1=A. Spec: Docs/spec/core-library.md (List). The frozen #4412 holds the original retain and dedup items.

Source: #5976 c1, c83-c88 (archived #3371).

criteria.text: `[T#N].filled(value)` and `[T#N].from_fn(make)` write slots directly (D-ARRAY-INIT1=A): `filled` with a value that is not Copy is refused with a registered error, and a `make` that fails part-way cleans up exactly the slots already written, on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ArrayInit` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter array_filled_refuses_non_copy`.

`List.retain(keep)` removes in place, keeps order and allocates no new list (D-LIST-RETAIN1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ListRetain` and its allocation count in the measurement manifest.

`drain(range)` owns its removal range: `drain(1..<3)` on [1,2,3,4] yields [2,3] and leaves [1,4] even when dropped after one read. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/DestructiveIter` on O0, O1 and O2.
`extract_if(pred)` removes only the visited values its predicate selects: stopped after the first odd it leaves 2,3,4; a predicate failure stops there and leaves the unvisited values in place.
`splice(range, replacements)` states when replacements are consumed: finishing gives [1,8,9,4] and cancelling leaves [1,4].

A live drain excludes any other access or resize of its list, and an unfinished splice guard is a registered error; no clone stands in for the intended mutation. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter drain_live_loan` and `--filter splice_unfinished_guard`.

cards.title: Borrowed views over collections: [View<T>] results, chunks and windows, loans that cannot escape
cards.body:
Destination: selections and iteration over a collection (top-k, filters, groups, chunks, windows, text splits) can work through views that read or mutate the live storage without copying it, keep the source's provenance, and cannot outlive or survive an invalidating change to their source.

Why it matters: copying move-only records to rank or walk them is wrong (they cannot be copied) and slow; a view that outlives its source is a memory-safety hole.

Decisions: D-MEM-COPYSEM1 (semantic copy for default read views), D-ITER-BORROW1=A, D-ITER-SLICEPRODUCERS1=A, D-ITER-MAPOWN1=A, D-ITER-VIEWCOLLECT1=A. Related: #3317 (iterator capabilities).

Source: #5976 c69, c70, c72 (archived #3041 c2-c5; option A of its ballot); #3317 c25-c35 (archived #3318, #3340, #3359, #3391, #3393).

criteria.text: An input-preserving top-k returns [View<T>] results that read the actual move-only records with no payload copy (`selected[2][0].score` reads the record), leave the source unchanged, and carry the receiver's provenance through keyed and fallible producers; counts of zero or below are checked before any read. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/TopkViews` on O0, O1 and O2.

A view result that escapes its local owner, or is used after a change that invalidates its source, is refused with a registered error; an allowed write does not re-rank existing results. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter topk_view_escape` and `--filter topk_view_invalidated`.

Owned, shared-borrowed and exclusive-borrowed iteration have distinct observable contracts: mutating a yielded element through ViewMut updates the original collection, replaced slots drop exactly once, and illegal overlap is refused before execution (D-ITER-BORROW1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/BorrowedIteration` on O0, O1 and O2.

Chunks and windows state width-zero, remainder, direction, overlap and mutability: non-overlapping mutable chunks update the source, and overlapping mutable windows are never built from ordinary references (D-ITER-SLICEPRODUCERS1=A).

Borrowed windows and chunks, and text split and lines views, allocate nothing per output where the source storage permits a view, and print their text, not handles. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/BorrowedIteration` with its allocation count on O0, O1 and O2.

A loan cannot escape its owner: an escaping loan, overlapping mutable windows and a resize during iteration are refused before execution, mutable-view escapes stay refused, and default read-view stores keep D-MEM-COPYSEM1 semantic copies (explicit borrowed aggregates are F083).

A mapper over owned items moves each move-only item exactly once; a shared view cannot move its items; exclusive-view mutation reaches the original storage; escaping callbacks respect their loans (D-ITER-MAPOWN1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/MapOwnedItems` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter map_move_from_shared_view`.

No `.view()` special case remains in the formatter (Compiler/JetParser/Source/Formatter/Expressions.jet:2595) or sema (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership/Checks.jet:2255 on dev 168e1e9e92); `values[range]`, `&values[range]` and `~values[range]` keep their contracts, and `.view()` is an ordinary unknown-method error. Proof: `git grep -n '"view"' -- Compiler/JetParser Compiler/JetSema` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter view_method_unknown` passes.

Proof: the paired cell row in the measurement manifest, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Text/` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3262 c33)

criteria.text: peek never pulls twice and its first side effects are documented; a rejected conditional consume keeps the pending item (or the rejection branch's replacement); an accepted consume advances once with no copy; peeked mutation targets the buffered item, and a loan cannot outlive or overlap a cursor mutation (D-ITER-LOOKAHEAD1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Peekable` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter peek_loan_across_next`. (was #3317 c10)

Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ReadExact`. (was #3317 c14)
