cards.title: core.time: one now, one sleep, one format-pattern meaning, and time zone data
cards.body:
Destination: Core time has one Instant identity for now(), one sleep that takes a Duration, one meaning for date and time format patterns, and time zone and calendar data with exact DST behavior.

Why it matters: two sleeps (one unit-less) and two pattern meanings are the classic source of off-by-1000 and wrong-hour bugs.

Decisions: D-TIME-FORMAT-CANONICAL1=A, D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A.

Source: #5976 c48, c49, c50.

criteria.text: `unix_ms(now())` equals the epoch milliseconds of the same instant: now and Instant share one identity.
criteria.evidence: dev fe5846cb32: cases --filter CoreLib/time_now_identity PASS on the batch 13 compiler (unix_ms(now()) equals the epoch milliseconds of the same instant).

criteria.text: Date and time format patterns have one meaning in formatting and parsing (D-TIME-FORMAT-CANONICAL1=A), driven by one pattern table. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Time/FormatPatterns` on O0, O1 and O2.

One sleep: `tasks.sleep(ms: Int)` (Core/Tasks/Tasks.jet:270, unit-less, clamps negatives) is deleted, every caller uses `time.sleep(Duration)` (D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A), and a negative Duration behaves as core-library.md states. Proof: `git grep -n -E '^sleep: fn' -- Core` prints only Core/Time/Time.jet, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CoreLib/sleep_negative_duration` passes.
criteria.evidence: Landed dev 3394753e0b (6873-c3). On dev 7ff5df3a66, git grep -n -E '^sleep: fn' -- Core prints only Core/Time/Time.jet:51, and no source outside the Tower history calls tasks.sleep(. The batch 15 compiler gives cases --filter CoreLib/sleep_negative_duration PASS (and NativeApp/ all PASS).

criteria.text: Time zone and calendar data: a lookup resolves a zone, a DST gap and an overlap resolve as core-library.md states, and a missing zone database is a typed error, not a crash.

UTC leap-second parsing, formatting and ordering live in Core time (23:59:60 is accepted and labelled), and checked Civil and Period methods route through one core.time method identity on O0, O1, O2 and web. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Time/LeapSeconds` and its UI snapshots.

The known-failing row this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv: CoreLibPartsEncodingSurface/random_and_time_output_pins_with_seed_and_epoch. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Mail and MIME parsing in Core: placement ballot, then hostile-input parsing
cards.body:
Destination: Core (or a first-party package, by ballot) parses and formats mail and MIME data: headers, encodings and attachments, separate from sending and authentication, safe on hostile input.

Why it matters: mail parsing is a frequent attack surface; it must have no network or credential side effects and must bound its work.

Related: #6826 (outgoing mail), #3280 (the MIME quoted-string scanner).

Source: #5976 c51, c52 (archived #3285, re-homed by the #6563 audit).

criteria.text: A research note under Docs/Research and a ballot settle the library, API and placement for mail and MIME parsing; parsing and formatting stay separate from sending and authentication. Proof: `git ls-files "Docs/Research/*mime*"` names the note, and the decision list shows the placement ballot.
Mail and MIME parsing handles hostile headers, encodings, size limits and attachment streaming, with no credential or network side effect.

One canonical quoted-string scanner parses MIME parameters: quoted `;`, escaped quotes, duplicate parameters, unterminated quotes and unknown extensions have explicit outcomes, and HTTP and web use the canonical type.

cards.title: core.io.progress: lazy, truthful progress over lists and iterators (D-PROGRESS-COUNTS1)
cards.body:
Destination: one progress adapter wraps a List or an iterator, stays lazy, counts the items actually pulled through every adapter, renders correctly on a TTY and off one, and gives the same output on every tier.

Why it matters: a progress bar that counts what it was told instead of what was read lies exactly when it matters (early break, filters, errors).

Decisions: D-PROGRESS-COUNTS1=A (truthful progress with automatic completion), D-COREIO1=A.

Source: #5976 c54-c58 (archived #1402), #3549 c13-c14.

criteria.text: `progress` accepts List<T> and Iter<T>, stays lazy until consumed, and reports count and percent when the total is known, with no caller bookkeeping. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter IO/Progress` on O0, O1 and O2.

Counts follow actual source pulls through map, filter, step, dedup, chunk, window, flatten, intersperse, zip, take_while, skip_while, filter_map and try_collect, including natural end, early break, unknown total and a ParseError mid-stream.
On a TTY progress redraws one line; off a TTY it prints one line per update; NO_COLOR strips ANSI from custom formats; description and format are explicit options rendered by the shared renderer.
progress_each, progress_bytes (a failed buffer is not counted) and a scoped progress_task with child tasks and unknown totals share one ProgressTask model and renderer.

core-library.md and the D-COREIO1 syntax record describe the shipped adapter, with no manual-bookkeeping claim left. Proof: `git grep -n -i 'progress' -- Docs/Spec/core-library.md` shows the adapter, and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_declarations` passes.

Every Jet-owned human status line (CLI, compiler, runtime) goes through the one output adapter: TTY capability, TERM, NO_COLOR and `--color` select ANSI or plain, and `--json` writes only the machine schema.

cards.title: core.db crash consistency: every write and sync boundary crashed, whole-or-absent transactions
cards.body:
Destination: a deterministic crash harness crashes the real DB bridge at every reachable write and sync boundary (including dropped and reordered unsynced writes), and every reopen shows each transaction whole or absent; metamorphic SQL tests catch wrong queries.

Why it matters: a database that can come back with half a transaction loses data silently; only exhaustive crash schedules show it does not.

Related: #6448 (the SQL engine leaves Core for the `sql` package).

Source: #5976 c99-c105 (archived #3000, #3001).

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): 3d. A db crash-reopen harness, its refusal rules and metamorphic SQL. Three cases are missing.

criteria.text: A Jet test db_crash_reopen crashes every reachable write and sync boundary of a two-transaction workload on the real emitted DB bridge under the stated storage model (including dropped and reordered unsynced writes); each reopen shows whole-or-absent transactions with `PRAGMA integrity_check` = ok, and the smallest failing schedule replays from its seed and reduces.
A timeout, an invalid oracle, unsupported storage or an incomplete schedule never counts as a pass, and network filesystems get no untested atomicity promise.

Metamorphic SQL pairs over generated data compare equal under core.testing.compare; a planted wrong query yields the first difference and a reduced replay; malformed DB or SQL input reports typed failures.

cards.title: One DataTree: duplicate keys, exact numbers, strict decode, readers and limits (D-DATATREE-RULES1)
cards.body:
Destination: every text and binary format parses into the one DataTree with the ratified rules: duplicate keys are errors unless asked for, numbers keep their exact text, decoding is strict, binary byte strings are Bytes; readers and limits have one shape; the duplicate encoding carriers are gone.

Why it matters: a second carrier or a lenient default gives the same input two meanings.

Decisions: D-DATATREE-RULES1=A (owner rulings 2026-10-05), D-ONE-CODECS1=A. The frozen #4602 holds the original per-format duplicate-key item.

Source: #5976 c2, c3, c6, c7, c93.

log.text: c29 checked on dev b66642b8bc: Data/JSON/JSONParseLimits passes on o0, o1 and o2, but `git grep -n parse_with_limits -- Core Jetpack Examples` still prints Core/Encoding/JSON.jet:97 and Examples/Data/JSON/JSONParseLimits.jet:1,27. Not met.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c4 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: JSON, YAML and TOML each report a duplicate object key as a parse error naming the key and both positions, and the explicit allow-duplicates option keeps the later value. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Encoding/duplicate_keys_`, one case per format.

Numbers keep their exact text (1.50 re-renders as 1.50; 1e400 and integers beyond Int survive), JSON "42" into an Int field is a decode error, and CBOR byte strings decode to the Bytes variant. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/DatatreeRules` on O0, O1 and O2.

`json.parse_allow_duplicates` accepts custom limits the way `json.reader_allow_duplicates` does (a `limits:` parameter defaulting to EncodingLimits.safe()). Proof: a #Test in Core/Encoding/JSON.jet; `jet test Core/Encoding/JSON.jet` passes.

`json.JSONReader` and `jsonl.JSONLReader` have one `next()` shape for text and file sources (today DataEvent for text and DataEvent? for files), as the ballot D-JSON-READER1 (on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15)) decides.
Lenient untyped JSON decode, declared pure, neither reads the wall clock nor writes to stderr: it runs with Time and IO denied.

The canonical DataTree and generated format and error source replace the duplicate encoding carriers, including the web ambient JSON, with byte and diagnostic parity. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/` on O0, O1 and O2.

Typed JSON decode allocates no DataTree, and its failure values and messages are byte-identical to the DataTree path on every fixture. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/TypedJSONDecode` and its allocation count in the measurement manifest.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6082 c5

criteria.text: Adjacent enum tagging (tag field plus a separate content field) encodes and decodes exactly: unit omission, shape, a wrong tag and missing content, and a content name that collides with a field is a compile error. Its spelling under D-CODABLE-OPTIONS1 is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/EnumAdjacent` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter enum_adjacent_content_collides`. (was #3236 c8)

An opt-in retained-unknown enum case keeps the parsed tree of an unknown variant; known-case malformed payloads still fail and the strict default is unchanged; an untagged enum, two unknown cases, a wrong payload and direct construction are compile errors. Its spelling is on the same ballot (Main's ballot list, 2026-11-15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/EnumUnknown` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter enum_unknown_`. (was #3236 c9)

Decode aliases read old variant names and write only the canonical name; an alias collision is a compile error before codegen. Its spelling is on the same ballot (Main's ballot list, 2026-11-15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/EnumDecodeAliases` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter enum_decode_alias_collision`. (was #3236 c10)

Field metadata in the D-CODABLE-OPTIONS1=A forms: `#Codable(unknown: .Deny)`, `#Codable(.Flatten)`, custom Decode precedence and required, default and optional fields; missing, null and wrong-type values are distinct; unknown fields are rejected or retained in order. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/FieldMetadata` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c12)

Explicit-ID graphs round-trip, alias duplication is handled, input-selected types are rejected, and CBOR tags 28 and 29 are refused. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/GraphIdentity`. (was #3236 c15)

Docs/Spec defines the boundary crossing grid (time, schema, checker, evolution and fact columns), records the ratified literal, manifest, dependency, link, wire, validation, migration, fact, trust and error rules as grid cells with no second mechanism, and every new boundary feature names one cell. Proof: the grid table in Docs/Spec and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter spec_links`. (was #3236 c17)
A boundary planned on the grid behaves the same on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/FiveProjectionShape` on every tier. (was #3236 c19)

Per-projection rename metadata reaches text formats, Env, Args, DB and Layout inspection; migration stays scoped to published schemas. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/FiveProjectionShape` (one Shape fixture over JSON, Env, Args, DB and Layout) on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c31)

Derived codecs work across modules: a derived encode has the visibility of its type (no E0605 from another module), a field whose type is declared in another file derives, and the None policy is one documented rule (omit or null) with a typed option for the other. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/DerivedCodecCrossModule` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c32)

D-CODABLE-OPTIONS1=A is built: #Codable alone means both directions; type options .Encode or .Decode, unknown: .Deny, tag: .External (default), .Field("kind") or .None, from: .Base and published; field forms #Codable(.Skip) and #Codable(.Flatten). #Encode, #Decode, #DenyUnknownFields, #Discriminant, #Untagged, #CodableAsBase, #PublishedSchema, #Skip and #Flatten are gone from the Prelude, the syntax registry and every caller with no teaching diagnostic (on dev 168e1e9e92, `#PublishedSchema` still appears in 24 .jet files). Combinations keep their results and E2407-E2415, E0905 and E0910 stay. Proof: `git grep -l -E '#(Encode|Decode|DenyUnknownFields|Discriminant|Untagged|CodableAsBase|PublishedSchema|Skip|Flatten)\b' -- '*.jet'` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/` passes on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3236 c33)

A field default that calls a fallible function uses its success type under the selected propagation or refusal, and generated locals stay bound (no unbound jet_serde_ok_value). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter codable_fallible_field_default`. (was #3236 c34)

unknown: .Deny composes with a .Flatten field: consumed keys are tracked across flattened fields and residual unknown keys are rejected. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/CodableDenyFlatten`. (was #3236 c35)
Synthesized encode and decode never collide with a type's own encode and decode methods. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter codable_own_encode_method`. (was #3236 c36)

core.data.jmespath (D-CORE-JMESPATH1=A): compile and search pass the pinned official compliance corpus including all 26 built-ins; work is bounded, there is no I/O, and compiled expressions are reusable; invalid function, type and arity, zero-step slices, mixed numbers and duplicate names are exercised. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Data/jmespath_compliance`. (was #3280 c9)

json merge patch passes the RFC 7386 appendix A cases (null deletes, arrays replace); the original is unchanged on failure; limits are enforced; typed re-entry goes through Decode. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONMergePatch`. (was #3280 c10)

`patch(before, diff(before, after)) == after` for every fixture; ordering and array policy are stated; nonfinite input is rejected; time and memory are bounded. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONDiff`. (was #3280 c11)

A merge diff whose null update cannot be represented returns Unsupported with a path, and representable pairs verify a round trip. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONMergeDiff`. (was #3280 c12)

Runtime field selection works at top level and nested, with empty, duplicate, overlapping and unknown paths; rename, skip and custom codecs are honoured; hidden fields are never emitted; array-element projection is refused; the json_selected_vs_dto pair is measured. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONSelect` and the paired cell in the measurement manifest. (was #3280 c13)

`json.update<T>` is atomic; missing, null, default and unknown fields have defined behaviour; validation and custom Decode precedence are kept. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONUpdate`. (was #3280 c14)

Top-level exclusions serialize all fields except the named ones: empty, duplicate, unknown and all-field exclusions are handled, order is preserved, newly added ordinary fields are emitted and Encode-omitted fields stay absent. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/JSONExclude` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3280 c54)
Exclusion keeps exact numbers and custom or renamed field meaning without a JSON round trip. Its allocation measurement is on #6957.

json.parse and json.decode take an optional `limits:` label defaulting to `EncodingLimits.safe()`, and a bare call behaves as today; the sibling `parse_with_limits` (Core/Encoding/JSON.jet) is deleted and its callers move (D-CORE-JSONLIMIT1=A, D-API-COMPOSE1=A). Proof: `git grep -n parse_with_limits -- Core Jetpack Examples` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Data/JSON/JSONParseLimits` passes on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3280 c59)

sign_extend takes `bits: Int(1..64)` and stays infallible (D-BINARY-SIGNEXT1=A; Core/Encoding/Binary.jet takes a plain Int today), and every caller migrates in the same change with no teaching diagnostic or jet fix rule (owner 2026-11-06). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter sign_extend_bits_out_of_range` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Encoding/sign_extend`. (was #4472 c1)

Scoped requested-capacity accounting enforces the encoding max_bytes limit exactly on every tier, including the error and Int-growth paths. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Encoding/max_bytes_exact_`. (was #4472 c7)

The 3 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: CoreLib/generated_struct_codecs_preserve_option_and_computed_fields, CoreLib/json_parser_is_rfc8259_complete, EncodingParity/published_schema_preserves_unknown_wire_order_across_tiers. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Byte streams and the HTTP server: read_into, WebSocket routes and wss upgrade (D-NET-READINTO1, D-WS-ROUTE1)
cards.body:
Destination: every byte stream reads into a caller-owned buffer, the HTTP server, client and TLS reader use it, and the HTTP mux has a WebSocket route kind that authenticates, validates and upgrades over TCP and TLS.

Why it matters: a fresh limit-sized buffer per read is the main allocation cost of a steady server, and WebSocket handlers returning a fake response after the socket is gone is a design defect.

Decisions: D-NET-READINTO1=A (2026-11-10), D-WS-ROUTE1=A (2026-11-10). Depends on the concurrent serve loop (#4635).

Source: #5976 c42, c43, c110, c112, c113.

criteria.text: `read_into(buffer, limit)` appends up to `limit` bytes to the caller's [U8] and returns the count, as an inherent method on TCPStream, UnixStream, TLSStream and file readers, with a deadline form; it returns 0 at end of stream and a limit below 1 is invalid input; the Reader trait is unchanged (D-NET-READINTO1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Net/read_into_` on O0, O1 and O2.

The HTTP server, the HTTP client and the TLS record reader use read_into, and a paired cell (a read(4096) loop against read_into: wall time, allocations per read, peak memory) is in the measurement manifest with read_into strictly winning. Proof: the manifest row and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/` on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6957 c15

criteria.text: `mux.websocket(pattern, handler)` and `#Server.WebSocket(path)` (D-WS-ROUTE1=A): the server runs authentication and Origin policy, then validates and upgrades, and the handler returns nothing; one adapter and handshake serve TCP and TLS; the route owns GET (an equal GET registration is refused, HEAD gets 405, OPTIONS lists GET); upgraded tasks stay inside server limits and shutdown; close codes are kept and 1011 is sent only before the transport closes; OpenAPI describes the handshake only. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/WebSocketRoute` on O0, O1 and O2.
The HTTP server upgrades a TLS connection to WebSocket (Core/HTTP's upgrade path no longer needs a raw fd >= 0).
WebSocket lifetime: two connection contexts stay isolated, a disconnect cleans up, MessageTooLarge is an explicit bound, an acknowledgement means queued only, and raw WebSocket is not Socket.IO.

HTTP/1 server framing, session policy and PEM/X.509 parsing are in Jet, with a real TLS server stream on every applicable tier (today Core TLS is client-only: #6317 refuses the core-tls-server cases). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPServerTLS` and `--filter core_net_tls`, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/TLSPeerIdentity`.

Server policy order: CORS never authorizes, security headers survive errors, untrusted forwarded identity cannot bypass rate or auth limits, and malformed or oversized input is rejected before any handler mutation. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/HTTPPolicyOrder` on O0, O1 and O2.

http-service run and dev tiers pass every probe with the same responses as AOT: a Jet case runs GET /health, PUT /kv and GET /kv against O0, O1 and O2 with byte-identical responses and no probe timeout. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPService/probes_identical_on_every_tier`. (was #2873 c4)

One documented retry rule (today Core/HTTP/Client.jet retries PUT and DELETE while the old runtime retried only safe methods), and every route calls the one Jet meaning: golden net/http_client shows a PUT retry and a POST non-retry with identical output on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/HTTPClient`. (was #3665 c2)

Pool reuse and decoding: pooled_h1_reuses_only_after_drain_and_decodes_gzip_natively, h1_skips_early_hints_reuses_final_response_and_rejects_upgrade, gzip_decoding_streams_before_the_response_finishes, custom_client_clones_share_pool_cookie_jar_and_transport_facts and public_client_policy_exposes_pool_cookie_timeouts_and_facts pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/` on those rows. (was #3665 c4)

HeaderName and HeaderValue are checked text types (D-HTTP-HEADER-BAD1=A): every header setter and builder takes them, dynamic parse returns HTTPError.InvalidHeader with no second runtime validation, an invalid written character is a compile error with a fix, session_retries bounds fail, and there is no silent unchanged-header fallback. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter http_header_` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/`. (was #3665 c9)

`http.Client.new()` and every builder method in core-library.md are Jet functions in Core/HTTP/Client.jet, and every semantic item from the old runtime HTTP policy has its Core home with only socket, TLS and gzip provider leaves left. Proof: `git grep -n 'HTTPClientNew\|jet_http_client_new_impl' -- Compiler Core` prints nothing (on dev 168e1e9e92 it matches 16 lines in 10 Compiler files). (was #3665 c11)

The http_client_law fixtures that call Client.new() typecheck and run: public_client_allow_http_downgrade_method_typechecks and public_client_retries_method_typechecks pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv (both name #6843). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/public_client_`. (was #3665 c12)

Incoming request and received response text projections use the one body lifecycle and the one-MiB default cap: default, explicit-limit, over-limit, consumed-body, error-identity, binary and streaming cases pass, and hostile streamed overruns report InvalidFraming. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPI9/` (http_text_projections_preserve_default_limits_and_body_lifecycle_on_all_supported_tiers and hostile_http_response_sinks_reject_streamed_overruns_on_both_dev_tiers leave Tests/known-failing.tsv). (was #3665 c16)

The request builder's json(value) takes a Codable value, uses the typed encoder, sets JSON framing and does not conflict with decode-side inference; the hand-escaped request example is replaced by malformed and error tests. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter http_request_json_body`. (was #3665 c17)

A one-shot HTTP response's second body().text returns Err(.BodyConsumed) and never yields the body again. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPI9/` (the BodyConsumed row passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv). (was #3665 c23)

An HTTP JSON body keeps malformed JSON, a wrong field type and a real framing failure distinct; the FieldError path survives with no second decode; body limits are unchanged. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter http_json_decode_errors_stay_typed`. (was #3665 c25)

The configured client's cookie jar is in Core: http_client_law cases cookie_jar_rejects_domain_attributes_on_ip_hosts, cookie_jar_uses_schemeful_registrable_sites_and_rejects_public_suffixes and cookie_jar_enforces_per_domain_and_global_count_bounds pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/cookie_jar_`. (was #3665 c27)

Redirect policy is in Core: follow_same_origin_credentials_strips_authorization_on_redirect, cross_origin_redirect_strips_request_credentials_and_rejects_proxy_auth and unreplayable_307_closes_redirect_body pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter HTTPClientLaw/` on those rows. (was #3665 c28)

cards.title: Core API shape: results come back as returns, no API that can never succeed, spec matches Core
cards.body:
Destination: public Core APIs return their results instead of filling out-parameters, none of them is a stub that can never succeed, core-library.md matches the declared signatures, and module identity does not depend on file paths.

Why it matters: out-parameters and never-succeeding stubs are the API smells the owner ruled out; a spec that drifts from Core teaches the wrong surface.

Decisions: D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A (the frozen #4561 holds the original item). Related: #6367 (API design principle), #6848 c5 (maturity as a typed fact).

Source: #5976 c25, c29, c30, c35.

criteria.text: No public API in Core, Jetpack, Compiler or Tools has an output-only `&` parameter: each returns a value, tuple or struct, with every caller and teaching doc migrated in one cutover (D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A); real edits, buffer reuse, streams and foreign boundaries keep `&`. Proof: a guard that lists output-only `&` parameters reports none: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter output_returns`.

No public Core function can never succeed: one that fails with Unsupported on every target is implemented or removed. Proof: a guard over Core's public functions reports none: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_never_succeeds`.

core-library.md documents each public Core function with the signature Core declares (the drift found by the 2026-10-05 API comparisons is fixed). Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_declarations` passes.
A Core module's identity is its module path, never its file path: moving a Core file without changing its module declaration changes no symbol, cache key or diagnostic name.

cards.title: Core names, modules and prelude follow the ratified contracts: one name, one owner, one prelude
cards.body:
Destination: Core spells each operation once, each job has one owning module under the ratified module map, the prelude is one short readable module with the ratified contents, and foreign spellings are taught by fixes, never aliased.

Why it matters: duplicate names and plural/singular module twins make every port and every doc guess; the decisions are ratified and only the cutovers remain.

Decisions: D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A, D-CORE-MODULE-MAP1=A, D-CORE-SPELLING1=A, D-LISTREMOVE1=F, D-ONCE-VERB1=A, D-ONCE-PRINT1=A, D-VERDICT-1321-1, D-CORE-PRELUDE1=A, D-CORE-PRELUDE2=B, D-NAME-ALIAS1=A, D-LANGNS-NAME1=A, D-RULEARG-TYPES1=A. Greenfield: each cutover migrates every caller in one change with no alias or teaching row for the retired name.

Source: #3548 c45, c47-c49, c51; #4022 c2, c4 (ballots ratified) and c21; #5976 c37.

log.text: c8 checked on dev b66642b8bc: Basics/ passes 165 of 165, but `git grep -n -E "io\.(println|sprint|repr)\(" -- "*.jet"` prints Tests/Cases/CLIPartsRuntime/Fixtures/Print/run.jet:4,6,7, Tests/Cases/CLIPartsSurface/Fixtures/UnresolvedCall/call.jet:5 and Tests/Cases/CLIRuntime/Fixtures/Printfamily/run.jet:4. If those fixtures prove the retired names are refused, the criterion needs to say so; as written it is not met.

Sweep at dev f768b6597e: the c6 and c14 proof goldens pass on O0, O1 and O2 in suite-p392, but neither criterion is met by them. c6: Examples/Collections/ListRemoveSelector.jet calls remove(1, .Slot) and remove(x, .Val) only. Plain remove(x), deleting the first equal item, is never exercised. c14: Examples/Collections/OperationContract.jet covers empty all and any, sum 0 and product 1, the first failure with no partial list, short and padded zips, and remainder continuation. Strict zip runs only on equal lengths, so its refusal of unequal lengths is never shown. Each needs that coverage added to its golden.

criteria.text: One Jet name per Core operation (D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A): each family's kept name is listed in core-library.md and every duplicate (such as loads/load) is deleted with its callers migrated. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` exits 0 and reports no alias pair.

The 20 most common Python collection and string spellings in the ScriptBench Python programs (`sorted`, `list(range(...))`, `Counter`, `join`, `split`, `strip`, `startswith` and so on) each map to one Jet name or get an E0311 whose `fix_edits` names it; `xs.sorted()` and `(0..<8).to_list()` no longer fail without a fix (today E0311 for both).

The module renames of D-CORE-MODULE-MAP1=A are done: collections to collection, files to file, jobs to job, tasks to task, units to unit, testing to test, args to cli, sync to replica, and tui nests as term.ui (Core/ still has the old directories on dev 168e1e9e92). Proof: `git ls-files Core | cut -d/ -f2 | sort -u` shows none of the old names, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden` passes on O0, O1 and O2.

Each job has one owning module (D-CORE-MODULE-MAP1=A): process owns the working directory, environment, pid, arguments and exit; Session lives in auth; app folds away; and a guard lists any export carried by two modules. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_module_owners` reports none.
Core names use one English (American) spelling (D-CORE-SPELLING1=A). Proof: a guard over Core's public names reports no British spelling: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_spelling`.

`remove(x)` deletes the first item equal to x, `remove(i, .Slot)` deletes a slot and `remove(x, .Val)` states the default (D-LISTREMOVE1=F). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ListRemove` on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: dev b66642b8bc, the a0.0.046 admit's candidate suite run (s2 compiler, evidence rows-candidate.json): `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ListRemove` → 3 of 3 PASS (o0, o1, o2).

criteria.text: One verb per collection job (D-ONCE-VERB1=A): pop removes and returns on every collection, replace keeps only the List swap meaning, bare `.from()` is the conversion constructor, and retired verbs are gone.

One print family (D-ONCE-PRINT1=A, D-VERDICT-1321-1): ambient print ends the line and prints each argument on its own line, io.print is its #NoPrelude twin, and io.println, io.sprint and io.repr are gone with callers migrated. Proof: `git grep -n -E 'io\.(println|sprint|repr)\(' -- '*.jet'` prints nothing, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Basics/` passes.

The prelude is one short readable Core module (D-NAME-ALIAS1=A, D-CORE-PRELUDE1=A): ambient basics are declared there, the rest are `pub use` aliases into the Core tree, the compiler opens it for every file, a user declaration replaces a prelude alias, and #NoPrelude opts a file out.

read_file, write_file and file_exists are ambient prelude names with their file effects visible in signatures; random stays in core.math.random (D-CORE-PRELUDE2=B). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Basics/PreludeFiles` on O0, O1 and O2.

Language declarations live in core.lang (D-LANGNS-NAME1=A) and marker argument types are the 14 generated prelude enums (D-RULEARG-TYPES1=A). Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_declarations` passes and `git grep` shows the enums in the generated prelude.

reactive.unsubscribe, reactive.is_active and the text.combinators module are admitted by canonical export generation, with import and call goldens. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Reactive/` and `--filter text/combinators` on O0, O1 and O2.

Every row in the one authored operation row set states receiver and result ownership, eager or lazy timing, callback count and order, stop-item consumption, failure channel, empty result and required buffering. Proof: a #Test in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet fails on a row missing any field (`jet test Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`). (was #3325 c7)

Examples cover empty all and any, zero, first failure, strict, short and padded zip, and remainder continuation, and no source error prints as a success. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/OperationContract` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3325 c8)
criteria.evidence: dev b66642b8bc, the a0.0.046 admit's candidate suite run (s2 compiler, evidence rows-candidate.json): `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/OperationContract` → 3 of 3 PASS (o0, o1, o2).

criteria.text: Generated docs mark each operation as shipped or source-only; LAST ties stay as #2298 pinned and eager defaults stay D-CORE-EAGER1=A and D-CORE-EAGER2=A. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/` passes and the generated operation docs show the marker. (was #3325 c9)

The four method tables in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet are replaced by one authored row set; JetSema, JetCodegen and the generated docs, completion and explain views all read it, with no second registry, and `jet check Compiler` is clean. Proof: `git grep -n -E 'sema_collection_method_(contract|argument_type|result_type|operation)' -- Compiler` prints nothing and `jet check Compiler` exits 0. (was #3325 c13)

A golden shows each shipped collection family's order, equality, invalidation and ownership contract. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/CollectionContracts` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3325 c15)

Set follows D-SET-DECLINE1=C: `sort` and `shuffle` ship on Set and return a List, `indexof` and `indexed` stay declined with that decision ID in the core-surface ledger. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` exits 0 and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CoreLib/set_sort_shuffle` passes. (was #3325 c20)

Every core.collections.set function runs through Core/Collections/Set.jet with no dispatcher row or tier-specific wrapper (none on dev 452b6443f3), and a test covers each one: Set.jet has no #Test today. Proof: `jet test Core/Collections/Set.jet` runs a #Test per public function. (was #3325 c21)

Every foundation member (text, collections, math, units, time, encoding, regex, args, files and path, io and mem, portable crypto) has a Jet body in Core or a typed provider leaf. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` exits 0 and lists no unowned foundation member. (was #3548 c1)

Each foundation module's Core #Tests pass, including hostile cases, on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter Core/<Module>` for text, collections, math, units, time, encoding, regex, args, files, io, mem and crypto. (was #3548 c3)

Compiler/Prelude/Core.rows has no dispatcher_row for a member that its module's source_module line owns (on dev 168e1e9e92 the foundation modules still carry 85 plain and 117 adapter rows), and every caller, route and generated projection uses the canonical contract. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` reports 0 Jet-owned foundation rows, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Text/` and `--filter serde/` pass on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3548 c8)

Core/Units owns constructor semantics: no core.units.from host row remains (none on dev 168e1e9e92), projections are regenerated, and units/from conformance matches on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Units/from`. (was #3548 c10)

Core unit validators no longer bind to `_`, equivalent multi-way branches use ordered arm tables (no side-effect reorder), and Core constants use plain names; each migrated module passes `jet fmt --check` and `jet check` with no tidy error. Proof: `jet fmt --check Core` and `jet check Core` exit 0. (was #3548 c11)

Every declaration in the system Core modules (archive, net, service, sys, log, http, term, sync, db, event, process, tasks, watcher, email) has a Jet body or a typed, policy-free provider leaf. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` reports no bodiless row for those modules. (was #3549 c1)

Core env APIs can read and write non-Unicode raw-byte values, as the ballot D-ENV-RAW-BYTES1 (on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15)) settles the API. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Sys/env_raw_bytes`. (was #3549 c18)

Every declaration in the specialized Core modules (Compute, Ui, Game, Testing, App, Perf, Plugin, Mod, Devtools, Reflect, Rt) has a Jet body or a typed provider leaf. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` reports no bodiless row for those modules. (was #3551 c1)

Specialized APIs pass their failure and effect proofs on O0, O1 and O2 through their Core/<module> Jet bodies. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter Core/Compute`, then the same for Ui, Game, Testing, App and Perf. (was #3551 c3)

After each specialized module cutover, every caller, route and generated projection uses the Jet body: Compiler/Prelude/Core.rows has no dispatcher row for a member its source module owns. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` exits 0. (was #3551 c6)

Core and the runtime have one internal home for byte, text and number primitives (ascii_lower, hex digits, UTF-8 validity, JSON escaping, checked arithmetic) that other Core modules import without it becoming public API; Core has 12 private ascii_lower copies on dev 72a8142651. A census flags a new same-name private helper (architecture review R3). Proof: `git grep -c -E '^ascii_lower: fn' -- Core` reports one file, and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter duplicate_helpers` passes. (was #5073 c5)

Core reaches the runtime only through ordinary use of jet.runtime modules. The dispatcher_row lines in Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet, the bound CoreCallRows, the IRRoute carrier rows for those functions and their RuntimeStopExports entries are deleted, and every in-repository caller is migrated in one cutover. Goldens prove o0, o1 and o2 for one call in each Core module that called the runtime. Proof: `git grep -n dispatcher_row -- Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet` prints nothing, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Runtime/OneCallPerCoreModule` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #6615 c5)

No Core constant declaration or reference uses a leading `@` sigil; every constant is a plain snake_case name. A quick grep on 2026-11-16 found 71 `@` plus letter sequences in Core sources (many may be strings or doc text). Proof: a guard in Tests/Guards scans Core declarations and references (not strings or comments) and passes with zero hits.

cards.title: Core I/O failures and producers: one IOError, typed failure paths, line, accept and resolve contracts
cards.body:
Destination: every Core I/O failure is one canonical IOError with complete context, every failure path cleans up in one order and reports a repairable, redacted diagnostic, and the I/O producers (lines, accepts, address resolution) state exactly what each outcome means on every tier.

Why it matters: an I/O error that loses its kind or context, or a producer that blurs waiting, failure and end, makes servers and tools misbehave under exactly the conditions they must survive.

Spec: F030 (cleanup of iterator items), F031 (channel readiness). Related: #3239 (task outcomes), #6878 (read_into).

Source: #3548 c53, c54, c56-c63 (archived #3248, #3226, #3395, #4910; first carried by #3239).

criteria.text: Malformed input, EOF, limits, I/O failure, cancellation and an unsupported target each give a repairable, redacted diagnostic; Core failure paths follow one cleanup order; archive deflate, compress and tar_add return ArchiveError. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Errors/CoreFailurePaths` on O0, O1 and O2.
I/O behaves under one semantic law on O0, O1 and O2, and process execution in the browser is a typed Unsupported failure, not a fake.

The line producer observes delimiter stripping, a partial final line, byte errors and resumption after an error per source. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter IO/LineProducerContract` on O0, O1 and O2.
Accept iterators tell waiting, a failed accept and permanent end apart, and keep the supported-platform gates. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Net/AcceptOutcomes` shows all three.
Address resolution yields the required sequence of addresses and is network I/O with its effects, never a pure source.

Owned and borrowed items from I/O and network iterators are cleaned up as F030 states, and channel readiness follows F031. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter IO/IteratorCleanup` on O0, O1 and O2.

The canonical IOError enum, its generated views and the runtime boundary agree on all eleven kinds, complete IOContext payloads and the ResourceLimit payload, on O0, O1 and O2 with real providers; callers and sandbox job settings migrate with no alias.

The io_error unit tests pass, a collect-all regression shows later independent cases still run after a failure with a nonzero aggregate, and a missing provider or build artifact is reported BLOCKED, never PASS.
IOOperation resolves to the canonical Core declaration even when a user type of the same name exists, and IOError's projection and Show/Debug agree on every tier with the original payloads.

System APIs pass their failure and effect proofs on O0, O1 and O2 through their Core/<module> Jet bodies. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter Core/Net`, then the same for Sys, Log, Http, Term, Process and Db. (was #3549 c3)

FileReader, FileWriter and FileLock are opaque source-visible values whose live state belongs to the provider, and TempDir, TempFile and FileLock cleanup stays with their provider values (D-FILES-HANDLE-ABI1=A): constructing or reading their path or state from source is refused, and alias close, replace, drop and task capture release exactly once at the final owner. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Files/handle_abi_` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter file_handle_state_private`. (was #3549 c11)

`sys.set` reports a failed set as an EnvError: Core/Sys/Sys.jet:61 declares it Never! while its leaf (`__env_set`, jet_std_env_try_set) can fail; a golden calls sys.set and handles the error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Sys/EnvSetError`. (was #3549 c17)

The known-failing row this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv: CoreLib/core_ioerror_preserves_kind_operation_and_resource. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Lazy adapters read only what they need: early stop, bounded state, flatten, intersperse, replay and cycle
cards.body:
Destination: every lazy adapter pulls only up to its semantic stop, keeps only its minimum state, and never builds a hidden whole-source list; replay, fork and cycle say exactly what they buffer and refuse a one-shot source they cannot repeat.

Why it matters: an adapter that reads past its stop runs effects the program did not ask for and breaks on endless or failing sources; hidden lists cost memory proportional to the input.

Decisions: D-ITER-NESTED1=A (flatten the existing iterable protocol), D-ITER-SEPARATOR1=A (separators only when demanded), D-ITER-KEYRUNS1=A (adjacent groups), D-ITER-REPLAY1=A (repeat a replayable source lazily), D-ITER-RESUME1=A. Related: #3317 (iterator capabilities), #6875 (progress counts follow pulls).

Source: #3317 c18, c36-c39, c41-c44, c46, c47 (archived #3320, #3106, #3358, #3384, #3350, via #4284).

criteria.text: Early-exit consumers stop at their semantic stop: pull traces stop at each adapter's stop, and a source that panics at its tail is never read past it. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/IterDemand` on O0, O1 and O2.

Each lazy adapter documents its minimum state and peak live memory, and no lazy path builds a whole-source list. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter iter_adapters_keep_minimum_state` (allocation counts per adapter on O0, O1 and O2).
is_sorted and lexicographic comparison stop at the first decisive item. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/IterDemand` shows the pull count.
Adjacent groups and dedup keep item order and never merge nonadjacent equal keys (D-ITER-KEYRUNS1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/AdjacentGroups` on O0, O1 and O2.

A consumer can start and stop before the whole source is materialized on the read_lines, JSON and CSV paths; buffers and size limits are explicit, and oversize or malformed input stops predictably. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter IO/StreamingConsumers` on O0, O1 and O2.

flatten composes nested user, view and suspended children with no intermediate List; empty children, an unbounded first child, child failure and early stop keep pull order and cleanup; move-only and borrowed items keep their provenance (D-ITER-NESTED1=A).

intersperse_with runs its factory only when a separator is demanded: empty and singleton sources emit none and an odd prefix runs no unneeded factory, and the constant form needs lawful repeated ownership (D-ITER-SEPARATOR1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/IntersperseWith` shows factory counts 0, 0 and 1.

A fork or replay of a source measures retained items and cleanup on the fast and slow branches, a finite capacity backpressures or fails explicitly, and cloned replayable sources are compared with buffered one-shot sources.

`[1,2].lazy().cycle().take(5)` prints [1,2,1,2,1], an empty replayable source ends, an effectful map runs once per source item per pass, `cycle(5)` is unchanged, and replay of an effectful source is never silent or unbounded (D-ITER-REPLAY1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/LazyCycle` on O0, O1 and O2.
Zero-argument `cycle()` on a Stream or other one-shot source is refused with a registered error.

A lazy map whose callback fails propagates the failure: the prefix witness prints only `visit=1` and `[1]`, the demanded-tail witness returns the callback error on every tier and never prints `[1, 7]` with exit 0, and infallible callbacks, error-as-data and propagating callbacks stay distinct. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/LazyMapCallbackFailure` on O0, O1 and O2.

Each row of the stable Rust iterator inventory (Docs/Research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md, finding iter-f005) has a Jet disposition, with positive and negative capability bounds, in one table in the Core collections spec. Proof: the table covers every inventory row. (was #3317 c1)

fuse() latches the first true end: a permanently exhausted wrapper stays exhausted, and a source that can resume after an empty poll is not labelled fused (D-ITER-FUSED1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/IterCapabilities` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3317 c4)

Capability facts are carried by the existing Iterable protocol and storage representations, with no public iterator hierarchy and no mandatory dynamic allocation. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter iter_capabilities_allocate_nothing` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3317 c5)

size_hint, fuse and by_ref ship (D-ITER-SIZE1=A, D-ITER-FUSED1=A, D-ITER-BORROW1=A; none exists in Core on dev 168e1e9e92): golden collections/iter_capabilities gives the same output on O0, O1 and O2, and Tests/UI/iter_by_ref_overlap.jet matches its snapshot. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/IterCapabilities` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter iter_by_ref_overlap`. (was #3317 c6)

A failing callback stops at the triggering item and the next pull starts at the exact next item; accumulator and partial-output ownership is explicit; the source is neither replayed nor destroyed; infallible, propagating and error-as-data callbacks stay distinct types (D-ITER-FAILCONSUME1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/FailRemainder`. (was #3317 c9)

size_hint tells a bound from an exact remaining length (equal bounds mean exact): filter drops exactness, map keeps it, chain checks representability, unknown, infinite and over-range sizes stay honest, and a hint never authorizes unchecked access (D-ITER-SIZE1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/SizeHint`. (was #3317 c11)

Mixed front and back pulls never duplicate or skip an item and meet exactly at exhaustion; reverse search reports the original index; adapters forward exact bounds; a forward-only stream is refused, never collected to fake the capability (D-ITER-BACK1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/IterBack` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter next_back_one_way_source`. (was #3317 c12)

A custom source's `map` runs without a second map implementation, and user sources, built-in Iter, Stream and ViewIter compose the same adapters with no hidden collection, replay or lifetime extension (D-ITER-INTEROP1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/IterInterop`. (was #3317 c13)

Cardinality checks read only the documented extra item and keep the remainder; equality keeps the representative policy and short-circuits. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/CardinalitySearch`. (was #3317 c15)

Fully draining a provably endless normal producer is a registered error from jet check (never a stop in jet run); `take(n)` removes it; effectful infinite loops are not flagged; the message explains demand, buffering and cancellation without inserting a bound (D-ITER-ENDLESS1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter endless_full_drain`. (was #3317 c19)

FromIterator is the one destination protocol (D-ITER-COLLECT1=A): [1,2,1] into List keeps [1,2,1], into Set dedups, into Map applies last-wins, String concatenates, a tuple destination and a user `impl Bag.FromIterator` build, each with stated ownership, order, duplicate and short-circuit rules (no FromIterator exists in Core on dev 168e1e9e92). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/FromIter` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3329 c1)

The destination is explicit at the call: an expected `Set<Int>` type never turns `list.map(f)`, a plain filter or a yielding loop into a Set, and a yielding loop always builds List<T>. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter from_iter_expected_type_no_retype`. (was #3329 c2)

One construction path handles ordinary and fallible input: a fallible source stops at the first error with the stated partial-result rule, and a failed construction leaks no resource. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/FromIter` shows the failing source and its close count. (was #3329 c3)

extend grows a destination in place from any iterable with no temporary List, using Map last-wins, Set dedup and the String and byte policy, with an explicit prefix-on-failure rule (D-ITER-EXTEND1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/ExtendIterable`, and the extend_lazy_vs_temp_list pair measures below 1.00. (was #3329 c6)

partition routes each item to exactly one typed destination with one classifier call, through the destination protocol, and a classifier failure is distinct from an error branch (D-ITER-BRANCHPARTITION1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/PartitionOutcome`. (was #3329 c7)

sum and product state their empty-input identities and cover custom domain values, reference items, Result and Option short-circuiting and numeric wrappers; Int overflow is the same failure as the shared list-sum kernel; there is one Sum and one Product trait; unsupported families are listed as gaps. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/AggregateMatrix` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3329 c8)

Yielding loops keep item order, nested List shape, filters, multiple sources and partial-list breaks, with effects, fallibility, ownership, source mutation, stream exhaustion, cleanup and allocation timing matching the eager ordinary-loop law, on O0, O1, O2 and at compile time. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/FromIter` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter yielding_loop_` on every tier. (was #3329 c11)

No duplicate terminal or iterator mechanism: collect and to_list are List terminals, every other destination goes through FromIterator (Set.from, Map construction, typed collection heads), and lazy work uses the existing adapters. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` lists no second terminal. (was #3329 c12)

`List.group_by` covers key changes, comparer order, a missing group, duplicate and empty keys and removal of an emptied group, on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/GroupBy`. (was #3329 c24)

The known-failing row this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv: DataflowStream/rolling_mean_nonfinite_matches_aot_and_default_dev. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Data formats beyond JSON each have one strict profile: TOML, XML, INI, BSON, BEVE, plist, MessagePack and layered config
cards.body:
Destination: each data format Core reads or writes has one strict, bounded profile over DataTree and Codable: typed values, exact limits, explicit Unsupported for what it cannot represent, malformed and hostile input rejected with a location, and a golden per format on O0, O1 and O2.

Why it matters: a lenient or partial format reader silently loses data or accepts hostile input; one profile per format keeps every caller's meaning the same.

Decisions: D-ENCBIN1=A (canonical binary interchange), D-ENCXML1=A (lossless XML over DataTree), D-ENCSTREAM1=A, D-ENCBASE-STRICT1=A. Fixed-buffer base encodings are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md (core findings).

Source: #3280 c19-c23, c25, c26, c28, c29 (archived #3267, #3269, #3275, #3284, #3312, #3251, #3282, #3283; via #3271 and #3272).

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c3, body reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: BSON: document roots, integer bounds, binary, ObjectId, time and decimal128 values; wire categories are kept or explicitly rejected; JavaScript stays inert; malformed input and limits are rejected. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/Bson` on O0, O1 and O2.
BEVE: the signed-int32 count fixture, typed-array, string and object boundaries, reserved bits, compressed sizes, padding, overflow and trailing input are handled, with explicit Unsupported.

Ballot (on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15)): whether base64, base32 and hex gain caller-owned output (encode_into and decode_into with an exact required size) and a borrowed byte view distinct from an owning conversion. Once chosen, `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/EncodingFixedBuffers` proves it on O0, O1 and O2.

Property lists: XML and binary plists cross-read and write with byte, date and UID values preserved; integer and UID limits, malformed offsets, cycles and hostile XML are rejected; root buffering is bounded.
MessagePack: every core category, timestamp 32, 64 and 96, and ext values round-trip; bounds and unknown fields are handled; there is no separate runtime.
TOML profile: typed dates, number bounds, error locations and the documented write order, with the same output on O0, O1 and O2.

Layered config: explicit include order with a final typed validation; root escape, symlink and cycle rejection; byte, depth and file caps; an invalid field reports its include path without secrets; a missing file is an IOError.

XML namespaces and canonicalization (C14N) are represented losslessly over DataTree as D-ENCXML1=A requires (Examples/Data/Formats/XMLProfile covers the profile without them). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/XMLNamespacesC14N` on O0, O1 and O2.

INI moves to the strict DataTree and Codable profile and the separate Ini and INIError surface (Core/Encoding/Ini.jet on dev 168e1e9e92) is deleted with its callers: section, default and typed-getter rules, exact case and duplicate policy, raw parsing distinct from Basic and Extended interpolation, bounded cycles, kept round-trip order and disclosed comment loss. Proof: `git grep -n INIError -- '*.jet'` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/EncodingIni` passes.

cbor.to_bytes and cbor.decode<[U8]> round-trip typed records and [U8] with located errors and no internal compiler error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Data/Formats/CBORRecords` on O0, O1 and O2.
Deeply nested XML parses and drops without hitting the typed-drop recursion limit, and numeric character references such as `😀` decode fully.

Core parses HTML by the pinned WHATWG algorithm, with parse_with, elements and text_content (D-HTML-PARSE1=B). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Data/Formats/HTMLParse` on O0, O1 and O2 over the html5lib tree-construction seeds.

Every format keeps its exact wire categories, malformed and limit behaviour and lossless subset, and selective and streaming readers mean the same as full decoding: a fixture table for non-string keys, tags, bytes, numbers and variants (typed against DataTree) is in Docs/Spec/encoding-decisions.md. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/DatatreeLosslessness`. (was #3236 c14)

JSONC is an explicit dialect: comments accepted, trailing comma rejected, source positions unchanged; strict JSON still rejects comments. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/Jsonc`. (was #3280 c15)

INI joins the data tree: core.encoding.ini reads into a Dyn tree and decodes to a typed struct through Codable, keeping section and key order and the exact number text, with its strict profile (duplicates, limits and malformed lines rejected with a line), plus an executable INI example with golden output on O0, O1 and O2. Today Core/Encoding/Ini.jet is configparser text only, with no Dyn view and no decode, and Examples/ has no INI example (Any audit, claim 7, probe p5). Proof: jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Serde/IniProfile and jet test Examples --filter Data/Formats/INIProfile.

cards.title: Core sockets and DNS: one TCP write, honest EOF and close, UDP truncation, resolv.conf, and explicit call states
cards.body:
Destination: TCP, Unix and TLS streams share one lifecycle law (positive limits, partial writes, EOF, half-close, cancellation, deadline, use after close), TCP writes have one spelling that never drops bytes, UDP keeps each packet's source, length and truncation, host DNS stays distinct from the wire resolver, and a TCP call says exactly when it was sent and what is uncertain.

Why it matters: servers and Jetpack's fetchers depend on these edges; a dropped byte or a fabricated success is silent corruption.

Related: #3665 (HTTP client), #6878 (byte streams and HTTP server), #6881 (I/O failures), #4954 (native UDP).

Source: #3665 c7, c14, c18-c22, c24 (archived #3227, #3080, #3444, #3445; via #3595).

criteria.text: TCP, Unix and TLS streams share positive-limit, partial-write and EOF semantics, and cancellation, deadline, half-close and use-after-close follow one law. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Net/stream_lifecycle_` on O0, O1 and O2.
UDP receive keeps the packet source, the original length and truncation.

Host DNS stays distinct from the wire resolver, and the runtime parses resolver servers from resolv.conf text through a text-taking function whose Core #Tests cover native fixtures and reject noise and malformed lines.
A service that accepts on tcp_listener and writes with tcp_stream.write_text builds and runs on O0, O1 and O2 with no ICE.
criteria.evidence: Sweep of open criteria against the full suite of the batch-7 -O1 compiler (dev 3019343199 + landed stack): jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/Services/ -> 18/18 PASS (JobQueue.jet@o0, JobQueue.jet@o1, JobQueue.jet@o2, ServicePartitionReconcile.jet@o0, ServicePartitionReconcile.jet@o1, ServicePartitionReconcile.jet@o2, ServiceProjection.jet@o0, ServiceProjection.jet@o1, ServiceProjection.jet@o2, ServiceTree.jet@o0, ServiceTree.jet@o1, ServiceTree.jet@o2, ServiceWorkflowOutcome.jet@o0, ServiceWorkflowOutcome.jet@o1, ServiceWorkflowOutcome.jet@o2, run.jet@o0, run.).

criteria.text: TCP writes have one spelling and never drop bytes: a write either writes everything or returns the short count to a caller that must handle it, and the five write spellings collapse to one.

A TCP call is sent exactly when the public API says, a timeout or lost reply after a possible mutation reports uncertainty rather than failure, and event publication never fabricates a handler result.
TLS consumes one opaque connected TCP stream carrier (no redial from host and port, no descriptor alias), and TLS typed success and failure agree on O0, O1 and O2.

The TCPStream defects found proving #3127 are fixed: a read through a by-value parameter no longer ICEs ("MIR place is not writable"), or sema requires `&`; net.set_timeout no longer copies the stream; slice semantics hold. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Net/tcp_stream_param_read` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter tcp_stream_by_value_read`.

`net.inherited_listeners()` returns every listening socket the service manager handed over as InheritedListener values (.Unix{name, listener} or .TCP{name, listener}); Core checks each is a listening stream socket, marks it close-on-exec, and clears the handover variables (D-CORE-NETINHERIT1=A).

`net.unix_peer(stream)` returns UnixPeer{user, group} as the kernel recorded at connect, with no process id (D-CORE-NETPEER1=A; the runtime already reads SO_PEERCRED in Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/NetUnix.jet).

http-client run and dev levels pass with byte-exact output, with the peer fixture server alive for every level. Proof: `node Tools/Gauntlet/Harness/run.mjs --entry http-client` passes on every level. (was #2873 c10)

Capped streaming fetch, redirect target policy and destination pinning (D-CORE-HTTPBODYLIMIT1, D-CORE-HTTPREDIRECT1, D-CORE-HTTPDEST1); `.Public` follows the dated IANA table (D-CORE-NETPUBLIC1); inherited listeners and Unix peer credentials work (D-CORE-NETINHERIT1, D-CORE-NETPEER1). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Net/public_destination_` and `--filter net/inherited_listener`. (was #3665 c5)

Jetpack/Foundation/Tests/PublicDestination.jet's three tests pass: every DNS answer must be public, comptime_http_fetch rejects loopback, and the pinned stream rejects an empty set. Proof: `jet test Jetpack/Foundation --filter PublicDestination`. (was #3665 c15)

Full duplex on one connection: a program can read from a TCPStream in one task while another task writes to it (the reader and writer pattern every bidirectional protocol needs: WebSocket, chat, proxies). Today Core/Net/Net.jet has no read/write split and no clone, every read and write takes `&TCPStream`, a task capturing the stream takes it, and a task.group child borrows it exclusively, so the pattern cannot be written; the only workaround is one owner interleaving with `ready` (HTTPI9 hostile_chunked was rewritten that way, IfHole 2026-11-20). The surface (a split into owned read and write halves, or another shape) is a new public API: ballot D-NET-DUPLEX1 with same-program alternatives first. Proof: a case where a reader task and a writer task share one connection on every native tier, with close ordering and EOF checked.

The 7 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: CoreNetTLS/configured_tls_client_keeps_native_builder_identity_and_exact_labels, CoreNetTLS/tcp_stream_and_listener_reject_public_fields_and_forged_records, CoreLib/core_net_dns_wire_lookup_observes_task_cancellation, CoreLib/core_net_ratified_named_forms_require_exact_labels, CoreLib/core_net_tcp_implements_nominal_io_reader_writer, CoreLib/core_net_udp_and_unix_waits_use_typed_scheduler_interrupts, CoreLib/core_net_unix_stream_implements_nominal_io_reader_writer. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Text formatting: exact number formatting, data templates, explicit locales and text diffs
cards.body:
Destination: Core formats numbers exactly (shortest round-trip digits, ties-to-even on the exact binary value, no crash on any tier), renders bounded data templates, formats and parses with an explicit Locale and no process-global default, and offers text diffs whose similarity, alignment, output and patch rules are stated.

Why it matters: number and template output is what users and files see; a rounding or locale surprise is a data bug.

Decisions: D-FLOAT-POSITIONAL1=A, D-CORE-TEMPLATE1=A. A Locale object and new diff operations are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Source: #3262 c6, c8, c9, c16, c17, c26 (archived #3252, #3307, #3311, #4417, #4331, #4407; via #4426).

log.text: c3 checked on dev b66642b8bc: Tests/Run/TextUnicode/FmtContract.out still pins decimal(0.125, 2) and tie:Fixed(2) as 0.13 (half away from zero), not 0.12 (ties to even). Not met.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c5, c6, body reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: fmt.shortest gives the shortest round-trip digits in positional layout with the exact special-value policy (D-FLOAT-POSITIONAL1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter TextUnicode/FmtContract` on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: dev b66642b8bc, the a0.0.046 admit's candidate suite run (s2 compiler, evidence rows-candidate.json): `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter TextUnicode/FmtContract` → 3 of 3 PASS (o0, o1, o2).

criteria.text: fmt.decimal never crashes on any tier, and fmt.bytes rounds binary units as selected, with the crash witnesses kept as cases.

fmt.decimal and the :Fixed(N) selector round the exact binary value ties-to-even (62.5 to "62"; Tests/Run/TextUnicode/FmtContract today pins 0.125 at Fixed(2) as 0.13, half away from zero). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter TextUnicode/FmtContract` with the corrected rows.

Data templates render bounded (D-CORE-TEMPLATE1=A): interpolation, sections, escaping and raw output; missing-field spans, malformed tags and depth, output and step limits; Encode renames honoured; reuse allocation measured.

Ballot (on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15)): an explicit Locale object, its data, default and API. Once chosen, Core/Text formats and parses en-US, de-DE, fr-FR and ja-JP number and date witnesses with an explicit Locale and no process-global default, kept separate from catalogs and normalization.

Text diff states similarity, alignment, unified, context and HTML output and patch application as distinct operations, with newline, tie and cost rules fixed against real consumers; each new public operation is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Case mapping and folding cover full Unicode, not Latin-1 only (generated tables, like the normalization tables): `casefold("Straße")` is `strasse`, Greek final sigma lowers correctly and Turkish dotted I follows the documented default; NFC, NFD, NFKC and NFKD, grapheme against scalar against byte counts, regex step-budget exhaustion and the invalid UTF-8 decode policy have witnesses. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Text/UnicodeContracts` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3262 c4)

Regex accessors are complete: pattern (source), flags, named_captures, count and escape exist and the core-surface ledger reports no regex accessor gap (Text/Regex and RegexSyntax goldens already pass on O0, O1 and O2 on dev e764ade14b). Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/CoreSurfaceLedger.jet --check` and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Text/Regex`. (was #3262 c5)

Text producers keep UTF-8 byte, scalar and grapheme positions distinct; an empty delimiter, a zero split limit, adjacent and trailing separators, CRLF and invalid bytes have stated results; borrowed substrings keep their lifetimes; output prints content, never view handles. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Text/TextProducerContracts` (bytes, scalars, char_indices, graphemes, words, lines and the split family). (was #3262 c10)
Padding targets the promised display width, not the scalar count. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Text/PadDisplayWidth` with wide-scalar fill rows. (was #3262 c12)

Generated Lowercase, Uppercase, Lt and UAX #29 word facts drive istitle, is_lower and is_upper on every route (D-UNICODE-CASE1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Text/UnicodeContracts` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3262 c13)

text.has_control reports any Cc character without allocating, with the ratified empty and non-ASCII laws, and the private grapheme helper is renamed (D-TEXT-CONTROL1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter Core/Text` covers it and its allocation count is zero. (was #3262 c14)

Core builds text from whole UTF-8 runs, never byte at a time through from_bytes, in every module that did (files, args, parse and the others listed in archived #4466), with one non-ASCII witness per module. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter Core/` and `git grep -n 'from_bytes(\[' -- Core` shows no byte-at-a-time builder. (was #3262 c15)

E0152 on a quoted regex containing `{4}` names the brace as the cause and gives a `fix_edits` entry rewriting the body to backtick raw text (`Regex{`\d{4}-\d{2}`}` already works); the files that double braces inside `Regex{…}` move to the backtick form. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter regex_quoted_brace_fix` and `git grep -c -E 'Regex\{[^}]*\{\{' -- '*.jet'` lists only intended cases. (was #3262 c19)

Case conversion has one home and one answer: String.lower and String.to_lower (Core/Text/String.jet:23-24), text.lower and Core/Text/Parse.jet:464 lower collapse to one Core name (D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A). Proof: `git grep -n -E '^(lower|to_lower): fn' -- Core` shows one definition, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Text/UnicodeContracts` passes. (was #3262 c32)

The 3 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: MathDisplayParity/builtin_math_family_has_named_field_parity_on_both_lenses, TextUnicode/word-sentence-segments, TextUnicode/normalization-casing-graphemes. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Translatable view text and the opt-in i18n package (D-I18N1=A)
cards.body:
Destination: view text parameters take ui.Text, so a literal in a view is a typed, translatable message (with plural forms), ui.verbatim marks runtime data that is never a catalog key, and translation is an opt-in i18n package: `jet i18n --add=pt` writes a catalog for the translator, and catalogs load explicitly with no ambient locale or filesystem access.

Why it matters: translation bolted on later means rewriting every view; with typed messages from the start, adding a language is a catalog, not a code change.

Decision: D-I18N1=A (ratified 2026-11-06). Nothing of it is built on dev 168e1e9e92 (no ui.verbatim, no i18n package).

Source: D-I18N1=A; #3262 c7 (archived #3289, message catalogs; D-CORE-CATALOG1).

criteria.text: View text parameters take ui.Text: a string literal in a view is a typed message, `ui.text("{count} bookings today", one: "{count} booking today", plural: count)` picks the plural form, and ui.verbatim(value) passes runtime data without translation. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter UI/TypedViewText` on O0, O1, O2 and web.
Passing a plain String where a view takes ui.Text is a registered error whose fix is ui.verbatim.
`jet i18n --add=pt` in a project that uses the i18n package writes a catalog listing every view message with its plural forms, and re-running it keeps existing translations.

The i18n package reads explicit catalogs: message context, three plural forms, ordered fallback and two concurrent catalogs work; malformed input is bounded; there is no ambient locale or filesystem access and no secret leakage.

cards.title: core.game: parallel system scheduling, the frame schedule, and editor, overlay and packaging tools
cards.body:
Destination: core.game runs systems in parallel from their declared access (D-SYSSCHED1=A) on one canonical frame schedule, and game developers get the tooling the ratified game designs promise: play and simulate in the editor, pause and frame advance, an in-game overlay debugger on the real window loop, typed launcher profiles, asset watch events, packaging with receipts, consented crash reporting, release devtools policy, and a complete `jet new game` scaffold.

Why it matters: these are what make Jet usable for real games rather than demos; each was designed and none is proven today.

Decisions: D-SYSSCHED1=A, D-GAME-ECS1=B, D-GAME-ENTITY1=A, D-GAME-BACKEND1=A, D-GAME-BUDGET1=A. Platform (windows, pixels, audio, input) is #5035; assets and hot reload are #238.

Source: #5035 c5-c18, c20, c23 (archived #2484, #2485, #2490, #2491, #2967, #3645).

criteria.text: Systems run in parallel by default from the conflict graph of each system's parameter access; conflicting systems keep source order; commands, events and logs merge in declaration order at each stage end; `schedule: .Serial` and `schedule: .Manual(stages)` are the expert forms, and a manual stage whose systems conflict is refused (D-SYSSCHED1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Game/SystemSchedule` prints the same on O0, O1 and O2 under each schedule, and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter game_manual_stage_conflict`.

Checked resource and hardware accesses produce one canonical frame schedule whose completion handles keep the resource guards until the provider completes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Game/FrameSchedule` on O0, O1 and O2.
Play In Editor, Simulate In Editor and return to editing keep the selected world state, and pause and frame advance are real state transitions (frame advance only while paused).
Ejecting a selection and the explicit Keep or Discard operations work with no implicit write to authored source.

The in-game overlay runs on the real window, frame, input and draw loop with typed console, stat, category and error-pause state, and its debugger categories and actor and world selection read the shared observation stream. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Game/Overlay` (headless).
Typed launcher profiles record target, mode and phase outcomes and are read by the headless path.
Declared asset watchers publish changed, created, deleted and skipped session events through the one bridge.
Game packaging has its phase and profile CLI with help, and each selected phase writes a machine receipt with target, profile, backend, source, result and error facts.
Crash reporting is an explicit consent and profile choice with inspectable routing, retention and upload policy, and an unavailable upload transport fails closed.
The target's ReleaseDevtoolsPolicy controls inspector data allocation, collection, publication and control, and a stripped release never builds the debug session.
Missing renderer authority gives the registered E1803 receipt path.

`jet new game` writes the complete scaffold (role homes, a runnable scene, profiles, error-pause behaviour, bounded remote protocol, typed tooling metadata and real session identity) and the result builds and runs.

Typed ECS storage, entity identity, deterministic queries and conflict-safe scheduling live in Jet with no host rows (D-GAME-ECS1=B, D-GAME-ENTITY1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Apps/Game/Ecs` on O0, O1 and O2.

Input action mapping and a fixed-step clock give identical tick sequences for identical input logs on every tier; replay divergence is detected and rollback works (D-GAME-INPUT1=A, D-GAME-REPLAY1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Apps/Game/Replay` on O0, O1 and O2.
Editor transitions and typed perf roles and budgets live in Jet semantics, with no host scene-budget rows (D-GAME-BUDGET1=A).
A playable vertical slice degrades or fails visibly without corruption under hostile states: device loss, missing assets, frame spikes, corrupt saves, input disconnect and replay divergence.
The live world inspector runs through the native host with typed scene projection, property and action routing, paused-frame evaluation and draw stepping.

Asset handles are typed and tied to their owning scene (D-GAME-ASSET1=A: `player: scene.assets.image("assets/player.png")?`); image and sound loading uses the checked importer fact and reports the declared path and kind; a successful reload publishes one deterministic handle and receipt. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Apps/Game/GameAssets` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #238 c2)

Asset handles are typed and tied to their owning scene (D-GAME-ASSET1=A: `player: scene.assets.image("assets/player.png")?`); image and sound loading uses the checked importer fact and reports the declared path and kind; a successful reload publishes one deterministic handle and receipt. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Apps/Game/GameAssets` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #238 c2)
