Missing files, wrong asset kinds, stale scene identity, corrupt import facts and a failed hot reload each give a safe error and keep the last valid asset state and its provenance, the same on O0, O1 and O2, and the check fails when the Jet asset path is bypassed. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Apps/Game/GameAssets`. (was #238 c3)

No asset policy remains outside Core/Game (or the game battery): the host keeps only file-read and decode leaves. Proof: `git grep -n -E 'assets_(image|sound)|reload' -- Compiler/JetRuntime` shows only those leaves, and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Apps/Game/GameAssets` passes on O0, O1 and O2. (was #238 c9)

Core reads and writes basic WAV files as ordinary game assets, bounded to common game-asset PCM with no specialist audio expansion (D-VERDICT-3287-1=A, ratified 2026-10-04). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Apps/Game/GameWav` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #238 c15)

Declared asset roots are discovered and watched with typed, coalesced dependency facts; imports produce validated runtime facts; hot reload swaps shared in-memory handles atomically only after a committed receipt and keeps the previous artifact on failure. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Game/asset_hot_reload`. (was #238 c16)

Frames are coloured against the declared D-GAME-BUDGET1 budget, and the frame critical path is computed from the trace's task dependencies. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Perf/TwoTaskFrameCriticalPath` names the critical task. (was #4632 c4)

cards.title: Core codecs: gzip and zstd live in core.compress and really compress, and image decode is bounded by one shared inflater
cards.body:
Destination: stream codecs (gzip, zstd) have one public home, core.compress, and their encoders actually compress; core.archive keeps only the zip and tar containers; one source-owned inflater checks the caller's output ceiling before every byte, and core.image decodes and encodes PNG, JPEG and GIF with bounded, typed failures on every tier.

Why it matters: an encoder that writes stored blocks only is a silent 0% compression; an unbounded inflater is a decompression bomb; two homes for gzip is two names for one thing.

State (dev 7259131021): gzip and zstd live in Core/Archive/Gzip.jet and Core/Archive/Zstd.jet (and Archive.jet compress/decompress); there is no Core/Compress; the encoders write stored blocks only (D-COMPTIME-SIZE1 review, 2026-11-12).

Decisions: D-CODECS1=A, D-CORE-COMPRESS1=A (split codecs from containers), D-CORE-ARCHIVE-BOUND1=A (bounded inflater, spelled core.archive.decompress_bounded), D-CORE-IMAGE1=A. The two module homes conflict; the choice is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Source: #3551 c9-c15, c17 (archived #499, #3561, #3562, #3564).

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c1, body reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: core.compress is the only public home for gzip and zstd byte-stream codecs and core.archive exposes only zip and tar (D-CORE-COMPRESS1=A): the module registry, prelude templates, examples, goldens, Core reference docs and module inventories name the split, with no alias or duplicate registry entry, and an old core.archive gzip call gets the ordinary unknown-member error. The conflict with D-CORE-ARCHIVE-BOUND1=A (later), which spells the bounded inflater in core.archive, is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: `git grep -n -E 'archive\.(gzip|zstd)|Archive/Gzip' -- Core Examples Docs` prints nothing.

gzip and zstd round trips run through core.compress on O0, O1 and O2, and zip and tar output stays byte-correct. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Systems/Files/Archive` and `--filter Systems/Compress` on O0, O1 and O2.

core.compress's gzip and zstd encoders compress: output for compressible input is smaller than the input and within 10% of the reference tool at its default level (today they write stored blocks only).

One source-owned inflater checks the caller's output ceiling before each output byte (stored, fixed and dynamic blocks), with a typed Limit error for zero, negative, above-cap limits and overruns (D-CORE-ARCHIVE-BOUND1=A), and core.image decode reports ImageError.Limit within budget.
core.image is one checked codec and value mechanism (D-CORE-IMAGE1=A): PNG round trip, GIF limits, and malformed and bomb input bounded with ImageError, with an example golden on O0, O1, O2 and web.

JPEG encode refuses non-opaque RGBA before allocating output, so fully transparent input never leaks RGB. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Image/jpeg_alpha_rejects_nonopaque` on O0, O1 and O2.

gzip.reader, zstd.reader (max_window default 128 MiB) and archive.tar_reader and tar_writer stream entry by entry with kind, mode and link target (D-CORE-CODECSTREAM1=A, D-CORE-TARSTREAM1=A): .tar.gz and .tar.zst fixtures with symlink, hardlink and PAX long-name entries stream on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Systems/Files/ArchiveStream`. (Frozen #3596 holds the original.)

The zstd decoder is a full RFC 8878 decoder written in Jet with no new dependency (D-CORE-ZSTDSOURCE1=A): RFC 8878 test frames and reference-tool .zst fixtures at levels 1, 3, 19 and 22 decode, and window-cap, dictionary and gzip multi-member CRC and ISIZE errors are typed.

A zstd frame whose declared output exceeds the bound reports the error kind the archive_hostile golden expects (Unsupported, not Malformed). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Systems/Files/ArchiveHostile` on O0, O1 and O2.

The known-failing row this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv: CoreLibPartsEncodingSurface/base_decoders_preserve_2026_union_with_comptime_aot_and_dev_parity. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: core.db tools: a bounded connection pool, `jet db` migrations with preview and receipts, the SQL console and EXPLAIN facts
cards.body:
Destination: core.db pools connections with a bounded FIFO deadline and health checks; `jet db` creates, previews, applies, steps and rolls back migrations with receipts and no partial schema change; the local SQL console reads typed sources, scripts and stdin within explicit bounds and inspects tables, plans and stats; a loopback-only browser inspector shows the same session; one typed fact stream gives bounded query stats and authority-gated read-only EXPLAIN without leaking credentials, query text or bindings.

Why it matters: these are the everyday database workflows; each was designed and none is proven.

Decisions: D-DB-AUTH-HOME1=A (core.db stays in Core; the SQL engine goes to the `sql` package, #6448), D-SQL-SAFETY (offline pull, diff and migrate; #4520 c4).

Source: #6448 c2-c12 (archived #2450, #2456, #2460, #2851).

criteria.text: core.db.pool enforces a bounded FIFO acquisition deadline, checks health on checkout, resets on release, replaces unhealthy connections, and reports readiness, drain and receipt facts, the same on O0, O1 and O2.
`jet db --help` shows the grouped command surface and explains create, preview, status, apply, target, step and rollback.
A migration declaration generates a deterministic versioned change and a SQL and data-risk preview without changing the database.
Status, apply, target, step, lock and rollback each write an explicit receipt, and a failed apply leaves no partial schema change.
Migration conflicts and authority failures are actionable errors in human and machine output.

The local SQL console accepts typed sources, scripts, stdin and bounded multiline input through the one SQL parser and executor, and enforces typed schemas and explicit byte, row and result bounds; projection, aliases and aggregates use the one SQL kernel.
The console's tables, schema, plan, stats and export commands and structured result metadata work on the same source and session.
The browser inspector binds loopback only and shows the same authorized source, session and query state; remote, file and export authority and resource limits fail closed with structured errors.
One typed database fact stream gives bounded query statistics and authority-gated read-only EXPLAIN to browser, terminal and native adapters without exposing credentials, query text or bindings.

The console attaches to a running app again with the same commands and output, by child-process attach over a local protocol or in-memory at O0, with one meaning on every tier (I9), and the attach failure path has UI snapshots. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Console/attach_` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter console_attach_failure`. (was #6386 c1)

The console attaches declared live services and database resources, takes commands from its prompt and from stdin, and starts with read-only authority. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Console/services_and_resources`. (was #6386 c128)

The console sends requests through the app's resident in-process router with status, headers, body and the shared request identity. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Console/router_dispatch`. (was #6386 c129)

Console sandbox transactions use the captured database resources and roll back on close or cancel, writing value-free audit records. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Console/sandbox_transaction_rollback`. (was #6386 c130)

The console refuses non-loopback, expired, release and missing-authority operations and records each denied request. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Console/guards_` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter console_guard_`. (was #6386 c131)

When the store is Postgres, live-query invalidations travel between servers through Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY instead of polling the store, so a write wakes the other servers' subscribers within one notification. Needs a Postgres client in core.db. (Moved from #6868 c4.)

cards.title: Lazy multi-source and combinatoric iterator adapters: sorted merge, join, combinations, interleave, Cartesian product and keyed set operations
cards.body:
Destination: iterators combine several sources lazily, buffering only what the contract needs: sorted merges keep only the frontiers, joins state their cardinality and sides, combinations, permutations and powersets are generated lazily, interleave and Cartesian products state their end and order policies, and keyed set operations state representatives and consumption.

Why it matters: today Core/Math/Combinatorics.jet builds whole [[T]] lists and Core/Collections/Collections.jet:640 merge_sorted takes only [Int]; eager forms blow up on large or endless input.

Decisions: D-ITER-SORTEDMERGE1=A, D-ITER-COMBINATIONS1=A, D-ITER-PERMUTATIONS1=A, D-ITER-POWERSET1=A, D-ITER-INTERLEAVE1=A, D-ITER-CARTESIAN1=A, D-ITER-SETOPS1=A, D-ITER-ITDEP1=A (no itertools dependency).

Source: #3327 c9-c14 (archived #3351, #3352, #3353, #3377, #3379, #3390); evidence Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md.

log.text: Sweep at dev f768b6597e: c7's proof golden Examples/Collections/Iterators/FilterMap.jet passes on O0, O1 and O2 in suite-p392, but it doesn't prove c7. It shows a Result callback keeping successes and try_collect stopping at the first error. Never exercised: a -> U? callback skipping None, a callback failure propagating out of filter_map, map_while stopping at None, and find_map continuing past None and consuming the triggering item. Not met until the golden covers them.

criteria.text: Two-way and k-way sorted merges buffer only the frontiers, the earlier source wins ties, and a comparator failure or an unsorted source has its stated result, never a silent re-sort (D-ITER-SORTEDMERGE1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Iterators/MergeSorted` on O0, O1 and O2.
A data join states duplicate-key cardinality, left and right projection, missing sides, order, one-shot input and DataLimits, with no second join library.

Combinations, combinations with replacement, permutations and powerset are lazy and generic, with empty and zero-width identities, ordering and invalid widths specified and lawful copying and borrowing (D-ITER-COMBINATIONS1, PERMUTATIONS1, POWERSET1 =A); Core/Math/Combinatorics.jet's eager list forms are replaced.
Interleave has longest (drain) and shortest end policies with pull traces for empty, non-fused and failing sources, and no fairness claim (D-ITER-INTERLEAVE1=A).

Cartesian products handle empty and zero-dimension inputs, give rightmost-fastest tuple order and allow `take(n)` over an unbounded left dimension; a reused one-shot dimension is a registered error (D-ITER-CARTESIAN1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Iterators/Cartesian` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter cartesian_one_shot_dimension`.
`union_by`, `intersection_by` and `difference_by` state the representative, which side is consumed for membership, the retained key state, second-source errors and provenance (D-ITER-SETOPS1=A).

filter_map's callback carrier picks the rule: `-> U?` skips None, an explicit Result keeps success-only selection, and a callback failure propagates; map_while stops at None and find_map continues past it, consuming the triggering item, with no new absence or error type (D-ITER-SELECTION1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Iterators/FilterMap` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3327 c4)
criteria.evidence: dev b66642b8bc, the a0.0.046 admit's candidate suite run (s2 compiler, evidence rows-candidate.json): `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Iterators/FilterMap` → 3 of 3 PASS (o0, o1, o2).

criteria.text: Scan keeps state separate from output: state and output types may differ (a move-only output too), the step runs once per demanded item with an explicit stop, error and remainder rule, and no whole-state clone; existing scan is unchanged (D-ITER-SCAN1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Iterators/ScanEmit`. (was #3327 c5)

Extrema take a key form and a binary Ordering form; ties keep the last item; callback count and error order are documented; empty and partial orders follow the existing law (D-ITER-CMPSELECT1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Iterators/ExtremaComparator` and the max_by_tie golden unchanged. (was #3327 c6)

chunk_by groups adjacent equal keys incrementally (A,A,B,A gives three runs) without materializing a run; keeping a group needs an explicit collection (D-ITER-KEYRUNS1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Iterators/ChunkBy` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter chunk_by_child_blocks_parent`. (was #3327 c7)

On A,B,A, adjacent dedup, first-occurrence unique and later-duplicate reporting give distinct results; order, representative and key-call count are explicit, memory grows with distinct keys, and hashing reuses the collection policy (D-ITER-UNIQUE1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/Iterators/UniqueVsDedup`. (was #3327 c8)

Shuffling goes through one explicit random state: every caller uses `random.rng(seed)` and `rng.shuffle(items)`, and the free Core/Math/Random.jet `shuffle` and `sample` over [Int] and the List and Iter shuffle are deleted (D-ITER-RNG1=A; greenfield, no teaching error). Proof: `git grep -n -E '^(shuffle|sample): fn' -- Core/Math/Random.jet` prints nothing. (was #3327 c15)

Seeded Rng sampling replays, splits are independent, bounded reservoir sampling is separate from full permutation, and endless input gets no full shuffle (D-RANDOMDIST1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Math/RandomSampling` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3327 c16)

cards.title: Guided input from #CLI: typed prompts and forms that match the parser, with accessible, non-TTY and pipeline modes
cards.body:
Destination: a `#CLI` declaration also drives interactive input: a guided field sequence and multi-page forms whose values, defaults, environment inputs and final typed result match the ordinary argv parser, with validation that keeps the invalid value, Unicode-safe editing, accessible and non-TTY modes that need no alternate screen, and small prompts that compose in shell pipelines.

Why it matters: one checked schema serves both flags and prompts, so an interactive run can never accept what the parser would refuse.

Decisions: D-DX-PROMPT1=A (guided input gets its fields from the CLI schema), D-TERM-COMMANDS1=A, D-CORE-TERMSTDIN1=A.

Source: #6315 c9-c13 (archived #2468, source-only acceptance, never run), #3242 c42 (archived #3294). The one CLI model is #3242.

criteria.text: A `#CLI` declaration derives a guided field sequence whose values, defaults, environment inputs and final typed result match the ordinary parser.

One command fixture driven once through argv and once through interactive selection gives identical ParsedArgs and validation; nested navigation, invalid input, EOF and cancel, secret input and I/O failure run under a real PTY; no handler runs before the caller dispatches, and no second command schema is added.
A multi-page form validates on field change and on submit, keeps the invalid value, and reports a semantic correction without running the command body.
Single-line and multiline fields accept Unicode paste, cursor movement and scrolling without splitting a code point or losing visible text.
TTY, accessible, NO_COLOR, CI and non-TTY modes give labeled deterministic prompts, need no alternate screen, and return a stable status for invalid input.
A small prompt composes in a shell pipeline, keeps machine output separate from the human prompt, and needs no full-screen application.

cards.title: core.log across boundaries: traces cross one service boundary, secrets never leak, and every record keeps a verified source
cards.body:
Destination: core.log carries trace identity across one permitted service boundary without inferring a principal from the header; secret-bearing values never reach logs, facts or exports; loss, sampling, retention and exporter failure are visible without blocking requests; and each record's event field locates its true source after composition, translation, redaction and wrappers, verified against source content before navigating.

Why it matters: observability that leaks secrets or points at the wrong line is worse than none.

Decisions: D-LOGTRACE1=A, D-LOG-SPAN-SCOPE1=A, D-LOG-LADDER1=A. The web app's request tracing is #6830.

Source: #6523 c1-c9 (archived #3088, #3101, #3176).

criteria.text: Trace identity survives one permitted service boundary, and no request principal is ever inferred from a trace header.
Secret-bearing values never appear in logs, facts or exports; the export holds only the chosen redacted fields.
Loss, sampling, retention and exporter failure are observable and never block request correctness.

A record's stable event field locates the right source after message composition, translation and redaction and through a wrapper call, and a developer-supplied key is distinct from compiler-verified source identity; fixtures cover a fixed message, a composed message, a two-language message (ordinary data, not shipped localization), a redacted field and a wrapper call. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Systems/Log/EventSource` on O0, O1 and O2.
Field values and redaction read the same through the text, JSON and telemetry views, never leak the redacted value, and treat an absent payload as absent, not empty.
A source lookup checks the source content identity before navigating, and fixed Prelude source metadata is never read as the original call site.

core.log records can carry optional, versioned source-site metadata: identity, content hash and relative file, line and column, with a known, redacted or unavailable state, kept separate from the emitter identity. Its cost claim is on #6958.

cards.title: core.plugin loads a sandbox component chosen at run time, checked against a Jet trait, under fuel, memory and time limits
cards.body:
Destination: `plugin.load<BuildStep>(path, policy)` accepts a path computed at run time and checks at load that the component exports every trait method with the same component type (D-CORE-PLUGINPATH1=A); an optional `limits:` label takes a plugin.Limits value whose fuel and timer reset before each call and whose memory and table caps hold for the component's life (D-CORE-PLUGINLIMITS1=A). The literal form and a bare load behave as today.

Why it matters: Jetpack's compiler-extension and build-plugin hosts load plugins chosen at run time (wasmtime in the Rust engine); without this the port cannot drop wasmtime.

Source: #5089 c4 (frozen #3598 item 4 holds the original).

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): 2d. plugin.load<T> with a run-time path plus a trait check at load (D-CORE-PLUGINPATH1=A ratified); the case doesn't exist yet.

Worktree save $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/wt-save/Rivet-6893.diff (2026-11-21; CoreSignatures, BuildRoutes, RuntimeRoutes, Prelude/Core.rows) has 12% of its 16 added lines on dev af651a6949: unlanded.

c1 stays open after D-PLUGIN-ENGINE1=A was ratified: A keeps run-time loads off until its own build is done (the separate x64 checker, the guard reservations, the instance split, the memory-key gates, SA_ONSTACK, the sealed child translator, the per-block jump fix, the spec runner and the fuzzer), the spec suite's core tests pass, the fuzzer has no open crash or checker refusal, and the time check holds. Loading a run-time path before then would let a guest escape. The unlanded sema and route surface for c1 (4 files) is saved as $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/wt-save/Rivet-6893-1545.diff and lands with that build.

Ballot D-PLUGIN-ENGINE1 posted to the owner (2026-11-21): the engine that translates a plugin loaded by a run-time path. Drafted by Rivet; Lens reviewed it four times (r0, r1 and r2 rejected with 10, 7 and 6 findings; r3 accepted; r4 applies Lens's three wording notes and was passed by Lens, sha256 0f5c80c3). The sema half of this card stays held until the vote.

Blocked on an engine choice (2026-11-21, Rivet): plugin.load today translates the literal artifact into native code at build time (JetPlugin Link.jet), and the runtime only verifies the bytes. A path computed at run time needs a run-time WASM engine, and none exists. D-CORE-PLUGINPATH1=A compiles at load but names no native engine (it was written against the Rust host Wasmtime). Ballot D-PLUGIN-ENGINE1 is being drafted (interpreter, load-time translator, baseline JIT, out-of-process helper). The sema/Core half is staged held until it is ratified, so no load-always-refuses surface ships.

c1 has no engine: guests are translated into the host image at build time (ir_plugin_guest, JetPlugin link step), and Docs/Proposals/plugin-wasm-engine-2026-10-29.md section 1 scopes run-time translation out. D-CORE-PLUGINPATH1=A doesn't say how a run-time path gets compiled, whether by JetPlugin+JetIR+x64 in the runtime or by another engine. That's on Main's ballot list. c2 (Limits) goes ahead on the build-time guests (DeclTypes).

criteria.text: `plugin.load<T>(path, policy)` loads a component whose path is computed at run time and refuses at load a component missing a trait method or exporting one with a different component type; `plugin.load("x.wasm", policy)` is unchanged (D-CORE-PLUGINPATH1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Plugin/load_runtime_path_checks_trait` on O0, O1 and O2.

`plugin.load(..., limits: plugin.Limits{...})` caps fuel and time per call (refilled before each call) and memory and tables for the component's life, each field defaulting to today's number; exhausting each limit gives its typed failure (D-CORE-PLUGINLIMITS1=A, D-PLUGIN-FAILURE1=A).
criteria.evidence: Holds on dev dbf05f4ced (landed 4315716f03): in the p276 suite, cases Plugin/limits_cap_each_budget_on_all_hosted_tiers passes, and so do the Authority/plugin_ budget cases (time budget, table growth cap, linear memory cap, wire budget, non-terminating component).

cards.title: The Jet SQLite engine in the `sql` package is complete: the sqllogictest corpus, WAL and crash recovery interoperate with C SQLite, and every SQLite 3.45 feature is ported
cards.body:
Destination: the in-Jet SQL engine, which leaves Core for the first-party `sql` package (D-DB-AUTH-HOME1=A, move card #6448), is a complete SQLite: the public sqllogictest corpus passes, WAL mode and crash recovery round-trip with C SQLite databases, and every SQL feature of SQLite 3.45 that Core/Db does not use yet is ported.

Why it matters: owner order 2026-11-09 moved full library completion to G3 (from #6695 c2 and c3); a Jet SQLite that reads and writes real SQLite files lets Jet programs drop the C library.

Source: #3550 c13.

criteria.text: The public sqllogictest corpus passes on the Jet SQL engine, with any skipped file listed with its reason.
WAL mode and crash recovery round-trip with C SQLite: a database written by each engine, including one crashed mid-transaction, opens in the other with the same contents.
Every SQL feature of SQLite 3.45 (statements, functions, pragmas and virtual tables) exists in the Jet engine, checked by a census #Test that lists the 3.45 feature set and fails on any missing one.

Core/DB/SQL.jet and Core/Auth/Auth.jet are gone from Core; their examples and tests import the `sql` and `auth` packages and their goldens pass on O0, O1 and O2; the old imports fail with the ordinary unknown-module error (no teaching error or snapshot). Proof: `git ls-files Core/DB/SQL.jet Core/Auth` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter DB/` passes. (was #6448 c1)

An SQL function the engine doesn't implement is an error, as SQLite's 'no such function' is, never a silent NULL or 0, and SQLite's date and time functions (julianday, unixepoch, datetime, date, time, strftime) are implemented. Today julianday('now') in the Jet SQLite engine gives no error. The jobs outbox read its clock as 0, so no job was ever taken: p210 regression, #6825 n6, n7 and n8, found by Speed-3-2. Proof: a sqllogictest-style case comparing each date function with SQLite's output, and a case where an unknown function fails with the engine's registered error.

cards.title: Likely bugs are tidy errors: dead constant ranges, unconditional recursion, discarded pure results, N+1 queries and misleading loop and type shapes
cards.body:
Destination: each likely-bug pattern below is a registered tidy error (D-NO-WARNINGS1=A, #6858): `jet check` and `jet build` list it with what/why/fix text and exit non-zero; `jet run` and `jet dev` never stop on it or print it. Each has a UI snapshot for the firing program and for the accepted fix.

Why it matters: these shapes compile today and do the wrong thing quietly.

Decisions: D-NO-WARNINGS1=A, D-RANGE-BACKWARD1=A, D-DISCARD1=A, D-TUPLE-ORDER1=A, D-SQL-CLASS1=A (Query class). The two-binding pairs loop is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

Source: Map card #6006 (Lints), batch D05 of the 2026-10-28 consolidation.

log.text: All criteria met with recorded batch-compiler evidence; closed in the near-done sweep. Batch 23's full suite rechecks every named row.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c7, body reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: A loop over a constant range that can never run (`10..1`, or a step pointing away from the end) is check error E0170 RangeDirectionMismatch offering the minus step, as D-RANGE-BACKWARD1=A states; a computed backward range (`0..n - 1`) stays empty and raises nothing; the stride rule is in the spec.
criteria.evidence: Sweep of open criteria against the full suite of the batch-7 -O1 compiler (dev 3019343199 + landed stack): jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter range_backward_constant -> 5/5 PASS (range_backward_constant.jet, range_backward_constant.jet@o0, range_backward_constant.jet@o1, range_backward_constant.jet@o2, range_backward_constant_quiet.jet). Stride rule in Docs/Spec/spec.md lines 588-592 (E0170).

criteria.text: A function whose every path calls itself again with no exit is a tidy error at the call, found over call-graph cycles.
criteria.evidence: Sweep of open criteria against the full suite of the batch-7 -O1 compiler (dev 3019343199 + landed stack): jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter unconditional_recursion -> 2/2 PASS (unconditional_recursion.jet, unconditional_recursion_quiet.jet).

criteria.text: A Float binding seeded with infinity but only ever assigned Int values is a tidy error naming the Int form.
criteria.evidence: Sweep of open criteria against the full suite of the batch-7 -O1 compiler (dev 3019343199 + landed stack): jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter float_infinity_seed_int_only -> 2/2 PASS (float_infinity_seed_int_only.jet, float_infinity_seed_int_only_quiet.jet).

criteria.text: A field-less struct holding only static functions is a tidy error whose fix makes it a module, and a constructor that does not return its owner type is an error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter static_only_struct` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter constructor_wrong_owner`.
criteria.evidence: On the batch 16 compiler (tree a2a8d238fb; landed on dev ce3b8e7f59): jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter static_only_struct -> 2/2 PASS (static_only_struct.jet, static_only_struct_quiet.jet); --filter constructor_wrong_owner -> 2/2 PASS (constructor_wrong_owner.jet, constructor_wrong_owner_quiet.jet). Landed as ebe277bc92.

criteria.text: Records compare and sort by written member order (D-RECORD-ORDER1=A): S73 in Docs/Spec/syntax-decisions.md says so, the List.sort and sort_desc docs say so, and an example shows written order and the sort_by spelling. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/NamedTupleOrder` on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: p325 batch compiler (dev e6ddae4d43): golden Examples/Collections/NamedTupleOrder.jet PASS on O0, O1 and O2. cards.title: No name silently wins: every shadowing and prelude-alias case is a tidy error with a rename fix
cards.body:
Destination: wherever two declarations could answer to one name and one silently wins (a local over a prelude alias, an import over a local, and the rest), `jet check` lists a registered tidy error with what/why/fix text and a `jet fix` rename; Core, Examples and the compiler are clean.

Decision (Main) on c4: one cutover. The package-stem rule (tidy error with a rename fix, UI name_repeats_package_*) lands in the same window as a sema-driven Jet codemod (Tools/Agent; --tree and --patch modes, idempotent, collisions reported not guessed). The window is the first cycle after p295: Main runs it on the dev tip, lands the rename as one commit, and rewrites queued SUB patches with --patch. c1 lands with c3.

cards.title: jet fmt is safe: lossless, meaning- and template-preserving, its own fmt cases pass, and the repository is formatted once
cards.body:
Destination: `jet fmt` keeps every token and every meaning (field order, loop heads, shebang, comment placement, template text), produces the canonical forms (suffix types, arrow before result, `[K:V]` map types, the arrow-loop form, one blank line between functions), prints minimal diffs, and passes every tests/cases/fmt case. Then the whole repository is formatted in one mechanical commit and a guard keeps it formatted.

Why it matters: a formatter that drops tokens or reorders fields cannot be run over the corpus, so the repo stays unformatted and every agent edit fights layout.

Decisions: D-FMTCOLLAPSE2=A (short blocks), D-NO-WARNINGS1=A (style is rewritten, never reported), D-DECL-COLON1=A (fixtures use `name: value` declarations). Greenfield: old spellings get no teaching diagnostic.

The tests/known-failing.tsv rows that name #6005 (12 fmt cases) belong to this card.

Source: Map card #6005 (Formatter), batch G15 of the 2026-10-28 consolidation. Simplify rewrites are #6850.

log.text: dev 61bf86113a (p266): the parser writes unions in canonical order, so jet fmt prints them canonically. Cases fmt_still_canonicalizes_valid_codable_union and fmt_canonicalizes_skipped_decode_union pass on p266 and are off known-failing. c19 (fmt keeps tokens in the 5 generated files) is in cycle p267.

c19 scope (p261): the generated files that still can't be written in fmt form because jet fmt would change their meaning are Spellings.jet, PreludeMarkers.jet, PreludeFacts.jet, PreludeDerives.jet and PreludeUnits.jet (HostErrors has since been handled by its generator). #6857 c6 is blocked on c19.
Cleanup 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2): #6790 c1 (FmtCorpus --check rc 0) is merged into c12, and #6790 c2 (idempotency, three excluded sources) moved here as #6898 c15; #6790 is closed.

criteria.text: Every Tests/Cases/Fmt fixture is written in current syntax and parses: fmt_preserves_named_payload_variant_dot_brace no longer stops with E0003 at `{`, and fmt_marks_only_value_returning_braced_callables_with_an_arrow no longer uses the retired `fn` keyword (E0081). criteria.evidence: dev bb5f0f28a0 (6898-c1-c4): cases Fmt/fmt_preserves_named_payload_variant_dot_brace and Fmt/fmt_marks_only_value_returning_braced_callables_with_an_arrow both PASS on the batch 13 compiler (dev bb5f0f28a0).

criteria.text: The formatter behaviour gaps are fixed: braced callables, the else-if chain to arm-table rewrite, comment fail-closed handling and the layout compiler-fact check. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Fmt/layout_compiler_fact_rejects_unknown_and_user_owned_at_members` and `--filter fmt/fmt_simplify_rewrites_a_classic_else_if_chain_to_an_arm_table` pass.

criteria.text: jet fmt produces the canonical arrow-loop form and is idempotent.

jet fmt emits suffix types (String?, MyErr!), arrow-before-result signatures, one blank line between functions and safe ordered-arm-table rewrites, idempotently; old spellings are ordinary parse errors with no teaching diagnostic.

jet fmt keeps every token of every Examples and Tests/UI source (on 95e5e3e027 it dropped or changed tokens in 131 files, could not parse 11 examples and wrote 4 outputs that do not lex). Proof: `jet test Compiler/JetCLI/Tests/FmtLossless.jet` (fmt_is_lossless_on_supported_source_corpus) passes.

criteria.text: jet fmt never changes meaning or order: it keeps named-tuple field order and adds no comma after a wrapped `loop … in` head (both seen on Compiler/JetCLI/Tests/ReceiptStorePorts.jet). Proof: a fmt case pins each, and `jet fmt --check Compiler/JetCLI/Tests` passes.

jet fmt keeps layout intent: a `#!/usr/bin/env jet` first line stays byte for byte, a blank line separating a standalone comment from a declaration stays, and text-block call arguments are indented one level. Proof: fmt cases for all three and `jet fmt --check Tools/Agent` clean of those shapes.

Every tracked .jet file under Compiler, Core, Jetpack, Examples, Tools and tests (negative fixtures and FmtCorpus rule exclusions aside) passes `jet fmt --check`, after one mechanical reformat commit that lands once the token and meaning criteria hold, and a guard keeps it so. The canonical syntax round-trip census, the full AST and form denominator, the fmt, LSP and Canvas coverage matrix, and the fail-closed gate for new syntax variants run as tests and pass.

jet fmt is idempotent on every corpus source: a second pass changes nothing, and the three sources left out for instability (Jetpack/Store/Tests/StoreIngestLate.jet and two Tests/Conformance/Corpus/Core/Web files, G5DevX-2 2026-11-13) rejoin the corpus. Proof: `jet Tools/Agent/FmtCorpus.jet --check` exits 0 with them included.

Owner ruling on C-G5-1: the formatter keeps one blank line after a file's leading comment block, so the header never merges into the first item's comment or doc (probes c01, c10, c13). A formatter case pins it, and jet fmt over Examples/ is unchanged apart from restored blank lines. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Fmt/leading_comment_block_keeps_blank_line`. (was #6566 c2)

Comment spellings come from the syntax registry (I7): the lexer and the about 30 comment scanners read COMMENT_PREFIX, BLOCK_COMMENT_OPEN and BLOCK_COMMENT_CLOSE (CoreSurface.jet:189-195, read by no Jet code today) and a new registry row for the /// doc comment; no Jet source types the literal "//" or "///" for comment scanning. Found by Research3, 2026-11-04 (comment-sigil study, probes c01-c14 under Docs/Research/Assets/20261104CommentSigil/, compiler 1f70b8d4bd). Proof: git grep for a quoted `//` or `///` literal in Compiler finds only the registry rows, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Fmt/` passes. (was #6566 c3)

Each syntax change this card makes (c5's //! ruling and c7's /% row) lands with its Data/Syntax registry row, a syntax-decisions.md log entry, editor grammars regenerated by jet self devtools grammars and re-blessed snapshots, and the syntax-ratification chore check passes. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter syntax_ratification`. (was #6566 c8)

jet fmt keeps meaning on every source, generated ones included. On p257 (dev 7d9dd2696d) it changed tokens in generated files that FmtCorpus leaves out: PreludeFacts.jet's triple-backtick raw text became double backticks, HostErrors.jet's `if … -> line += I64{1}` arm became a braced block, and Spellings.jet moved comments between declarations. The 9 Tests/Conformance/Corpus sources that do not parse (nist_gcm and seed_differential `~|`, JSON/load interpolation, dns_ptr and unix_listen match literals, the Sync/condition_* detached blocks, and Core/Compiler/package.jet `use api:`) are rewritten in current syntax. Proof: jet fmt over each of those files changes no token (whitespace-normalized compare), and `jet fmt --check Tests/Conformance` reports no parse error.

The whole-tree FmtLossless check (every source under Compiler, Core, Docs, Jetpack, Tests and Tools) passes with no exemption list, and its oracle accepts only rewrites a spec line ratifies. On dev dd5b0059df it found 7 token changes against ratified lines: comments moved (FmtBoxDrawingComment; block comments in MultilineCollectionLiterals; `impl ... using x // c` in GenericModuleAndLibraryBodies library.jet; RepeatedListHead commented.jet), grouping parens dropped against D-FMTPARENS1 (SubjectFirstRefutableTestBind `(parse()) == .Ok(v)`), and written arm braces dropped (TableArmComments; ValueTailBlocks). Each fix carries a Fmt case. Two more first counted as bugs are ratified rewrites that the oracle accepts narrowly: `#Layout: (c)` becomes `#Layout: c` (spec.md, marker arguments: "prints one simple argument without parentheses"), and `.Ready(value: x)` becomes `.Ready{value: x}` (spec.md, labeled payloads use `Type.Variant{label: value}`).

cards.title: Docs are runnable and true: every doc code block and public Core function example runs in CI, and the spec claims only what builds
cards.body:

cards.title: LSP references and rename follow checked identity across files, versions and Unicode
cards.body:
Destination: definition, references, prepareRename, rename and document symbols in `jet self lsp` resolve by checked semantic identity, not by name text: they pick exactly the declaration meant across aliases, shadowing, same-name modules and qualified calls; return real absolute URIs and exact identifier spans; apply edits at the checked overlay positions of unsaved documents; refuse when the target or document version is not current; and handle UTF-8 and UTF-16 boundaries.

Why it matters: a rename that touches the wrong `letter` or edits stale positions breaks code silently.

The proofs are tests/cases/lsp/lsp_checked_identity_and_versioned_rename and lsp_document_symbol_returns_symbols_for_imported_package_module (known-failing on dev 6f82527b17, rows naming #6386).

Source: #4917 c11, c37, c39-c46 (from #3183, #3184, #2370, #6164).

log.text: All criteria met; the last proofs ran on tip22, the compiler built from landed dev e271dd7f56 (batch 22).

Closer ranking (orchestrator, 2026-11-24T10:07Z), smallest remaining work first: 1 #6901 (c10 fix in batch 22; proof only), 2 #5007 (c10/c11 fix in batch 22; proof only), 3 #6853 (c4 in batch 23; c8 needs c8b-fix, ~1h), 4 #4720 (all 5 open criteria have fixes in batch 23; proofs plus fixes), 5 #6727 (c4 per-turn REPL retention, root fix ~2-4h), 6 #6902 (5 open, completion work ~1 day). Closer A G1Facts-2: #6853, #5007, #4720. Closer B G2Editor: #6901, #6727, #6902. Epoch agents on G1: G1Generation-2 (#6851), TypeIDSlice3-3 (#6852).

cards.title: Editor assists from checked facts: completion with foreign-word rows, semantic tokens and inlay hints
cards.body:
Destination: completion, semantic tokens and inlay hints in `jet self lsp` read lexer tokens and checked facts. Completion maps foreign method words (append, length, size, push_back) to the Jet name through the same registered rows E0311 uses; semantic tokens follow current syntax; inlay hints show call marks (D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A), automatically passed-up failures and scattered-method breadcrumbs.

Why it matters: these are what an editor shows on every keystroke; a private scanner or a second table drifts from the compiler.

Source: #4917 c10, c24-c27, c31, c49-c52 (from #6164, #4625, #662, #6014, #88).

log.text: Reopened: Tests/known-failing.tsv still names #6902 for two completion cases (Core member docs, package discovery index), and Tests/Guards/known_failing_owner.jet requires that the owning card be open. The two cases are now criteria on this card. The earlier criteria stay met.
All 11 criteria met; c11 proved on dev cba553447ac with the batch-40 compiler (ui TodoCandidates and cases LSP/lsp_todo_candidates both pass).

Closer ranking (orchestrator, 2026-11-24T10:07Z), smallest remaining work first: 1 #6901 (c10 fix in batch 22; proof only), 2 #5007 (c10/c11 fix in batch 22; proof only), 3 #6853 (c4 in batch 23; c8 needs c8b-fix, ~1h), 4 #4720 (all 5 open criteria have fixes in batch 23; proofs plus fixes), 5 #6727 (c4 per-turn REPL retention, root fix ~2-4h), 6 #6902 (5 open, completion work ~1 day). Closer A G1Facts-2: #6853, #5007, #4720. Closer B G2Editor: #6901, #6727, #6902. Epoch agents on G1: G1Generation-2 (#6851), TypeIDSlice3-3 (#6852).

criteria.text: Hover, references and completion find identifiers from lexer tokens, with no private text scanner in Compiler/JetLSP. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_hover_` and `--filter lsp/lsp_references_finds_all_uses` pass, and JetLSP has no character-class identifier scanner (`git grep -n -E 'is_ident_(start|char)' -- Compiler/JetLSP` prints nothing).
criteria.evidence: On a compiler built from landed dev 6ab0b5a5c8 (tip20), run in an export of that commit: cases LSP/lsp_hover_; cases LSP/lsp_references_finds_all_uses; 9 PASS 1 KNOWN-FAILING (exit 0); PASS 1/1; the known-failing hover row is typestate facts, owned by #6921. The card's lowercase `lsp/...` filter matches nothing. The is_ident grep over Compiler/JetLSP found nothing

criteria.text: Typing `nums.app` on `nums: [Int]` returns an item labelled `push` whose filter text is `append` and whose edit inserts `push`; the same for `.length` and `.size` to `len` and `push_back` to `push`.

criteria.evidence: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter LSP/lsp_completion_foreign_words` PASS 1/1 on tip23 (jet build Compiler from dev 45bbcdbd34).
