cards.title: A notebook becomes a local app: `jet notebook --app` serves cells and controls from the running kernel, with isolated tabs and live edits
cards.body:
Destination: `jet notebook --app` starts a loopback server. It renders the notebook's cell outputs, layouts and controls from the running notebook kernel, with no second evaluator. Each browser tab has its own typed session state. Edits under `jet dev` update the running app and keep the state whose type did not change. A machine-readable receipt names the bind address, sharing, data reads and trust grants.

Why it matters: marimo and Streamlit users turn notebooks into apps. Jet does it from the same checked kernel.

Depends on the notebook kernel, #6619.

Source: #6619 c11-c14 (split 2026-11-15).

criteria.text: `jet notebook --app` starts a loopback server that renders the notebook's cell outputs, layouts and controls from the running notebook kernel, with no second evaluator.
Two browser tabs on one notebook app get separate typed session state, run callbacks in a fixed order, and reset or reconnect independently; one tab cannot read or change the other's state.
Editing the notebook or one of its typed functions under `jet dev` updates the running app, keeps state whose type did not change, and names the reason when it resets state or shows a stale output.
The notebook app binds to loopback only unless sharing is asked for, and prints a machine-readable receipt of its bind address, sharing, data it reads and trust grants.

Editing a defining cell reruns only its pure transitive dependents automatically, records the dependency order, and marks effectful dependents for confirmation, labeling skipped work stale (D-DX-CELLS1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/shared_session_identical_stale_rules_across_clients`. (was #6619 c1)

A typed function argument renders as a validated control, and changing the control reruns the affected cells, while invalid input keeps an explicit error state. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/notebook_typed_argument_control`. (was #6619 c2)

Deleting a defining cell scrubs its bindings and invalidates the dependent outputs, and an old cached value is never shown as current. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/notebook_declarations_are_file_wide_but_state_cells_stay_ordered`. (was #6619 c3)

Closing and reopening the browser reconnects to the same bounded kernel only when the source and build identity and the authority checks pass, and an unauthorized reconnect is rejected with a registered error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/headless_protocol_interrupt_stdin_debug_perf_and_clients`. (was #6619 c4)

Text, HTML, SVG and table results stay attached to their cell, imported output stays quarantined, and exports report any semantics they drop. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/jetnb_cache_merge_ipynb_and_jet_export_never_hide_loss`. (was #6619 c5)

A `.jetnb` file holds only source and cell markers; outputs are recomputed when the notebook runs and are not stored between runs, and editing one cell changes only that cell's lines in `git diff`. Proof: a Tests/Cases notebook row under `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jetnb`. (was #6619 c6)

A Jupyter kernel adapter runs Jet cells: a scripted `jupyter nbconvert --execute` of a three-cell notebook passes where Jupyter is installed and is SKIP-HOST with a reason elsewhere. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/jupyter_kernel_runs_three_cells`. (was #6619 c7)

`jet run nb.jetnb` and `jet build nb.jetnb` print the same output as running every cell in order, and a corpus of 20 notebooks reruns from a clean state with identical output 20 of 20 times. For comparison, 4% of Jupyter notebooks reproduce, and marimo cannot build a native binary. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Notebook/run_and_build_match_cell_order` and `--filter notebook/corpus_reruns_identically`. (was #6619 c8)

Editing one cell of a 10-cell notebook reruns only its dependents and shows the new output sooner than marimo does on the equivalent notebook (Jet time over marimo time below 1.00). Proof: a committed measurement under Docs/Audits with both timings and the commands. (was #6619 c9)

The 4 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: Notebook/notebook_browser_matrix_uses_production_server-chromium, Notebook/notebook_browser_matrix_uses_production_server-firefox, Notebook/notebook_cli_headless_journey_uses_production_session, Notebook/notebook_first_hour_uses_shared_prelude_ambients_and_path. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Moves never copy: field, parameter, pattern, destructure and task-capture moves lower to moves in JetIR
cards.body:
Destination: every move the checker decides (a last use, a written `x.move()`, a destructure of an owned temporary, a pattern payload binding, a task argument or capture) lowers to a move in JetIR on O0, O1 and O2, and no copy appears without a sema decision.

Why: a hidden copy costs time and memory, and it breaks D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A (the compiler chooses moves when unmarked; `x.copy()` is the only way to ask for a copy). Returning several results must cost no more than output parameters (D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A). The copy ledger and the zero-unjustified-copy guard live on #3836; this card fixes the lowering that makes copies the checker never asked for.

Source: map #5989 (board consolidation 2026-10-28), carrying folded cards #4562 (task moves, SP13), #4564 (stage-2 copy gaps), #4567 (frozen; destructure copies), #4569 (linear copy residues), #4916 (field moves), #5821 (task capture lifetime), #5031 (pattern payload copies) and #5041 (no implicit copies).

criteria.text: `s.f.move()` and moves out of struct fields and parameters lower to a move in JetIR, with no clone, and the clone-gate copies the old FieldMove lowering added are removed. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/field_and_param_move_no_clone` on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #7040 c1

criteria.text: Destructuring an owned temporary (`(program, values) := returned_tuple()`, or a returned struct) moves every field on every tier, with no clone of the fields (D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A; frozen #4567 holds the original report). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/destructure_returned_tuple_moves_fields` and a paired cell against output parameters.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #7040 c2

criteria.text: Pattern payload bindings of owned locals and parameters move at the last use or alias under a stable root, never deep-copy the payload.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #7040 c3

criteria.text: Task arguments are moved or borrowed exactly as the sema decision says, and typed lists of tasks lower to the right types. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Tasks/` passes, and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/task_args_follow_sema_decision` shows no clone without a decision.

When a task body moves a captured value out or drops it, the closure environment no longer keeps it alive. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/task_capture_moved_out_frees`, where a task moves out a large captured value and then allocates as much again, and peak RSS stays below twice the value's size.

The three linear copy residues in Compiler/ (the L1 payload copy, element leftovers and the ref-binding move) use the sema copy decisions, so no copy appears without one. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/linear_copy_residues` and a lower copy count from `jet inspect choices` over the self-hosted compiler.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #7040 c4

criteria.text: The about 64 remaining dead parameter copies at O1 are gone. Proof: the entry-clone count from `jet inspect choices` over the self-hosted compiler is 0 (receipt with command and count).
criteria.evidence: Moved to #7040 c5

criteria.text: A `#Static` fixed array is one shared addressable constant, so a hot loop over it (the SHA-256 K table) emits no array copy. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Moves/static_array_loop_no_copy` on O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #7040 c6

criteria.text: The stage-2 copy-work repros for E0204, E0320 and the false L0102 are each accepted or rejected as the Jet spec says, each with its own UI snapshot.

D-RESOURCE-REASSIGN1=A: once a replacement value is ready, the displaced owner is released before the next statement, the next statement observes the released owner, and a surviving alias keeps its provider alive until its final owner ends; the ratified sample prints false, true, true, true. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/d_resource_reassign1_contract` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #5989 c21)

A record returned from a call is built in its caller's destination, not in a value slot that is then copied: a hot loop that gets a record from a helper costs no more instructions than one that builds the same record in place. Today on gate-p288 the returned record costs 2.88 G more instructions in the hot loop ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballot-rework/probes/zipcolumns-r5/ir_*.txt; found 2026-11-18 by the D-ARRAY-ZIPCOLUMNS1 r5 probes). Proof: a paired measurement (the helper record against the in-place record, built at -O2) shows equal instructions within noise, plus a second program that returns a different record shape.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #7040 c7

criteria.text: A field of borrowed storage moved into a call (for example `slot.held.move()` or permit.value passed to a && parameter) leaves the moved value unshared: today it stays shared with its source until the source field is written, so every write in the callee deep-copies it (copy-on-write). Found by Lens on #6841 c66: the debugger s held program deep-copied on every print (25 ms per print, 1.8 ms once the slot is emptied before the call), and JetDriver Pipeline jet_driver_held_eval_lend(held.probe.program....move()) likely pays the same. Repro $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Lens/c66held/mv/main.jet (jet run -A at -O0 and -O2): 5.2-5.9 ms per step on 400k strings against 0 us for a local s field. Proof: a case where a moved borrowed field written in the callee costs the same as a moved local field on O0, O1 and O2, with no deep copy (an allocation count of zero per step).
criteria.evidence: Moved to #7040 c8

cards.title: Plain data is freed in one step: root regions and no exit teardown
cards.body:
Destination: dropping plain data (no Close, consume or scrub duty) is O(1) at its last use. Trees and lists of plain data are allocated from a region owned by their root or phase, so releasing the root frees the region in one step. At process exit, plain memory is not torn down; only values with duties (files, locks, connections, flush and commit protocols) still close.

Why: in the stage-1 self-compile profile, about 25% of all CPU time was the allocator's free path, almost all of it drop glue walking trees node by node (owner direction 2026-10-02, #4320).

Source: #5989 c16, carried from #4320 by way of #4318 and #5041.

criteria.text: Plain-data trees and lists (no Close, consume duty or #Scrub) are allocated from a region owned by their root or phase, and dropping the root frees the region in one step with no per-node walk. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/plain_tree_region_release`, which counts one free for the whole tree, plus a paired cell against the node-by-node walk.

At process exit, plain memory is not torn down, and every Close, consume and scrub duty still runs. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Memory/exit_skips_plain_teardown`, which prints each Close's output and counts no frees of plain memory after main returns.

Fields drop in the order D-FIELD-DROP-ORDER1=A sets, in the JetIR drop glue. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Memory/DestructureDropOrder` (nested structs holding cleanup values) on O0, O1 and O2, and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter field_drop_order`. (was #5989 c5)

A panic inside a Close while a panic is already unwinding is process-fatal, as Docs/Spec/core-library-native-contract.md says: exit 70 with a Stop E3001 report, on run and --release. On 2026-11-07, Tests/Run/Ownership/ReleaseDeferClosePanic.jet (the body panics, then the second close panics) printed 'body / close second', then 'panic in a destructor during cleanup', and exited 1 on both tiers. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Ownership/ReleaseDeferClosePanic` passes on O0, O1 and O2, and its known-failing row is removed. (was #5989 c17)
criteria.evidence:
On the p391 batch compiler (census build of dev 55614ffe3b):
- p391 full suite: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Ownership/ReleaseDeferClosePanic` gives PASS on o0, o1 and o2. The row is PASS, not KNOWN-FAILING or UNEXPECTED-PASS, so no known-failing row remains.
- Run by hand: `jet run ReleaseDeferClosePanic.jet` exits 70 and prints "body", "close second", then "Stop: Jet.Panic: `panic: close stop` --> ReleaseDeferClosePanic.jet:10 in close" (the E3001 report under its current Jet.Panic heading). The second close panics while the body's panic unwinds, which is process-fatal: the first close does not run.
- `jet build -O2` of the same program, run as a binary: the same output and exit 70.

cards.title: Core crypto and service keys: the file-seal contract, one Secret mechanism, and no signing key derivable from a public token
cards.body:
Destination: Core/Crypto's file seal meets the JETC v2 contract and D-CRYPTO-ENVELOPE2=A's signatures, sealing works for an unprivileged user on every supported Linux kernel, every secret (crypto keys included) uses the one runtime Secret mechanism that wipes on Close and on crash, and no service signing key can be derived from a public token.

Why: these are the security defects the 2026-10 Core crypto and memory reviews found (I8: one mechanism per job).

Source: #1387 c13-c15 and c18-c20, carried from folded #4777, #4841, #4861, #4863, #5891 and #4821. Two items are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15): D-SERVICE-AUTH-KEY1 and D-EDPOINT-ORPHAN1.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c5, c6, body reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: Core crypto file_seal and migrate (Core/Crypto) meet the JETC v2 contract: bounded streaming, and no overwrite of an existing destination. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter file_seal`, with a Core #Test that seals a stream larger than the buffer limit and a second seal onto an existing path that fails without touching it.

file_seal reports failure as a FileCryptoError instead of returning Bool, and file_open borrows the identity (`&X25519SecretKey`), as D-CRYPTO-ENVELOPE2=A specifies; every caller, example and test moves in the same change. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter file_seal_signature`, and git grep finds no Bool-returning file_seal.

On Linux, the seal publish step uses the portable form the vault already uses (linkat through /proc/self/fd/N with AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW), not linkat with AT_EMPTY_PATH, so an unprivileged seal works before Linux 6.10 (RouteACrypto.jet). The O_DIRECTORY and O_NOFOLLOW constants are checked for every Linux target. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter file_seal_unprivileged_publish` run as an unprivileged user.

There is one Secret mechanism: core.crypto.Secret and every crypto key are built on the runtime Secret (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Secret.jet), which wipes spare capacity and is wiped on a crash. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Crypto/secret_wiped_on_close_and_crash`, and git grep finds a single Secret wipe implementation.

A service authority signing key comes from a secret issuance and registry and can never be derived from the public token (Core/Service/Service.jet reads the authority proof from hex today), and the receipt does not carry the authority as a public String. The issuance design is the ballot D-SERVICE-AUTH-KEY1, on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).

crypto.EdPoint (Core/Crypto/Crypto.jet:1645), which no public function takes or returns since the constant-time dedupe (af3a27c3c), is removed in one cutover or given a documented public use with a test, as the ballot D-EDPOINT-ORPHAN1 (on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15)) decides. Proof: `git grep -n EdPoint -- Core Compiler Examples` matches the ruling.

D-CRYPTOENV1=A: core.crypto offers misuse-resistant seal, open, sign and verify; the expert raw and exposure operations (a raw nonce or algorithm) require #Unsafe; and a secret value cannot be printed, compared, reflected or serialized in ordinary code (Docs/Spec/syntax-decisions.md).

core.crypto and core.net.tls contain no file derived from mbedtls: every file is MIT, written from the cited specifications (RFC, FIPS, SP 800), and the public and private module boundaries are unchanged. Proof: `git grep -l -i mbedtls -- Core/Crypto Core/Net/Tls` prints nothing, and each file header cites its specification. (was #6748 c1)

The rewrite passes the same vectors (NIST CAVP plus the fetched Wycheproof), the interop matrix and the constant-time checks as #6694. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter Crypto` and `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter tls` with the CAVP, Wycheproof, interop and constant-time rows. (was #6748 c2)

The full mbedtls surface that Core does not use is complete in Jet: every mbedtls test-suite vector, interop with OpenSSL and the old mbedtls build on every TLS 1.2 and 1.3 version, suite and curve, client certificates and the remaining X.509 and PSA features, with constant-time checks on every secret-dependent primitive. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile core --filter Crypto` with every mbedtls test-suite vector, and the interop receipt for every TLS version, suite and curve. (was #6748 c3)

password_hash_with_salt leaves the public core.crypto surface and all public compiler rows, and fixed-salt tests use expert.argon2id (D-CRYPTO-SALTROW1=A). Proof: `git grep -n password_hash_with_salt -- Core Compiler/Prelude Examples` prints nothing. (was #6748 c4)

No external dependency is added (I6), and the RSA rows New, generate_key, private_encrypt, private_decrypt, public_encrypt and public_decrypt stay refused as not built; building or deleting them is on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter crypto_rsa_not_built`. (was #6748 c6)

The 2 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: SecretsExpiry/expiring_secret_loan_can_call_cross_file_read_helpers, SecretsExpiry/expiring_secret_loan_can_call_read_helpers. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Channels and streams: every outcome stays distinct, no item is lost, and pipelines stay bounded
cards.body:
Destination: channel capacities, closing, cancellation and failure are distinct observable outcomes; streams never turn not-ready into end-of-stream, never lose an item or spin, and clean up through the task path when broken, dropped or failed; parallel stream helpers keep order rules and in-flight bounds; and `Sender.try_send` hands optional work to a background queue without waiting (D-CONC-BACKGROUND1=A).

Why: a lost item, a silent end-of-stream or an unbounded queue is a correctness bug that tests rarely see.

Source: #3239 c13, c15, c21-c29 and c38 (carried from #3261, #3343, #3344-#3346, #3365-#3367 and #4451).

criteria.text: Channel outcomes are distinct: capacity 0 (rendezvous) differs from capacity 1, and full, closed-send, dropped-receiver, cancel and receive-after-close each report their own outcome. A public API change needs a ballot. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/ChannelOutcomes` on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: dev b66642b8bc, the a0.0.046 admit's candidate suite run (s2 compiler, evidence rows-candidate.json): `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/ChannelOutcomes` → 3 of 3 PASS (o0, o1, o2), with no public API change.

criteria.text: A non-blocking drain stops at Empty without closing the channel, later items stay readable, and closed, cancelled and failed states stay distinct.

A stream's not-ready state never becomes a normal end-of-stream, and consumer demand and producer wakeup can never lose an item or spin. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter StreamReadiness` prints the same output on O0, O1 and O2.
Breaking out of, dropping or failing a pipeline cancels and cleans up through the existing task path. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter StreamCancelOnBreak` on O0, O1 and O2.

Sync and suspended stream callbacks keep their declared effects and output order on every tier, with no second StreamExt-style dialect. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter StreamFailureAdapters` on O0, O1 and O2.

Exact splitting, zip, reverse, positions and chunked folds are offered only when their bounds hold, encounter order stays separate from callback effect order, and cheap kernels stay serial (the speed pair is on #6085). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/ParaGenericSources` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter para_indexed_after_filter`.

A parallel stream map's limit bounds in-flight work and results, ordered and completion-order modes both exist, failure and cancellation cleanup is defined, and capture rules apply (the speed pair is on #6085).

Merging ready streams keeps per-source order, orders across sources by readiness, closes only the named sources on an owned end, drop or error, keeps keyed-source identity, and states its fairness and in-flight bound.
Timed batching keeps processing time, event time and readiness distinct and states its timeout, partial-batch and cancel rules.

A worker-pool stream reports per-worker initialize, clone and drop counts, ordered versus any-completion results, and the effects still in flight after cancel, with no new pool, scheduler or tuning API. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Concurrency/worker_pool_counts` on O0, O1 and O2.

D-CONC-BACKGROUND1=A: a nonblocking `Sender.try_send` returns ownership of the value when the queue is full, and a bounded worker, panic isolation and shutdown compose with it, with no Worker wrapper type.

A task body's `Err(e)` of domain type E reaches the joiner as E, not as `TaskFailure.Panicked`, and Core declares the single `TaskFailure` enum that sema and the runtime both use. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/TaskDomainError` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3239 c5)

Examples/Concurrency/Parallel/ParallelScan, Examples/Concurrency/DeadlineContext and Examples/Memory/Views/ReturnedViews match their .out goldens on O0, O1 and O2 (BrowserLockedProvision is on #6552), and each rebless is justified as correct new output. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter ParallelScan`, `--filter DeadlineContext` and `--filter ReturnedViews`. (was #3239 c6)

A task group shows capacity-one backpressure, the two-worker limit, first-failure identity and sibling cancellation through observed transitions, plus its join, shield and detach obligations. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/ConformanceCapsule` on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3239 c10)
criteria.evidence: dev b66642b8bc, the a0.0.046 admit's candidate suite run (s2 compiler, evidence rows-candidate.json): `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/ConformanceCapsule` → 3 of 3 PASS (o0, o1, o2).

criteria.text: Task affinity, blocking offload, admission and backpressure, caller buffers, allocation and cancellation association each map onto an existing owner, and each new control goes to its own owner ballot (cost claims are G11, #2858). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Concurrency/control_mapping_`, one case per mapping on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3239 c11)

core.tasks has no sentinel or silent rail: a send on a closed channel is an error (never -1), a lock always locks, nothing is dropped silently, and a negative or zero capacity never means unbounded (STREAMS owns what 0 and 1 mean). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Concurrency/no_sentinel_`, one case per rule on O0, O1 and O2. (was #3239 c61)

A checked operation that fails inside a task (overflow, division by zero, list bounds) publishes `TaskFailure.Panicked` to the joiner instead of stopping the process. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Concurrency/checked_failure_in_task_`, one case per operation on O0, O1 and O2, each showing the joiner's report and the process continuing. (was #3239 c62)

Task-group expansion in concurrency services gives each generated function a unique JetIR identity, and the bounded workload reaches its exact expected output with no duplicate-function internal error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Concurrency/task_group_expansion_unique_ids`. (was #3239 c79)

JetSema enforces the spec's task detach and freeze rules, each refusal a registered error with a UI snapshot. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter task_detach_` and `--filter task_freeze_`. (was #3239 c80)
Task control, run-time stop codes and run-time I/O work at O0 under `jet run`. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter TaskControlTiers/` passes its O0 rows. (was #3239 c84)

D-SEND-ERROR1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). sender.send(v) returns nothing on success and fails with SendError<T> when no receiver remains; err.value moves the unsent value back. Core declares conversions from SendError and Closed into Err, and from SendError into Closed, so a bare send in run, a task block or a function naming no error type passes the failure up with a message naming the send, and inside a function failing with Closed it passes up as Closed. Freeing queued values runs each value's drop. Depends on #6787 (generic conversions into Err). Proof: cases for a bare send, send ?? handler recovering err.value, and a send inside a Closed function, on O0, O1 and O2; every in-repo send caller is migrated in the same cutover. (was #3239 c85)

Stream.key_by, window, watermark and the late-event disposition share one SendFn callback identity and the bare event side-output shape on O0, O1, O2 and web where applicable; a callback whose result is not sendable, or that escapes, is refused. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Collections/StreamWindows`. (was #3317 c45)

cards.title: Cancellation reaches everything: timers, idle loops, signals, deadlines, supervised restarts and job queues
cards.body:
Destination: after a cancel or shutdown, no timer, interval, scheduled job, signal handler, listener or supervised worker survives; an idle event loop costs almost nothing; root cancellation, signals, request deadlines, listener drain and stdin close share one Prelude semantics; supervised restarts follow the #1076 policy; and core.jobs runs its typed queue lifecycle through one owner.

Why: a producer that outlives its cancel leaks work and keeps a process alive.

Source: #3239 c7, c8, c40, c50-c52 and c75 (carried from #3095, #3108, #4347, #6013 and #2787).

criteria.text: After `tasks.cancel`, no timer or interval producer survives, and app shutdown cancels and joins, or reports, every scheduled job; clock and missed-tick behavior is recorded, and nothing replays on restart.
A 2 s idle wait with 10 ticks uses under 5% of one CPU, shows exactly 10 wakeups, and file descriptors return to the baseline after cancel.

Root cancellation, signal handling, request deadlines, listener drain and ProcessStdin close run through shared Prelude semantics. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Concurrency/SignalDeadline` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLISignals/` on O0, O1 and O2.
The #1076 restart policy (limit, window, backoff) works for services on the self-hosted toolchain, with its Rust-era acceptance tests ported.

A task group can carry the same restart policy: a worker that fails 3 times is restarted 3 times, and a 4th failure inside the window fails the group with a report naming the worker and its last failure.
Cancelling a supervised group stops restarts and joins every worker, so no worker outlives the group.

The ratified core.jobs typed queue methods (enqueue, delay, claim, acknowledge and the rest) and the job error lifecycle check and run through one owner. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Jobs/TypedQueueLifecycle`, deterministic on O0, O1 and O2.

A cancel that arrives while a Close runs is held until the close finishes and is delivered at the next wait, as Docs/Spec/core-library-native-contract.md says. In the case, the close signals the parent on entry, the parent cancels the task, and the close then waits on a channel; the output is 'close worker: finished', then 'worker: cancelled'. On 301567cec7 the cancel cut the close's wait on run and --release. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter TaskControlTiers/a_cancel_at_cleanup_entry_waits_out_the_close_on_every_tier` passes on every tier, and its known-failing row is removed. (was #5989 c18)

A #Shield body always runs to its end before the cancellation lands: Examples/Concurrency/ShieldCommit.jet (a task.race whose losing task sleeps 20ms inside #Shield, then prints "committed") lost its "committed" line in 1 of 6 runs at -O0 on both the p406 and p407 jets (dev 113879859e and 50aae50f71, 2026-11-21; it printed only "7"), and the p407 full suite failed its O0 golden on it. The shield either did not defer the cancellation, or the cancelled task's output was dropped. Proof: ShieldCommit run 200 times at each of O0, O1 and O2 (and under parallel load) always prints "committed" then "7", with a runtime unit test that cancels a task sleeping inside a shield and checks the body's effects.

The known-failing row this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv: WsLaw/ambient_deadline_cancels_recv. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Restricted code and sandbox guests: one sandbox package kind, lent Authority, scoped file access and the Capabilities run case
cards.body:
Destination: `target: sandbox` is the only package-kind spelling (no `plugin` word left for it); a sandbox guest names the rights it needs and the host lends an Authority value tightened to a folder or host (D-FOUND-SANDBOX1=A); restricted code derives one opaque file scope from Authority while trusted scripts keep direct fs calls (D-FILES-SCOPE1=A); every tier calls the one canonical resource, no-follow and IOError policy; and the sandbox foundation runs end to end with a generated guest snapshot.

Why: a guest that can reach past its lent authority, or two spellings for one package kind, breaks the authority promise.

Source: #4268 c4, c5, c33-c36, c41-c44 and c58 (ratified contracts from #1731, #2786 and #2805, and #6753 c2). Build-graph plugins are a different word and stay.

log.text: c14 not met at dev f768b6597e. The golden Examples/Modules/Packages/SandboxMathKit/run.jet passes in suite-p392, but git ls-files '*.wasm' -- Examples prints two tracked files: Examples/Modules/Packages/SandboxMathKit/mathkit.wasm (25911 bytes, the prebuilt guest c14 says must not ship) and Examples/Modules/Packages/PluginFailure/malformed_guest.wasm (41 bytes, a deliberately malformed input, which the proof also forbids as written). Both date from 2c3e68a70b (11-06). Remaining: build mathkit.wasm from SandboxSource in the example's own build; make the malformed input inside the PluginFailure example rather than commit it.

criteria.text: D-FILES-SCOPE1=A: trusted scripts keep direct fs calls, while restricted code derives one opaque scope from Authority and uses the familiar methods on it; folder and host narrowing hold, and a derived Authority escaping through a loop header or step is refused.
D-FOUND-SANDBOX1=A: a sandbox guest declares the imports it needs, the host lends an Authority value tightened to a folder or host, and a missing grant fails before any side effect.

`target: sandbox` is the only manifest spelling for the package kind; `target: plugin` is gone with no rewrite or alias (PackageModel Targets.jet and PackageViews.jet still map `.Plugin` on dev 02cb957084). cards.title: Checked text values (SQL, HTML, Sh, URL, Path, DateTime) are built only from checked literals or an audited `.raw`, never from a runtime string in a public field
cards.body:
Destination: outside its defining module, a checked text value cannot be built by filling its public fields with runtime text (`SQL{text: s, values: v}`, `HTML{markup: s}` and the other checked heads); the checked literal or `.raw` (D-SQL-RAW1=A, the one audited gate) is the only way in, the text is read back through accessors, every `.raw` call in a package is listed, and checked literals keep working.

Why: a public field that accepts runtime text makes injection possible and the checked literal a false promise (I1).

Source: #6277 c8-c11 (carried from #6402). D-SQL-RAW1's gate itself is #4520 c3.

criteria.text: Outside its defining module, `SQL{text: s, values: v}` with a runtime `s` is a compile error whose fix names the checked literal `SQL{"...{value}"}` and `SQL.raw(...)`, and r01f_sql_inject_db.jet fails `jet check` with it.

The same holds for `HTML{markup: s}` (r10_html_fields.jet) and every other checked text head that carries trusted text (Sh, URL, Path, DateTime), and reading the text back goes through accessors (`template()`, `params()`, `display`). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter checked_text_runtime_field_refused_`, one negative fixture per head.
`SQL.raw` and `HTML.raw` are the only ways to build these values from runtime text, and the audit listing lists every `.raw` call in a package.

Checked literals keep working unchanged: the db_policy, typed_sql and checked_sql_query fixtures pass on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter DBPolicy` (and typed_sql, checked_sql_query).

A checked-text type's check runs on every way in: its generated decoder and its from_string run the type's check, not only .from, so no safe code builds an unchecked value (found 2026-11-15 by a D-APP-ID1 probe on gate-p174; it affects every user checked-text type). Proof: a case decodes, from_strings and .froms an invalid text and gets the same refusal from all three on O0, O1 and O2. (was #6277 c13)

cards.title: The store is crash-safe and deterministic: one producer transaction, cycle-safe graph queries, concurrent open, parallel verify, and offline closure moves
cards.body:
Destination: every Jetpack producer registers objects, outputs, references and package records through one crash-recoverable transaction; reference, referrer and closure queries are deterministic and cycle-safe; N processes can open a fresh store at once; verification and hashing fan out across threads; and a toolchain closure over 1 GiB moves between Hangars with no network and no host Nix.

Why: the store is the ground truth for every build and environment; a torn write or a nondeterministic query poisons everything above it.

Source: #6632 c2, c11, c12, c105 and c106 (carried from #3590, #420, #3578 and #3598).

criteria.text: Every production producer registers canonical object descriptors, named outputs, references, action/output relations and package records through one crash-recoverable transaction, and migrating old stores is idempotent. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Store/producer_transaction_` including a crash failpoint case.
Direct and transitive references, referrers, closures and action/output queries are deterministic and cycle-safe, and inconsistent graph state is refused or quarantined.

Opening a fresh store is idempotent under concurrent runs: N jet processes started on an empty store all succeed with one consistent store. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Store` (the concurrent open case).

Store verification and hashing fan out across OS threads through a task group (D-TASKRUNTIME1=A), and the store verify and hashing performance cells record the speedup (frozen #3598 item 2 holds the original). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Store` (the parallel verify case) and the perf cells in the measurement manifest.

cards.title: `fn build` graphs: every action fully declared and identified, failures before publication, typed probes, action policy, and the BuildPlan evaluator in Jet
cards.body:
Destination: programmable builds run in Jet. `fn build` is checked and its BuildPlan is evaluated in compile-time code (natively at O0); targets have dependencies, kinds and declared toolchains; each action's identity covers everything that affects it, so plan, cache, execution and receipt agree; anything undeclared or failing stops before publication; typed probes feed the plan; and actions run under declared policy, helpers, signing and resource pools.

Why: a build whose identity misses an input caches wrong results; one that publishes partial output makes broken artifacts look valid.

Source: #6632 c14, c15, c19-c22, c39, c40, c73 and c91 (carried from #692, #1041, #1042, #427, #933, #3521/#3933 and #6096). Dependency builds (`b.include`) are on #6621, remote scheduling on #6026, build plugins on #6935.

criteria.text: `fn build` is checked and its BuildPlan is evaluated in compile-time code, natively at O0.

Generation rounds, cycle locking and the host executor seam work for programmable builds: a build that generates code runs its next round, a cycle is refused, and the executor runs the planned actions.
A `fn build` graph declares targets with their dependencies, kinds and toolchains, and the production executor builds them in dependency order with the declared toolchain.

Action and probe identity covers toolchain, every declared input, output, tool, effect and platform fact, environment, authority, resources and provenance; plan, cache, execution and receipt agree, and a repeated build gives the same result identity.

Missing locks, ambient-tool access, undeclared inputs or access, policy denial, probe failure, cycles, invalid outputs, cancellation and partial stage results all fail before publication, leave no valid-looking artifact, and cannot be waived by a boolean label. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter BuildGraph/fails_before_publication_`, one case per failure.

With conflicting host and declared toolchains the executor uses the declared one, locked and ambient probes are told apart, a denied grant stops the action, and changing any identity input invalidates its cache entry. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter BuildGraph/declared_toolchain_wins` and `--filter build_graph/cache_invalidation`.
Build actions run under their declared action policy, with helpers, artifact signing and resource pools that bound concurrency.
Typed probes run once under the lock and feed the plan, and a driver runs a build end to end through the production executor.

The staged-plan action path is deterministic and complete, and refuses sandbox and graph failures without producing an artifact (the Rust tests staged_plan_action_production_path_is_deterministic_and_complete and staged_plan_action_rejects_sandbox_and_graph_failures_without_artifact; model-level tests landed in 19d19cb61f).

build.jet declares no C compiler, musl, ar or nm (#6693, #6687 c2). Every tool it still needs is declared with b.toolchain and b.probe, JET_PACK_MUSL_LIB and the other toolchain environment variables stay deleted, and a missing tool fails at once with a registered error. Proof: `git grep -n -w -E "JET_PACK_MUSL_LIB|musl|ar|nm|cc" -- Compiler/build.jet` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter build_missing_tool`.

The known-failing row this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv: BuildEntry/toolchain_sdk_signing_and_probes_reach_the_executor. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Build plugins: packaged Wasm components load with version negotiation, run isolated, and fail closed with full rollback
cards.body:
Destination: a build plugin ships as a packaged Wasm component; the driver loads it with interface version negotiation; package identity, component bytes, interface version, granted authority, limits, guest output, graph changes, provenance and receipt agree; and every hostile or failing plugin fails closed and rolls back fully. Build plugins are a build-graph word, unrelated to the sandbox package kind (that is #6930).

Source: #6632 c23-c26 and c45 (carried from #695 and #1048).

criteria.text: A build plugin ships as a packaged Wasm component and the driver loads it with interface version negotiation; an incompatible version is refused.
Package identity, component bytes, interface version, granted authority, resource limits, guest output, graph changes, provenance and receipt agree for a plugin run.

Tamper, an incompatible version, denied authority, a trap, timeout, fuel or memory exhaustion, malformed guest output and a partial graph change each fail closed and roll back fully. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter BuildPlugin/fails_closed_`, one case per failure.
Benign and hostile packaged components are instantiated through the driver, proving guest output, isolation limits, rollback and provenance (header validation alone does not count).

cards.title: Existing builds import into the typed action graph: CMake and Make, Gradle, npm and Cargo
cards.body:
Destination: each legacy build system is an optional import into the shared typed action graph. Imported commands, tools, inputs, outputs, environment, dependencies, resources, cache identity and provenance are inspectable; policy can forbid the import (for example in CI); and a denial, unsupported construct, undeclared access, tool failure, path escape, nondeterminism or partial import fails clearly without running an unreviewed fallback command.

Why: teams adopt Jet over existing projects; an import that silently shells out defeats the graph's guarantees.

Source: #6632 c41-c44 (carried from #694 and #1044-#1047, built in the retired Rust engine and not yet in Jet).

log.text: Owner order 2026-11-21: CMake/Make/Cargo build import lives in G5 Jetpack and stays frozen until Jet core bones are complete.

criteria.text: A CMake project and a Make project import into the typed action graph with every import fact inspectable, the import can be forbidden by policy, and an unsupported construct fails clearly with no fallback command.
A Gradle project imports the same way, with the same inspection, policy ban and clear failure.
An npm project imports the same way, with the same inspection, policy ban and clear failure.
A Cargo project imports the same way, with the same inspection, policy ban and clear failure.

cards.title: Environment lifecycle: one typed planner for dotenv, hooks, checks and reload, hash-bound trust, one deterministic environment graph, and services
cards.body:
Destination: one typed lifecycle planner covers dotenv, unset, on_enter, checks, reload and the D-ECO7 hook; first use asks for trust and grants bind role modules and plan hashes; background reload coalesces changes and applies a checked plan at the next prompt; composition, profiles, follows, lifecycle and locks resolve to one deterministic environment graph, and every failure keeps the previous usable environment; and service facts drive one observable lifecycle.

Source: #6632 c27-c33 and c46 (carried from #784, #790, #793, #1069-#1073, #1083, #1085, #1090, #1093, #1094, #1103 and #1104).

criteria.text: One typed lifecycle planner supports dotenv, unset, on_enter, checks, reload and the D-ECO7 hook, with simple defaults and expert policy.
First use asks for trust; grants bind role modules and plan hashes; a denied or unseen hook is skipped and the shell still opens.
Background reload is on by default, coalesces changes, refuses cycles, and applies a checked plan at the next prompt.
Dotenv allowlists, secret redaction, task effects, plan order, failure policy, rollback and retained-state facts each have a case.
`jet env test` starts from a clean shell, and the dossier JSON, errors, docs, examples and goldens match the ratified lifecycle.
Composition, profiles, follows, lifecycle, locks and active-facet disclosure resolve to one deterministic environment graph.
Cycles, stale grants, conflicting profiles, unsafe paths, denied hooks and failed reloads keep the previous usable environment.
Service, task, file, readiness, dependency and discovery facts drive one observable service lifecycle with bounded behavior.

cards.title: Trust and secrets: the trust gate and repo secrets go through the vault, composed secrets and per-secret metadata work, and no write skips a policy gate
cards.body:
Destination: the trust gate, Jet pins and repo secrets use the one vault owner; composed secrets (D-JPK-SECRETCOMPOSE1=D) and per-secret metadata (D-JPK-SECRETMETA1=B, Docs/spec/spec.md) are built; the new secrets verbs are registered; and the Jet port of Jetpack refuses any write that skips a policy gate (E3415).

Source: #6632 c3, c47-c49 and c108 (carried from #3634/#3667 and #1779).

criteria.text: The trust gate, Jet pins and repo secrets read and write through the one vault owner, with no second secret store. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Secrets/` and `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Trust/pins_use_vault`.

D-JPK-SECRETCOMPOSE1=D: secret parts (host, user, password) plus one declared template give an assembled value read through the same Secret-effect path, and rotating one part changes the composed value.

D-JPK-SECRETMETA1=B: per-secret metadata (required, description, per-profile default, generated value) is built, and a required secret that is missing fails activation with a registered error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Secrets/metadata_` and `--filter secrets/secrets_unset_reencrypts_store_and_removes_value`.
The new secrets verbs are registered in the syntax registry (Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax), and section I of Docs/Research/2026-07-24-devenv-parity.md records the 0.18 delta.
The Jet port of Jetpack refuses any write that skips a policy gate (TrustStore, workspace lock or invocation flags) with E3415.

Identity, signatures, provenance, locks, advisory policy and offline state give one deterministic allow or deny, and tamper, rollback, freeze, mix-and-match, stale metadata and a compromised key fail closed with a useful recovery path.

After the owner-controlled key ceremony, https://keys.jet-lang.dev/nix-index-v1.ed25519.pub serves the exact client format, and the client verifies against its existing local pin and never trusts a host-returned replacement. Proof: a committed receipt of fetching the URL and verifying a signed index against the local pin.

The pinned client reads the staged index key: the output of `jet Tools/JetpackInfra/StageTrustRoot.jet`, read by the index client from its local pin, verifies a signed fixture, and a host-served substitute key is refused.

The signed package index and the content-addressed binary cache are served as static content under the owned domain; an official endpoint is never the default until it verifies, and the keyless local tier is unchanged. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter PkgIntegrationTrustRoot/official_endpoint_not_default_until_verified` and a committed receipt of the served index verifying.
The Trust and TrustRoot claims pass in `jet test Compiler --profile packages` (no blockers, run first).
Jet tools collect no telemetry and post nothing to external services without an explicit user command.

cards.title: Registry: `jet registry publish`, `keygen` and `jet fetch` are built, publishing fails atomically and refuses confusable names, and credentials stay redacted
cards.body:
Destination: `jet registry publish` and `jet registry keygen` are built; publish failures are atomic and redact secrets; names within edit distance 1 of an existing name are refused (D-1912-NAME1=A); `jet fetch` and `jet fetch --locked` round-trip a foreign provider; and netrc credentials are parsed exactly and never leak.

Source: #6632 c36, c75, c80, c107 and c109 (carried from #928, #6418, #1912 and #4268). The public-API promise checks are on #6860.

criteria.text: `jet registry publish` and `jet registry keygen` are built, and every cases row that reported E2104 for them passes. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Pkg/cli_publish_` and `--filter pkg/registry_keygen_`.

A concurrent publish, duplicate version, interrupted upload, stale index, bad credential or corrupt artifact fails atomically and redacts secrets. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Publication/publish_fails_atomically_`, one case per failure.

D-1912-NAME1=A: publishing refuses a package name within edit distance 1 of an existing name, an exact confusable match or a reserved suffix; a name at distance 2 is reported but publish proceeds; the rule is the same for core and community packages.

`jet fetch` and `jet fetch --locked` are built: a stale or missing provider artifact fails with E1256 and writes no lock, and a good one fetches, projects .jet/bindings/js/plotly.jet, compiles, and verifies byte-identical in locked mode. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Pkg/foreign_package_provider_fetch_lock_and_locked_round_trip` passes and leaves Tests/known-failing.tsv.

The netrc parser follows the exact netrc rules (default entry, macdef, quoting, malformed input) rather than treating netrc as INI, keeps credentials out of errors, and adds no ambient file discovery or network authentication as a side effect. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Jetpack/netrc_parse_` and `--filter jetpack/netrc_redacts_credentials`.

cards.title: User tools update to one exact verified release, keep a complete working generation through every failure, and drift is found at no cost
cards.body:
Destination: a user-tool update resolves, authorizes, acquires, hashes, realizes and activates one exact release for the next launch; origins, trust and authentication are gated before any request; known pins check identity and SHA-256 before and after the GET; raw assets, archives and app bundles need no manual hash, catalog entry or recipe edit; every failure keeps a complete working generation; and drift detection costs nothing on a normal command (owner ruling 2026-08-25: no shim).

Source: #6632 c52 and c92-c104 (carried from #3032, #3033, #4275 and #2193). Proofs live in Store/Tests/ReleaseActivation.jet and the Jetpack Trust area.

criteria.text: A user-tool update resolves, authorizes, acquires, hashes, realizes and activates one exact release for the next launch, while a project update changes only the channel lock and the later project realization acquires and activates.

`jetpack update --deps` resolves the project channel lock without realizing packages, and `jetpack use <ref> --prep` realizes a user profile independent of the project directory and lock. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTool/update_deps_lock_only` and `--filter jetpack_tool/use_prep_user_profile`.
The shared lifecycle gates candidate and redirect origins before any request, direct-source trust before an unsigned GET, and existing authentication before acquisition.
Known pins require the matching concrete identity and expected SHA-256 before and after the GET, and a same-identity change in bytes never replaces the working install.
Raw assets become executable entries, archives use declared safe roots and entries, and app bundles use one declared .app root and executable entry.
Raw, archive and app-bundle updates need no manual hash, catalog entry or recipe edit.

Every metadata, trust, origin, authentication, acquisition, extraction, install, validation, cancellation and crash failure keeps a complete working generation. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter ReleaseActivation/failpoint_` (the failpoint claims).
A failed first install leaves no active entry, and a failed update leaves the prior active entry and lock facts unchanged.
Concurrent activation revalidates source, grant, candidate, artifact and generation facts inside the transaction.
A running old app keeps its executable and resources, and the next launch selects the verified complete closure.

Updates reuse the existing Store, lock, receipt, producer facts, sandbox and recovery mechanisms, with no parallel copy. Proof: git grep finds one release-activation path in Jetpack/Store, and the c1-c10 cases pass.

A direct source without authentication needs interactive approval before the first artifact GET, which `-y` and `--trust` cannot grant; the grant binds source, metadata authority, repo, resolver, selector, asset policy, target, platform, proof floor and ordered HTTPS origins, and excludes mutable version, tag, digest and URL; an unchanged scope needs no new prompt, a new origin stops before the request, and any scope change invalidates the grant; release trust never authorizes builds, execution or elevation. Proof: `JETPACK_WORKER=check jet Jetpack/Bootstrap/Check.jet --area Trust --tests` prints CHECK OK.

Drift detection adds no closure resolution, network call or full-binary hash to a normal jetpack command, measured against the command time before the change. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTool/tool_profile_reports_drift_without_prompt_and_yes_moves_pin` and a committed timing receipt.

Executable identity, lease ownership, replacement, restart, receipts and rollback agree under concurrent processes and upgrades. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackEngine/parent_env_unchanged_after_use`, `--filter jetpack_engine/use_fails_closed_when_executable_lease_service_key_is_invalid` and `--filter jetpack_platform/platform_gate_reaches_store_authenticated_lease_service`.
A crash, lock contention, an interrupted replacement, stale leases or a reboot never publishes a partial executable or deletes the last good version.

A tool installs with no accidental project capture, and its version, PATH exposure, update and offline behavior are explicit (D-CHANNEL-AUTO1=A). Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTool/tool_install_publishes_real_projection_and_generation` and `--filter jetpack_tool/use_ephemeral_execs_inside_and_outside_project_without_path_projection`.

The first release and LTS dates are scheduled under D-ADOPT-LTS1=A and recorded in the release documentation. Proof: git grep finds the dates in Docs/spec. The dates are the owner's choice and are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15).
The complete custom HTTPS example declares metadata, three ordered HTTPS origins, the Acme decoder, one archive selector and one existing installer, and it evaluates.
The finite decoder types and ReleaseDecodeError are defined; the decoder is pure and bounded and cannot expose direct-feed signature, key or proof fields.
Release.github derives one repository from the `Releases` source (`RefSource.Releases`), and Release.https keeps the logical source target and the metadata authority separate.
Provider validation refuses empty fields, malformed RFC3339 times, unsafe URLs, unsupported formats, unsafe paths, oversized data and ambiguous trees, each with its registered error.
Bare and prefixed SHA-256 assertions normalize to one lowercase 64-hex Sha256 value, and malformed values and unknown algorithms fail.
Metadata, artifact and redirect origins are authorized before their requests or follows, and a new origin cannot be trusted after the fact.
Raw, archive and app-bundle selectors stage one explicit asset and reuse exactly one existing installer, and release trust never authorizes a build or a launch.
The existing BuildStep.fetch hash and credential-free rules are unchanged by this card. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter BuildStep/fetch_` passes unchanged before and after.

The syntax this card adds has its Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax row, its Docs/Spec/syntax-decisions.md entry and regenerated editor grammars in the same change (Pkg.adapt resolver and asset fields). Proof: after `jet self devtools grammars`, `git status --short Tools/Editors` is empty, and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter grammar` and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter syntax_reconciliation` pass.

Option A (D-RELEASE-RECIPE1=A) is the only form: `Pkg.adapt` carries `resolver:` and `asset:` beside `source:`, and no `Recipe.release` wrapper exists. Proof: `git grep -n 'Recipe.release' -- Jetpack` finds only the E1270 rejection claim.

PackageModel/Tests/Release.jet and EnvModel/Tests/ModuleEvalReleases.jet cover the A declaration, the E1270 refusals (another source, a duplicate selector, `Recipe.release`) and SHA-256 normalization. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile packages --filter Release` and `JET=jet jet Jetpack/Bootstrap/Check.jet --area EnvModel` exit 0.
A first unpinned install and an explicit update discover moving releases, while a launch and a pinned offline replay never do discovery.
A channel SHA-256 identifies bytes only, direct feeds have no public signature, key or proof fields, and an existing authenticated-provider failure is a hard failure.
GitHub release pagination completes within 100 pages and 10,000 candidates, or fails with a typed error.
A moving selector needs a valid RFC3339 published_at and fails only on a tie at the latest time, and an exact tag selects one tag.
GitHub and custom feeds map to one candidate record, and installs and user-profile realizations share one candidate, origin, trust, hash and artifact contract.
Pins, caches and receipts bind candidate identity and observed bytes, and no credential or signed URL is ever persisted.

The 3 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: Pure/store_generations_empty, Pure/store_record_generation, JetpackTool/multi_store_root_commit_crash_recovers_before_pointer_switch. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: The PowerShell adapter keeps foreign meaning through the real adapter, or refuses precisely
cards.body:
Destination: values, errors, shapes, widths, calling conventions and imported source keep their declared meaning through the real PowerShell adapter, and anything unsupported, a toolchain failure, an ABI mismatch or a non-equivalent import gets a precise error with provenance instead of a guessed translation.

Source: #6632 c37 and c38 (carried from #986, the polyglot enterprise adapter for PowerShell, built in the retired Rust engine).

criteria.text: Foreign values, errors, shapes, widths, calling conventions and imported source keep their declared meaning through the real PowerShell adapter.
Unsupported constructs, toolchain failure, an ABI mismatch and a non-equivalent import each give a precise registered error with provenance, never a guessed translation.
The PowerShell binder round-trips dynamic state and cleans up its workers.
