cards.title: C imports marshal every C ABI shape on the native backend, and the C binder emits plain user-namespace declarations
cards.body:
Destination: `jet build` calls C functions with every supported ABI shape (F32 results, #Layout(c) structs by value, #Layout(c) enums, raw pointer parameters, #ABI(sysv64) imports, capability handles), C member lists resolve each library, the C binder emits user-namespace names and plain scalar returns, and the FFI example and the sqlite3 fixture run on every tier.

Why: C is the base boundary every other language reader builds on (D-FFI-PRIMS1=A, D-FFI-LANG1=A).

Source: #6366 c12, c24, c34, c35 and c44, plus its known-failing rows for cffi_write_capability and c_member_lists. Design: Docs/proposals/ffi-perfect-boundary-2026-10-31.md.

log.text: Owner order 2026-11-21: FFI work lives in G2 Dev Experience and stays frozen until Jet core bones are complete.
c2 multi-byte half landed in 462bbd1099 (p227): the C-import byte-span E0003 is gone; cffi_card436 now stops at E2104 for F32 parameters and the struct-by-value make_point, the rest of c2.

criteria.text: Examples/Interop/FFI/FFI.jet builds and passes its golden at O0 and O2 with no ICE (today: foreign import requires a checked direct C scalar signature), and its known-failing row is removed.

`jet build` marshals F32 results, #Layout(c) structs by value, #Layout(c) enums, raw pointer parameters and #ABI(sysv64) imports, and a C-import source holding a multi-byte UTF-8 character builds without E0003. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Cffi/cffi_card436_c_abi_shapes_round_trip`, `--filter cffi/cffi_repr_c_enums_match_native_c_layout`, `--filter cffi/cffi_raw_status_out_pointer_reads_only_on_success` and `--filter cffi/cffi_sysv64_abi_executes_native_symbol`.
A write-capability handle round-trips through a native C call.
A C member list resolves each library and its alias without E0105.
The C binder generates user-namespace names (no reserved `__bindgen__`, no E0067), and opaque-handle headers bind and check.
`#Import(c)` of an infallible fixed-scalar function gives a plain scalar return, not a Result with an undefined Never.
The sqlite3 C-module fixture imports through `use c.sqlite3`, and its calls dispatch to the C library on O0, O1 and O2.

Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Foreign/C/HeaderBinder.jet emits current Jet syntax, not the Rust-era `Task<I64 ! String>`, and special-cases no name (emit_async, unsubscribe). Proof: Examples/Interop/Polyglot callbacks, PolyglotGo and PolyglotPython pass their goldens on O0, O1 and O2 where their host tool exists, with their known-failing lines removed. (was #6418 c153)
A C function returning a `*U8` string reads as a Jet String? on the native backend: a null result is absent and a non-null result is copied as UTF-8, with no Jet.PointerAcrossCBoundary refusal.

cards.title: C boundary types: counted pointers as lists, sized booleans, pointer-sized integers, exact Int range stops and C strings
cards.body:
Destination: C pointer and integer shapes arrive as safe Jet types: a counted pointer is a list with no copy (D-FFI-CMAP1=A), `ffi.Bool<U32>` (D-PRIM-BOOLSIZE1=A), `ffi.USize`/`ffi.ISize` (D-PRIM-USIZE1=A), an Int out of range stops with E1003 at the boundary, and C strings follow their ballot once one exists (gate row FC1).

Source: #6366 c25, c29, c39, c40 and c41.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c4, c5 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: An `#Import module c.<lib>` row may declare a C counted-pointer parameter as a list of a fixed-width `T` (`[T]` or `View<T>` when C only reads, `&[T]` when C writes); Jet passes the element pointer and count with no copy, and a 64000-byte `[U8]` round-trips through a C checksum. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Interop/FFI/Adaptations/PointerCount` at O0 and O2.

An Int outside i64 passed to a C Int parameter stops with exit 70 and exactly one Stop [E1003] 'Integer value is outside destination width' at the call site, not E3010 in core.prelude, and its known-failing row is removed.

`ffi.Bool<U32>` in core.ffi holds a C API's sized true-or-false field (VkBool32, Win32 BOOL) with exact conversions to and from Bool (D-PRIM-BOOLSIZE1=A), and misuse is a registered error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter FFI/SizedBool` on O0, O1 and O2 and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter ffi_sized_bool_`.

`ffi.USize` and `ffi.ISize` in core.ffi are sized to the target, so a C binding is right on 32-bit and 64-bit targets (D-PRIM-USIZE1=A), and a lossy conversion is a registered error; core.mem.CSize (D-USIZE-TARGET1, #4524 c4) is reconciled to one type, as the ballot on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) decides. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter FFI/PointerSizedInts` on O0, O1 and O2 and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter ffi_usize_`.

C strings: once their ballot (on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15)) decides them, the chosen type has a registry row, an example with golden output on every tier and a misuse UI snapshot, or the spec lists the refusal with its reason and the Jet mechanism that covers the use. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter FFI/CStrings`, or the spec row and `jet test Tests/Guards --filter core_declarations`.

The 2 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: UI/CffiEnumBoundaries/CffiEnumOutOfRangeDiscriminantStaysAtTheCheckedBoundary, CffiEnumBoundaries/cffi_enum_out_of_range_discriminant_stays_at_the_checked_boundary. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Jet functions cross to C as callbacks with explicit registration lifetimes, including from foreign threads
cards.body:
Destination: a named pure Jet fn or a lambda passes to C as a function pointer with a stable symbol; captured and asynchronous callbacks get an owning registration plus a borrowed event per invocation, which can request stop without waiting on itself (D-FFI-CALLBACK2=A, D-FFI-CONCUR1=A); a callback that re-enters Jet from a foreign thread completes on a Jet task.

Source: #6366 c10, c13 and c31, plus its known-failing row for foreign_callback_reenters_jet_and_completes_on_a_jet_task.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): 2d + BLOCKED(host). c2: the async callback registration lifetime, days. c4 (MetaSuite J34) needs a C toolchain: on this host `Examples/Interop/FFI/Callbacks/run.jet` is SKIP-HOST tool:cc, and cffi_named_pure_callback_has_stable_c_symbol FAILs with "the C archiver is not installed".

criteria.text: A named pure Jet fn and a lambda cross to C as `int32_t(*)(int32_t)`, also from 4 threads, printing 42 10 40, and the known-failing row is removed.
criteria.evidence: Landed ab804c93a8 (p274, a named fn with an inferred carrier). On batch compiler p274 (dev d7285f91e6): cases Cffi/cffi_named_pure_callback_has_stable_c_symbol PASS (no known-failing row).

criteria.text: A captured async callback registration keeps its capture alive, the borrowed event can stop without waiting on itself, in-flight calls drain before release, and a later invocation is refused (D-FFI-CALLBACK2=A).
A foreign callback that re-enters Jet completes on a Jet task.
criteria.evidence: Landed ab804c93a8 (p274). On batch compiler p274 (dev d7285f91e6): cases FFICallbacksTasks/foreign_callback_reenters_jet_and_completes_on_a_jet_task PASS.

criteria.text: MetaSuite family J34 (native callbacks and C calling convention) passes its witness Examples/Interop/FFI/Callbacks/run.jet on every applicable tier, so the MetaSuite check reports no owed J34 row. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter MetaSuite` lists no owed row for J34.

cards.title: Foreign calls carry checked facts: derived effects, evidence per fact, out-of-bounds reach probes, and header-driven C++
cards.body:
Destination: each ownership, lifetime, effect and failure fact on a foreign row carries its basis and artifact coverage (D-FFI-CONTRACT1=A, D-FFI-FACTS1=A); foreign effects are derived from the locked artifact, never declared by hand; each extern form has a probe of what Jet memory a stray foreign write can reach; and C++ is adopted through the header-driven binder and ordinary Jet calls (D-CPPINTEROP1=A).

Source: #6366 c30, c32, c36 and c38. Design: Docs/proposals/ffi-perfect-boundary-2026-10-31.md.

log.text: Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c3 reworded; the text waited on an owner answer that ratified decisions already give, or on a choice within ratified scope; it is recorded as decided (Main's operational authority) and nothing waits.

criteria.text: Every ownership, lifetime, effect and failure fact on a foreign row names its basis and artifact coverage, and a wrong target, digest or ABI, or missing evidence, refuses admission (D-FFI-CONTRACT1=A).

Foreign effects are derived for a locked artifact: the compiler reads its imported symbols and call graph, maps libc and system calls to Jet effects through one table, and propagates with the same solver as Jet code; unknown reach stays every effect, and facts bind to the artifact hash (D-FFI-FACTS1=A). Proof: cases where libc `abs()` is admitted under `!Net`, a C library calling `connect` is refused under `!Net` with the chain named, a raw syscall stays every effect, and a changed artifact re-derives: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Cffi/derived_foreign_effects_`.

Each extern form has a probe recording which Jet memory foreign code can reach when it writes out of bounds, ending with measured no-surface fixes or a row for Main's ballot list with measured options. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Cffi/oob_reach_probe_` and a committed receipt.
Header-driven C++ makes real linked calls with supported ABI and value layouts and refuses unsupported types, including the C `Ptr<T>` boundary (D-CPPINTEROP1=A).

The 6 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: UI/ffi_boundary_evidence, UI/ffi_inline_c_mismatch, Cffi/ffi_capability_boundary_is_safe_for_qualified_c_calls, Cffi/cffi_close_capability_round_trips_through_the_native_c_boundary, Cffi/foreign_close_contract_registers_only_a_matching_consuming_function, PolyglotSystems/mixed_repo_edit_test_debug_profile_and_recovery_workflows.c. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: `use x: <lang>.<lib>` resolves the generated binding cache for every active foreign language, and planned ones stay reserved with clear errors
cards.body:
Destination: the resolver reads `.jet/bindings/<lang>/` for every active foreign root (D-FFI-LANG1=A, D-FFI-BINDER1=A) instead of reporting E1002 ReservedRootShadowed; planned roots (swift) stay reserved with E1002; a cache without a descriptor stamp fails closed; COM is honestly Windows-gated; binder errors (E0956, E3208) name the real cause.

Source: #6366 c3, c4, c17, c18 and c27, plus its known-failing rows for the js and com imports. The 2026-11-12 diagnosis on #6366: the rule is jet_driver_check_reserved_import (Loader.jet:2956).

criteria.text: `use plot: js.plotly` with a canonical-stamped `.jet/bindings/js` cache is accepted, while a planned `use swift.[foundation, ui]` reports E1002 with a UI snapshot. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Cffi/foreign_active_js_import_is_accepted_while_planned_swift_stays_reserved` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter swift_reserved_root`.

The js binding cache supplies symbols for plain, inline member-list and `pub use` imports, and a js import with no cache invents no symbols. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter Cffi/ForeignJS` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Cffi/foreign_js_import_without_cache_does_not_invent_symbols`.
A cobol binding cache with no descriptor stamp fails closed with E3208, not E1002.
A COM import is honestly Windows-gated with its registered error on other hosts, not E1002.
E0956's fix text names the real limitation and a workaround that is not the failing command.
E3208 carries the binder's root cause, including file-not-found.

jet inspect bind, inspect codemod and inspect audit (audit copies included) are built. Proof: every Tests/known-failing.tsv row on #6418 that reports E2104 for them passes on the default tier, and the rows are removed.

lowlevel/polyglot_go (Examples/features/lowlevel/polyglot_go.jet) passes its golden on the run and build tiers:  resolves through jet inspect bind output instead of E1002, and its known-failing row is removed.

The Go, Java, C# and Fortran binders live behind `jet inspect bind <lang>`. Each has an end-to-end example with a golden, error snapshots, a jetpack-provisioned toolchain, and registered effect roots. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter CLIPartsBindings/` (fortran_bind_runs_checked_column_major_array and the JVM and .NET rows), with their known-failing rows removed.

The 6 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: Cffi/foreign_js_import_uses_generated_binding_cache_for_symbols, Cffi/foreign_js_inline_member_list_uses_the_same_binding_cache, Cffi/foreign_js_inline_pub_member_list_reexports_the_namespace, Cffi/foreign_member_list_rejects_one_invalid_member_without_partial_import, Cffi/inline_foreign_alias_collision_is_rejected_in_one_scope, PolyglotSystems/cpp_clang_ast_binder_links_external_namespace_and_on_demand_surface. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: Language binders run real foreign code: Python, JavaScript, Lua, Ruby, Perl, PHP, R, Go, COBOL and Octave
cards.body:
Destination: each ratified language binder (D-FFI-PY1, -JS1, -LUA1, -RUBY1, -PERL1, -PHP1, -R1, -GO1, -COBOL1, -OCTAVE1) is a Jet package implementing trait Language (D-FFI-LANG1=A, #6519), generates its `.jet/bindings/<lang>/` module, and runs real foreign code with its ratified host model. PowerShell is #6942.

Source: the #6366 known-failing rows for the *_bind and sidecar cases. Each needs the binding-cache resolver (#6949).

criteria.text: Python: the sidecar binds, runs and launders failure.
JavaScript: the sidecar binds, runs and refuses dynamic types.
Lua: the embedded VM runs and recovers after hostile calls.
Ruby: dynamic state, timeout and cancellation round-trip.
Perl: dynamic state, timeout and cancellation round-trip.
PHP: a persistent bounded worker pool runs.
R: dynamic state and the worker lifecycle round-trip.
Go: a c-archive scalar call and a move-only cgo handle run.
COBOL: the copybook binder runs real GnuCOBOL and keeps COMP-3.
Octave: the sidecar runs a real matrix round trip.
`jet test Compiler --profile packages` passes the PackageModel claims of #3611–#3615 (FFI and C binders, language binders).

The 8 known-failing rows this card owns (rehomed by #6843 c7) pass and leave Tests/known-failing.tsv: Examples/Interop/Languages/Cobol, Examples/Interop/Languages/Lua, Examples/Interop/Languages/Octave, Examples/Interop/Languages/Perl, Examples/Interop/Languages/PHP, Examples/Interop/Languages/Python, Examples/Interop/Languages/R, Examples/Interop/Languages/Ruby. Proof: each named test passes in its suite on a batch compiler, and no row of Tests/known-failing.tsv names this card for them.

cards.title: User Rust crates in native programs: offline cargo, builds inside packages, foreign panics as stops, and undo hooks
cards.body:
Destination: a native Jet program uses a user Rust crate (D-FFI-RUST1=A, D-FFI-RUSTIMPORT1=A): cargo metadata forwards only CARGO_NET_OFFLINE, extern rust builds inside a package, a foreign panic stops as E3014 with one Jet source frame, and #Undo inverses of extern rust calls run with distinct identities across modules.

Source: #6366 c6 and c15, plus its known-failing rows for transact_ffi_with_undo and cross_module_foreign_undo_bindings. E3014 must be registered again with its emitter (2026-11-12 log on #6366).

log.text: Owner order 2026-11-21: CMake/Make/Cargo build import lives in G5 Jetpack and stays frozen until Jet core bones are complete.

criteria.text: Native user-Rust FFI: cargo metadata forwards only CARGO_NET_OFFLINE (the hosted path forwards all ambient CARGO_*).
extern rust builds inside a package (base64 prints aGk=).

A foreign panic stops with exit 70 as Stop [E3014] --> ffi.jet:7, and E3014 is registered with its emitter and a UI snapshot. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter DiagnosticsCoverage/ffi_runtime_stop_keeps_one_jet_source_frame` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E3014`.

The #Undo inverse of an extern rust call runs on rollback (prints `undo 3`), and two modules' undo bindings keep distinct identities. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Effects/transact_ffi_with_undo_registers_rollback_hook` and `--filter effects/cross_module_foreign_undo_bindings_keep_distinct_identities`.

cards.title: `jet generate` runs a checked #Job generator explicitly, previews and applies writes atomically, and records a reproducible receipt
cards.body:
Destination: D-DX-GENERATE1=A is built. A #Job with `generates:` and `inputs:` metadata is a source generator; `jet generate <Job>` previews and `--apply` writes every declared output atomically after an authority check; build and test never run generation; an unchanged plan gives an identical receipt.

Why: generated source must be reviewable and reproducible, never a hidden build side effect.

Source: #3693 c14-c18 (carried from #2442). Decision: D-DX-GENERATE1=A (reuse #Job for generators).

criteria.text: `jet generate --help` describes the explicit invocation, preview mode, authority requirements and receipt output.

An explicit `jet generate <Job> --apply` writes the declared outputs in deterministic order and records generator identity, source location, inputs, outputs, package authority and toolchain provenance.
Repeated generation with unchanged inputs is reproducible and rewrites no equivalent output, while changed inputs give a receipt naming the affected outputs.
Build and test never invoke source generation, and a missing or stale generated input is reported as an actionable source-local error rather than silently repaired.
A generator failure leaves no partial outputs, and the audit trail records the failed command, authority decision and source context without exposing unauthorized environment data.
Every jetpack_tasks case passes and its known-failing rows are removed.
A built binary dispatches the same jobs with the same output as `jet jobs`.

The built binary runs `after:` predecessors in order, stops on a failing predecessor, refuses a bad root argument with E1331 (exit 2) before any predecessor runs, and prints byte-identical output to `jet jobs` and `jet run`.

`jet jobs web --port 3000` forwards `--port` to the job while global flags stay with jet and `--` forwards, typed job arguments parse from argv, and reserved job names fail with E0928. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/jet_top_jobs_forward_flags_after_name`, `--filter jetpack_tasks/jet_run_job_typed_cli_args` and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter E0928`.
Job graphs, authority context, working directories and arguments are validated before any job effect runs, with a failure-path case per check.
Declared input and output freshness, dependency invalidation, per-job working directories and affected-subgraph watch work together.
Job dependency, status, inspection and the canonical lifecycle events use the one process and job identity model, with no second model.

`jet <job>` runs a project job by name before retired words, paths and path plugins are considered, and an unknown name suggests the project's jobs. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter JetpackTasks/top_level_jobs_precede_retired_words_paths_and_path_plugins` and `--filter jetpack_tasks/jet_top_job_runs_by_name_and_unknown_suggests_jobs`.
An executable example sets STAGE=prod through ProcessSpec.env on launched commands, with golden output on O0, O1 and O2.

Every generator is listed in one generator registry with a `--check` mode and one implementation, and the lander runs every check as a gate, so a generated file cannot drift (architecture review Repo1; census F20, F21). Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter generators_fresh` runs each registered generator's `--check` and passes.

Every generated registry table (CoreEnumRows, CoreStructureRows and the rest) comes from `b.generate` over its source registry, so it cannot be stale, and the precommit generator checks for those tables are deleted. Proof: `jet test Tests/Guards --filter generated_tables_from_build` and no precommit generator check for those tables remains.

cards.title: The gauntlet scores every cell by one peer law: in-group Jet/peer below 1.00 per metric, AOT against systems peers, run and dev against Python and JS, tiers as context only
cards.body:
Destination: the gauntlet harness, its status projection, the integrated gate and the Tower view apply one comparison law. AOT builds are scored against Rust, C, Zig and Go; `jet run` and `jet dev` are scored separately against Python and JavaScript; Node, Bun and Vite stay required web-development comparisons against `jet dev`; the main chart has one JS column and no Node or expert columns; the four peer tiers (scripting, managed, systems, ceiling) are reporting context only.

Why: a speed claim is only as honest as its comparator. A missing, mismatched or averaged result must never pass, and an out-of-group comparison must never block.

Decisions and rulings: AGENTS.md performance gate (Jet/peer < 1.00 with no Rust band, then Jet/ceiling <= 1.00 against Tools/perf/asm-parity); owner directions 2026-09-14 (group split, one JS column, hide expert columns) and 2026-11-08 (four tiers); D-PERF-RUNCELL2=A (the `jet run` wait is gated against Lua, LuaJIT, Python and Node), which supersedes D-PERF-RUNCELL1=B. Historical receipts are immutable.

Source: split from #2858 (measurement gate) on 2026-11-15; carries the merged #3404 harness-split criteria.

log.text: Wave 3B (dev ead79f56ba): cold jet run hello.jet peak RSS cut 62.09 -> 44.64 MiB (-17.45 MiB, -28.1%), wall 17.94 -> 17.32 ms via generalized stop-pad tail sharing (-1.40 MiB .text) and regenerated hot-text.list (8,262 entries, 0% stale).

Owner order (2026-11-22 13:37 EST): Gauntlet is a representative sample of general universal default codegen (any Jet program compiles to hand-optimized machine-code quality, never specialized example files). Run clean unloaded Gauntlet refresh + Latest Briefing delta once Wave 3 + compiler streamlining + sub-10s cold self-compilation milestone land, then pivot to G1-G6 burndown.

Pareto Stream B Wave 2A landed at dev ed1bac94eb: cold jet run hello.jet 20.04ms->17.51ms (-12.6%, min 16.60ms, RSS 80->70.5 MiB; driver+IR+x64+object+link now ~1.8ms total, remaining 10.8ms is JetSema); cold script30.jet 156.2ms->146.63ms (-6.1%, RSS -11.2 MiB).
