cards.title: Memory kernel performance: zero cost against the plain spelling, and the machine-code ceiling for every kernel primitive
cards.body: The memory kernel (#6842, D-MEM-CHOKEPOINT1=A) is built: one audited chokepoint for every raw memory action, with the address rule, single-use values, windows, sentry-tracked mappings and the runtime cutover proven there. Its two performance criteria move here under the owner's 2026-11-15 order that speed and size work belongs to G11 and does not block other goals. Work in flight: the inline-under-auto SUBs (kernel owner methods and from_addr inline under the default policy, constant divisors no longer stop inlining, the E0917 false positive for same-named calls) and the zero-cost paired cell (Tools/perf/ZeroCostPair.jet, 64 losses on p171). Ceiling cells measured on p160r (Jet/ceiling cycles): mapping 4.73x, allocfree 2.77x, compare 3.19x, resize 1.88x, rawword 1.35x, atomics 1.00x. Planned roots: an inlined call's Result boxes kept in the frame (landed 6595a58009), the allocator header cut from 24 B to 8 B, finer size classes.

log.text: Burn-down ranking (2026-11-24, by remaining workload; G2Regressions read the open criteria against dev 8a8ea0ee0b): weeks (perf). Kernel primitive ceiling cells.

criteria.text: (was #6842 c6, moved to G11 by owner order 2026-11-15: speed and size work moves to G11 so it does not block) Zero cost: kernel primitives inline at O1/O2. A paired two-program cell (kernel primitives against the direct spelling) and the cold self-compile show no wall or peak-memory regression on the reference machine; any loss is fixed before ratification. Proof: a committed receipt of the paired cell and the cold self-compile on the reference machine.

(was #6842 c11, moved to G11 by owner order 2026-11-15: speed and size work moves to G11 so it does not block) Owner order 2026-11-14: the kernel is safe and at the theoretical maximum performance for machine code, so the ceiling stage is open for it now. Each kernel primitive (allocate, free, resize, raw read and write, pointer offset, byte copy, move, fill and compare, atomics, mapping) has an asm-parity ceiling cell in Tools/Perf/asm-parity. Each cell uses the best known technique for its workload: SIMD copy, fill and compare chosen by size class and CPU features, branch-light fast paths for allocation and free, no redundant checks on paths sema has proved. Jet/ceiling is at most 1.00 in both cycles and code bytes at O2, measured live. Any safety check the kernel keeps appears in the reference at its smallest hand-written cost, and no check is removed to meet the ceiling. Any loss is fixed in the general lowering, not per cell. Proof: asm-parity `--gate` reports ok for every kernel primitive cell (as logged for rawword on p146).

cards.title: Shrink #Unsafe beyond memory: one typed syscall table, safe once-only runtime state, and no per-call regions for host leaves
cards.body: After the memory kernel (#6842) the inventory (jet Tools/agent/UnsafeRatchet.jet --inventory, p175) shows 842 #Unsafe regions in Compiler, the runtime, Core and Jetpack, and 0 outside the kernel files perform a raw memory action. 506 are not memory actions. By a first sort: about 160 runtime call sites each spell a raw Linux syscall (os_syscall_i64) inside their own region; about 52 write process-wide runtime state during start-up ('runs before any other thread exists'); about 48 are Core calls to private runtime host leaves; about 37 manage Secret zeroizing owners; 26 call crypto expert primitives; about 200 are unclassified. About 336 are raw memory actions inside the kernel files themselves. This card cuts the non-memory regions at their roots, so each unsafe fact is stated once in an audited home instead of at every call site.

log.text: Landed SSoT-3 (dev fd58fdc119e329df4d74248f90d90906c6886710): migrated all 42 remaining raw os_syscall_i64 calls and deleted duplicate LOADER_SYS_PERF_EVENT_OPEN/LOADER_SYS_CLOCK_GETTIME constants in Compiler/JetBackend/Source/Image/Loader.jet onto 8 new typed single-home wrappers in Compiler/JetBackend/Source/OS/Linux.jet (0 production os_syscall_i64 calls left anywhere outside OS/Linux.jet; SIGNAL_BOUNDARY strictly preserved). Unwrapped 14 redundant per-call #Unsafe blocks: UnsafeRatchet shrunk 1660->1654 (-16 cumulative from 1670, 0 outside kernel). Stage-2 self-host, CodegenCeiling 9/9, JetBackend 30/30, copy_ratchet, closed_lists, Hello.jet all PASS.

Landed SSoT-2 Slice 1 (ba92e090d6): migrated all 70 raw os_syscall_i64 calls across 19 Compiler/JetRuntime files onto 30 single-home typed Linux syscall wrappers in Compiler/JetBackend/Source/OS/Linux.jet using canonical OS_SYS_* constants, unwrapping 40 redundant #Unsafe blocks. UnsafeRatchet shrunk 1670->1660 (runtime regions 596->555, memory kernel outside=0). Verified full Compiler+JetRuntime+Core+Wasm build, Hello.jet run, JetBackend 30/30, CompilerData 0 rises, Tests/Guards 217/217.

criteria.text: The inventory's 'other' class is split into named classes (syscall, start-up state, host leaf, secret owner, crypto expert, and any further class the code shows), so no region is unclassified. Proof: jet Tools/Agent/UnsafeRatchet.jet --inventory prints 0 under other, and its test pins one region per class.

Syscalls: the OS layer has one typed wrapper per Linux syscall the runtime uses, each holding the only #Unsafe region for that syscall with its contract stated once. Runtime call sites call the wrappers and hold no region of their own. Proof: git grep -n os_syscall_i64 -- Compiler/JetRuntime outside the OS-layer wrapper file is empty, the inventory's syscall count equals the number of distinct syscalls, and the runtime fragment cases pass on O0, O1 and O2.

Start-up state: runtime state written once before other threads exist goes through one audited once-only primitive, so its writers hold no region. Proof: the inventory's start-up-state count is 1, and the runtime fragment cases pass on O0, O1 and O2.

Host leaves: Core calls runtime host leaves through the D-HOST-LEAF1=E ordinary-library route (#6615), so a Core call site holds no #Unsafe region for a host leaf. Proof: the inventory's host-leaf count under Core is 0.

Every remaining #Unsafe region names an irreducible reason (a raw action inside the kernel, a foreign crossing, or a ballot-approved expert boundary), and the ratchet's total falls with each step. Whether crypto expert primitives keep requiring #Unsafe is an owner choice on its own ballot. Proof: the ratchet baseline in Docs/Spec/safety.md falls in each landing commit, and the ballot is ratified.

Each core.os fact is computed once, in Core, not inside the runtime host, and reports the same value on O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter OS/Facts` on O0, O1 and O2, with the core.os examples passing. (was #3549 c19)

Every runtime function Core calls is a pub function of jet_runtime with a Jet name, Jet types (Int, not I64; typed handles) and a declared effect row. A generated comparison over every bound function proves each declared row equals the effect_kind and effect_leaf the compiler row held before the cutover, with zero differences. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Runtime/declared_rows_match` shows zero differences. (was #6615 c4)

A safe package that names a runtime function that isn't pub fails with the ordinary visibility diagnostic, and reaching a runtime C symbol needs #Import(c) inside #Unsafe. Proof: a UI snapshot for each. (was #6615 c6)

The runtime is an ordinary library (D-HOST-LEAF1=E) and the IR route tables (IR_RUNTIME_ROUTES, the route.export rows and the generated handle helpers) are deleted, so Core's runtime calls take the ordinary call path. Proof: `git grep -n -E 'IR_RUNTIME_ROUTES|route\.export' -- Compiler` prints nothing and `jet test Compiler --profile golden` passes on o0, o1 and o2. (was #6615 c8)

The compiler's effect-scope covers check reaches the runtime's one covers rule through the jet.runtime.authority binding `covers` (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Public/Authority.jet, export jet_authority_right_covers), not a C import. Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Policy/EffectScope.jet declares no #Import(c) and no #Unsafe, Tests/Guards/c_imports.jet has no CI_ALLOWED row for it, the C-string export jet_authority_covers is gone, and jet test Compiler/JetFoundation/Tests/Policy/EffectScope.jet passes the 33-row covers table on a jet built with it. SUBs: G8Scope-1c (any train), then G8Scope-1d (after a seed with 1c). Placed on #6615 rather than #6129 so this follow-up to G8Scope-1b's interim CI_ALLOWED row doesn't hold G8's closure. Proof: `jet test Compiler/JetFoundation/Tests/Policy/EffectScope.jet` passes the 33-row table and `git grep -n jet_authority_covers -- Compiler` prints nothing. (was #6615 c11)

Sema classifies the reachable Prelude closure into core, alloc and hosted layers (D-FREESTAND-PRELUDE1=A), and a program that reaches a layer its target lacks is refused with a registered error. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter freestanding_missing_layer_`. (was #6615 c16)

The 28 #Unsafe regions added outside the debugger and profiler since 2026-11-15 are reviewed, never blessed: UIBackends, Secret, World, Linux, Channel, Host, NetUnix, Scheduler and Sync runtime files; Core/Tasks/Tasks.jet (2833eeefb5); the Docs/Proposals DebugEvalNative probes (566d71f803); and 14 Tests rows (unsafe-diagnostic UI fixtures plus two Comptime and Conformance fixtures). Each is replaced by a safe API where one exists, or kept with a checkable reason, and the safety.md baseline accepts only the reviewed rows.

cards.title: Continuous landing cycle: Land.jet cycle runs census, batch compiler and full suite as one loop
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-15 ~15:30: fix the landing bottleneck and codify the efficient process durably. AGENTS.md (Delegation) now states the cycle. Until Land.jet carries it, Main runs it through scratch scripts (cycle.sh, suite.sh). The bottleneck was: two compiler builds per cycle (census build plus a separate batch build), the full suite only every three or four batch compilers (regressions found across ~50 commits and bisected by hand), generated-file conflicts returned to workers, and stages started by hand, leaving the heavy slot idle.

log.text: Cycles p189b and p189c ran this process with Main's scratch cycle.sh. p189 (16:00): the census went red in 1 minute, but the script built the unchanged tip for 20 minutes; fixed so a red census exits at once. p189b: a door-2 ICE held 1 submission. p189c: 20 landed at 15:57; the census build was the batch compiler; the full suite against p188 gave 18 new and 956 fixed rows, each new row routed to its owner by 16:20. Land.jet's generated-diagnostics retry landed in 488d251515 (c2 partial: its fixture proof is still open). The suite worker (c4) is GoalsB-5-2's queued SUB.

Finding 15:58: Land.jet serve and batch already set aside failing jobs and land the rest (bisect), publish the census-verified compiler as install-latest (the batch compiler), regenerate runtime generator outputs, and run each job's tests plus ui and golden for compiler changes. Main had been landing through scratch scripts instead of the service; that, plus intake.md rule 3 ('Full suites belong to milestones'), was the bottleneck. Real gaps in the tool: (1) the whole suite (cases and core included) on each train's compiler after landing, with new and fixed rows against the previous train, routed to that train's jobs; (2) DiagnosticRows regeneration for a conflict only in generated diagnostic pages. SUB Main-landing-cycle-intake fixes intake.md rule 3 and the AGENTS.md broad-suite line. Next: switch landing to Land.jet serve from cycle 190 and add (1) and (2) to batch.
Cycle 189 runs through Main's scratch cycle.sh (census build as batch compiler, full suite in parallel profiles, new.txt against suite-p188). c1 lands with SUB Main-landing-cycle in it.

criteria.text: AGENTS.md (Delegation) states the continuous landing cycle: one census takes every ready submission, the census build is the batch compiler, every batch compiler runs the full suite against the previous cycle, and the next cycle starts at once. criteria.text: Land.jet cycle applies every ready submission, drops only one whose hand-written source does not apply, and regenerates generated files instead of refusing a submission that conflicts only there. Proof: a fixture with one generated-file conflict and one hand-written conflict lands the first and returns the second.

Land.jet cycle keeps the census build as the batch compiler when the landed tip's tree equals the census snapshot, and builds the tip otherwise; one compiler build per cycle. Proof: the cycle log names the batch compiler's source and the tree comparison.

Land.jet cycle runs the landed submissions' proof lines and the whole suite (cases beside ui, golden and core) on the batch compiler, writes fails, new and fixed against the previous cycle, and names each new failure's candidate submissions. Proof: two consecutive cycles' new.txt and fixed.txt.
A census failure holds back only the submissions it implicates (by the files of its rows), and the rest land in the same cycle. Proof: a fixture census row on one submission's file lands the others.
Main's scratch cycle.sh and suite.sh are retired once Land.jet cycle passes c2-c5; the lander uses only Land.jet cycle. Proof: cycle logs of two consecutive cycles run through Land.jet cycle.

The census judges the snapshot's guards with the compiler under test: once the census build makes jet and its runtime pack, every guard shard and guard package runs on that jet, with it as $JET; with no build, or a build that failed or made no runtime pack, they run on the seed, so a broken build still lists every guard failure. Found in p393: the machine-door guard ran on the seed, so the ratified jet.report/v4 change (#3202 c10, D-DIAG-ONESHAPE1) failed the census, and an unintended change to machine output would have passed it. Proof: a census of a submission that migrates the Tests/Fixtures/MachineDoors goldens with the output change passes its guards row, and the census log shows the guard runs started on the snapshot's jet.

cards.title: Memory placement: the compiler puts values whose lifetimes nest on per-thread scope stacks (Goose learnings)
cards.body: Owner discussion 2026-11-16 on the Goose and Lobster mining run (Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-10-23-goose-lobster.md once landed). Goose keeps every growable value on compiler-assigned data stacks: an address reservation with a bump pointer, freed by one store at scope exit. It pays for that with restrictions (one growable per stack, no growable array elements, restricted recursion, whole-program specialization, wasm growth checks) and its own record shows prior region systems retreating to a collector or ownership. Jet already has the explicit route (#Context(allocator:), D-ALLOC-SITE1=A), the default heap (D-ALLOC-DEFAULT1=A) and the scratch escape rule (D-REGION-ALLOC1=F). The open question is what Jet does for code that names no allocator. Ballot D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 carries it; whichever option wins, the build's first criterion is a passing adversarial review in Docs/audits.

criteria.text: A dated adversarial review in Docs/Audits attacks the ratified option of D-PLACE-DEFAULT1: it states Goose's, the ML Kit's, Cyclone's and Rust/Zig arena practice at their best case with sources, and tests every claimed gain with a runnable probe or measurement (allocation cost, peak memory on a long scope, web checked growth, task-crossing values, recursion). Every gap ends on a criterion here or a ballot; the build starts only on a passing verdict.
criteria.evidence: Landed 3cbcaa71a0 (p406, dev 113879859e, 2026-11-21): Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, by Lens, states Goose, the ML Kit, Cyclone and Rust/Zig arenas at their best case with sources and tests each claim with runnable probes (Docs/Audits/PlaceDefault20261121/Probes: alloc, peak, pushes, recur, sends, tasks, web; log run-p400.log). Verdict: FAILS, so the build does not start. Every gap ends here: G1-G3, G5-G7 and G9-G12 are criteria c2-c4 and c6-c12, G8 is folded into G3 (c4), and G4 is c5, the calling-convention ballot that must be ratified first. Its audit case audit_reports_list_findings_without_a_disposition passed in the p406 proofs.

criteria.text: G1: A scope-stack allocation path exists that beats the heap: a prototype that leaves the thread's cache rows in place runs the review probe alloc.jet's `small`, `count` and `words` at O0, O1 and O2 faster than `heap` by the margin the design states; the review measured a 12-13 ns ceiling per short-lived value with today's bump route 1.4-2.7 times slower than the heap. Proof: the run logged beside the review in Docs/Audits/PlaceDefault20261121/Probes. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G1.

G2: The spec states what "outlives" means for list elements, map values, struct fields and boxed links, and cases show a word pushed into a stacked list, a field of a returned struct and a list of lists, each with the placement `jet inspect placement` reports. If the answer stacks elements, the element restriction (Goose) or a second mechanism goes to a ballot first. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G2.

G3: A census of reach, which also covers recursion (G8): `jet perf run --lens=alloc` on a compiler package's `jet check`, a Core test and a web example splits allocations by the rule that places them (stacked, stored-in-older, sent, recursive, returned through an indirect call), and the stacked share is published with the census; the review found the list path is 12 of 14,012 allocations in its story program. The gain claims stand or fall on that share. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G3.

G4: The calling convention for values returned to a caller's stack is ratified on a ballot before any build: a hidden argument on every function returning a growing value, specialization by destination, or the heap for any value returned through an indirect call (function values, trait objects, closures, plugin guests, C exports, hot patch, the debugger's evaluator), with each choice's cost at an indirect call measured. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G4.

G5: The design states the most stacks a thread holds and each stack's reservation, and a 64-thread probe reports VmSize and RSS within it; today the first arena block a process opens costs 16 GiB of address space and each further arena 256 MiB, and the review measured scope-end free at 110 times the peak, so last-use free is required. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G5.

G6: Chunked task stacks replace `context.scratch`'s 256 MiB per-task reservation as the one mechanism: the review probe tasks.jet with 10,000 tasks that each stack a value stays within twice the `none` row's VmSize and RSS. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G6.

G7: A value sent on one branch only is placed on the heap on every path: a case shows it, with `jet inspect placement` naming "sent". Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G7.

G9: Web growth holds: the review probe web.jet's grown-against-reserved share on V8 stays within one point of today's 12% once stacks are chunked. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G9.

G10: Stacked values stay visible: the alloc lens and the heap view report stacked bytes by call site and by placement rule, `jet inspect placement` names stacked values as well as heap ones, and checked mode poisons a stacked value's bytes at its reset and reports a later read as a use after free with the value's line. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G10.

G11: Placement is one meaning on every tier (I9): `jet inspect placement` prints the same placement for a fixed program at O0, O1, O2 and `--os=web`, and a case holds that output. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G11.

G12: A stacked value's last use counts every view, borrow and iterator over it, and every exit (return, break, `?` propagation, a stop) resets its stack: cases cover a view kept past the owner's last plain use and an early return. Found by the D-PLACE-DEFAULT1 adversarial review (Docs/Audits/2026-11-21-d-place-default1-review.md, landed 3cbcaa71a0, verdict FAILS), gap G12.

Fix it without weakening detection, inside D-PERF-ATTACH-WINDOW1=A: make the window load-robust (e.g. bound it in target CPU time rather than wall time) or derive the bar from the CPU the target actually used, never a looser fixed bar. Proof: the case passes in 3 consecutive full suites, and a sampler that keeps no samples still fails it.
criteria.evidence: Fix 3f49d4ac83 (on dev since p392, whose tree f768b6597e contains it): the outside attach window is the samplers own, and its CPU is the sampled threads schedstat run time. The case drops the fixed `samples > 250` and holds samples to that CPU: samples > 0, window_cpu_ns > 0, window_cpu_ns <= 2000000*samples + 20000000 (Tests/Cases/Perf/attach_samples_a_plain_jet_process.case:38-41). Perf/attach_samples_a_plain_jet_process PASSED in 3 consecutive full cases suites, p392, p394 and p399 (it failed in p391 before the fix). A sampler that keeps no samples fails `samples > 0` at line 38, and fails the ratio once the spinner runs 20 ms.

criteria.text: A release build never breaks the next command in its package. Found proving c19 on the p391 batch compiler: `jet build --release --output-dir=rel app.jet` inside a package writes `rel/app.debug` as a symbolic link to `.jet/symbols/.build-id/..`. The next `jet run app.jet` in that package then fails with Jet.DriverOperationFailed: "Can't securely read the sources ... rel/app.debug is a symbolic link", and its Fix tells the user to remove a file Jet itself wrote. Jet's own build outputs (the image, its debug link, .jet/) never count as package sources, or the debug file is written so no source walk trips on it. Proof: a case that builds --release with --output-dir inside the package, then runs `jet run` and `jet check` there with exit 0, and `jet crash` still names the frames of that release image's raw report.
criteria.evidence: Landed 996f45aa18, with the hard-link debug file; its split-unit regression fixed by Lens-p399-fixes (089970018b). Case BuildEntry/release_output_dir_inside_the_package_keeps_it_runnable (jet build --release --output-dir=rel inside the package, then jet run and jet check exit 0, then the image overflows and jet crash names `depth` from the store) PASSED in the p399 and p400 full suites. The unit a_split_debug_image_is_read_through_its_debug_link passes on p400 (proof row sp399fixes-1, rc=0; units 0 failed).

criteria.text: At a fault inside a runtime routine, jet debug shows at least what the crash report shows. Today, on the program_owned_main `plain` image (p392), the crash report backtrace lists jet_rt_stop_domain and unit.trap_simple_report above run at plain.jet:7, but `backtrace` at the SIGSEGV stop lists only `#0 run() at plain.jet:7` and `frame 1` is refused. Neither the stop nor any command names the faulting instruction, the address it read or the registers. The user line stays the stop line; the runtime frames are listed under it, and the stop names the faulting pc, instruction and address. Proof: a JetDebug unit test on a fault dev still has (mem.list_append from address 0x40 under #Unsafe in a release build with debug info, faulting inside jet_rt_mem_move) whose stop text names the routine and fault address 0x40 with the pc and instruction, and whose backtrace lists jet_rt_mem_move above the user frames, with the routine frame selectable.
criteria.evidence: Landed 64683b5928 (p401, dev 9a0ab2b757). On the p401 batch compiler: `jet test Compiler/JetDebug/Tests/Native.jet` rc=0 PASS, including the test at Native.jet:1180-1207 asserting "Program received SIGSEGV  prog.jet:6  in spill()\n  through jet_rt_mem_move\n  fault address 0x40  pc 0x", " <jet_rt_mem_move+", bt "#0  jet_rt_mem_move  at 0x" and the selected routine frame; the Debug cases a_fault_stops_like_a_breakpoint_with_its_stack_readable, stopping_exit_pauses_with_the_stack_whole, crash_dump_opens_typed and a_worker_s_stopping_exit_ends_after_delete_and_continue pass; UnsafeRatchet --check PASS. p401 full suite: no new failure from this commit.

criteria.text: jet debug says when it cannot read a stop's source instead of printing a blank line: on the p394 compiler, `jet debug JET --break $TREE/Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet:759 -- check hello.jet` run from a directory other than the tree root stops correctly at CheckProgram.jet:759 in sema_function_result() but prints "759 |         <- here" with the source text missing; from the tree root it prints "759 |     complete: value != None        <- here". The image records the source path relative to the build root, and the debugger resolves it against its own working directory. It should find the source relative to the build root recorded in the image (or the absolute path given to --break), and when no readable file exists it should print that the source is unavailable, with the path it tried, never an empty source line. Proof: a Debug case that runs jet debug on a built image from another directory and shows the stop's source line, and one with the source file removed that names the missing path. Transcripts: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/proof-6995-c23/transcript.txt (blank) and transcript-root.txt.
criteria.evidence: Landed Rivet c27.r2 as 9aee67021d in p400: the debugger resolves a stop source against the build root recorded in the image (digest-verified, .git walk capped) and says when it cannot read it. p400 full suite (49abf9184a): Debug/built_image_shows_its_source_from_another_directory PASS, Debug/built_image_names_its_missing_source PASS, Debug/built_image_never_shows_a_changed_source PASS, Debug/built_image_finds_its_source_through_a_breakpoint_path PASS, and the Debug suite 151 PASS, 0 FAIL.

criteria.text: The task-clock accounting holds under load: a run's period ends equal its kept samples plus those that fell in kernel mode, and the sampler reports and accounts any the kernel threw away (throttled or lost records) instead of letting the totals disagree. In the p401 full suite (dev 9a0ab2b757, 2026-11-21) Tests/Cases/Perf/task_clock_nominal_matches_kept.case failed at -O1 with nominal 460 against kept+kernel 458; the same case passed alone on the same compiler and in p399 and p400. Proof: the case passing in a full-suite run, plus a unit test in which the sampler's count includes injected lost or throttled records.
criteria.evidence: Landed c6406715ce (p425, dev 8ea723d82c): the drain tallies PERF_RECORD_LOST and THROTTLE/UNTHROTTLE records into the samples file (throttled period ends reported apart from kernel-mode ends). Unit test: Compiler/JetRuntime/Tests/Fragments.fixture/PerfRingTests.jet writes a fake ring with samples, one LOST record of 5 and 3 THROTTLE/UNTHROTTLE records, drains it and requires perf_samples_lost() == 5, the dropped tally == 5 and every throttle record in the file; its case RuntimeFragments/the_perf_ring_fragment_counts_lost_and_throttled_records PASS in the p425 full suite. Perf/task_clock_nominal_matches_kept (nominal = kept + kernel + throttled) PASS in the p419, p420, p422 and p425 full suites (suite-pNNN cases.out).

criteria.text: Jet tools report a built image's section sizes and dump a named section's bytes, so Tests/Cases CoreActivation (nm and size -A) and BuildEntry (readelf -x) drop the external binutils; the surface goes on a ballot first unless an existing jet inspect or jet debug --do form fits (D-DEBUG-LISTING1 lists symbols and segments, not section sizes or bytes). Found by Lens finishing c17 on p407 (2026-11-21). Proof: both cases run with no nm, size or readelf and check the same facts.
criteria.evidence: Landed b11ffab4c2 (D-IMAGE-SECTIONS1 A: `jet debug IMAGE --do sections`, `--bytes` adds their bytes) and 1eb8510abe (p420, dev 4f1f6c1c7f). BuildEntry/a_folded_string_read_only_for_its_length_costs_no_bytes and Debug/sections_list_an_image_and_its_bytes PASS in the p420 full suite, and neither calls readelf, size or nm (checked on 4f1f6c1c7f). CoreActivation (Tools/Perf/CoreActivation.mjs and its Jet twin run.jet) reads section sizes and symbols through `jet debug IMAGE --do sections|symbols`; `jet Tools/Gauntlet/PortBars.jet --entry CoreActivation` on gate-p420: parity PASS 8/8 cases do the job. The same run reports the twin losing the speed port bar (wall 3.15x, peak memory 3.38x the original), which keeps the original running under the port rules; that is a port-bar gap of the entry, not of c29.

criteria.text: Expressions evaluate at a stop in the compiler itself. Found by Main on dev b66642b8bc (gate-p429 jet), 2026-11-21, doing c5: `jet debug <jet> --break Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Casing.jet:216 --do "print function.name" -- check hello.jet` stops at Casing.jet:219 in sema_casing_function and its Locals show function = Func{… name: "greet_user" …}, but `print function.name` and `print function.params.len()` fail: from the tree root "no Jet function holds Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Casing.jet:219", and from another directory "couldn't read Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Casing.jet: not found". The evaluator finds the stop's function and source by the image's own recorded paths, whatever the working directory. Proof: a Debug case that builds a two-package program, stops in the dependency's function and prints a field and a method call of a parameter, from the root and from another directory.
criteria.evidence: Fix 717de0191d (on dev c137227f92). On the p436 batch compiler (dev 942f0c6d93): `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter Debug/print_evaluates_in_a_dependency_from_any_directory` PASS: a two-package image (pkgs/app, pkgs/lib) stops at lib.jet:11 in total() and prints made.count = 3 and made.doubled() = 6, from the build directory and from another directory, with no "Can't evaluate".

criteria.text: `bt N` prints at most N frames. Found by Main on dev b66642b8bc doing c5: `--do "bt 3"` at a stop in the compiler printed all 19 frames. Proof: a Debug case where `bt 2` at a stop three calls deep prints frames #0 and #1 and a line saying how many more there are.
criteria.evidence: dev 7693055e59, the p431 batch compiler (census build of that tip), its full cases suite (2026-11-21): Tests/Cases/Debug/backtrace_count_shows_the_first_frames.case PASS (commit aba25a8ca1: bt 2 three calls deep prints #0 inner and #1 middle, then "(2 more frames; `bt` shows them all)").

criteria.text: Expressions evaluate at a stop in the compiler itself, the jet binary built from Compiler: on the p436 batch compiler (dev 942f0c6d93), `jet debug <jet> --break Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Casing.jet:216 --do "print function.name" --do "print function.params.len()" -- check hello.jet` stops at Casing.jet:219 in sema_casing_function, and Locals show function = Func{… name: "greet_user" …}, but both prints fail with "Can't evaluate `function.name`: `Byte` changed its layout (its size changed from 9 to 16 bytes)". The evaluator compiles against the image's own layout of each type it reads, or reports which declaration differs. Proof: that command prints function.name = "greet_user" and the parameter count, and a Debug case covers a stop in a program whose layout facts include Byte.
criteria.evidence: Fix b4913d8f00 (Lens-6995-eval-compiler-layout, landed p438; dev d643d1e71a). On the gate-p438 jet (built from d643d1e71a), from the tree root: `jet debug <jet> --break Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Casing.jet:216 --do "print function.name" --do "print function.params.len()" -- check hello.jet` stops at Casing.jet:219 in sema_casing_function and prints function.name = "greet_user" and function.params.len() = 1, rc 0; Tests/Cases/Debug/print_evaluates_beside_an_enum_payload_it_never_reads PASS 1/1. Transcript: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/handover/6995-c32-p438.out.

criteria.text: A breakpoint given as an absolute path binds to the wrong function: on the gate-p438 jet (dev d643d1e71a), `jet debug <jet> --break <tree>/Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Casing.jet:216 … -- check hello.jet` reports "Breakpoint hit Casing.jet:216 in sema_casing_split_words()", while the same file given relative to the tree root binds to sema_casing_function (stops at 219). The absolute and the relative spelling of one file must bind the same line of the same file, or the absolute one must be refused naming the ambiguity. Proof: a Debug case that sets one breakpoint both ways and stops in the same function. Transcript: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/handover/6995-abs-path-break-p438.out.
criteria.evidence: 4b896b057d: native_line_file_match longest-suffix absolute path matching + JetDebug unit test + Tests/Cases/Debug/absolute_and_relative_break_stop_in_same_function.case PASS

criteria.text: jet debug: bt prints at most 256 frames with no way to see the outermost ones, so a stack overflow's caller (the frame that starts the recursion) is unreachable; bt must reach every frame, with an outermost selector. Repro: generate Tests/Cases/CompilerStack/LongChainScale.fixture/gen.jet 100000, then jet debug JET --do continue --do bt -- check sum.jet against a compiler that overflows on it.

jet debug: compiler-generated drop glue (jet_ir_drop_HASH, jet_ir_last_HASH) shows no type or source, so a frame cannot be tied to the type being dropped; glue frames must name the dropped type. Repro: generate Tests/Cases/CompilerStack/LongChainScale.fixture/gen.jet 100000, then jet debug JET --do continue --do bt -- check sum.jet against a compiler that overflows on it.

jet debug console: no thread or task listing (threads is an unknown command) and no run alias at the start stop, so a crash on a worker task cannot be placed among the tasks. Repro: generate Tests/Cases/CompilerStack/LongChainScale.fixture/gen.jet 100000, then jet debug JET --do continue --do bt -- check sum.jet against a compiler that overflows on it.

jet debug names a program image's missing symbols with no fix for a copied compiler: ~/.local/share/jet-lsp/tip23/jet (a copy of a stage-1 jet) gives Jet.DebuggerUnavailable because jet.debug is not beside it. The copy that editors run cannot be debugged where it runs. Proof: a case shows that jet debug finds a copied image's symbols by build id (or that a documented install step places them), and debugs the copy.

jet debug --do run fails with `Unknown command run`: the program starts paused at entry and only `continue` starts it. Every other debugger spells this run. jet debug --help never says the program starts paused. Proof: --help states the start state, and a case shows that `run` is accepted or rejected with a fix line naming continue.

A panic inside a Core builtin reports `--> <core.builtin>:0` with no Jet frame. The LSP crash `can't slice 11548 characters from 11545 to 11550` needed jet debug to find semindex_type_refs Build.jet:553, though the Jet.Panic text promises the Jet file and line. Proof: a case panics inside String.slice and the report names the calling Jet file and line.

jet perf attach --help and jet perf view --help print only `Usage: attach` / `Usage: view`, and jet perf attach PID fails with Jet.DebugAttachFailed under ptrace_scope=1 with no fix naming the cause. Proof: both --help pages list their flags, and the attach failure names ptrace_scope and its fix, in UI snapshots.

jet perf run loses its trace's syscall section under load. In the batch 38 full cases suite (dev b872a051a81, stage-2 compiler), Tests/Cases/BuildEntry/program_owned_main_print_writes_whole_buffers_at_every_level.case failed: the program printed all 3000 lines in order, but writes.py found 0 write syscalls in many-O0.jettrace (expected 2). Run alone, the same case passes 2 of 2. A trace taken under machine load must still record every syscall the program made, or say that it is incomplete and fail; it must never report a silently empty section. Done when the trace records the writes, or marks itself incomplete, with the machine under suite load.
criteria.evidence: dev 930090f78c8 (batch 44), run on the batch-44 compiler (its suite build also held #6852 p1/p2a, which this landing excludes; the landing tree passes all 240 guards without them): cases program_owned_main_print_writes_whole_buffers PASS.

criteria.text: jet perf run --help and jet perf view --help print only Usage, with no flag list (found by C16Perf, 2026-11-25, profiling CoreMathPair on the batch-44 compiler).

jet perf view --instructions with no argument shows only the hottest function; --instructions=<fn> works but is undocumented, and --frames accepts only jet or all, so a native function's samples (e.g. jet_rt_alloc_value_8) are reachable only through --json plus jq (found by C16Perf, 2026-11-25).

jet perf run takes only a .jet source, not a built binary, and comparing traces from two compilers needs --override-identity; profiling a built artifact and diffing two compilers' traces should work directly (found by C16Perf, 2026-11-25).

cards.title: Compile speed beyond the G7 pillars: 30M lines per second (fused per-function pipeline, direct image writer, compiler compiled well)
cards.body: Split from #5479.

log.text: Owner direction 2026-11-23: the G7 architectural pillars (#6978, #6795, #6794, #6796, #6797, #6798, #6793) target about 400K lines/s (#6794 c3); the rest of the road to 30M lines/s is G8 Hillclimbing work, this card. Measured 2026-11-23 on the 1.09M-line compiler corpus at O0: 25K lines/s, 92 us CPU per line, parallelism 2.2 of 32; 30M on 32 cores needs about 1 us CPU per line.

criteria.text: End metric: `jet build` of the corpus runs at 30M lines per second or faster, with output identical to the slower build. Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median).

Plan step 3, fused per-function pipeline: each function goes parse -> check -> lower -> select -> encode while its data is still in cache, with no whole-program intermediate copy, and a direct executable image writer replaces the object-then-link path. Gate: at most 1.5 µs of CPU per line and at least 20M lines/s. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens). Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median).

Plan step 4, the compiler compiled well. Starts only once the language is mostly stable (the major syntax, semantics and Core churn is done), so tuning isn't wiped out by later cutovers: Jet's own release code generation (register allocation, inlining, bounds-check hoisting, SIMD selection) and a SIMD lexer at 1 GB/s or more close the gap to hand-written machine code on the compiler's five hottest loops, each with an asm-parity ceiling cell (Tools/Perf/AsmParity). Every gain is general, applies to all generated code (owner, 2026-10-23), and is proven on a second program. Gate: at most 1 µs of CPU per line and at least 30M lines/s end to end, which is c3. Measured by the c1 cell: cold and uncached, `jet build` of Compiler plus Core on the reference machine (32 hardware threads), n=3 median, recording wall, user+sys CPU-s, CPU-ns per line, average parallelism (CPU-s / wall) and peak RSS. Output is identical to the previous stage's build (chain fixed point plus goldens). Proof: the c1 cell receipt (`jet Tools/Perf/CompileThroughput/Throughput.jet`, cold and uncached, n=3 median). and `node Tools/Perf/AsmParity/AsmParity.mjs --jet $JET --gate` for the hot-loop cells.

cards.title: Write and take marks move from & and && to ^ and ^^ (D-MARK-CARET1 cutover); links keep @
cards.body: Owner ruling, 2026-11-24, verbatim: "I approve the & and && to ^ and ^^ conversion". The write mark &T becomes ^T and the take mark &&T becomes ^^T in every position: signatures and receivers (^self, ^^self), function types (fn(^T) -> R, ^^fn(...)), write windows and element marks (edit: ^xs[a..<b], slot: ^xs[i]), matches that write into their subject (if ^place == { ... }), the stated receiver footprint (^self.field, ^self.[a, b]) and task captures (task ^^name { ... }). Meaning and placement are unchanged. & and && keep only their operator meanings; infix ^ stays a parse error and exclusive-or stays ~. Links keep @ (D-MEMREF1=A); the drafted link move D-LINK-CARET1 is withdrawn because ^ now marks a write. Size: about 24,200 signature write marks in 1,836 files, 2,650 value-position windows in 253 files and 2,900 take marks in 1,065 files (crude scan, 2026-11-24). Greenfield: one canonical form, no alias, no teaching diagnostic for a leftover & mark.
cards.plan: Two landings, because the compiler is written in Jet and its seed only reads & marks. Step A (one batch): the lexer and parser read ^ and ^^ as marks wherever & and && are marks, beside the old spelling; the formatter prints ^ and ^^. This bridge exists only until step B lands in the next batch. Step B (on the step-A batch compiler): a jet fix migration plan (mark-caret1) rewrites every mark in Core, Compiler, Jetpack, Tools, Examples, Docs code blocks and every Tests tree, case fixture and template; the parser stops reading & and && as marks; the registry (CoreSurface SIGIL_WRITE and SIGIL_MOVE, Spellings, MathLayout OP_CARET and OP_AMP notes), diagnostics text, UI snapshots, semantic tokens, editor grammars, spec and reference prose and LANGUAGE_REWRITES move in the same commit. The converter rule: a & or && is a mark when no operand ends before it (or a keyword such as task, if, return, in precedes it) and a name, [ or ( follows it.

log.text: Every criterion met on dev 930090f78c8 (batch 44): the ^/^^ marks show in the registry, diagnostics, LSP and grammars; dead-key fixes and the take-collapse report have UI proofs. Closing.

n=12 is open: probe on the batch-44 compiler, peek: fn(xs: ^[Int]) -> Int { xs.len() } and get: fn(^self) -> Int { self.n } check and run silently (2 2, 7 7). n=6 is open in part: Tests/UI/dead_key_circumflex_type.jet and _qualified_type.jet pass, but there is no ŝelf case, and the getting-started guide has no dead-key text (git grep nodeadkeys finds only Audits, Proposals and syntax-decisions).

Fresh-review findings for c6 and c4 (G1Generation-3-3, batch-42 compiler): the composed-letter hint covers type names only. A name such as `ŝelf` is told to write `ŝelf: Type`, and a parameter named `êntries` compiles silently. The lexer still has a `^=` token, so `a ^= 3` gets a misleading message. The comptime token names call the marks operator.caret and operator.caret_caret. The c4 grammar patch in batch 43 makes tree-sitter read ^^ as one token, colors the take mark in Zed (jet.wasm rebuilt), and flips the take_mark_is_colored_apart_from_logical_and guard to ^^; 7 guard filters pass on the batch-42 compiler.

D-MARK-CARET1: the fresh review by G1Generation-3-3 rewrote the record, which passes Tools/Agent/Ballots/Validate.jet. It was reviewed, posted and ratified A with the owner's two quotes from 2026-11-24. The review's addendum (Docs/Audits caret-marks review) and the c4 grammar patch (tree-sitter ^^ token, Zed take-mark queries) are queued in batch 43. Findings: the ĵson.Dyn panic and the silent ^^-to-^ dead-key collapse are now criteria; a stale `^=` token and the comptime names operator.caret/caret_caret belong to c4.

Batch 41 landed on dev e128950680d with the caret-marks docs and audit, the syntax-decisions record, the CaretMarks fixture and the dead-key E0119 type snapshot. On the rebuilt compiler, cases --filter CaretMarks passes 1/1 and ui --filter dead_key_circumflex passes 1/1. c6 stays open for the unknown-name and parameter diagnostics.

c6 finding from the dead-key UI snapshot (Tests/UI/dead_key_circumflex_type.stderr, batch 41): when a parameter type is a dead-key composite such as `x: Înt`, the write mark is lost, so `x += 1` in the body also reports Jet.ImmutableAssignment. That follow-on error says "`x` was made with `:`" and suggests `x := ...`, which is wrong for a parameter. The c6 work should suppress this follow-on after a dead-key E0119 and correct the parameter wording, then update the snapshot.
Correction: the migration commit on dev is f5d6176d36.

Step B landed on dev: 6998-b-core 640f60846a and the migration (2921 files, every change & to ^ / && to ^^) 3d at the e7155486f3 tip, merged into master 9ddc0975d6. Sweep items owned by G1Generation-2: diagnostic message texts still spell & marks (53 UI snapshots), the migration misses a mark after the && operator (one site, DebugCompile.jet, fixed by hand in batch 28), and 9 golden sources the migration did not reach.

Owner ruling, 2026-11-24, verbatim: "I approve the & and && to ^ and ^^ conversion". It followed the side-by-side comparison of the two spellings (24 excerpts from dev, five whole files and a layered program that runs today). The card now carries the mark cutover; the drafted link move D-LINK-CARET1 is withdrawn because ^ now marks a write, and links keep @. D-MARK-CARET1 holds the ruling as a draft until its review is posted, after which it is ratified A with the quoted ruling.

Correction, 2026-11-24: the previous log entry is wrong. The owner asked to discuss moving the write and take marks to ^ and ^^ (and with it keeping @ for links); he did not decide it. Everything that entry changed is reverted: the title, body, plan and criteria are restored, D-MARK-CARET1 is deleted, and D-LINK-CARET1 is restored as a draft. The link move stays as the owner approved it, pending that discussion.

Owner ruling, 2026-11-24, verbatim: "Yes Im saying cancelling the ^ from @ conversion and use ^ in place of &", following "what about ^ for edit permission and ^^ for move marking vs & and &&?". This cancels the link move recorded above (D-LINK-CARET1 draft deleted; links keep @ under D-MEMREF1=A) and authorizes ^ for the write mark and ^^ for the take mark, amending the spelling of D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A and D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A only. D-MARK-CARET1 is saved as a draft because Tower requires a full ballot record for syntax decisions; it documents this ruling and does not reopen it. Known cost, recorded from D-MOVE-SIGIL1: ^ is a dead key on German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Swiss and Nordic layouts.

Owner ruling, 2026-11-24, verbatim: "i approve the @ to ^ transition directly." This authorizes the spelling change (link type ^T, linking a new value ^value) and amends D-MEMREF1=A's spelling only. D-LINK-CARET1 is saved as a draft because Tower requires a full ballot record for syntax decisions; that record documents this ruling and does not reopen it.

criteria.text: First: a dated adversarial audit in Docs/Audits attacks the ^/^^ spelling against the strongest alternatives (today's &/&&, C++ T&, Rust &mut, Swift inout, Odin ^) on reading, typing (dead keys on European layouts), diff noise and tooling; every gap it finds is engineered away or named with its cost and mitigation. D-MARK-CARET1 then carries the full ballot record, is reviewed and posted, and is ratified A with the owner's quoted ruling.
criteria.evidence: Docs/Audits caret-marks review plus its fresh addendum (0a8ae1ce960 on dev). The gaps it found are engineered away or carried as criteria with their cost and mitigation: dead-key typing (c6), dead-key qualified type panic (c11, now met), collapsed take mark (c12). D-MARK-CARET1 was posted with the full record and ratified A.

criteria.text: Step A: the lexer and parser read ^T and ^^T as the write and take marks in every position & and && hold today (signatures, receivers, function types, windows, element marks, match subjects, receiver footprints, task captures), beside the old spelling, and the formatter prints ^ and ^^; a UI case covers each position, nested and layered (the Layers.jet program from the comparison runs and prints the same output in both spellings).

cards.title: Compiler cleanup: Rust remnants, one source of truth, architecture and idiom
cards.body: Owner order (2026-11-24 12:00): handle every finding of the cleanup analysis by 15:00. This work takes precedence over #6851. Tools written in other languages are NOT removed yet; they are only deduplicated and organized. Findings (measured on dev e7155486f3): about 3,800 comment lines in Compiler/Core/Jetpack cite the deleted Rust original; the Core API is restated in up to six places (Core sources, Core.rows, CoreSurfaceInventory.rows, the Registry signature tables, CoreRecordRows/BuiltinMethods/BuiltinStatics/RuntimeHandles, 27 backend *ABI.jet hand layouts); 938 hand closed lists without a home and 315 shared-member pairs; about 93k committed generated lines; the tool roots table in four copies; 701 sema signatures thread the same context bundle and 407 functions take 12+ parameters; 2,067 panic( calls in compiler source; few yielding loops, patterns, pipes or methods against 8,585 push loops.
cards.plan: Ranked by size of the finding: B (one Core truth) and E (sema context) are largest, then A (Rust remnants), D (closed lists), F (idiom), C (generated copies), G (panics), H (tool roots). E's redesign needs its adversarial review audit first. Staffing: G1Generation-2 B then D; G1Facts-2 A then G; TypeIDSlice3-3 E then F; orchestrator H and C.

log.text: Follow-up found by BallotCutover while proving n22: 36 RuntimeHandles flags say display/show/debug: true with no matching jet_rt_handle_* export (DataStatus, DataError, LogField, WalkEntry, HTTPRequest/Response show, DeliveryEvent and others). The probed ones render through their Core declarations, so the flags look stale; they go with n2's single source of truth for the Core API.

n16 perf half holds: on dev 43951bb7788 (batch 47 compiler), JET_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT=<batch47 export> jet Tools/Perf/CoreMathPair.jet --jet <b47> --rows <batch-43 rows> → 'core math pair: pass', bodies/rows: -O1 wall 0.937, cycles 0.932, peak RSS 0.993; -O2 wall 0.988, cycles 0.986, peak RSS 0.993 (even). Examples/Math golden: 144/144 PASS on o0/o1/o2. Still open: the accuracy half. No submission proves each function within 1 ulp of the correctly rounded result on the reference set (+-0, +-inf, NaN, subnormals, huge sin/cos arguments) on every tier. Assigned to C16Perf.

B n=2 ruling: term.take (keyword name; Jet has no raw identifiers) and the three non-String tls.client forms (first-param and error types differ; no overloading) stay as the last compiler-known Core call rows. A #Builtin.Serves marker would be a second naming mechanism (I8), and renaming public members is public API: both owner-gated. G1Checkers drafts one ballot (rename / marker / keep two guarded rows) after the CoreCallRows deletion. Every other row is removed in the current series.

n=22, revised 2026-11-25: the opaque-handle print crash comes from the structural derive admitting a Core handle that IR lays out opaque (FileReader too, which is not on the list), not from the list. About 70 Core handle types print correctly through their record schema or native type row, so the refusal keys on IR's own fact: a carried handle with no record schema, native type or Core-owned shape. That fact moves to JetFoundation with IR_NATIVE_TYPES and IR_RECORD_SCHEMAS as one source, which IR, Comparability and the derive all read. This also fixes a false refusal of printing a struct whose fields are printable handles (Hold{limits: EncodingLimits, how: NetShutdown}).

n=22, decided 2026-11-25: TempDir, TempFile, FileLock, UnixListener, UnixStream, Pool, TLSStream, HTTPRequest and HTTPResponse are on sema's synthetic Printable list, but showing any of them is an internal compiler error (display of core.files.TempFile, display of Shared<…>). They leave the list. The structural derive refuses a Core type whose own handle row has no render form, through the existing derive-refusal diagnostic with a UI snapshot. They never printed, so no feature is removed, and no output format is invented. Giving these types a Display text would be a public product choice, made only by a ballot.

B (n=2) slice 3 plan, accepted 2026-11-25 (G1Checkers): 38 Core.rows dispatcher rows in 4 families. A: 16 receiver role rows on Core structs (Query, DataGroupedQuery, Stream, JobQueue) become #Builtin.Role methods. B: 8 native receiver rows become methods over jet.runtime #Import(c) bindings, in two seed stages. C: 8 module rows become Core declarations, with the sema specials moving into bodies or Core rule impls. D: 6 native module rows become bodies over jet.runtime bindings. CoreCallRows.jet, CoreCalls.jet and TExpr CoreCall are deleted last (about 300 references). Rulings: list .query gets no role-resolved receiver sugar (a hidden second dispatch path); it uses an existing [T] method form, or a ballot if none exists. reflect.of may add a RoleKind case if role cases are compiler data, not registered syntax. worker handler_name goes to a ballot only if no comptime form exists.

n=22, decided 2026-11-25: SocketAddr and UDPPacket are runtime-owned native addresses, so their façade fields become priv in Core. A literal outside core.net gets the private-field diagnostic (UI snapshot), not an ICE. Handles print through their Core Display impl as the one path, not through an IR fallback. Still open: sema rewrites addr.host/addr.port into net.socket_host/socket_port calls (JetSema Places.jet:484), a field read the declaration doesn't carry. Whether it moves to Core-declared accessors is a public-surface question for a later B slice, and goes to a ballot if the spelling would change.

B (n=2) scope, decided 2026-11-25: Core.rows rendered by the compiler from hand-written CoreCallRecord rows (CoreCalls.jet, CoreCallRows.jet) is a second source of truth and does not meet n=2. Plan, largest first, G1Checkers: (1) field-default params on the declared-signature path; (2) plugin.load moves to a Core declaration with a body over a jet.runtime.plugin binding, in two seed stages, which deletes CoreSignatures.jet (p5 leaves plugin.load as its only row); (3) the dispatcher rows migrate family by family to Core-declared forms, and CoreCalls.jet and CoreCallRows.jet are deleted with the last family. Any form not already registered goes to a ballot first.

Batch 45 landed: dev 4b48f2bc485, master 2df1af6a626 (22 commits). Met A (n=1), n=19, H (n=8); E (n=5) reworded to its review's narrowed design, proof JetSema/Tests pending. Suite regressions routed as batch-46 fixes: c36B TypeId handle crash (~110 rows, c36B-fix3), Atomic miscompile (p2b2a1-atomic), related_rows effects and the Data.jet citations (watch-effects-fix-r2), copy ratchet (c36B-fix2). coremath-residual second program at -O1: 0.358 s -> 0.170 s (ratio 0.473), same output. The CoreMathPair gate script built its rows side against dev's Core, so it gave no result; it gets fixed before the n=16 rerun.

Batch 44 landed on dev 930090f78c8 (113 commits; #6852 p1/p2a held for their r2/r3). Met n=4, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15. Open: B n=16 (the CoreMathPair gate still loses at -O2: wall 1.022, cycles 1.025; the fix is the batch-45 coremath-residual), n=19 (n19a/n19b in batch 45), n=20 (compiler-data rises, C16Perf), n=21 (freshness_ms). Known regression carried to batch 45: HTTPServerLifecycle handler-task-failure comptime ICE (cause between stage44b and 44c, fixed by 6999-B-b44-fix5).

Correction: criterion 18 (a '??' fallback in an intrinsic argument never runs) was added from a diagnosis C16Perf has since withdrawn, and is removed. The probe used stage44f-exp's Core, where from_bits is wrapping(I64{bits}). The batch-44 tip's Core uses checked(..) ?? core.math.__numeric_stop(..). Its IR keeps the stop call, and FloatBitsRangeStop exits 70 natively. The batch-44 rebuild's golden run checks the remaining tiers.

B ranked plan, as counted on batch-44 tip 4b640637407 + p3a-c, largest share first:
(1) Registry/CoreRecordRows.jet, 1,236 lines: 1,159 field rows over 265 owners. 130 owners (505 rows) restate a Core struct and become generated by Tools/Agent/CoreRecordRows.jet --check|--write from the Core declarations, with a guard (CoreEnumCases precedent). The 135 undeclared owners (654 rows: Compiler* records, reflection *Info records, AsyncPolicy and others) get Core declarations, after which their rows generate too.
(2) Hand ABI layouts: 25 files, 578 offset/size constants over about 123 records (UIABI 134, DataABI 133, RealtimeABI 40, NetErrorABI 34, ScalarReflectABI 30, WsABI 28 and smaller ones). They become generated from the checked Core layouts by one generator.
(3) Core.rows: 37 dispatcher rows left (from 72): 17 source-role, 8 native receivers, 4 max_arity, 2 deprecated, and others.
(4) Signature tables: CoreHostSignatures 10 rows, CorePlatformSignatures 3 rows plus about 285 lines of grammar, CoreSignatures network. CoreValueSignatures and WebCoreSignatures are gone.
(5) CoreSurfaceInventory.rows 60 entries, CoreEnumPayloadRows about 31, CoreCallExtensions 11.
Owner: C16Perf. p2 is in batch 44; p3a-c are queued for batch 45.

A facts (batch-44 tree): name_mangle is gone, but its scheme survives. RuntimeHandles.jet runtime symbols are still mangled (__jet__x3ccorelib_x3e_score_d…), ast_comptime builds "__jet_{name}" (Comptime.jet:826-834), and InlineModules.jet:370 encodes module paths the same way. __jet_ is also the general generated-name prefix (Predicates.jet GENERATED_NAME_PREFIX, Jetpack SyntaxRegistry copy) used by sema temporaries, CLI entry, link and panic edges. The criterion needs a ruling on scope: the mangled-symbol encoding goes, and generated temporaries keep a reserved prefix. Stale Rust prose still in Docs/Spec: Contributing/agent-engineering.md:36 (NativeTaskBody.rs), Contributing/bootstrap.md:145 (cargo build of the Rust jet), architecture.md R6 (line 2243), core-library.md:149-150 and 193, cli.md:1626 and 2051, canvas-parity.md:12, stdlib-api-laws.md:621.

D decision (orchestrator, within criterion n=4): a duplicates.tsv pair whose lists share variant names but carry different payload types (value-model enums such as the SQL, JSON, CLI and form scalar enums) or whose packages cannot reach each other (layer) is not a shared-member duplicate. The closed_lists guard derives both reasons from the checked source and refuses a row whose stated reason fails; no hand-written label counts. Every other pair collapses to one home.

H finding (batch 43): Roots.jet locates the roots table from sys.executable(). That is the script path under jet run, but a compiled tool copied outside its checkout finds no table, and roots.value() then reads only the environment. cb935728c30 swapped CompiledWorkloadPeerLauncher's HOME-derived fallback for roots.value(JET_SCRATCH_ROOT), so its self-test (which runs a copy in scratch) reported a fail-closed host. Fixed in the batch tree (cb773ec5808): the self-test passes the launcher its checkout's scratch root through the launcher's own override variable. Real use keeps the launcher inside the checkout. Any future tool run as a copied binary must be given its roots the same way.

c10, decided: a Core constructor whose meaning is an IR construct with no runtime C symbol (tasks after/__channel_new/__channel_bounded, event __event_with_policy/__hook_new/__decision_hook_new/__async_new) leaves Core.rows as a Core declaration filling an Inline builder role. That is the existing role mechanism, as InlineFloatSqrt uses; Core still declares the function, which is what B requires. Condition: the stage-3 patch deletes every row fallback and the row-path wrapper, so one implementation remains (6999-B-c10b-rows does).

B, decided (implementation within ratified scope): after 6999-B-c10a-rows, no Core.rows row declares CoreCall frame_accesses; only JetSema/Tests/FrameCoreCallFixtures exercises the machinery. It is deleted as a separate patch stacked on c10a-rows (with_frame_accesses parsing, BodyCodec field, CoreCall-only Frames.jet scheduling, the fixture case; E2967 retired by the registry route if nothing else emits it), unless a queued row stack adds a frame_accesses row. Basis: B's end state removes the dispatcher rows; a mechanism with no production user is dead (AGENTS.md I8, greenfield cutover).

Batch 43 regression from the sema .copy() cleanup (F stream; landed in batch43-tree as 740d2b8d2fd): the codemod removed .copy() text inside string literals as well as the calls, in 34 lines across 7 sema files. Effects: E0120/E2307/E0201/E0209 autofixes inserted an empty edit while marked Safe and BehaviorPreserving; fix text lost its .copy(); the generated CLI parser pushed borrowed argv entries, so MissingMoveMarker hit every typed-args program, including the wordfreq and csvtransform perf builds. Run43c found 41 golden, 68 ui and about 30 cases failures from it. Fix c83ca982de1 in the batch tree restores every in-string .copy() (each file's count equals its count before the cleanup) and raises the copy_ratchet ceilings to the actual counts. TypeIDSlice3-3's E-4 codemod now proves string and comment invariance with strscan before submission. Batch 43 also fixed: H's Roots.jet import missing from the CodegenCeiling case's copies; B's receipt.attach role needing core.encoding loaded (loader demand, 9994790c236).

Correction to the binding Int defect, after C16Perf read ir_route_declared (BuildRoutes.jet): every route Word, binding or row, Int or IntN, already reaches its export as the exact-Int carrier. A .Word slot is boxed with jet_int_owned_from_i64 before the call. So the 134 exports that read the carrier and the four process limits are correct. The defects are the exports that read a route Word natively: c9's new _ns pair (held), jet_task_timeout_duration_ns and any others the sweep finds. A value of 2^62 or more reaches them as a node pointer and is used as a number. The fix: drop the binding narrowing, flip every native reader to the carrier, and add a guard ratchet and witnesses. IntN keeps the carrier ABI in that patch. IntN crossing natively (no box for fixed-width values) is a separate speed change, ranked once its gain is measured.

The I1 defect above is systemic. A runtime binding crosses an Int parameter as a native I64 (ir_route_call_args -> ir_core_native_int), but 134 runtime exports read 196 such parameters as the exact-Int carrier (jet_int_owned_to_i64, host_native_int, int_fits/int_word and others). Any value outside the inline range [-2^62, 2^62) is then read as a boxed node pointer. Families affected include db_vfs, sys_fd/sys_shared, crypto_jetc, ui_host, fs_directory, process_signal, file_reader, fs_lock, job_queue, ws and net_unix (scan by C16Perf). Implementation choice, within the binding contract: a binding lends an Int-typed parameter as the exact-Int carrier, the same ABI rows use (one mechanism). Each export applies its own range policy in the runtime, and codegen does no narrowing (I9). The few exports that read native are flipped. The runtime_leaf_exports guard refuses a native read of an Int binding parameter. Witnesses cover 2^62, 2^63-1, 2^64+5 and a negative value. C16Perf builds it as one stage patch before c9's bindings and before c10.

Defect found by C16Perf while doing c9 (memory safety, I1): spec_output_limit, memory_limit, open_file_limit and memory_scope have Int bindings in jet.runtime.process that pass a native I64. Their runtime exports read the value as the exact-Int carrier (jet_process_limit_i64: int_negative/int_fits), so a limit of 2^62 or more is read as a boxed-Int pointer. ProcessSpecWitness tests only the carrier form. Fix: make each export read the form its binding passes, with a witness at and past 2^62 for each limit; C16Perf takes it before c10. The c9 patches (runtime bindings, then roles, then rows) are queued for batch 44, with the bindings as its first stage.

c15 second half (jet_http_build_resolve gets a Jet body and loses its row) is held back from batch 43: stage 43e failed. The seed compiles Core/HTTP/Client.jet with its own built-in Core.rows, where core.http.client does not own the name (Jet.UnknownFunction at Client.jet:1965). The body and the row removal must be two stages: a priv Core body under a new name first, then the public name and the row drop on a compiler built from it. Sent back to its author as -r3. Batch 43 was rebuilt without it, door ceiling 6, and relaunched.

c16 stage 3 (core.math Float leaves as Jet bodies) is held back from batch 43: the paired cell Tools/Perf/CoreMathPair.jet, bodies (stage 43c) vs rows (stage 43b), failed the perf gate. -O1 wall 5.68x, cycles 5.76x, peak RSS 1.007x; -O2 wall 5.86x, cycles 5.89x, peak RSS 1.014x (receipt $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/tmp/orch/perf43/receipt.json). The stage also declared __numeric_stop without priv, which Jet.PublicDunderName refuses. Batch 43 was rebuilt without stage 3 and 3b. Its door ceiling is 5, since __to_bits_f32 and __from_bits_f32 stay compiler-known. Until the role declarations land, the raw_memory_lowering_rows guard row 'every core.mem intrinsic row lowers a primitive the memory kernel declares' fails on dev, because stage 1's InlineFloatSqrt row has no Core declaration. C16Perf is finding the cause with jet perf, fixing it in the general mechanism, and splitting out the role declarations first. #6852 c8 met on dev.

Batch 42 landed on dev (7 commits, eb7aaf51a8b; master aa346cc3f06). F: 9ea3e765bb1 drops nine unused JetSema imports, and 3e121525551 applies jet fix's safe class across JetCLI. B c13: a3114e69049 routes a binding's function parameter as a callback, and f48b199fee2 adds the receipt_attach binding. B c16 stage 1: 5b76d9fd0ca builds Float sqrt, fma and the F32 bit roles as operations. H: 9e9bc24cfa6 lets a #! script reach the files it imports; cases script_reaches_the_files_it_imports passes. Suites vs batch 41: golden, ui and cases have no new failures, except the keep_sink_survives_o2 timing check, which passes alone. Guards: 2 rows fail until batch 43's Core halves land (raw_memory_lowering_rows InlineFloatSqrt, and copy_ratchet BuildRoutes.jet 28/27, fixed by 5422c69f2c9). Batch 43 started on the batch-42 compiler.

Batch 41 landed on dev e128950680d (36 commits, merged into master). It carries the stage 1-3 jet.runtime bindings, stop-dotenv, E-3 record links and the caret-marks docs. Five fixes found by the batch-41 suite land with it: (1) env.decode now reaches FS.Read through jet.runtime.sys.dotenv_read, so ShapeProjection, AppConfig, the env_config UI fixtures and the EnvOverlay decode fixture list FS.Read; (2) chunks(size) names its Core bodies by role (ProcessStdoutChunks/ProcessStderrChunks), which the door fix had missed; (3) the build_time guard sliced lines by bytes; (4) kernel.tsv gains the circumflex lists; (5) runtime_leaf_exports reads a Never result as no word. On the rebuilt compiler, every row batch 41 lost passes, and Tests/Guards gives 236 passed, 0 failed.

H (c8) status on dev cba553447ac: the table Tools/Agent/roots.env, its three readers and the three byte-identical Roots.jet copies under Tools/Agent hold, and Tests/Guards/tool_roots.jet passes. It only scans Tools/Agent, though. Outside it, about 20 sites in 18 Jet tools still restate the defaults (jet-dev, jet-seeds): Tools/CI/{AgentWorkloads,CompiledWorkloadPeerLauncher,CompiledWorkloadPeerLauncherCheck,CompiledWorkloads}.jet; Tools/Gauntlet/PortBars.jet; Tools/Gauntlet/Kit/Source/PerformanceSurface.jet; Tools/Gauntlet/Entries/CoreLibCompare/check.jet; Tools/JetpackInfra/TestToolchainUpdate.jet; Tools/Perf/{CodegenCeiling,WebBundleCheck}.jet; Tools/Perf/Scaling/Gate/Source/Gate.jet; Tools/Perf/Selfhost/Run/run.jet; Tools/Perf/{CoreLibCompare,EnumCodecBench}/run.jet; and shell text in Tools/Perf/{CoreActivation,EnumCodec/JetAdapter,EnumsetBench,FunctionBoundary/Run,HelloCompile/Bench,JetcProfile/Live}/run.jet; plus Tools/Release/Seed.jet and Tools/AgentEval/RunColdContext.jet. c8 stays open until they read the table and the guard covers all of Tools/. The duplicated-scripts part of c8 has no recorded sweep yet. The shebang import defect (a #! first line breaks sibling file imports) is still open.

E-3 decision (orchestrator): environment and program join the one checking record as View<T> windows over one-element lists built at the thread roots (D-MEM-VIEWRET1 stored views). freeze() is not used: it lowers to a clone (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Direct.jet:sema_call_check_freeze). The 87 ancestors from sema_check_bodies_parallel take View parameters, readers keep their no-copy read parameters, and the record init takes the views as ^^View so jet audit copies shows 0 copies. A probe checks and runs a view in a task.group child and in a task capture at O0, O1 and O2. Gap recorded as fact: Jet has no view of a single value, so one-element lists stand in for it; a single-value view is new language surface and needs a ballot before anyone builds it.

F (#17 follow-up), recorded as a fact: a jet fix sweep of a package compiled through another unit (the runtime's merged unit.jet) is proven by that unit's check (LaneCheck runtime_check) or jet build --profile dev Compiler, never by a per-package check. Root of the JetRuntime sweep failure: L0101/L0102/E0514 edits were offered in bodies with an unresolved name (E0102/E0107). 6999-F-fixer-unit withholds them there, with a mutation-checked test. cards.title: Clause sublanguages become marker vocabularies: #States, #Protocol, #Migration, #Defer, x.freeze() and Distinct<T>
cards.body: Owner approved greenfield proposal item P1 ('Clause sublanguages become marker vocabularies') on 2026-11-25 in chat. Each remaining contextual-keyword clause becomes a Prelude marker or method that takes an ordinary value; the generated handle types, checks and diagnostics stay the same. 13 words leave the language here: state, protocol, client, server, migration, rename, add, remove, change, via, defer, freeze, distinct. validate and check go with item P5, policy and wrap with item P2. The second tier (extern, task, yield, it) is not part of this approval and waits on the owner. Source: Docs/Proposals/2026-11-24-greenfield-language.md, Part 2, item P1; evidence and first review: Docs/Audits/2026-11-24-greenfield-language-review.md (both in the master checkout, not yet on dev). Second-tier ballots posted 2026-11-25 (reviewed by ReviewTierTwo): D-FOREIGN-MARKER1 (recommends building the ratified #Import rust.<crate> form), D-TASKS-SPAWN1 (recommends keeping task), D-YIELD-EMIT1 (recommends emit(v) through Emit<T>), D-TABLE-IT1 (recommends retiring it). Their review is Docs/Audits/2026-11-25-p1-second-tier-review.md (in the master checkout, to land on dev). Note from the review: a retired word stays reserved until its lexer row is deleted (Keywords.jet:2), so each cutover deletes the row.

log.text: Posted the four P1 second-tier ballots; recorded two defects the review found.

criteria.text: Design review: a dated audit in Docs/Audits attacks the whole mechanism of proposal item P1: it names every place the same fact or operation lives today, the exact cutover list and the copies it deletes, and passes; every gap it finds becomes a row here or a ballot.

`state { A -> B }` becomes `#States({…})` taking a record of transitions, and `protocol { client: … server: … }` becomes `#Protocol([…])` taking a list of message steps; both keep today's generated types and diagnostics.
`migration { rename add remove change via }` becomes `#Migration(from:, steps: [...])` whose steps are ordinary values built with typed key paths (proposal item P8).

`defer` becomes a `#Defer { }` block marker, `freeze` becomes the method `x.freeze()` beside `x.copy()`, and `distinct T` becomes `Distinct<T>` with its invariant written as `#Check` (proposal item P5).
One greenfield cutover: the 13 words leave JET_KEYWORD_LIST and the syntax registry, every in-repository use migrates, and no old spelling or teaching path remains.
An executable example with golden output proves the feature on every applicable tier, and the spec, reference pages and editor grammars describe it.

The ballot D-FOREIGN-MARKER1 (proposal item P1 second tier: foreign code blocks `extern rust "…" { }` become a `#Foreign(…)` marker) is decided, and its ratified outcome is built in one cutover with every in-repository use migrated.

The ballot D-TASKS-SPAWN1 (proposal item P1 second tier: the `task` word becomes `spawn` inside a `#Tasks { }` scope) is decided, and its ratified outcome is built in one cutover with every in-repository use migrated.

The ballot D-YIELD-EMIT1 (proposal item P1 second tier: the `yield` word becomes an `Emit<T>` effect) is decided, and its ratified outcome is built in one cutover with every in-repository use migrated.
The ballot D-TABLE-IT1 (proposal item P1 second tier: the table word `it` becomes a bound name) is decided, and its ratified outcome is built in one cutover with every in-repository use migrated.

Independent of the ballots: the loop meaning of `it`, which D-LOOP-SUBJECT1=A rejected, is built anyway (`loop nums -> it * 2` gives [2, 4, 6] on jet a0.0.46), and Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Diagnostics.jet:381-382 teaches it. Proof: that loop is refused with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot, and no diagnostic text teaches it.

Independent of the ballots: E0805's text says "declare `Stream<T> ->`" but Jet writes `-> Stream<T>` (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Statements/Loops.jet:196, Tests/UI/yield_outside_generator.stderr:6-7), and the comments at Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax/Spellings.jet:153 and PackageFiles.jet:461 call `task` reserved although it is contextual (`task: "…"` binds). Proof: corrected text, regenerated snapshot, and `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter yield_outside_generator` passes.

cards.title: Marker roles as one ladder, a wrap role that replaces policy declarations, and a jet expand source lens
cards.body: Owner approved greenfield proposal item P2 ('Marker roles, a wrap role, and a source lens') on 2026-11-25 in chat. A marker's power is the effect row of its compile-time methods: note, check, generate, wrap, rewrite; only rewrite needs consent. A marker struct may implement a run-time wrap method, which replaces the policy … { wrap(call) { … } } declaration form; policy and wrap leave the grammar. Source: Docs/Proposals/2026-11-24-greenfield-language.md, Part 2, item P2; evidence and first review: Docs/Audits/2026-11-24-greenfield-language-review.md (both in the master checkout, not yet on dev).

criteria.text: Design review: a dated audit in Docs/Audits attacks the whole mechanism of proposal item P2: it names every place the same fact or operation lives today, the exact cutover list and the copies it deletes, and passes; every gap it finds becomes a row here or a ballot.

A marker struct that implements `wrap` wraps the function or block it is written on at run time without changing its body; `apply(Name(args), f)` keeps working, and the `policy … { wrap … }` declaration form and its two words are removed in one cutover.
metaprogramming.md names the role ladder (note, check, generate, wrap, rewrite), and a root can deny any role per dependency with a registered diagnostic.
`jet expand --lens source FILE` prints the checked file with every derive, template and marker output inlined and labelled with its marker, and `jet debug` can step through that text.
The examples that use policy declarations (Examples/Basics/Functions/CallablePolicies.jet and its siblings) migrate to wrap markers with unchanged golden output.
An executable example with golden output proves the feature on every applicable tier, and the spec, reference pages and editor grammars describe it.

cards.title: One Boundary trait drives CLI, HTTP, MCP, jobs, tests, exports and foreign-language bridges
cards.body: Owner approved greenfield proposal item P4 ('One boundary contract') on 2026-11-25 in chat. A function's signature is the schema at every edge: decode arguments from a wire, call, encode the result, map failures to the right audience, and derive the typed client, schema, docs, form and help text. This widens the endpoint contract of card #6865 into a Core Boundary trait. Owner condition: foreign-language interop is planned to ship as libraries, so those bridges implement the same Boundary trait instead of a compiler-side derivation per language. MCP keeps its SDK (D-MCP-SURFACE1); its builder accepts any Boundary value. Source: Docs/Proposals/2026-11-24-greenfield-language.md, Part 2, item P4; evidence and first review: Docs/Audits/2026-11-24-greenfield-language-review.md (both in the master checkout, not yet on dev).

criteria.text: Design review: a dated audit in Docs/Audits attacks the whole mechanism of proposal item P4: it names every place the same fact or operation lives today, the exact cutover list and the copies it deletes, and passes; every gap it finds becomes a row here or a ballot.

Core declares a `Boundary` trait (decode, call, encode, failure mapping, schema, client, help) and #6865's endpoint contract becomes its HTTP implementation, with one decoder, one error mapping and one schema generator shared by every edge.
`#CLI`, routes, `#Job`, `#Test` and `#Export` all implement `Boundary`; one function gains a CLI command, a route and an agent tool by adding markers, with identical validation and errors.

Foreign-language bridges, which ship as libraries, implement `Boundary` for both directions (calling into Jet and calling out), so a Python, Node or Rust bridge library needs no compiler-side per-language derivation.
The MCP SDK's builder accepts any `Boundary` value with no compiler discovery, keeping D-MCP-SURFACE1.
An executable example with golden output proves the feature on every applicable tier, and the spec, reference pages and editor grammars describe it.

cards.title: One Predicate value: #Check replaces validate, check and #Invariant, and feeds the prover, decode, forms, db filters, schema and tests
cards.body: Owner approved greenfield proposal item P5 ('One predicate value') on 2026-11-25 in chat. A predicate is a pure Bool expression over a value and its key paths. #Check(p, text) on a type is an invariant checked at construction and decode and proved where the prover can; on a field it validates. #Pre/#Post and range types such as Int(0..150) stay and produce the same Predicate value. validate and check leave the grammar.
